THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THAT RETRACTION: func_8005A90C at 99 of 103 words and
87 DIFF with none of it, 13 with the boundary, 11 with the late temporary back
in its parameter, and 2 with the dead reference -- the last three all at 103 of
103 words. It is still 2 DIFF, so none of this is confirmed by a match; what is
measured is that each step moved the floor, which the retracted sentence said
it could not.

### A DEGENERATE LOOP BEFORE THE FIELD STORES BUYS CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS

When a run of field stores is followed by a call that takes some of the same
values, sched1 hoists the whole `$aN = value` setup to the TOP of the block --
above the chain that computes the structure pointer. Read in `verify.py --full`
on both sides, each value so hoisted then has its last reference at its copy
instead of at its store, so it no longer overlaps the pointer, and the
allocator needs that many fewer callee-saved registers. A `do { } while (0);`
early in the block splits it so the setup cannot rise past the split.

Measured on func_8005A90C (unk_2CDC0, 103 words), each step on the last:

     99 words, 87 DIFF   no boundary: 4 callee-saved registers, frame 0x28
    103 words, 13 DIFF   + `do { } while (0);` after the first store:
                           6 callee-saved registers, frame 0x30

Four words, and it is the whole frame difference: two `sw`/`lw` pairs. In the
build without it b and c both have their last reference at their argument copy,
which the hoist has moved above the pointer, so b then shares a register with
k, c with e, and i with the late temporary -- four in all; the listing has
`{p, b, c, i, k, e}` mutually conflicting -- a six-clique -- and spends $s0-$s5
on it. `advise.py`'s `CALLEE-SAVED ... target saves $s5, built does not` and
its FRAME row are the diagnosis; the register-only rows under it all follow
from this one and are not worth reading first.

The START position is the lever, as in the degenerate-loop section. The same
`do { } while (0);` on the same 87-DIFF base, by the statement it follows:

    k = i;                101 words, 95 DIFF   -- too early, buys nothing
    e = &D_80086A40[k];   103 words, 12 DIFF
    e->unk_14 = c;        103 words, 13 DIFF
    e->unk_18 = 0x7F;     103 words, 17 DIFF
    e->unk_00 = i;        103 words, 17 DIFF
    e->unk_04 = p;        103 words, 19 DIFF
    e->unk_08 = c;        103 words, 19 DIFF
    e->unk_1B = 0x40;     103 words, 21 DIFF
    e->unk_10 = b;        103 words, 21 DIFF

So anywhere from the pointer's own statement to the last store buys the
registers -- the word count is right in all eight -- but only the first two
slots lead anywhere: the full chain below reaches 2 DIFF from either of them
and from none of the others. WRAPPING the stores in the loop instead of
separating them with it is 16, 19 and 18 DIFF for one, three and six of them.
An `__asm__ volatile("")` in the best slot measures 12 as well, so the lever is
the block boundary and not the asm -- prefer the loop, which is plain C and
needs no `DEVICE` comment.

WHICH ARGUMENT REGISTER IS SET FIRST is not a lever: `calls.c:1852` emits the
wholly-register parameters with `for (i = 0; i < num_actuals; i++)` over an
`args[]` filled front-to-back, because `PUSH_ARGS_REVERSED` (calls.c:41) is
gated on `PUSH_ROUNDING` and the mips config does not define it. So `$a0`
before `$a1` is what every call site emits, and a listing with the other order
got it from sched giving the later copy a strictly higher priority -- which
needs that value to have a use in the block besides the call. func_8005A90C's
park is 2 DIFF on exactly this and records the spellings that do not reach it.
CORRECTED 2026-10-31: that sentence was inferred and is wrong -- a use of the
value after its copy is after the call, and the call pins the block end. The
listing's order came from the `$a1` copy being emitted BEFORE the call, as the
fence insn after the loop notes. func_8005A90C LANDED on it; see "TWO ARGUMENT
COPIES IN THE LISTING'S ORDER" at the end of this file.

The spelling does not matter: in the full chain `do { } while (0);`,
`while (1) { break; }`, `for (;;) { break; }` and -- which the degenerate-loop
section does not say -- a `while (0) { }` whose body never runs all measure
identically, as do two of them in a row and any of them with a dead
`c = c;`/`b = b;`/`e = e;` inside. `expand_start_loop` has already emitted the
NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG by the time the condition is known, so a zero-trip `while`
buys the boundary the same way a one-trip `do` does.

### A DEAD TEST ON THE STORED VALUE STOPS THE ARGUMENT-REGISTER SHARING

Once the registers are there, one store may still read `$aN` rather than the
value's own register (the section two above). Giving the value one more
reference -- anywhere, including a reference that emits nothing -- stops it.

On func_8005A90C the `unk_08` store read `$a1` against the listing's `$s4`.
Writing the function's existing `return -1;` as

```c
    if (c)
    {
        return -1;
    }
    else
    {
        return -1;
    }
```

is 9 DIFF, 11 -> 2, and costs no words: the arms are identical, so jump.c
merges them, but `c` has been counted one more time before that happens.

It has to be THAT value. On the same 11-DIFF base, the same shape with the test
on e, i, k, p or r is 11 -- no effect at all -- on `c || b` it is 3, and on b or
on `b || e` it is 12, i.e. WORSE than doing nothing. `c` and `c || c` and
`c || e` are all 2. So the lever is one extra reference on the value whose store
is sharing, and register pressure in general is not it.

This is the "A DEAD reference is still a reference" lever applied to the
sharing rather than to allocno priority, and it is the counter-example to the
claim above that the sharing can only be chased through the register count.

### THE LATE TEMPORARY GOES BACK INTO A DEAD PARAMETER

A value produced by the last-but-one call and consumed after the last one needs
a callee-saved register, and gcc gives it the register of whichever parameter
has just died rather than a fresh one. Spelling it as that parameter is what
reproduces the listing.

On func_8005A90C the result of `func_8005ECA0` lands in `$s3`, which is the
parameter `b`'s register; `b` is dead from its own argument copy onward. A
fresh `u32 t` puts it in `$s1` instead: `b = func_8005ECA0(r);` in place of
`t = func_8005ECA0(r);` is 13 DIFF -> 11, with the word count unchanged at 103
either way. Reusing a dead parameter is free -- no copy, no word -- and the
permuter finds it readily (it was the first thing it produced from a 12-DIFF
base), so it is worth trying by hand before a search: the candidates are the
parameters whose last reference precedes the call.

### COMBINE CANNOT FOLD ACROSS A BASIC BLOCK BOUNDARY

`try_combine` only ever runs on a pair joined by a LOG_LINK, and LOG_LINKs are
built by life analysis with an explicit same-block test:

    if (y && (BLOCK_NUM (y) == blocknum)
        && (regno >= FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER || asm_noperands (PATTERN (y)) < 0))
      LOG_LINKS (y) = gen_rtx (INSN_LIST, VOIDmode, insn, LOG_LINKS (y));

                                                     -- 2.7.2 flow.c:2135-2146

So a copy whose single use is in ANOTHER block is never a combine candidate at
all. That is the one general way to keep a reg-to-reg copy that combine would
otherwise fold, and it is worth knowing because the other routes are closed on
this target: `REG_USERVAR_P` is `SMALL_REGISTER_CLASSES`-only in combine.c
(see the REG_USERVAR_P section), and `volatile` is not a fence between two
insns (section 10). The remaining in-block route is the one func_800599B0's
park describes -- modify the copy's SOURCE between the copy and its use, which
`can_combine_p` does refuse -- and that needs a source the C can name.

The price is whatever the boundary costs. A basic block boundary needs a label
with a live use or a jump, and func_80041E70's park prices all five ways of
buying one in a straight-line body: `thread_jumps` runs before cse, jump1's
dead-set DCE removes the obvious ones, a duplicate store is deleted, identical
if/else arms cost one to two words, and `do { } while (0)` -- which does end a
cse block via NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END -- cost a word in all three placements there.
So this lever is free only where the function already HAS a branch between the
copy and its use, and otherwise it costs about what it saves. Check for an
existing boundary before building one.

### A CONSTANT FOLDED INTO A LATER SHIFT needs a SECOND SET, not a boundary

func_80041E70's one remaining word is `p->unk_87 = 0x10;` followed, in the body
of `if (p->unk_54 & 1)`, by a doubling of it. The listing doubles the register
the store left live:

    80041E8C  addiu  $v1, $zero, 0x10
    80041E94  beqz   $v0, .L80041EB0
    80041E98   sb    $v1, 0x87($s0)
    80041EA0  sll    $v1, $v1, 1
    80041EA4  sb     $v1, 0x87($s0)

Eighteen C spellings emit `addiu $v1, $zero, 0x20` at 80041EA0 instead, all at
270 words: the field read, in place or through a temp, `<< 1`, `2 * x`, `x + x`,
`((u8 *) p)[0x87]`, a `(s32)`, `(u8)`, `(s8)`, `& 0xFF` or `| 0` on either side,
and `(u8) 0x10`, `(s8) 0x10` or `~0xEF` as the stored constant.

**The boundary from the section above does not stop this fold.**
`do { } while (0)` as the first statement of the if's body is free here -- 270
words, unlike the three straight-line placements this park prices -- and the
fold still happens, so whatever folds it is not reading a cse block table.

What stops it is a SECOND SET of the pseudo between the constant and the shift,
which is the `can_combine_p` route above. A non-volatile

    __asm__("" : "+r"(v));

on an `s32` local carrying the 0x10 emits the listing's `sll $v1, $v1, 1` and
costs no word. `volatile` costs one in all six placements measured: it is a
scheduling barrier, so `addiu $v1, $zero, 0x10` can no longer be scheduled into
the load-delay slot after `lw $v0, 0x54($s0)` and a `nop` appears there.

It still does not land the function, because moving the 0x10 out of the field
and into a local is what pays for it. The local's live range now crosses the
branch, sched1 hoists `lw $v0, 0x54($s0)` above `sh $v0, 0x6E($s0)`, those two
stop sharing $v0, and the local falls to $a0: 9 to 12 DIFF over fourteen
placements, against the 1 DIFF of the folded spelling. `register s32 v
__asm__("$3")` puts it back in $v1 -- the pin alone is free, 1 DIFF on the
unmodified park -- and then the `sll`, both `sb`s, the `sra` and both branches
match; 4 DIFF is the best of nineteen pinned placements, and what is left is the
0x100 store scheduled after the unk_87 store instead of before it.

**IT LANDED on 2026-10-30, and the fix is that the SECOND SET BELONGS TO THE
CONSUMER, NOT TO THE CONSTANT.** The paragraph above puts the extra set on the
pseudo that carries the 0x10, which is the one thing that must not have one:
`birthing_insn_p` (section 8's sched1 lever) bumps `addiu $v1, $zero, 0x10`
only while that pseudo is set exactly ONCE, and the bump is what places it
after `lw $v0, 0x54($s0)` instead of above the 0x100 store. Launder the value
on the way OUT instead and the constant stays single-set:

    s32 v = 0x10;
    ...
    p->unk_6E = 0x100;
    p->unk_87 = v;
    if (p->unk_54 & 1) {
        __asm__("" : "=r"(r) : "0"(v));
        p->unk_87 = r * 2;
        p->unk_6E = p->unk_6E * 2;
    }

`r` is the local that later holds `func_80042900`'s result, and reusing it is
load-bearing: a fresh local for the laundered value is 271 words, and an asm
that does the shift itself into a fresh local is 3 DIFF, because what is left
is the sign-extension falling from $v1 to $v0. The asm must sit inside the
`if` -- hoisted above it, 268 DIFF. `__asm__ volatile` also MATCHes in this
position; the plain form is kept because volatile is a scheduling barrier
elsewhere. The three equivalent spellings `r * 2`, `r << 1` and `r + r` all
MATCH, and so does an untied `"r"(v)` input.

**AND A FIELD READ-BACK CAN NEVER PRODUCE IT, which retires that whole
family.** cse forwards a QImode store to a later read only as a CONSTANT. Put
a value cse does not know into `p->unk_87` -- launder the local before the
store rather than after it -- and the read in the `if` body becomes a real
`lbu $v1, 0x87($s0)`: 271 words, measured in four placements. So the listing's
`sll $v1, $v1, 1` on a still-live $v1 is proof that the original held the 0x10
in a LOCAL, and the eighteen field-read spellings above were never going to
work. Splitting the field read from the shift through an `s32` temp is 4 DIFF,
and holding the 0x10 in a `u8` or `s8` local is 4 DIFF, against 12 for a plain
`s32`, `s16` or `u16` one -- all still folded.

### A PARAMETER always reserves its incoming register, unless there is a call

`set_preference`'s second branch (global.c:1611) fires on the incoming copy
`(set pseudo (reg aN))` whenever `reg_allocno[pseudo] >= 0`, and records both a
copy preference and a full preference for that argument register. `find_reg`
then avoids it for every higher-priority allocno, because `regs_someone_prefers`
(global.c:956) is built from `hard_reg_full_preferences` (global.c:883). So a
parameter that global-alloc allocates holds its own argument register against
everything else, however the source is spelt. The four ways out, and what each
needs -- worked on func_8004F330 and worth checking before spending a session
on "why does this value not take $a0":

* **Downgrade the preference**: no. `set_preference` records a plain rather
  than a copy preference when the SET's source is an expression rather than a
  bare register (`copy = 0`), but `regs_someone_prefers` carries both kinds.
* **Make the register illegal for the parameter**: needs the hard register live
  inside the parameter's range, which in a function with NO CALL it never is.
* **The `prune_preferences` size escape** (global.c:879): a rival's
  preferences are dropped from `regs_someone_prefers` when the rival is not
  larger AND this allocno prefers the same registers -- so a competing value
  CAN take the argument register, if it prefers that register itself. A
  hard-reg preference comes only from a copy to or from that register, i.e.
  from an argument setup or a return value. In a function with no call there is
  nothing to supply one. (`allocno_size` counts WORDS, so the "larger" branch
  never applies between two pointers.)
* **Confine the parameter to ONE basic block**, so `reg_allocno < 0`,
  local-alloc owns it, and `set_preference` never fires. This is the one that
  works -- and it is the same shape whose entry copy then coalesces away, which
  is a word short wherever the listing spends that copy.

The last two lines are the usable content: in a function WITH a call, give the
competing value its own preference by making it an argument; in a function
without one, the parameter's register is simply not available, and a park that
needs it should be read as needing a different parameter or block structure
rather than a different spelling.

**AND THE FOURTH ESCAPE DOES NOT DELIVER THE REGISTER TO A RIVAL.** Confining
the parameter to the entry block does stop `set_preference` firing on the
parameter's own pseudo -- `.greg` loses that allocno entirely -- but the insn
left behind is `(set local (reg aN))`, which is itself an incoming copy, so the
preference transfers to that local. Measured on func_8004E9EC (unk_1C540)
2026-10-30: with `n` used in two blocks, pseudo 81 prefers $a1, conflicts with
the function's flag, and the flag is pushed to $t0; with `kk = n;` as the only
use of `n`, pseudo 81 is gone from `.greg` and pseudo 89 (`kk`) carries
`preferences: 5` instead, takes $a1, and the entry copy coalesces away. An
intermediate also confined to the entry block (`tt = n; kk = tt;`) collapses
the chain and changes nothing. So the escape frees the argument register only
when nothing else has to live across the function; where the listing SPENDS
that copy, the parameter's register is not obtainable by any spelling, and the
park should say so rather than keep trying.

### Keep $v0 busy to make a `lui`/`addiu` pair share its register

`lui $a0, %hi(SYM)` / `addiu $a0, $a0, %lo(SYM)` and
`lui $v0, %hi(SYM)` / `addiu $a0, $v0, %lo(SYM)` are the same two
instructions; which you get is whether the `(high)` pseudo and the address
pseudo were allocated the same register. The high dies at the `lo_sum`, so
they CAN share, and local-alloc hands the high the lowest free register --
$v0 -- unless something is live across it.

So the lever is to put a value in $v0/$v1 across the materialisation. In
func_800387D0 that is reading the clamped counter into a local BEFORE the
table pointer is assigned: `w = (s16) p->counter; t = SYM;` instead of
`t = SYM;` first. 2 wrong words otherwise, and it is the last thing that
function needed.

### A VALUE-PRESERVING NARROWING CAST in a test still moves the allocation

`(u8)(p[1] - 0xF) < 3` and `(u32)(p[1] - 0xF) < 3` are the same test when
`p[1]` is a `u8` -- the wrapped values 0xF1..0xFF are all >= 3 -- and both emit
the same `addiu $v0, $v1, -0xF` / `sltiu $v0, $v0, 0x3`. The cast reaches no
instruction of its own, because combine folds the truncation into the compare.
It still changes which hard register the operands get.

On func_8004AC3C the `(u32)` spelling put func_80042A80's result in $v1 and
`p[1]` in $a0, so cse kept `p[1]` live into the table blocks: no reload there,
and the `lui` could not reach the `beqz` delay slot -- 127 of 128 words, 101
DIFF. The `(u8)` spelling puts the result in $a0 and `p[1]` in $v1, the blocks
reload `p[1]` into $a0, the `lui` lands in the delay slot, and the function
matches. Nothing else about the source changed.

Two consequences. First, when an ALLOC row is down to a transposed pair and the
declarations and statement order are already right, re-check the *casts* in the
conditions -- a narrowing that provably cannot change the value is free to try
and is not a semantic break. Second, this is the shape `search.py` flags as
REVIEW REQUIRED, so read the narrowing it offers rather than discarding it on
sight: on this function the same sweep also offered `r: s32 -> u16` and
`f: s32 -> s16`, which were real breaks (`lw` became `lhu`, and an `sll`/`sra`
pair appeared), and the one worth keeping was the one that could not change a
value.

### A POINTER LOCAL at ONE store site hoists that symbol's `(high)` to the TOP

A store straight to a global, `SYM[0] = 1;`, generates its `(high)` beside the
store, so the `lui`'s live range starts there and local-alloc hands it the
lowest register free at that point. Assigning the symbol to a pointer local
first and storing through the local moves the `(high)` to the local's
DECLARATION, at the top of the entry block, where it conflicts with the
incoming parameter's $a0 and with any other address pseudo still live -- so it
takes a higher register and the `lui` can be scheduled before anything else.
combine folds the `%lo` back into the store through the local, so the local
costs NO instruction: the `addiu` that a materialised pointer would need never
appears.

Measured on func_8005C4D0, which stores 1 to D_80085F98 on entry and 0 at each
of its two exits. The listing hoists `lui $a1, %hi(D_80085F98)` to the second
word of the function and keeps the store's own `%lo($a1)` eleven insns later,
in a branch delay slot.

    D_80085F98[0] = 1;  at all three sites        64 words, 15 DIFF
    f = D_80085F98 for the ENTRY store only       64 words,  2 DIFF
    f for all three stores                        64 words, 47 DIFF
    f declared but entry store through the symbol  63 words, 55 DIFF

So the lever is PER SITE, and spending it at the other two sites is worse than
not spending it at all: those stores want their own re-materialised `lui`,
which is what a bare symbol reference in another block gives you. Note also
that MOVING the entry store earlier is not the same lever and does not work --
`D_80085F98[0] = 1;` as the first statement, ahead of the `lhu` it precedes in
the listing, pins the store at the top (a store cannot sink past a load under
cc1psx's alias test), costs the load-delay `nop` the `li` was filling, and is
65 words.

### A PHANTOM ARGUMENT FROM A WRONG SIGNATURE COSTS A SCHED2 CYCLE

m2c reads an argument count off which argument registers are live at the call,
so a value that merely happens to sit in $a2 becomes a third parameter. Reload
turns the extra `$a2 = value` into `$a2 = $a2` and deletes it, so the word
count is right and `verify.py` shows no extra instruction -- but sched2 runs
BEFORE that deletion and schedules the phantom, which occupies one cycle.

func_8005C4D0 calls `func_80056D44(n, e)`, a function this unit already
declares `void func_80056D44(s32, u8 *)`, and `e` is in $a2 at the call. With
the park's inferred `func_80056D44(n, e, e)` the phantom takes T-10; the table
load `lw $s1, 0($s0)` is released at T-10, blocked one cycle behind the `sh`
at T-9, and so loses T-12 to `addu $a1, $a2, $zero` -- the two come out
transposed, 2 DIFF, through every statement order and declaration shape tried
(twelve spellings, all 2 DIFF). Dropping the third argument matches.

Worth checking FIRST on any park whose residue is a transposition near a call:
grep `csrc/` for the callee before trusting m2c's arity. No spelling of the
caller can reach this one, so it is cheap to rule in or out early.

But the callee's declaration is a LEAD, not authority. A callee whose
parameters are unused compiles identically whether it is written `(void)` or
with them -- it never reads them -- so a landed, byte-identical `(void)` callee
does NOT prove its callers pass nothing, and the arity csrc/ happens to carry
may itself be under-determined. The caller's own listing is the only authority
on what the caller sets up. Measure both arities; on func_8005C4D0 the
one-argument-fewer form is what matched, but that was a measurement, not an
inference from the prototype.

A sweep of every park on 2026-10-30 found four carrying this discrepancy, each
noted in its own park header under `CALLEE ARITY`: func_80056E10 (passes 5 to
a `(void)` callee), func_8005914C (3 and 2, both to `(void)` callees),
func_8005B4D0 (3 to a one-parameter callee) and func_8005BBFC (3 to each of
two). The sweep also found the parks inconsistent with each other:
func_80056E10 declares func_8005EC0C with ONE argument through an `__asm__`
alias while func_8005B4D0 and func_8005BBFC declare the same callee with
three, so at most one group can be right.

### THE FREE REFERENCE PAIR: ADD AND CANCEL A LIVE VALUE, NOT A CONSTANT

This is the working recipe for ":2436 A DEAD reference is still a reference",
and it is what landed func_800500B4 (unk_1C540) 2026-10-30 from 18
register-only words. That entry says a free reference needs an insn that
survives FLOW and is removed by a later pass; it does not say which insns
survive, and the obvious ones do not.

**A constant adjustment is folded by cse, which runs BEFORE flow.** All of
these leave the reference count and the function bit-identical:

```c
    u8 *r = qq + 0xA5;  r = r - 1;       /* 18 DIFF, same as qq + 0xA4 */
    u8 *r = qq;         r = r + 0xA4;    /* 18 */
```

**A VARIABLE adjustment survives it.** `i` is not a known value, so cse has
nothing to fold and the two insns reach flow; combine then folds them back:

```c
    u8 *r = qq + 0xA4 + i;  r = r - i;   /* 4 refs where qq + 0xA4 has 2 */
    i = i + 2;  i = i - 1;               /* 7 refs where i++ has 5 */
```

THE WHOLE FAMILY IS ONE QUESTION -- WHICH PASS READS THE FIELD YOU ARE AIMING
AT -- and there are now three answers in this file, which only make sense
together:

* `reg_n_refs`, the priority input this lever targets, is built in FLOW. So a
  reference must survive cse (hence: adjust by a variable, not a constant) and
  may be folded by anything after flow (hence: combine folding it back is
  free). A reference flow itself deletes is worth nothing -- ":2436".
* `regno_first_uid`, which `reg_in_basic_block_p` reads to decide hoisting, is
  filled by `reg_scan` BEFORE loop.c, and flow is later still. So there a
  DEAD set that flow eventually deletes still changes the decision and still
  costs no word -- "A USER-VARIABLE POINTER WITH A DEAD EARLIER SET".
* `reg_qty`, which `combine_regs` needs before it will tie a chain, is
  local-alloc's and is never given to a pseudo referenced from two blocks --
  "THE SAME VARIABLE IN TWO BLOCKS".

Before reaching for any of them, name the field and find the pass that fills
it; the three recipes are not interchangeable and two of them look identical
in the source.

Both emit exactly the instruction the one-statement form does -- the single
`addiu $t0, $a2, 0xA4` and the single `addiu $t1, $t1, 0x1` -- so the word
count never moves. `qq` here is `q + i`, so the pointer pair computes
`q + 2*i + 0xA4` and then `qq + 0xA4` again: value-identical, no
uninitialised read, no `-Wall` warning. Note that `i = i + 2; i = i - 1;` DOES
survive cse while the constant pointer form does not, so the rule is about
whether the ADJUSTMENT is a constant, not about the mode.

The measurement, all on the same otherwise-final source, with
`advise.py --greg`'s own priorities:

| spelling                                 | r      | i      | q      | DIFF |
|------------------------------------------|--------|--------|--------|------|
| `qq + 0xA4` and `i++`                    | 0.118  | 0.123  | 0.262  | 18   |
| r's pair only                            | 0.400  | 0.123  | 0.262  | 20   |
| i's pair only                            | 0.118  | 0.279  | 0.262  | 18   |
| both                                     | 0.400  | 0.279  | 0.262  | MATCH |

The target wants $t0/$t1/$t2 for r/i/q and the plain source gives
$t2/$t1/$t0, so `q` -- a parameter, 16 references over the whole function and
a doubled `reg_live_length` from its REG_EQUIV -- has to come LAST of the
three. Nothing reduces a parameter's references, and the MARGINS table priced
the two lifts exactly: `to flip 86: 8 refs (+3)` and, after that,
`r` needed 4. Three references on `i` and two on `r`, at no word cost.

**Read the table as the method, not the numbers.** Two lifts were needed and
either alone made the function worse or no better, so the thing to do with a
MARGINS chain is to solve it as a chain -- compute the whole permutation the
target wants and lift every value that has to move, rather than attacking the
narrowest adjacent gap and re-measuring. Attacking the 4.7% gap between `i`
and `r` first, which is what the table invites, swaps exactly those two and
leaves 27 DIFF.

Second roles do the same job and are NOT free: giving `r` the pre-loop store's
pointer (`r = *(u8 **) (pp[8] + 8);`) and `i` the tail's `q + 0x14` read buys
the identical permutation and reaches 5 DIFF -- the five words being the five
places those two roles then hold a $t register where the target has $v1. Worth
knowing as the diagnostic, because it is the cheap way to CONFIRM that the
permutation is what the remaining words are: if a second role for each value
takes 18 DIFF to exactly the words that role costs, the margin is the whole
story and a free pair will close it.

### A FREE REFERENCE PAIR ON A LOOP CURSOR DOES NOT FOLD BACK

Measured on func_8005B4D0 (unk_2CDC0) 2026-10-30, as a correction to the entry
above. The pair is free on an integer counter and is NOT free on a pointer
cursor whose stride is a constant:

```c
    i = i + bank;  i = i - bank + 1;    /* folds back: one addiu, no word */
    r += 0x10 + prog;  r -= prog;       /* does NOT: a real subu survives */
```

Both are value-identical and both survive cse, so both add the references. The
counter form reaches the emitted loop as the single `addiu $t0, $t0, 0x1` that
plain `i++` gives and costs no word. The cursor form leaves `subu $v1, $v1,
$t0` standing beside the `addiu $v1, $v1, 0x10`, which advise.py prints as
`OPCODE built subu v1,v1,t0  target addiu v1,v1`; two cancel variables were
tried (`prog` and `a`) and both left the subtraction.

WHY is not established. The entry above's own pointer example is an
INITIALISATION -- `u8 *r = qq + 0xA4 + i; r = r - i;` -- rather than an in-loop
update, but that cannot be the discriminator, because the counter pair that
DOES fold here is itself an in-loop update. Nor does that entry's own rule
("the rule is about whether the ADJUSTMENT is a constant") separate these two:
`bank` and `prog` are both variables. So read this as a measurement with the
mechanism still open -- price a pair on an in-loop pointer cursor before
believing it is free, and treat the integer counter as the only form shown to
be free.

### ONE SCRATCH LOCAL PER HALF, or the PARAMETER keeps its argument register

The third member of the family above ("ONE variable per LOOP" and "THE SAME
VARIABLE IN TWO BLOCKS"), and the one that costs a WORD rather than a register.

func_800500B4 (unk_1C540) computes two unrelated `(delta * scale) / span`
quantities before its loop, each a load, a product, a divide and a shift. With
ONE pair of scratch locals `a`/`b` serving both halves, local-alloc gives `a`
$a2 and the parameter `q` keeps its own $a1, so the incoming copy coalesces
away and the function is 138 words against the target's 139 -- `advise.py` says
`VERDICT: LENGTH`, with the single finding `MISSING 800500B4 addu t2,a1,zero`
and 58 register-only words behind it. Every opcode and displacement in the body
is already right at that point, so the missing word reads as a shape defect and
is not one.

A SECOND pair `e`/`f` for the second half, with no other change, makes each of
the four locals single-set, hands the first half's `a` the $a1 the parameter was
holding, pushes `q` out to a $t register, and the entry copy survives: 139 words
and 28 DIFF, `VERDICT: ALLOC`. Measured 2026-10-30; the two listings differ at
the first instruction, `lw $a2, 0x18($a1)` against `lw $a1, 0x18($t0)`.

So read a one-word-short candidate whose body is otherwise exact as a question
about how many scratch locals the source has, not about the parameter: ":2946 A
PARAMETER always reserves its incoming register" is about global-alloc, and
local-alloc runs FIRST and can take the argument register out from under that
preference -- but only if some local-alloc quantity wants it, and a multi-set
local reused across two regions does not get it.

### THE ACCUMULATOR MUST OUTRANK THE COUNTER, and a call-result scratch is how

":1262 ONE variable per LOOP" is about a counter whose refs sum across regions
until it takes the low registers. The complement costs just as much: in a loop
that accumulates, the accumulator and the counter conflict, so one of them gets
the lower argument register, and `allocno_compare` decides which.

func_80056E10 sums a halfword table and counts with `c`, which also counts the
program-entry scan earlier in the function:

    sum = 0;  c = 0;
    do { sum += *w; w++; c++; } while (c < *(s16 *)(e + 0x16));

`c` is 6 refs over the two loops' ranges against `sum`'s 4 over one, so `c`
wins $a1 and `sum` takes $a2 -- and the target has it the other way round, in
BOTH loops, because the two counters share a register once `sum` is out of the
way. Splitting `c` into one variable per loop does NOT fix it (99 DIFF either
way): halving the refs halves the live length with them and the ratio barely
moves. What fixes it is giving `sum` a reference of its own somewhere else --
reusing it as the scratch for a call result at a nearby one-armed test:

    sum = func_8005EB78(D_80073740[i]);
    if (sum == 0)
    {
        goto found2;
    }

20 -> 4 DIFF, and the five words of the earlier scan come right with it.
Either of the two one-armed tests does it; the two three-armed tests keep
their own `st`. Ruled out, with scores: unifying `st` and `sum` outright
(529), using `st` for this scratch instead (20, i.e. no effect -- it has to be
the accumulator's own allocno), reusing `sum` for the `x` scratch in the pan
computation after the loop (6), `sum = 0;` again after its last use (20, a
dead set is not a reference here because it is also the last one).

### A PRODUCT WRITTEN BACK INTO ITS VARIABLE TIES TO ITS QUANTITY

`local_alloc`'s `combine_regs` (local-alloc.c:1791) ties the destination of a
single-set insn to a source that dies in it, and the tied pair shares one hard
register. An expression used once in a larger statement does not get that: the
product is a fresh pseudo with its own quantity, and it takes a fresh register
even though the operand is dead after it.

func_80056E10, 2 words:

    D_80084918s.addr = ... .unk_10 + sum * 8;   /* sll $v1,$a1,3 ; addu $v0,$v0,$v1 */

    sum = sum * 8;                              /* sll $a1,$a1,3 ; addu $v0,$v0,$a1 */
    D_80084918s.addr = ... .unk_10 + sum;

4 -> 2 DIFF. `sum *= 8;` is the same. `(sum << 3)` inline is NOT -- it is the
expression that has to be a statement, not the operator. So a listing that
reuses a value's own register for a derived quantity, where the built code
takes a scratch, is asking for the derivation to be its own assignment.

## 4. Re-dereference rather than cache

If a store invalidates cse's memory entry for another object, the target will
show a genuine reload. Caching the value in a local removes the reload and
costs a lot: 11 words in func_80043FD0, 22 in func_80043A68, 55 in
func_80046E38, 86 in func_80041CBC. The same goes for a value read either side
of a call.

Conversely, a value the target keeps in a register across a call wants a local;
one it recomputes wants the expression written out twice (func_8003F8F8
computes its size twice, once for the fit test and once for the accumulation).

**And a re-read that cse turns into a register copy can be load-bearing in its
own right.** When a redundant load's value is already in a pseudo, cse rewrites
the load's SET_SRC to that pseudo; if the statement then writes the *same*
pseudo in place, it has two sets, so combine will not substitute it away and
flow will not delete it. That is how a `(set p2 p1)` + `(set p2 (op p2 ...))`
pair survives into the output:

    v = *(s32 *) X;                 /* p1 */
    ...
    *(s32 *) X = *(s32 *) X << 8;   /* -> addu p2,p1,zero ; sll p2,p2,8 */

Taking the value from the local instead collapses it to a single `sll`. Worth 2
words in func_8003D0F0 -- the copy, plus the `nop` that the freed `sll` would
otherwise have filled in the next load's delay slot -- and it is sensitive to
statement order: only one of the six permutations of its three stores produces
the copy at all.

**The bytecode cursor is the same copy, and it is a whole family.** unk_72A8's
opcode handlers read through the stream pointer at `p + 0x1C` and advance it in
the same statement pair, and the advance is a read-modify-write of the FIELD,
not of a local:

    u8 **q = (u8 **) (p + 0x1C);

    p[0x26] = **q;      /* -> lw p1 ; addu p2,p1,zero ; lbu */
    *q += 1;            /* -> addiu p2,p2,1 ; sw        */

Caching the cursor (`u8 *c = *q; ... *q = c + 1;`) collapses the pair to a
single `addiu p2,p1,1` and comes out exactly ONE WORD SHORT with every other
insn in the right order. That signature -- one missing word, nothing else
misplaced -- is worth recognising before re-deriving the logic: eleven source
shapes and all 24 permutations of the surrounding stores were tried on
func_80039730 before the re-dereference was, and only `**q` with `*q += n`
produces the copy. The two trailing stores have to come AFTER the pair.
Matched: func_80039730, func_80039C44, func_80039D10 (one byte) and
func_80039578, func_800395B0, whose halfword is `(*q)[0] + ((*q)[1] << 8)`
followed by `*q += 2`.

**A LOOP BOUND gets the same copy from an explicit guard.** A `for (i = 0;
i < SYM; i++)` reads the global once and uses the one pseudo for both the
entry test gcc's loop inversion builds and the bottom test, so there is no
copy. Writing the guard yourself gives the bound two reads: loop.c hoists the
in-loop one into the preheader, cse2 finds it redundant against the guard's and
rewrites it to a register copy, and that copy is what holds the bound for the
`sltu`:

    u32 i = 0;              /* NOT inside the if: see below */

    if (D_800869B4 != 0) {
        do {
            ...
            i++;
        } while (i < D_800869B4);
    }

Worth one word in func_80059D1C and func_8005C818. The declaration initialiser
is the second half: with `i = 0;` written as a statement inside the `if`, the
branch's delay slot gets a `nop` instead of the `addu $a0, $zero, $zero`,
because the move is then below the test and the filler will not sink it into
the slot -- above the test it is a candidate to be moved down. Two words apart,
one lever each.


* **The rule is about a FIXED-address scalar against a VARYING-address struct
  reference, in either order -- so it governs store placement as well as load
  delays, and the fix can be applied from either side.** gcc 2.7.2's
  `true_dependence` assumes those two do not conflict. Measured on
  func_8003E758, 12 words across five sites: as plain scalars its D_800814D3
  dispatch read lifted ABOVE a `D_80083958.unk_0A |= 1` store group, and four
  `sb D_800814D2` stores SANK PAST the array load they have to precede.
  Nothing there is a load-delay nop; it is pure store/load placement in sched.

  **Making the SCALAR in-struct is the other half of the lever**, and it is the
  half this doc did not have. Where the struct side has to stay a struct -- in
  func_8003E758 the array reference is what produces the target's index-first
  `addu`, see the entry below -- the scalar is what you change. But it needs a
  real `COMPONENT_REF` or an `ARRAY_REF` on an actual array DECL:
  **`((u8 *) &X)[0]` does not work.** Declaring the object `u8 X[1]` does
  work, and so does a one-byte struct cast; the array declaration is the one to
  prefer, because it keeps the cast out of the source.

  > **CORRECTED 2026-11-03. The measurement above stands; the REASON given
  > here was wrong, and the wrong reason rules out a spelling that works.**
  > This entry used to say that `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` for an `INDIRECT_REF` is
  > `AGGREGATE_TYPE_P (type)`. That is one of FOUR conditions, any of which
  > sets the flag -- `expr.c:5344-5350`:
  >
  > ```c
  > if (TREE_CODE (TREE_OPERAND (exp, 0)) == PLUS_EXPR
  >     || (TREE_CODE (TREE_OPERAND (exp, 0)) == SAVE_EXPR
  >         && TREE_CODE (TREE_OPERAND (TREE_OPERAND (exp, 0), 0)) == PLUS_EXPR)
  >     || AGGREGATE_TYPE_P (TREE_TYPE (exp))
  >     || (TREE_CODE (exp1) == ADDR_EXPR
  >         && (exp2 = TREE_OPERAND (exp1, 0))
  >         && AGGREGATE_TYPE_P (TREE_TYPE (exp2))))
  >   MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (temp) = 1;
  > ```
  >
  > The FIRST condition is the one that fires most often, and it is about the
  > SHAPE of the address, not its type: the flag is set when the `PLUS` is the
  > OUTERMOST node. So a subscript through a cast pointer IS in-struct, as
  > long as the index is nonzero. Measured on `func_800BE4D4` (ovl_town, 363
  > words, landed): `*((s16 *) &v + 5)` and `((s16 *) &v)[5]` are both 0
  > differing -- `build_array_ref` on a non-decl gives the same
  > `INDIRECT_REF (PLUS_EXPR)` -- while `*(s16 *) ((u8 *) &v + 0xA)` is **29
  > differing**, because the pointer cast's `NOP_EXPR` is then the outermost
  > node and none of the four conditions holds. **The lever is the CAST, not
  > the subscript.** (Condition four does not rescue a cast either: in
  > `(s16 *) &v` the `exp1` the code tests is the `NOP_EXPR`, not the
  > `ADDR_EXPR` underneath it. Only a bare `&aggregate` reaches it.)
  >
  > `((u8 *) &X)[0]` still fails, and now for a reason that is itself a
  > lever: `fold` collapses `p + 0` to `p`, so at index 0 there is no
  > `PLUS_EXPR` left for the first condition to see.
  >
  > **PREDICTION FROM THE SOURCE, NOT YET MEASURED.** The offset-0 access
  > through a casted pointer is therefore the one member of such a group that
  > is NOT in-struct, while every later offset is. If a stack record's first
  > field schedules differently from the rest, test this before anything
  > exotic; the fix is to write that one access as a `COMPONENT_REF`.

  Also worth knowing for reading the other side: a pseudo holding `&SYM` via
  `lui` + `addiu` counts as a **varying** address, because
  `init_alias_analysis` does not canonicalise a `lo_sum`-set pseudo to its
  constant. That is why a struct reached through a materialised base is the
  "varying" side at all.

* **The same flag decides whether cse keeps a cached load at all, which is a
  bigger consequence than ordering.** `true_dependence`'s differing-flags
  exception is what cse's `invalidate` consults too. In func_8003F2A4 the target
  reads `arg0->unk_04` TWICE around two stores to small `$gp` globals. Declared
  as plain `u32` scalars, each store is a non-struct reference at a non-varying
  address, the exception applies, `invalidate` does not drop `MEM(a0+4)` from the
  table, the second read is shared into a `move`, sched1 then hoists both loads
  above both stores and the function needs an extra `move` to free `$a0`: **29
  words against 31, all 31 differing**. Declared `u32 X[1]` and stored through
  `X[0]`, each store is an ARRAY_REF, both sides are in-struct, the base load is
  invalidated and re-emitted, the stores stay interleaved with the loads, and the
  function matches. So the array-element spelling buys a RE-DEREFERENCE, not just
  an ordering -- and it is the cheapest instance of section 4's "re-dereference
  rather than cache", because the declaration causes it rather than the source.

* **When sched1 lifts an arithmetic insn above stores that should precede it,
  hoist its operand's LOAD into a local one statement earlier.**
  `t = (s8) p[-2]; sp->a = t; sp->b = t; t = t + (u16) sp->f;` lets sched1 lift
  the `addu` above both `sh`s, because its dependence chain is longer. Reading
  the operand first -- `h = (u16) sp->f;` *before* the two stores, then
  `t = t + h;` -- leaves the `addu` where the target has it. Worth 10 differing
  words across two four-store groups in func_8003CCB0 at an unchanged word
  count. Section 1's lever for a wrong sched1 order is block membership and
  section 7's is the number of sets; this is a third and cheaper one for the
  specific case of an arithmetic insn floating above stores.

* **A re-read after a pointer store PINS the store, which is worth more than
  the copy it makes.** cse's `note_mem_written` sets `writes_ptr->var` for a
  store through any pointer, and `invalidate_memory` then drops EVERY
  `in_memory` entry whose address `cse_rtx_addr_varies_p` -- with no offset
  check at all, since the offset-aware `refers_to_mem_p` path in `invalidate`
  only handles the stored MEM's own entry. So after *any* store through *any*
  pointer, cse has forgotten every pointer-based load, and a C-level re-read
  survives expand as a real `(set rN (mem))`. That load has a true memory
  dependence on the earlier store of the same field and a consumer after it,
  so **sched1 can no longer sink that store to the end of the block** -- and
  in a switch arm, a store that reaches the end of its block is cross-jumped
  into the shared tail by jump2, costing a word per arm.

      *(u32 *) (p + 0x10) = *(u32 *) (p + 0x10) + *(u32 *) (p + 0x40);
      *(u32 *) (p + 0x40) = *(u32 *) (p + 0x10) & 3;   /* store through p   */
      *(u32 *) (p + 0x10) = *(u32 *) (p + 0x10) >> 2;  /* re-read after it  */

  gives `sw $v0,0x10 ; addu $v1,$v0,$zero ; andi $v0,$v0,3 ; srl $v1,$v1,2`,
  with the store AHEAD of the arithmetic it feeds; holding the sum in a local
  gives `andi $v1,$v0,3 ; sw $v0,0x10 ; srl $v0,$v0,2` and the store sinks.
  **Worth nine words and 25 register differences in func_80059814** -- one
  word per arm from the cross-join plus the copy per arm. Only the ORDER
  matters, not the locals: keeping `m` and `t` but storing `m` to +0x40
  *before* reading +0x10 again for `t` also matches.

  **And it is how a listing reads ONE field at several widths.**
  func_8003A2E0 copies the four bytes of an `s32` field into four byte slots
  and the listing shows FOUR loads of three widths -- `lbu 0x48`,
  `lw 0x48` with `sra 8`, `lh 0x4A`, `lb 0x4B` -- not one load and three
  shifts. Each store through the destination pointer invalidates the field's
  entry, so each `*(s32 *) (t + 0x48) >> n` is a real load again, and gcc
  narrows each one to the width its shift needs. A local for the field gives
  the one-load form. Its sweep row had chased a misplaced `sll` through 120
  permutations; with the re-reads written out, that function and its mirror
  both matched on the first compile.

  Read the direction off the listing: `sw $rA, OFF(base)` sitting before the
  ALU ops that consume `$rA`, followed by `addu $rB, $rA, $zero` with both
  registers then modified in place, is a re-read. A store at the END of a
  block with no copy is a local. The intervening store need not be through
  the same pointer -- a store through another pointer or to a fixed-address
  global makes the re-read survive too, and there it stays a real `lw`,
  because sched1 cannot hoist it over a possibly-aliasing store.

  One caveat on the copy itself: between the `.lreg` and `.greg` dumps the
  load is rewritten in place (same UID, same LOG_LINKS, `REG_EQUIV` kept)
  from `(set v1 (mem +0x10))` to `(set v1 v0)`. FSF 2.7.2.3's reload has no
  path that touches an insn needing no reload, so this looks like the gcc 2.8
  `reload_cse_regs` backported into this cygnus-2.7.2-970404 binary alongside
  its `regmove` pass (2.7.2 has none). Not confirmed from source -- the
  binary is all we have.

## TWO LOCALS INITIALISED TO THE SAME CONSTANT -- the second becomes a copy

Symptom: a `move $sN, $sM` where the target has `move $sN, $zero`, in a
function that sets two locals to the same constant near each other. On
`func_8008CABC` (a max-search seeded with 0, alongside `i = 0`) this was word
10: the candidate emitted `02208021  move s0,s1` for the target's
`00008021  move s0,$0`.

Cause is the same `reload_cse_regs` backport described above. Both inits are
`(set (reg:SI) (const_int 0))` in one label-free region, so the second is
rewritten in place between `.lreg` and `.greg` into a reg-reg copy of the
first.

The fix is to make the two sets differ in MODE: declare the accumulator
`s16`, so its init is `(set (reg:HI) (const_int 0))`, the lookup misses, and
no copy is emitted. The narrower local costs nothing elsewhere -- `best = r`
becomes `store_bit_field`'s lsb-aligned move (a plain `addu`), `(s16)r > best`
still gives the `sll`/`sll`/`slt` triple with no `sra`, and `return best`
against an `s32` declared return still gives the tail `sll`/`sra` pair.

Worth 1 word directly, and 4 counting the combine reordering it also
prevents: with `s32 best`, cse1 substitutes the equal constant into the loop
guard, combine then absorbs `best = 0` into the guard and re-emits it after
`i = 0` (`.combine` shows `note 15 DELETED` and a new `(set reg83
(const_int 0))`), so the statement order in the source stops mattering.

Ruled out, each measured on this function: statement order (all four orders
give the same insn stream); an empty `__asm__ __volatile__("")` or a
`"memory"` clobber between the inits (3 differing, worse); a `do {...}
while (0)` cse boundary around the guard (still 1); and a non-foldable
spelling of the zero such as `i = n - n` (still 1). A branch between the two
inits is NOT enough -- `reload_cse_regs` forgets register values only at a
`CODE_LABEL`, and the copy was measured crossing a `blez`.

Note this applies only when the two constants are EQUAL. `func_8008CA20`,
the min-search twin seeded with `0x7FFF`, has nothing to unify and does not
need the narrow accumulator.

## STORES TO DISTINCT CONSTANT OFFSETS off one base do not pin source order

Reach for this when the emitted store order does not match any statement
order you can write, and permuting the statements changes the score a lot.

`memrefs_conflict_p` (sched.c:629) proves two `MEM`s at different constant
offsets off the SAME base register disjoint, so sched reorders those stores
freely. The emitted `sh`/`sw` order therefore carries no information about
the order the statements were written in. On `func_800CE2D4` the target emits
`sh 0x2, sh 0xA, sh 0x6` from a source whose order is `0x2, 0x6, 0xA`.

What this means in practice is that statement order is a real search
dimension and a cheap one: sweeping all six permutations of three such stores
moved that function 34 -> 13 differing, and nothing else tried moved it at
all. Sweep it BEFORE reaching for locals or spelling changes.

The asymmetry that makes the sweep worth doing: a load through a DIFFERENT
pointer cannot be disambiguated from a store through the first (distinct base
pseudos conflict, and the `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` escape at sched.c:834 needs one
address to be non-varying while both vary). So a load through the other
pointer is PINNED on one side of every store, while loads through the store's
own base float freely. That is what decides which value gets hoisted into a
post-call load slot, and why hoisting a delta into a local can move the wrong
one there -- a spelling that scores LOWER can be the structurally wrong one.

Full measurement table, including the six permutation scores and what was
ruled out, is in `docs/near-misses/func_800CE2D4.c`.

## A REDUNDANT OUTGOING ARGUMENT is a FREE REFERENCE -- the cheapest tie-break

Use this when two parameters land in each other's callee-saved registers and
nothing you do to the body moves them.

`local-alloc`'s `qty_compare_1` priority is
`floor_log2(refs) * refs * size / (death - birth)` (local-alloc.c:1705). Two
parameters with the same reference count and equal live ranges tie, and the tie
falls to the lower qty number -- which is the one born first, i.e. the earlier
parameter. To flip them you must change a reference COUNT.

Passing a parameter the callee does not need, in the argument register it
already occupies, does exactly that and costs nothing:

    func_80094984(a->unk_44->unk_24, a, c);   /* c re-passed in $a2 */

`reg_n_refs` is built once, by flow, and never recomputed, so flow counts the
extra `(set (reg a2) (reg N))` and the parameter reaches local-alloc with one
more reference than its rival. `jump2` then deletes the insn for free: it is
jump.c:485's `noop_moves` / `find_equiv_reg` arm, and `$a2` still holds that
value because the prologue copy was `addu $sN, $a2, $zero`, so the move back
is redundant. Counting `set (reg:SI 6 a2)` across the dumps shows 2 in every
pass and 1 only in `.jump2`.

On `func_8009A344` this took 24 words / 21 differing to 0. It also fixes a
load-delay `nop` as a side effect: the prologue copy now has an
anti-dependence on the `$a2` setup before the call, so sched2 cannot sink it
into the `lw`/`lw` hole and the hole stays a bare `nop`.

WHY THIS BEATS THE NARROW-PARAMETER LEVER. Declaring the rival parameter `s16`
also flips the allocation -- every register comes out right -- but pays for it
with an undeletable `sll`/`sra` on the outgoing argument (24 words, 11
differing). The free reference gets the same flip with no extension.

AND IT IS USUALLY NOT A DEVICE. Check the callee's other callers first: here
five landed, 0-differing sites already pass a third argument to the same
unprototyped `func_80094984`, so the three-argument call is the family idiom
and the "redundant" argument is simply the real one. Nine local-variable
spellings were measured on this function and all nine are byte-identical to
the base, because copy propagation erases them -- no local can move an
allocation, so reach for a reference count instead.

## A WHOLE-STRUCT ASSIGNMENT's copy expansion is picked by ALIGNMENT

Symptom: a struct assignment comes out as a pair of `lwl`/`lwr` + `swl`/`swr`
loops where the target has a plain `lw`/`sw` loop, and the function is tens of
words too long.

gcc cannot assume either side of the copy is word-aligned unless the TYPE says
so. A struct built entirely from `u8` has alignment 1, so the copy is expanded
as the runtime-safe unaligned form -- two loops plus a tail. One `u32` member
raises the alignment to 4 and the same copy becomes the four-word `lw`/`sw`
loop plus one trailing word.

On `func_8009DFD8` a 0x54-byte record assignment was 54 words as the all-`u8`
spelling and 26 as the `u32`-first spelling: 172 candidate words against a
144-word target, closed entirely by the member type.

THE COROLLARY IS ABOUT REUSING TYPEDEFS ACROSS UNITS. The same object already
had a typedef in another unit (`Unk800102F0` in csrc/unk_1C540.c), built from
`u8` and correct there, where it is only ever SUBSCRIPTED. Reusing it verbatim
here was the 172-word version. A cross-unit typedef is only reusable if its
alignment suits how THIS unit uses it -- so the overlay carries its own
`UnkTownItemRec` with the same size and a different alignment, which is why
two names describe one object.

## READ A FIELD BACK OUT OF ITSELF to make cse forward the store

When the target keeps a just-stored byte in a register and reuses it, while
your candidate emits a second load of the ORIGINAL source, the fix is to read
the DESTINATION field rather than the source.

Intervening stores through another pointer invalidate cse's memory table, so an
earlier load of the source cannot be reused and a fresh `lbu` appears. Reading
the field that was just written forwards the stored value out of its register
with no load at all -- provided nothing has been written since.

    *((u8 *)p + 0x4F) = a[3];
    ...
    x = *((u8 *)p + 0x4F) & 0x1F;   /* forwards; `a[3] & 0x1F` reloads */

THE DIAGNOSTIC IS THE ASYMMETRY INSIDE ONE BLOCK. On `func_8009DFD8` the target
DOES reload `p+0x4D`, because two more byte stores follow it, and does NOT
reload `p+0x4F`, because nothing is written after it. Which field the target
reloads tells you which field the source reads.

## FOLD REASSOCIATES `A + K - B` INTO `A - (B - K)`; a STATEMENT BOUNDARY stops it

Symptom: the constant is built into the SUBTRAHEND -- `lui` of the negated
constant and an `addu` onto the term being subtracted -- where the target adds
it to the loaded value and then subtracts.

`fold`'s `associate:` path moves an `INTEGER_CST` out of the surrounding
expression whenever one is still there to move. Giving the addition its own
statement leaves the final tree with no literal to move:

    ang  = func_80064584(...);          /* shift stays at its USE site */
    base = D_80100D60 + 0x500000;       /* its own statement */
    D_80100D60 = base - (ang << 10);

Both halves are needed and they fix different things. On `func_800AA5F8`:

  | spelling | differing |
  |---|---|
  | all one expression | 6 (the `lui`/`addu` land in the subtrahend) |
  | shifted term hoisted into a temp as well | 2 (`sll` and `lui` swapped in the schedule) |
  | as above, shift left at its use site | 0 |

The 2-differing row is the useful one to recognise: the arithmetic is already
right and only the schedule is off, because hoisting the shift into the temp
puts the `sll` BEFORE the `lw`/`addu` instead of after.

## A COMPONENT_REF vs a CAST controls a SCHEDULER DEPENDENCE (MEM_IN_STRUCT_P)

Reach for this when a store floats past loads it should stay ordered against,
and a whole group of instructions is hoisted above it.

`true_dependence` / `anti_dependence` / `output_dependence` (sched.c:835) DROP
the dependence between two MEMs in one specific case:

    && ! (MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (x) && rtx_addr_varies_p (x)
          && GET_MODE (x) != QImode
          && ! MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (mem) && ! rtx_addr_varies_p (mem))

i.e. when one is in a struct at a VARYING address and the other is NOT in a
struct at a FIXED address. `*(s16 *)((u8 *)b + 2)` is an `INDIRECT_REF` of
scalar type, so `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` is clear on it; a store through it then floats
freely past loads of the form `rec->field->field`, which ARE in-struct at a
varying address. Spelling the same bytes as a struct member sets
`MEM_IN_STRUCT_P`, the exclusion stops applying, `memrefs_conflict_p` returns 1
for symbol-vs-register, and the dependence survives.

On `func_8008FFC8` that one change was 36 differing -> 25.

THE POINT FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT IT CUTS AGAINST THE HOUSE IDIOM. The
`*(s16 *)((u8 *)b + 0xA)` spelling is used everywhere in ovl_town for the
integer halves of 16.16 words, because a named `s16` field cannot coexist with
the word it lives inside. That idiom is the WRONG one whenever a store to one
of those halves must stay ordered against a load through a pointer. The way out
is a SECOND typedef over the same bytes, used only in functions that touch the
halves and never the words -- `UnkTown2AE8Int` next to `UnkTown2AE8` in
csrc/ovl_town.c.

## A CAST beats a LOCAL for an `extern u8 []` whose address is used late

A local pointer's INITIALISER materialises the `%hi`/`%lo` pair in the
PROLOGUE. A cast expression at the point of use lets cse place it at the first
use instead, which is usually where the target has it. On `func_8008FFC8` the
local form scored 60 differing against 11 for a macro over the cast.

The converse holds too, and the discriminator is where the LAST reference is: a
symbol whose final store is after an if/else merge DOES want a local, because a
fresh cse block otherwise re-materialises the address instead of reusing the
register. But assign it as a STATEMENT, not as an initialiser, or the address
goes back to the prologue. Measured on the same function: direct references 11,
local with initialiser 16, local assigned in place 8.

## A MISSING PROTOTYPE for a MANY-ARGUMENT callee costs a word per narrow arg

Symptom: the candidate is dozens of words SHORT and the missing words are all
`sll 16` / `sra 16` pairs on outgoing arguments.

With no prototype in scope the arguments stay `int` and no truncation is
emitted at all. Declaring the callee with narrow parameters is what puts the
truncation at the CALL SITE -- it does not come from casts in the body, and
adding casts instead is not equivalent. `func_8009CFE0` calls an 8-argument
`s16` function:

  | spelling | result |
  |---|---|
  | `s32 f(s16 a, ..., s16 h);` in scope | 139 words, 0 differing |
  | no prototype (implicit int) | 107 words, 98 differing |

32 words, from one declaration line.

AND THE CALLEE'S OWN LISTING WILL MISLEAD YOU ABOUT THE SIGN. That callee
loads its stack arguments with `lhu`, which reads as `u16` parameters -- but
`u16` at the call site emits `andi 0xffff`, not `sll`/`sra`. It is the CALLER's
truncation that tells you the sign: `sll`/`sra` means `s16`. Read the
narrowness from the callee if you like, but read the signedness from the
caller.

## AN EARLY `return` IS LAID OUT INLINE; the same test as an `if/else` is not

Symptom: the candidate is one word short, a block that should end in a `j`
falls through instead, and a large stretch of branch offsets and registers
differs as a consequence.

An `if (c) { ...; return; }` placed before the rest of a function is emitted
INLINE, at that point in the stream. The same condition written inverted, with
the short arm as the `else` of the long one, puts the short arm OUT OF LINE
after the long arm -- which is what forces the long arm to end in a `j` rather
than fall through to the tail.

On `func_800ADD80`, `if (s->unk_14 < 9) { s->unk_14 = s->unk_14 + 1; return; }`
ahead of the direction chain measured 142 words / 65 differing. Inverting it to
`else if (s->unk_14 >= 9) { chain; s->unk_14 -= 1; } else { s->unk_14 += 1;
return; }` measured 143 / 0, and all 65 differences resolved together.

This is the mirror of the MISSING-`else` case recorded elsewhere, and the two
share a diagnostic: when a large block of branch-offset and register-only
differences sits downstream of one test, suspect the LAYOUT of that test's arms
before suspecting allocation.

## `lhu` FEEDING A `mult` means the source CASTS to `u16`; `lhu` feeding a store does not

Both appear in one function, so the discriminator matters.

An `s16` field multiplied as `f(a) * r->unk_1C / 0x1000` emits `lh`. If the
target has `lhu` there, the source cast to `u16`: the low 32 bits of `mult` are
NOT invariant under swapping sign- for zero-extension, so gcc will not
substitute one for the other, and the `lhu` can only have come from the type at
the use site.

The same field read for a `+=` whose result is stored back with `sh` is ALSO
`lhu`, and there it is NOT evidence of a cast -- the truncating store makes the
extension irrelevant, so gcc picks the cheaper load by itself. `func_800A8CA8`
contains both spellings of the same field: `lhu`+`addu` for
`p->unk_88 += r->unk_20`, and `lhu`+`sll`+`sra`+`srl 31`+`addu`+`sra 1` for
`p->unk_80 += r->unk_20 / 2`.

So: `lhu` into arithmetic that keeps more than 16 bits is a cast; `lhu` into
something the store truncates is free.

## `x * 2` and `x << 1` ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE in a once-set local's INITIALISER

Both emit a single `sll`, so this looks like it cannot matter. It does.

With `s32 a2 = a * 2;` and three later uses, local-alloc split the quantity: it
emitted a `move s4, s0`, which reorg then stole for a delay slot -- displacing
the instruction the target has there -- and read `$s4` at the third use.
`s32 a2 = a << 1;` keeps one pseudo in `$s0` across all three uses and the
delay slot goes back to what the target has. Measured on `func_800A8CA8`:
3 differing -> 0, at the same 144 words.

The defect is specific to a once-set local INITIALISED from a multiply.
Inlining `a * 2` at all three use sites also gives 0; assigning the same
`a * 2` in the body rather than in the declaration stays at 3.

## AN INT SUM ASSIGNED TO AN `s16` LOCAL swaps the add's operand order

Symptom: an `addu` has its two operands the other way round from the target,
and reordering the source does nothing.

`s16 x; x = ox + p->unk_10;` lets `convert_to_integer` (convert.c, the `trunc1`
path) distribute the truncation INTO the `PLUS` and compute the addition in
HImode. The HImode add then goes through `expand_binop`'s widening path, which
emits the operands in the order (field, param) regardless of how the source
reads. Keeping the sum in SImode and truncating afterwards preserves source
order:

    s32 tx; s16 x;
    tx = ox + p->unk_10;    /* addu $t0,$s6,$t0 -- source order survives */
    x = tx;                 /* the HImode truncation; emits addu $s2,$t0,$zero */

SOURCE ORDER IS NOT A LEVER HERE. `ox + p->unk_10` and `p->unk_10 + ox` compile
to identical RTL -- verified in both `.rtl` dumps -- so swapping the operands in
the source cannot fix it. The TYPE of the destination is the lever.

And the `s16` copy is not free scaffolding: it is what emits the target's
`addu $s2, $t0, $zero`. Spelling the narrow arguments as `(s16)tx` off the int
sums instead drops both copies and the function comes out two words short.
Measured on `func_8009DA50`: 143 words / 6 differing with the shortened add,
143 / 0 with the int sum plus an `s16` copy.

## TWO PARAMETERS THAT TIE IN PRIORITY allocate in DECLARATION ORDER -- copy one

`allocno_compare` (global.c:587) ranks by
`floor_log2(n_refs) * n_refs * size / live_length` and breaks ties by allocno
NUMBER, which for parameters is declaration order. Two parameters used
symmetrically tie exactly, so the earlier one always takes the lower register
-- and if the target has them the other way round, nothing about the body
reaches it.

Copying the LATER one into a local fixes it and costs no word, because the copy
replaces the prologue's own parameter move:

    s32 oz = a3;        /* moves a3's birth out of the prologue */

That shortens its live range by one insn, which breaks the tie.

THE ROUNDING IS THE TRAP, and it is why this looks impossible before you do the
arithmetic. On `func_8009DA50` both parameters had 3 refs and were live across
all 214 insns, scoring `3 * floor_log2(3) * 1 / 214` -- and 3/214 * 10^4 =
140.19 while 3/213 * 10^4 = 140.85, both of which floor to 140. So the
one-insn birth gap between the two prologue parameter moves is INVISIBLE at
this live length; at 215/214 it would not have been.

Two diagnostics confirmed the mechanism rather than assuming it: declaring
either parameter `s16` flips the same four registers at +1 word, and adding one
unrelated store to the body also flips them. If a register pair is swapped and
both candidates are symmetric, compute the priority before reaching for the
permuter.

## WHEN TWO if/else ARMS END IN MIRROR STATEMENTS, the ELSE arm's copy is merged

Symptom: the branch is the right test but the wrong POLARITY, and two
mirror-image tails (`|= 1` against `&= ~1`, or a 0/1 pair) are swapped between
the two arms.

gcc's cross-jumping merges whichever of the two tails the source puts in the
ELSE arm, so the ARM ORDER is observable even when the logic is perfectly
symmetric. `if (x & 1) { A } else { B }` and `if ((x & 1) == 0) { B } else { A }`
are the same program and do NOT compile the same: the first lays A at the
fall-through and merges B's tail, the second inverts the test to `bnez` and
merges A's.

On `func_800AB1E0` that was the only defect in an otherwise exact first draft:
4 words -- the `beqz`/`bnez` at word 99, and `ori 1` against `andi 0xFFFE`
swapping at words 110, 120 and 123 -- for a transformation that changes no
semantics at all.

So when the only residue is a branch polarity plus a pair of swapped mirror
tails, do not look for a logic error; swap the arms.

## `ori` WHERE THE TARGET HAS `addiu` off a held base: address-of a MEMBER

Diagnostic, and it corrects a note elsewhere in this project. When a candidate
materialises a scratchpad or fixed-address argument as `lui` + `ori` -- a fresh
32-bit constant at every call site -- and the target has `addiu $sN, $sM, 0xNN`
instead, the source took the ADDRESS OF A STRUCT MEMBER off a base pointer, not
a literal constant.

    f(&p->unk_44);                /* addiu off the held base: right */
    f((void *)0x1F800044);        /* lui + ori at each site: wrong */

Taking the member's address lets the base live in a callee-saved register and
be reused across blocks, which is what the target does. On `func_800A1080` the
literal form was 136 words / 124 differing and the member form 139 / 16.

THIS CONTRADICTS `csrc/unk_1811C.c`'s landed note, which says to use one
scratchpad pointer local but LITERAL constants for the libgte arguments. That
is right for that function and wrong here, so neither form is the idiom --
read which one the target wants off the `ori`/`addiu` distinction above.

## TWO INDEPENDENT IN-PLACE INCREMENTS: their source order is load-order visible

Two `x->a += k; x->b += k;` statements touching different fields of one object
are independent, so they look reorderable. They are not: gcc emits the LOADS in
source order, and if the target's two loads are in the other order, the
statements were written the other way round.

On `func_800A1080` that was the last 16 differing words, all of them in the
first basic block, and swapping the two statements fixed every one at once --
including sinking a `lui` out of a branch delay slot back into the prologue.
Worth checking before reading it as an allocation problem: that is now the
third case in this sweep where a block of register-looking differences was
really statement order or layout.

## `abs()` IS ONE INSN, and its delay slot tells you how it was SPELLED

MIPS `abssi2` is a single `define_insn` whose output template emits its own
branch AND its own delay slot, so reorg can never fill it. That makes the
triple a three-way diagnostic:

  | emitted | source |
  |---|---|
  | `bgez` / `nop` / `negu` -- a REAL nop | `x = abs(x)` (same destination) |
  | `bgez` / a COPY / `negu` | `t = abs(x)` (distinct destination) |
  | `bgez` / something USEFUL / `negu` | a hand-written `if (x < 0) x = -x;` |

The third row is the one that costs you: an `if`-spelled conditional negate
leaves the delay slot FILLABLE, so reorg duplicates the following instruction
into it, and that extra word cascades. A real `nop` inside the triple is
positive evidence of `abs()` with the same destination -- it is not a missed
scheduling opportunity.

This refines the existing entries that name `abs()` for the `bgez`/copy/`negu`
shape: the copy and the nop are different spellings, not noise.

AND WHICH `abs()` COMES FIRST IN THE SOURCE DECIDES A REGISTER. On
`func_8008C758`, two `abs()` calls on different components: abs'ing the SECOND
component first scored 5 differing, and every ordering with the first component
first scored 99 or 100 -- a 139-word function against 140. With the other
order the accumulator takes `$v1` and the other value is pushed to `$a0`, which
is then live on a fall-through, so reorg cannot steal an `addiu` from the
branch's target thread into the delay slot and the function grows a word. An
allocation choice with a WORD-COUNT consequence, which is the inverse of the
usual tie-break case.

## `sll`/`sll`/`slt` WITH NO `sra` means BOTH operands are 16-bit

A narrowing diagnostic, and it cuts the other way from the obvious reading.

`(s16)r < best` where `best` is an `s16` parameter compiles to
`sll $v0,$a0,16` / `sll $v1,$s4,16` / `slt` -- two shifts and NO `sra` --
because combine turns `sign_extend(a) REL sign_extend(b)` into a HImode
comparison. The same `s16` value compared against a CONSTANT, `(s16)r !=
0x7FFF`, keeps its `sll`+`sra`. So one function can narrow one value two
different ways, and `sll`/`sll`/`slt` is positive evidence that BOTH operands
are 16-bit rather than that a shift was hand-written.

Two corollaries from the same function:

* `lhu` on a 16-bit PARAMETER is not evidence of `u16`. `force_to_mode` drops
  the sign-extension when every use is `x << 16`, so `s16 best` read from the
  stack gives `lhu 0x68($sp)` by itself.
* "Truncate in the BODY, not in the type" applies to LOCALS, not only to a
  callee's return. `s16 r` made `r = r - (...)` two quantities and forced a
  `move` into a `beq` delay slot; `s32 r` with a `(s16)` cast at each
  comparison put the subtraction in place and the real instruction in the slot.
  Same word count, 5 differing words.

## AN OUT-OF-LINE `else` ARM: read it off the LABEL PAIR

A cheaper tell than counting words for the same transformation recorded
elsewhere. When the target has `j <tail>` followed by TWO labels with a
duplicated instruction between them, that is reorg hoisting a one-instruction
`else` arm into the branch's delay slot and redirecting past it -- so the
source has the arm out of line:

    if (c) { ... } else { d = 0; }      /* arm out of line: right */
    d = 0; if (c) { ... }               /* hoisted 9 words early: wrong */

Writing the zeroing BEFORE the `if` lets sched1 hoist it across both calls --
it is call-saved, so calls are not a barrier -- and it lands early enough to
flip two registers with it. On `func_8008C758`: 139 words / 60 differing with
the assignment before the `if`, 139 / 11 with it as an out-of-line `else`.

## A cse BLOCK ends at a LOOP-END note, not only at a label

Worth knowing whenever the problem is "cse folded a constant it should not
have known". `cse_end_of_basic_block` (cse.c:8101) scans forward to the next
CODE_LABEL, but it also breaks on two notes: NOTE_INSN_SETJMP, and
NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END -- the latter only when `after_loop` is clear, i.e. in cse1
and not cse2. So a loop's END is a cse run boundary for the first run, and
values known before it are not carried past it.

The cheapest source construct that buys one is `do { ... } while (0)`, which is
also idiomatic enough to be plausible as original code. MEASURED on
func_80041E70, where exactly one word hangs on a cse boundary: it is NOT free
on this target -- all three placements cost one word (271 against 270) and the
diff goes to 265-267. So reach for it when a boundary would buy more than a
word, and price it before believing it.

## A LIBRARY CONSTRUCT can have the shape the hand-written form loses

`abs()` landed func_8003BD84 after the hand-written conditional negate had
been measured four ways and all four lost the same word.

The problem is canon_reg. `ax = x; if (ax < 0) { ax = -ax; }` puts the copy and
the negation in one cse equivalence class; cse then canonicalises the
negation's operand to the OLDEST member of the class, which is the parameter,
so the negation reads `x`'s register directly and the copy -- now feeding
nothing on that path -- is hoisted above the branch. The result is one word
short of the listing, which keeps all three insns:

    bgez $s1, L      ;  move $v0, $s1   (delay slot)  ;  negu $v0, $v0

`ax = abs(x)` produces exactly that. The ternary `(x < 0) ? -x : x`, testing on
`x` rather than `ax`, and computing the negation first (`ax = -x;
if (x >= 0) { ax = x; }`) are all identical to the conditional negate -- 37
words against 38, 24 DIFF -- because cse folds the operand back in every one.

So when a shape is lost to cse canonicalisation, check whether a declared
library function covers it before rearranging the source further: `abs` is
declared in include/structs.h and the project had already used it in
func_800345B8 without noticing it was a cure for this family. This is also the
first cure for carved-sweep's "same missing word three times" row that works on
a PARAMETER -- the other five all need the value to have a second live range,
which a parameter does not.

## 5. MEM_IN_STRUCT_P decides sched1's alias calls -- and cse's invalidation

A struct or array reference sets `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P`; a bare pointer dereference
does not. `true_dependence` returns "no dependence" when two MEMs' in-struct
flags **differ** AND the non-struct side's address does not vary -- which frees
sched1 to interleave things the target keeps sequential, and vice versa.

**Both halves are required**; do not simplify this to "differing flags make
them independent". Measured, each as `store; return load + 1;` so that sched1
has a load-delay slot it would fill if it could:

    s32 e1(S *p, s32 *q) { p->a = 5; return *q + 1; }       -> sw then lw: dependent
    s32 e5(S *p)         { p->a = 5; return D_80081480 + 1; } -> lw MOVES AHEAD

e1 differs in flags but the non-struct side is a register base, which varies,
so the exception does not apply. e5's non-struct side is a symbol, which does
not vary, so it does. Both-in-struct and both-non-struct are dependent as you
would expect.

**A register base does not always vary, and this is the half that was missing.**
`sched.c`'s `init_alias_analysis` builds `reg_known_value`, which records a
pseudo with a SINGLE set from a constant as equal to that constant. So a local
like `u8 *sp = (u8 *) 0x1F800000;` is a constant address to
`true_dependence`, not a register one, and every non-struct
`*(T *) (sp + off)` store is independent of every *in-struct* read around it --
sched1 will lift those reads up into the store group and fill their load-delay
slots. That is why the scratchpad functions are so sensitive to which accesses
are casts and which are struct fields, and it is **per-site, not blanket**:
func_8003D0F0 needs `*(u16 *) ((u8 *) e + 6)` to keep one `lhu` last (2 words,
and the target's `nop` only appears with the cast), while the neighbouring
`e->unk_04` read does not need the cast at all, because by then nothing is left
in the block to hoist it past.

**THE VOLATILE CLAUSE IN `true_dependence` NEEDS BOTH SIDES.** Its return is

    return ((MEM_VOLATILE_P (x) && MEM_VOLATILE_P (mem))
            || (memrefs_conflict_p (...) && ...));

so `volatile` on ONE of a store/load pair creates no dependence at all -- the
only question then is whether `memrefs_conflict_p` separates the addresses, and
two constant displacements off one base register are always separated.
Measured on func_80038CB8 2026-10-28, where the open question is how to stop a
`sh` to +0x20 sinking past an `lb` of +0x28:

    `volatile` on the +0x28 READ only        166 words, 71 DIFF
    `volatile` on the +0x20 STORE only       164 words, 12 DIFF -- NO CHANGE
    both                                     166 words, 63 DIFF

The middle row is the rule in action: one volatile side is inert. Both
together do force the order, and it is still not usable there, because the
volatile read costs two words. So this IS a lever for pinning two memory
accesses in a chosen order -- the only one that works on non-conflicting
addresses -- and its price is whatever `volatile` costs on the read side, which
has to be checked before the ordering is worth having.

**AND THE OTHER ESCAPE IN `true_dependence` IS UNREACHABLE FROM C, so stop
looking for it.** Its first line returns 0 for an UNCHANGING read against a
changing store:

    if (RTX_UNCHANGING_P (x) && ! RTX_UNCHANGING_P (mem))
      return 0;

which would separate any read from any store, QImode included. It cannot be
bought with `const`. expand_expr sets the flag as

    RTX_UNCHANGING_P (temp) = TREE_READONLY (exp) & TREE_STATIC (exp);

(2.7.2 expr.c:5359), and the comment immediately above it says why the obvious
version is wrong: "the fact that a location is accessed through a pointer to
const does not mean that the value there can never change". The OFFSET_REF path
that did set it from `TREE_READONLY` alone is `#if 0`'d out (expr.c:4907) with
the same comment. So RTX_UNCHANGING_P reaches a MEM only for an object that is
readonly AND static -- file-scope `const` data -- and never for a cast
dereference, a const-qualified pointer, or anything on the stack. Measured
before it was read: `*(const s16 *) (q + k)` on func_8004D294 left the MEM
printing as a plain `(mem:HI` with no `/u` and changed nothing. This closes the
idea for func_8004C36C's three `nop`s as well.

**A QImode load can never be freed by the exception, whichever way round.**
Both arms of the test require the non-QImode side to be the one with the
varying in-struct address, so a BYTE read through a walked pointer always
depends on every store before it through a scratchpad struct -- there is no
spelling of either side that separates them. In func_80033D54 that is six
words: the two extra `lbu` feeding the UV wrap clamps have to be between two
particular scratchpad stores, and since they cannot be hoisted across one,
only the statement order decides which side of it they land on.

**SO ORDER THE SOURCE SO NOTHING HAS TO BE HOISTED -- that is the lever the two
notes above leave out, and it was worth four words on func_8004C36C.** A
byte-copy block (`prim->code = p->unk_01; prim->u0 = p->unk_08; ...`) spelled
one statement per copy stalls on every load, because each `sb` conflicts with
the NEXT `lbu` and sched1 cannot lift it. The listing instead batches two loads
into two registers ahead of the two stores that consume them -- and you get
that by putting the loads before the stores IN SOURCE ORDER, where the
dependence never applies:

    g0 = p->unk_01;  g1 = p->unk_08;
    prim->code = g0; prim->u0 = g1;

**In PAIRS, not all at once.** Reading all four values into locals before all
four stores is three differing words WORSE there: sched keeps the four loads
together, while the listing's second pair sits after the first two stores. So
match the listing's batch size, and read the count off the listing -- on that
function one group is two reads and a third inline, and hoisting the third as
well goes a word short. The general shape: **when a dependence you cannot
remove is blocking a hoist, check whether the original simply did not need the
hoist.**

* `*(u16 *) ((u8 *) p - 2)` keeps two read-modify-writes strictly sequential;
  every struct or array spelling of the same address lets sched1 interleave
  them and fill both load-delay slots. func_80043FD0, 2 words.
* Making a pointee a struct lets three loads interleave against two
  non-struct scalar stores. func_80040CBC, 5 words.
* A whole region reached through `*(T *)(base + off)` instead of struct fields
  lets sched1 hoist every unrelated load above the region's stores and shuffle
