**Step zero, before any compile: give the agent its own wine prefix.** This
applies to a BACKGROUND SWEEP in your own session too, not just to subagents:
a sweep left running while you measure anything by hand is two concurrent
`ccpsx` runs on one prefix, and the loser exits 0 having written nothing.
This used to be the single biggest hazard of running several agents at once:
concurrent `ccpsx` runs shared one wine prefix and silently lost an output --
the compile exited 0 having written nothing, or having written another run's
file. The native compiler removed it, so the only thing left to separate is
the scratch directory. Put this in the brief verbatim:

    export AZURE_SCRATCH=/tmp/azure-decomp-$$

`dump.sh` and `asmlib` both write there, defaulting to a shared
`/tmp/azure-decomp`, and it has to be exported in every shell command the
agent runs, not just the first. An agent that measures a number under a
shared prefix cannot tell a lost output from a real regression, and will report
the regression.

**Tell it what has changed since this document was last read.** Three briefs in
a row went out without the levers that had landed that hour, and the agents
re-derived them or worked around them. A brief is cheap; a re-derivation is a
session. Name the specific sections that are new and say which functions they
closed, so the agent knows they are load-bearing rather than background.

**The recipe, in order.** Do not start by reading this document end to end:

    python3 tools/decomp/annotate.py <unit> <func>        # which levers can apply
    ... write a candidate with the right LOGIC ...
    python3 tools/decomp/search.py zz_foo.c <unit> <func> --only=<families>
    python3 tools/decomp/unname.py <func>                 # delete each local
    python3 tools/decomp/nmcheck.py                       # headlines still true?

`annotate.py` enumerates the lever families whose signature is in the listing;
`search.py` sweeps the source shapes mechanically at 0.7s a variant. The two
compose -- the first decides *where* to look, the second explores the choices --
and between them they replace the loop of "write a variant, read the diff,
reason, write another" that costs a model turn per variant. What neither does
is derive the logic: that is the irreducible part, and a structurally wrong
candidate will not be rescued by any combination of rewrites.

`unname.py` is the cheapest of the three and belongs at the END of a session
as well as the start, because SWEEPS COMPOSE: it deletes one local at a time,
so every hit you adopt changes the base and may expose another. On 2026-10-28
it took func_8005C4D0 from 22 to 18 and then, re-run on its own result, to 15 --
and both of those locals were ones the park file had explicitly reasoned FOR.
Read its header before trusting a hit: a better number can be the wrong source,
and it needs its own wine prefix if anything else is compiling.

Pass `--only` once a function is large. `search.py` confines its transforms to
the function body, but a 437-word function still offers ~74 candidate changes
and one greedy pass compiles every one of them, so narrow to the families
`annotate.py` implicated.

* **This document, read end to end.** It is 9,000 words, every agent was told
  to read all of it, and most of it cannot apply to any one function. Run
  `python3 tools/decomp/annotate.py <unit> <func>` instead: it matches the
  listing against `tools/decomp/levers.yaml` and prints only the entries whose
  signature is actually present, with their costs and their ruled-out shapes.
  On func_8003D0F0 it emits, in a tenth of a second, the same HImode-consumer
  paragraph that was hand-written into a brief and closed that function first
  try after two sessions of being parked.
* **`verify.py` output.** The full side-by-side of a 437-word function is about
  10k tokens, and an iterating agent pays that again on every subsequent turn.
  It is abbreviated by default now -- differing words plus two of context, runs
  of matches collapsed -- and `--full` is there for when the word counts differ
  and you need to see the whole structure. A MATCH prints four lines.
* **Inherited context.** A `fork` subagent starts with the parent's entire
  conversation and is charged for it every turn. Now that this document exists,
  the compiler knowledge no longer has to come from the parent's context, so a
  fresh agent told to read it is the cheaper dispatch. Reserve forks for cases
  where the parent has state that is genuinely not written down.

Also: grep the reference listing and the dumps rather than reading them whole
(`grep 'Register 8' .../lreg`, `sed -n` a range of the `.s`), and do not re-read
a file you have already seen.

**Measured costs, so a dispatch can be budgeted rather than guessed** (one
function each, fresh general-purpose agents told to read this document):

| function | outcome | tokens | tool calls |
|----------|---------|--------|------------|
| func_80042560 | MATCH | 130K | 25 |
| func_80044D24 | MATCH | 212K | 47 |
| func_8003D0F0 | MATCH | 230K | 57 |
| func_80045CC4 | 436 of 437 | 316K | 85 |
| func_80041588 | 164 of 164, 21 DIFF | 316K | 82 |
| a fork of the main session | one function | ~890K | 326 |

The pattern: a function whose mechanism is already named costs 130-230K and
lands; an open-ended one costs about 315K and comes back short but with
measurements. Either is far cheaper than a fork, which pays for the parent's
whole conversation on every turn.

**Rename with word boundaries when you test a variable SPLIT.** Giving one
reused running value two locals is a routine experiment, and the obvious
`text.replace(" t;", " w;")` leaves `w = t + x;` behind -- a candidate that
mixes the two and scores wildly worse than either shape. func_80037714 was
parked for a session on exactly that: the two-variable shape was recorded as
343 DIFF and discarded, and when re-run with `re.sub(r'\bt\b', 'w', block)`
it was a MATCH. Any measurement that comes back far worse than both
neighbours is worth re-reading as a broken edit before it is believed.

**Batch functions that share a mechanism.** Ten of the `$gp`-blocked functions,
all needing the same `.sdata` definition recipe, came back all-MATCH in one run
of 152K tokens and 52 tool calls -- about 15K per function, an order of
magnitude under the per-function column. Eight matched on the first compile,
and the second instance of each shape cost one tool call. The recipe was handed
over verbatim in the brief, which is the same lesson as below, applied to a
group.

Two things that make the difference between those columns:

* **Tell the agent the mechanism you think it needs, in full, in the prompt.**
  func_8003D0F0 had been parked for two sessions; the agent that landed it was
  sent one paragraph naming the HImode consumer and closed the gap first try.
  A brief that just says "finish this function" buys the 315K column.
* **Resume an agent with `SendMessage` instead of spawning a fresh one.**
  Everything it measured is in its context, and a new agent re-derives it.
  Killing a long-running agent throws all of it away for nothing -- asking it
  to report what it has now caps its remaining turns and keeps the
  measurements.

## Which of two givs is initialised first, and the bias on a walked pointer

When a loop walks two arrays, the order of the two `lui`/`addiu` pairs before
the loop and of the two increments at its end is decided entirely inside
loop.c, and the source cannot reach it by moving the references around.

`record_giv` PREPENDS to the biv's giv list; the reduction loop (loop.c:4029)
walks that list and emits each giv's initialisation before `loop_start` and
each increment before the biv's own increment, in list order. **Emission is
the reverse of creation, and creation is insn order.** The array whose first
reference comes LAST in the body is initialised FIRST.

That is not the whole story, because `combine_givs` (loop.c:5783) collapses
every giv with the same `mult_val` and an `add_val` differing by a constant
into one group, and the representative it keeps is the first eligible `g1` in
the giv list -- that is, the group's LAST-created member. Two consequences:

* Putting a reference to the second array ahead of the first does NOT move its
  initialisation. The early giv is combined into the late one and loses its
  place in the list. Nothing in the source body can change the order when one
  array's references are all inside a nested loop, because the nested loop's
  own invariant hoist (`move_movables`) creates copies LAST -- loops are
  processed innermost first.
* The representative's `add_val` becomes the base register's value, so a
  source-level WALKED pointer (`u8 *r = D_80085458;` with `r += 0x78`, which
  makes `r` a biv and every field access a giv on it) comes out biased to the
  offset of its LAST access, with negative displacements for the earlier
  fields. That is the "biased giv" seen on func_80057948 and func_8005914C,
  and it is why the matching form is almost always the block-scoped
  `u8 *q = BASE + i * STRIDE;`: a pointer that is itself a giv records no
  further givs for its field accesses, because `update_giv_derive` clears
  `cant_derive` at the first conditional jump in the body.

Read all of this out of `tools/decomp/dump.sh`'s `-dl` dump rather than
guessing: the loop pass prints every giv it records (with `mult`, `add`,
`replaceable` and lifetime), every `giv at N combined with giv at M`, and
every `giv at N reduced to (reg:SI R)`. Measured on func_80057D20's case 64,
where this is the last six words.

## TWO SAME-STRIDE GIVS STAY APART ONLY IF ONE `add_val` IS A REGISTER AND THE OTHER A CONST_INT -- WHICH IS WHERE YOU PARENTHESISE THE OFFSET

MEASURED on func_80026B18 (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), 2026-11-01: 56 words /
50 DIFF to 58 / 0, in one compile, and the whole of it is which side of the
parenthesis a constant byte offset sits on.

The section above says `combine_givs` collapses every giv with the same
`mult_val` and an `add_val` differing by a constant. **That is only half the
rule, and the missing half is the lever.** `combine_givs_p` (loop.c:5733) has
exactly two ways to merge g2 into g1:

* `rtx_equal_p` on BOTH `mult_val` and `add_val` (loop.c:5739) -- identical
  givs, merged unconditionally; and
* `express_from (g1, g2)` (loop.c:5694) for a DEST_ADDR g2, which **returns 0
  unless `GET_CODE (g1->add_val) == CONST_INT`** (loop.c:5704), and whose
  result must then pass `memory_address_p` (loop.c:5752).

So a giv whose `add_val` is a REGISTER can never be the g1 of an
`express_from` merge, and when the CONST_INT giv is g1 the expression comes
out `(plus g1_reg (plus base -K))` -- two registers and a constant, not a
valid MIPS address -- so `memory_address_p` rejects it. **Two givs of the same
biv with the same stride, one with `add_val` a const and one with `add_val` a
register, are therefore uncombinable in either direction.** That is the only
way to hold two same-stride induction variables in two registers here.

In C it is decided by the parenthesis, on the same axis as func_800269B4's
`+ 4`:

| spelling of the 0xC-stride references | giv `add_val`s | words |
|---|---|---|
| `p + off` for the call and `*(s32 *)(p + off + 4)` for the store, one `off` | both `(plus p 4)` -- identical, merged | 56 |
| `p + (i * 0xC + 4)` for the call, `*(s32 *)(p + i * 0xC + 8)` for the store | `(const_int 4)` and `(reg p)` | **58, MATCH** |

The `.loop` dump is unambiguous either way -- `giv at 67 combined with giv at
88` and one `reduced to (reg:SI 110)` for the folded form, against
`mult 12 add 4` reduced to one register and `mult 12 add (reg/v:SI 80)`
reduced to another, with no `combined with` between them, for the match.

Three corollaries worth having:

* **The parenthesised one is the INTEGER giv.** `p + (i * 0xC + 4)` reduces
  `i * 0xC + 4` on its own, so the register holds the OFFSET (`li $s3, 4` in
  the preheader, `addiu $s3, $s3, 0xC` in the loop) and the base is added at
  the use: `addu $a0, $s7, $s3`. The unparenthesised one is the POINTER giv,
  initialised `addu $s4, $s7, $zero` -- a copy, per the `emit_iv_add_mult`
  rule at `:11685` -- and used with the leftover constant as the MEM
  displacement, `sw $zero, 0x8($s4)`. An `addu` of two registers feeding a
  call argument next to a non-zero displacement on a store of the same stride
  is the listing signature of this pair.
* **One of the two increments gets DUPLICATED for free, and that is `reorg`,
  not loop.c.** Both giv updates land in the shared block after the if/else
  join; the true arm's `j` to that block then has its first insn stolen into
  the delay slot and its target bumped past it, so the FIRST-emitted giv's
  `addiu` appears twice in the listing and the second's once. Do not read the
  two identical `addiu $s4, $s4, 0xC` as two source statements, and do not try
  to explain why cross-jumping failed to merge them -- there was one insn
  before `reorg` ran.
* **Splitting the giv can un-hoist an invariant, because it adds insns to
  `insn_count`.** Here the extra giv took the loop from 25 to 31 real insns
  and flipped `%hi(D_80027E68)` from `move-insn savings 1 moved to 136` to
  `not desirable`, which put the `lui` back inside the loop and handed `$s7`
  to `p` -- most of the remaining DIFF. See the next bullet for why 25 and 31
  bracket it.

**And this measures the CALL half of the hoist threshold.** The threshold
lever at `:11212` brackets `threshold` at 60 on a call-free loop and notes
only in passing that a call would halve it. This loop contains a call, and the
same movable (savings 1, lifetime 1) moved at `insn_count` 25 and did not at
31, so `25 <= threshold < 31` and `threshold = (loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (1 +
n_non_fixed_regs)` = 30 (loop.c:631). **In a loop with a call, an invariant
with one set and a lifetime of 1 stays in the loop as soon as the body passes
30 real insns** -- which is a small loop, so this is reachable by accident.
Read the `insn_count` off the dump's "Loop from A to B: N real insns" line
before blaming a hoist on anything else.

## fold's `associate:` moves a constant onto the wrong operand

`x - (y + K)` and `x - (y - K)` do not survive the front end. `fold`'s
`associate:` case (fold-const.c) calls `split_tree` on each operand; for an
operand that is a PLUS or MINUS with a constant it returns (var, con) and
rebuilds the expression as `(x -+ K) - y`. The four instructions are the same
but the constant lands on the OTHER operand: where the listing has
`lw; lui; addu; subu` -- the constant added to the loaded word -- gcc gives
`lui; lw; addu; subu`, the constant added to the other side.

Two things block it, and func_800517CC's case 5 needed both:

1. **Write the constant SIGNED.** The listing's literal is `+ 0xFF280000`,
   which in C is an `unsigned int`, so the whole expression goes unsigned and
   a following `/ 2` becomes one `srl` instead of the signed
   `srl 31 / addu / sra 1`. Spell it `- 0xD80000`. Eight words on that
   function.

2. **Put the second operand in a LOCAL.** `split_tree` strips NOP_EXPRs of
   the same machine mode, so no cast helps -- but a VAR_DECL gives it nothing
   to split. This also fixes the ORDER: the listing loads the subtrahend AFTER
   the call that computes the minuend, which no single statement can express,
   so the minuend needs a local too and the two assignments run in the
   listing's order. sched cannot move a load across a CALL_INSN, so the order
   has to come from the source.

And then **declare those locals in a brace of their own**, one per block. Two
function-scope locals reused across four such blocks are two allocnos whose
references SUM over all of them (the one-variable-per-loop rule above),
which inflates their priority and takes a register the listing reuses: 32
register-only words on func_800517CC, 28 with one brace per `case`, MATCH with
one brace per block. Keep the struct updates as `+=` too -- an explicit
`a = field + delta` local makes the second update read `a` instead of the
word just stored, and the permutation comes back.

### Both halves of this are in search.py now

`tools/decomp/search.py` has `t_decl_order` (transpose two adjacent
declarations), `t_decl_per_arm` (give each switch arm its own copy of a
shared local, in a brace of its own) and `t_volatile` (make one pointer
dereference `volatile`, reads only -- the section 5 lever, which was the one
documented lever the sweep could not reach). They are the two zero-cost knobs on
local-alloc's choice between equally-weighted locals, and the second is the
rule above. Run it over a park before hand-permuting anything: the sweep is
free and it records what each accepted change was worth.

## An explicit `goto` is how you get a loop that is NOT rotated

loop.c's `duplicate_loop_exit_test` copies a top-tested loop's exit test to
the bottom. Whether you want that is a question for the listing, and both
answers have now been measured:

* func_8005914C WANTS it. Its listing has the guard-plus-bottom-test shape
  with ONE `lui` serving both tests, which is exactly what the duplication
  produces from a `while` -- and a hand-written guarded do-while is two
  expressions, two `lui`s, two words worse.

* func_8005B4D0's two scan loops do NOT. Their listings have a single copy of
  the test at the top and the back edge jumping to it. `while (cond) { ...
  if (bound) break; ... }` and `for (;;) { if (!cond) break; ... }` both
  rotate and come out four words longer, with a second copy of the test.
  The shape that matches is an explicit label and `goto`:

      scan:
          if (cond)
          {
              i++;
              if (bound) { i = -1; }
              else { p += STRIDE; goto scan; }
          }

  A loop built this way gets no loop notes at all, so nothing rotates AND
  nothing is strength-reduced -- which is the other tell: that listing walks
  its pointer (`addiu $a0, $a0, 0x78`) where every indexed loop in the same
  unit gets a giv. Ten words over the two loops.

So: count the copies of the exit test in the listing before choosing the loop
form. Two copies means a `while`; one copy with a back edge to it means a
`goto`.

## Put each accumulation next to the channel it consumes

func_8004E6F4 matched on this and nothing else, after sitting at the right
word count with thirteen differing words.

Three channels are interpolated and folded into one accumulator. Written as
the listing's own grouping suggests -- all three sums, then all three
accumulations -- the merged tail computes both sums before processing either,
and no register assignment makes that agree with a listing that folds the
first sum into the accumulator before computing the second. Written
interleaved, and with all three accumulations INSIDE both arms of the
branch:

    r  = c[0] * w[i - 1] + b[0] * (4 - w[i - 1]);
    acc += r >> 5;
    g  = c[1] * w[i - 1] + b[1] * (4 - w[i - 1]);
    acc += g & 0x3E0;
    bl = c[2] * w[i - 1] + b[2] * (4 - w[i - 1]);
    acc += (bl & 0x3E0) << 5;

it matches exactly. jump2 cross-joins the identical suffixes of the two arms
at no cost in words, so the duplication is free; what it buys is that each
`addu` sum lands immediately before its own shift or mask. With the three
accumulations hoisted out of the arms it is thirteen words wrong, with only
the first inside thirteen, and with all three inside but the sums batched two
words over.

The companion shape on the same function: the weight and its complement
INLINE at all six products rather than through locals, because a local makes
the weight load first where the listing loads the first-named operand of the
first product first. cse shares both subexpressions either way, so the inline
form costs nothing and only fixes the order. Neither shape alone matches.

## `potential_hazard` acts ONLY inside one priority group

Worth stating before the entry below, because two park files have leaned the
other way. `schedule_select` (sched.c:2663) walks the ready list -- which is
already sorted by descending priority -- in GROUPS OF EQUAL PRIORITY. For the
first group it queues whatever `actual_hazard` blocks, then, if more than one
insn remains, picks the one with the largest `potential_hazard`, and then it
BREAKS. It only reaches a lower-priority group if EVERY insn in the higher one
was queued.

So potential_hazard can never promote a lower-priority insn over a higher one.
An explanation of the form "the listing has the priority-1 insn first, which is
potential_hazard rather than priority" is wrong on its face: if the two insns
really are in different groups, no hazard reordering reaches it and the only
lever is priority itself (which grows across load delays -- section 8). Check
the SCHED2 dump before reasoning this way, not sched1: on func_8005A608 every
insn in the entry block is priority 1 in sched2 while sched1 shows a spread,
and the park file had quoted the sched1 numbers.

## sched2's tie-break inside a priority group is MEMORY OVER ALU

Section 8 says the keys are priority, then the dependence class, then
INSN_LUID. The middle key has a name and a shape, and
`tools/decomp/sched.py` prints it: `;; insn N has a greater potential
hazard`.

`schedule_select` (sched.c:2662) walks the ready list in runs of EQUAL
priority, queues anything blocked this cycle, and among what is left in the
FIRST such run picks the insn with the largest `potential_hazard`
(sched.c:1349). That function is zero unless the insn's function unit has a
`max_blockage` above 1 -- it reads the machine description, not the insn --
so on MIPS it splits the ready list in two: insns that touch memory, and
everything else.

Measured on func_80054B08, every promotion the dump reports, six of six:

    insn 107 (sw D_800847D0)   over 109 (high)
    insn 227 (sw ra, 20(sp))   over 196 (li 4096), 194 (and)
    insn 229 (sw s0, 16(sp))   over 196, 194, 227
    insn 23  (lhu 0(v0))       over 20 (lo_sum), 39, 220
    insn 39  (lw 12(v0))       over 20, 220
    insn 44  (sb 0x31(a3))     over 73 (lshiftrt)
    insn 68  (sw 0x18(a3))     over 73, 44

A load or store always wins; `and`, `li`, `high`, `lo_sum` and `lshiftrt`
always lose. Ties among memory insns fall through to ready-list order,
because `best_cost` starts at -1 and a later insn must be STRICTLY greater to
displace the first.

**What that means for a reordering you are trying to fix.** If the listing
has an ALU insn where your build has a load or a store, and `sched.py` shows
them sharing a priority, no statement reordering will swap them -- the
promotion is unconditional. The only thing that moves them is the PRIORITY,
and priority here is the longest LATENCY path from the insn to the end of its
basic block, not a count of instructions: `insn_cost` is zero for an
ALU-to-ALU edge, so only loads, multiplies and divides lengthen a chain. That
is why the whole top-of-function region sits at priority 1 and why a call can
sit there too. To move a memory insn later, give the insns after it a longer
latency chain; to move it earlier, shorten what follows it.

The other mechanism in the same dump is separate and easy to confuse with
it: `;; blocking insn N for M cycles` is `actual_hazard`, the memory unit
being busy in that cycle, which DEFERS an insn rather than promoting one.

## A declaration NARROWING can be a semantic break that scores better

search.py's `t_decl_width` family is one of the most productive it has, and
it is also the only one that can change the VALUE a local holds rather than
just its representation. The score cannot tell the difference, and neither
can a word count.

Measured the hard way on 2026-10-27. A sweep over all forty-four parks
proposed nine accepted changes; four were narrowings, and ALL FOUR were
wrong:

* func_80054B08, `u32 w` to `u8 w`, 32 DIFF to 29. `q->unk_08` is a `u32`
  field whose top byte the listing splits off with `srl $v0, $v1, 24`. At 8
  bits that shift folds to zero and the build emits `sb $zero, 0x31` where
  the listing has real code.
* func_8004DE88, `u32 a` to `s16 a`, 59 DIFF to 47. `a` holds the address of
  D_80083D88 and is written out as four bytes with `>> 8`, `>> 16`, `>> 24`.
  The top two shifts die.
* func_8004AC3C, `s32 r` to `u16 r`, 94 DIFF to 90. `r` takes
  `(s32) ((u8 *) 0x80010324 + ...)` and several `*(s32 *)` reads -- it holds
  ADDRESSES.
* func_8004A330, `s32 r` to `s16 r`, 74 DIFF to 43. `r` takes
  func_8004B404's return value, and that is `u32 func_8004B404(s32)`, used
  elsewhere as `(u8 *) func_8004B404(0x104)` -- an allocator returning a
  pointer.

Every one improved BOTH metrics. The pattern is the same each time:
narrowing deletes high bits the function actually uses, the deleted code
cannot differ from the listing because it is no longer there, and the score
reads the absence as agreement.

**How to check one in a few seconds.** Take the local the sweep narrowed and
ask what the LISTING does with that value: a shift by more than the new
width, a mask wider than it, a store through a wider pointer, or an
assignment from a function whose declared return type is wider. Any of those
and the narrowing is wrong however well it scores. A narrowing is safe when
the value genuinely is that narrow -- a `u8` field read into a `u8` local, or
an index compared against a small bound (func_8004951C's `k` reads a `u8`
struct field, and that one stands).

search.py now prints a REVIEW REQUIRED block naming every accepted
narrowing, so the check cannot be skipped by accident. It was skipped once,
because a batch script applied nine sweep results without anybody reading
the diffs.

**All 44 parks were then audited for the same hazard** -- every `s8`/`u8`/
`s16`/`u16` local whose park uses it at a wider width (a shift at or beyond
its width, an assignment from an `*(s32 *)`/`*(u32 *)` read or an `(s32)`
cast, or a store through a wider pointer). Four came back and none is a new
silent break:

* func_8005B4D0 and func_8005BBFC, `u16 t` stored through `*(u32 *)`: both
  FAITHFUL. The listing reads the field with `lhu` and stores it with `sw`,
  so the value really is sixteen bits.
* func_8005A90C, `s16 r`: already flagged in its park as unproven.
* func_8004B954, `s16 cx` stored through `*(s32 *)`: already known wrong, and
  its park now says outright that the 283-word draft is parked for its
  measurements rather than as a candidate.

So the scan is worth re-running after any width change, and two of its four
hits are the kind of false positive to expect: a genuinely narrow value
stored into a wider field is fine.

## `REG_USERVAR_P`: where NAMING a value changes a decision, and where it cannot

A pseudo carries `REG_USERVAR_P` when it is the RTL of a declared variable or a
parameter (`stmt.c:3390`, `function.c:3629`, `varasm.c:721`); a pseudo that
expand or cse invented does not. Dumps print it as `/v` -- `(reg/v:SI 90)` is a
user variable, `(reg:SI 132)` is not. So "write it inline" against "give it a
name" is a real switch, and this is the complete list of what it switches on
this target, read out of the 2.7.2.3 tree. Check the list before building a
theory on it: most of the places that mention it are not reachable here.

LIVE:

* **`loop.c:3956` -- `benefit -= copy_cost` on a giv.** Section 9 has this one
  in full; it decides whether an address is strength-reduced, and it landed
  func_80059DAC.
* **`loop.c:5852` -- the same charge inside `combine_givs`**, applied to each
  giv that is ABSORBED into another:

      g1->benefit += g2->benefit;
      if (! g2->replaceable && REG_USERVAR_P (g2->dest_reg))
        g1->benefit -= copy_cost;

  Note what is NOT in that condition: `bl->eliminable`. So in a loop whose biv
  the dump says can be eliminated -- where the `:3797` charge is dead -- naming
  an absorbed giv still costs the representative four. The two sites are worked
  the same way but they are not gated the same way, and a loop that is immune
  to one is not immune to the other.

  BUT THE OBVIOUS WAY TO SATISFY IT IS SELF-DEFEATING, measured on
  func_8003C67C 2026-10-28. The charge needs a giv that is BOTH
  non-replaceable AND absorbed, and the cheap way to clear `replaceable` is to
  put a biv update inside the giv's lifetime (`record_giv`, loop.c:4739-4750)
  -- which is also what stops `combine_givs` merging it. The dumps either side:

      before   Insn 38: giv ... benefit 4 ... replaceable mult 8 add (reg 88)
               giv at 38 combined with giv at 50
      after    Insn 38: giv ... benefit 4 ...             mult 8 add (reg 91)
               giv at 46 reduced to (reg:SI 107)
               giv at 38 reduced to (reg:SI 110)

  `replaceable` is gone exactly as intended and the combination goes with it,
  so nothing is ever absorbed and nothing is ever charged -- both givs are
  simply reduced on their own. Two givs separated by a biv update are not
  derivable from one another, so the two requirements are in tension whenever
  the biv update is the thing clearing `replaceable`. To use this site, clear
  `replaceable` the OTHER way `record_giv` can: the `else` at loop.c:4764 takes
  it when the giv's first use is not its setting insn or when the giv is live
  past `loop_end` -- neither of which disturbs combinability.
* **`loop.c:797` -- whether an invariant can be HOISTED to the preheader.**
  `move_movables` needs one of three things, and the second is "it is not a
  user variable and it is not used in the exit test". So when the set is not
  guaranteed to run once the loop starts (`maybe_never`) and the register is
  not confined to the set's own basic block, a compiler temp is still hoisted
  and a NAMED local is not. Naming an invariant is therefore a way to hold a
  materialisation down inside the loop, and spelling it inline is a way to
  lift it -- the other half of the preheader-ordering levers in section 2.

  `maybe_never` IS CHEAPER TO TRIP THAN IT SOUNDS: `scan_loop` sets it at the
  first CODE_LABEL or JUMP_INSN it walks past in the body (loop.c:1020-1029), so
  everything after the body's first `if` is "maybe never". An invariant
  computed at the TOP of the body, before any branch, is hoisted whatever it is
  called, and no naming reaches it -- which is why func_8005ACDC's
  `%hi(D_80085458)` cannot be held down: the movable's SET is the first
  statement of the body even though the second reference that creates it is
  buried three conditionals deep.
* **`regclass.c:1826` -- `REGNO_POINTER_FLAG` propagation.** A named local
  keeps the pointer-ness its type gave it; for an unnamed pseudo gcc infers it
  from the set. Minor, and it moves alignment assumptions rather than
  allocation, but it is the one allocation-adjacent entry on the list.

NOT LIVE ON THIS TARGET -- do not build on these:

* **All four uses in `combine.c`** (`:954`, `:1134`, `:1765`, `:1831`, and the
  i3 test at `:1279`) are inside `#ifdef SMALL_REGISTER_CLASSES`, and
  `config/mips/` never defines it. **Combine cannot be defeated by naming a
  value.** That closes the direction func_800599B0's park asks for in so many
  words ("defeat combine, not cse"): no spelling of that read-back can stop
  combine folding its copy, so the remaining word there is not reachable this
  way.
* **`cse.c:478` (`CHEAP_REG`)** requires `REGNO (N) < FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER`,
  so it only ever fires on a hard register. Before reload the named local is a
  pseudo and the macro is false either way -- naming does not change cse's
  costs.
* **`flow.c:1290`** is inside `#if 0`.
* **`integrate.c`** is inlining, which this compiler does not do here, and
  **`reload1.c`** only clears the flag.

## A use before the assignment: a cure for a PARAMETER's copy, and it is not valid C

`func_8004D880` (landed 2026-10-29) is the shape `docs/carved-sweep.md` had
been tracking as "the parameter and the call's argument both prefer $a0 and
conflict, and the parameter wins it here on references": the target copies the
incoming `$a0` into `$v1` at entry, keeps `$v1` for the arithmetic, and spends
`$a0` on the outgoing argument. The seven cures recorded for that copy all work
by rearranging the source around it, and none applies to a parameter.

The eighth cure does apply, and it is undefined behaviour -- a dead `if (c)`
with identical arms, reading `c` before it is assigned:

    if (c) { c = x; } else { c = x; }
    d = c;

One construct pays for both halves of the diff, which is why nothing legal got
either:

* **cse canonicalisation.** `cse.c:make_regs_eqv` makes the destination of a
  copy the canonical register of the class only if
  `uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[new]] > cse_basic_block_end` **or**
  `uid_cuid[regno_first_uid[new]] < cse_basic_block_start`. Reading `c` ahead
  of the block that assigns it satisfies the second disjunct. Without it `x`
  stays canonical, every read of `c` is rewritten to `x`, and `c + 0x7D7F`
  folds with the later `+ 0x61` into a single `addiu 0x7DE0` -- the listing
  keeps the two adds apart.
* **the $a0 preference.** `global.c:expand_preferences` merges a dying copy
  source's hard-register preferences into the destination unless the two
  CONFLICT. Reading `c` at entry makes `c` live from entry, so `c` conflicts
  with `x` and cannot inherit the parameter's `$a0`; `c` falls to `$v1` and `d`
  takes the `$a0` it already prefers as the call argument.

The two requirements are contradictory in legal C, which is the useful part of
this entry: the first needs `x` dead at the copy, and the second needs `x` live
across it. Measured, all 5 DIFF: `goto L; L:`, `switch (0) { case 0: }`,
`c = c ? x : x`, and `if (c) { }` with the assignment outside -- gcc folds all
four away before cse. An identical-arm `if` on an INITIALISED value is 30 DIFF,
because the test itself emits code. A dead `c = 0` in the fallback arm reaches
the first half only (`cse_basic_block_end` disjunct): it fixes the immediate,
then lets `c` coalesce into `$a0`, dropping the entry copy for 27 words.

Allocation priority cannot be used instead. `global.c:allocno_compare` ranks on
`floor_log2(n_refs) * n_refs / live_length`, so the 5-reference accumulator
(0.6) outranks the 2-reference saved copy (0.13) by too much for the argument
to win `$a0` on references; moving the `d = c` later shortens its range but
only reaches 0.22.

Since 2026-10-31 this is no longer the only cure. `__asm__("" ::"r"(p))`,
measured on func_8004CECC, also keeps a parameter's entry copy alive, by
reference count rather than by cse canonicalisation -- see the
`__asm__("" ::"r"(x))` entry. It is a DEVICE too, but not undefined
behaviour.

## An unused `return p` is where a post-call copy of a PARAMETER comes from

The entry above is the cure for a parameter copy you do *not* want. This is the
cure for one you *do*: a `addu $vN, $sM, $zero` sitting after a call, where
`$sM` holds an incoming pointer parameter and nothing afterwards reads `$vN`.

`func_8004827C` (landed 2026-10-29, unit `unk_1AF38`) parked at 18 of 19 words
and 12 DIFF -- VERDICT LENGTH, one word short, with four register-only diffs
around the call. The missing word is the return-value copy for

    return p;              /* p is the incoming u8 * */

on a function whose result no caller uses; nothing in `include/` or `csrc/`
even prototypes it. Declaring the return type and returning the argument costs
one word and pays for all five diffs at once, because the copy is scheduled
into the slot just after `sll $a0, $v0, 3` where the call's own return value
has died, and it claims `$v0` -- which is what pushes the shift result to
`$a0` and the loaded pointer to `$a1`.

The generalisation to check before reaching for a device: **a trailing copy of
a parameter into a return register is a return statement, even when the
function is used as `void` everywhere.** The declared return type is not
evidence about the call sites; it is evidence about this function's epilogue.

Twelve legal spellings of the body were measured at 18 words and 12 DIFF with
byte-identical output -- three forms of the array address, four local and
parameter struct shapes, the call inlined or hoisted, and `q = p` (a no-op move,
deleted before flow, as the entry at line 2266 predicts). They are recorded at
the function in `csrc/unk_1AF38.c`. `search.py` offered `k: s32 -> s16` at 19
words and 5 DIFF; it is the narrowing trap of section 7, rejected because the
target does `sll $a0, $v0, 3` with no sign-extension and the callee is declared
`s32 func_80047BC0(s32)` in the same unit.

## A pointer BUMPED AND RETURNED needs to be its own variable

The entry above gets a post-call copy out of a *parameter*. This is the same
missing word on a *local*: a function whose last two words are an `addiu` on a
callee-saved register followed by `addu $vN, $sM, $zero`.

`func_80048C3C` (landed 2026-10-29, unit `unk_1AF38`) parked at 48 of 49 words
and 15 DIFF -- VERDICT LENGTH. The target closes with

    addiu   $s1, $s1, 0x4
    addu    $v0, $s1, $zero

and the park's `e++; D_80080A89 = 0; return e;` gives one word for both,
`addiu $v0, $s1, 0x4`: one variable means one pseudo, the bump sets it from
itself, and regmove rewrites that set's destination to the return register and
drops the move. Nothing about statement order changes this, because the fold is
not a scheduling decision.

The cure is to make the bumped pointer a **second variable**, used for the
body's own load and returned:

    n = &e[1];
    q = (u8 *) *n;
    ...
    return n;                       /* 49 words, MATCH */

Then `n`'s address arithmetic is a set of a *different* pseudo, regmove has
nothing to merge, and the `addiu` is scheduled after `n`'s last use as a load
base -- which is where the target has it. The displacement folds into the load,
so `*n` still assembles as `lw $s2, 0x4($s1)`: the second variable costs
nothing but the one word it is there to buy.

It pays for the prologue too. In the folded form `addiu $a0, $zero, 0x6` sits
*below* the `%hi`/`%lo` pair for the array base; in the two-variable form it
sits above it, as the target has it. Both insns tie on `INSN_PRIORITY` and on
`rank_for_schedule`'s dependence class, so the tie-break is `INSN_LUID` --
original RTL order -- and the extra pseudo is what moves it.

What is load-bearing is that the index is a **variable**, not which variable or
what type. `s16`, `s32` and `u16` locals holding 1, used only as `e[k]`, all
match at 49 words; so does initialising at the declaration, and declaring `k`
last. The expression form is not enough: `q = (u8 *) *(e + 1)` with `e++` is
still 48 and 15. Neither are the two `1` arguments to `func_80047200` -- a
variable there and a literal index scores 48 and 15.

Measured at 48 words and 15 DIFF before the second variable: `e += 1`,
`return ++e`, the store before the bump, `e = &e[1]` with `return &e[0]`,
`(u32 *) ((u8 *) e + 4)`, `return e + 0`, `&D_80071210[i * 2]` as an array ref,
a split `k = i * 8`, hoisting `e[0]` into a local, and three forms of folding
the assignment into the first call's argument
(`(e = &D_80071210[i * 2])[0]`, `*(e = ...)`, and a comma). `search.py`
compiled 17 variants with no improvement and `unname.py` none.

Devices tried and not needed, all on the one-variable shape: an
`__asm__ volatile("" ::"r"(e))` after the bump does buy the word (49) but the
bump is then scheduled up to the first use of `$s1`, 27 DIFF; adding
`: "memory"` is also 27; putting it after the store is 30; and
`__asm__ volatile("" : "=r"(e) : "0"(e))` is 30. Dropping the local entirely
and spelling the first call's argument `D_80071210[i * 2]`, with `e` assigned
after the call, is 49 words and 23 DIFF -- it fixes the prologue on its own but
swaps `$s1` and `$s2`, because the base then lives in a cse temp born after
`q`'s pseudo.

## An in-place `x &= MASK` blocks the shift/and/scale fold, and costs nothing

The `last_call_cuid` section above ends by saying the other combine blocker --
`use_crosses_set_p (src, INSN_CUID (insn))`, reassigning the SOURCE between the
insn and its use -- "needs a second assignment that usually has to be
invented". This is the case where it does not: the function already needs the
assignment, and only its PLACEMENT is in question.

`func_800398BC` (landed 2026-10-29, unit `unk_72A8`) indexes an array by a
masked shift of a word it also masks in place:

    i = (u >> 0x13) & 0x1F;        /* srl 19 ; andi 0x1F ; sll 2 */
    u &= 0xFF07FFFF;

Written as an argument expression instead -- `func_8003F540(..., u & 0xFF07FFFF,
...)` -- combine folds the array scaling into the index extraction,

    (ashift (and (lshiftrt u 19) 0x1F) 2)  ->  (and (lshiftrt u 17) 0x7C)

which is 75 words against the target's 76. Hoisting the mask to its own
statement, placed AFTER the index is computed, sets `u` between the `andi` and
the `sll` that scales it; `use_crosses_set_p` then refuses the substitution and
the separate `srl 19` / `andi 0x1F` / `sll 2` survives. That is the 76th word,
and it left zero allocation differences behind.

The order is the whole lever. The same two statements with the mask FIRST do
not block anything -- there is no set between the shift and its use -- so this
is not "add a masking statement", it is "put the masking statement between
them".

Worth checking whenever a function is one word short and the listing shows a
shift, a mask and a scale as three separate insns where the obvious C folds
them into two. The other mechanisms that landed the same function were already
recorded: the mixed `4(v0)` / `1(v1) 2(v1) 3(v1)` bases are the cse entry at
line 4350 (a named second pointer at `q + 4`, with the second store still off
`q`), and the byte loads have to precede the pointer store in source order.

## A COMPARISON TEMPORARY'S $v1 PREFERENCE TRAVELS TO A LATER ZERO-EXTEND

`func_8005947C` (landed 2026-10-29, unit `unk_2879C`) tests a `u8` local twice
in different blocks -- once against `0xFF`, once as a `switch` selector -- and
the target computes the second test IN PLACE:

    andi  $v1, $a0, 0xFF        /* first test: b != 0xFF        */
    ...
    andi  $a0, $a0, 0xFF        /* switch: same register as b    */
    beq   $a0, $v0, ...
    bne   $a0, $v0, ...

The obvious C puts the second mask in `$v1` as well, and nothing short of a
pinned register moved it. The chain, read off the `.lreg`/`.greg` dumps
(`python3 tools/decomp/advise.py ... --greg`; this once needed
`AZURE_WINEPREFIX` pinned, because dump.sh read the shared wine prefix while
`ccpsx` wrote to a pooled one and the dumps came back silently missing):

1. The first test's zero-extend lands in a *block-local* pseudo, so local-alloc
   assigns it, and it picks `$v1`.
2. `global.c`'s `set_preference` runs after local-alloc, converts that pseudo
   through `reg_renumber`, and records `$v1` as a hard-reg preference ON `b`
   -- because for `(set (reg T) (zero_extend (reg b)))` it takes
   `XEXP (src, 0)`, i.e. `b`, as the preferencing operand.
3. `expand_preferences` then merges `b`'s preferences onto the switch's own
   zero-extend pseudo: `b` dies in the insn that sets it and the two do not
   conflict, which is exactly its trigger condition.
4. `find_reg` scans preferences in REGISTER-NUMBER order, not
   `REG_ALLOC_ORDER`, so `$v1` ($3) beats `$a0` ($4). The preference is only
   dropped when the register conflicts, and nothing in this function makes
   `$v1` live across the switch.
5. `$a0` is additionally removed from `find_reg`'s first pass by
   `prune_preferences`, because the lower-priority parameter allocno prefers
   `$a0`; and the first pass is further confined to `regs_used_so_far`, which
   `global_alloc` seeds with every call-used register, so `$v1` is always a
   candidate there.

So the second mask's register is decided by where local-alloc happened to put
the FIRST one, two blocks earlier, and no local rewrite of the switch reaches
it. What did: a local register variable pinned to the register the target uses,

    {
        register u32 e asm("$4") = b;

        switch (e) { ... }
    }

which is a device (annotated at the site) and was worth 3 of the function's 81
words. Pinning the same local to `$3` reproduces the unpinned 3 DIFF exactly,
which is the control.

Measured negatives on that function, all at 81 of 81 words and 3 DIFF unless
noted: `switch (b & 0xFF)`, `(u32) b`, `(s32) b`, `b &= 0xFF` before the
switch, a second `u8` copied from `b`, `(u8) r != 0xFF` for the first test (4),
an if/else chain for the switch (12 and 13), switching through `r`/`i`/`c`/`d`/
`t` (4 to 27), ALL 720 permutations of the six declarations, `search.py`'s 47
transforms, `unname.py`, and 180 dead-test arm-duplication sites. Declaring `b`
as `u32`/`s32` with the masks written explicitly loses the `addu` entirely
(78 to 80 words): cse coalesces a same-mode copy with `r`, which is the rule at
line 5979 seen from the other side.

decomp-permuter found a dead-test duplication of `c = b`
(`if (c) { c = b; } else { c = b; }`) worth the function's other 3 differing
words in about 30 seconds -- it adds a reference to `b` and moves it off `$a2`
-- but the pinned register subsumes it, and with the pin `c = b` plain matches.
Reach for `register ... asm()` when `--greg` shows a preference, rather than a
conflict, deciding the register: a preference cannot be moved from the source,
and the suggestion list in `advise.py` (refs, live range, second roles) only
reaches the priority and conflict halves of the allocator.

BUT IT IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR EVERY REGISTER, AND THE FAILURE IS A COMPILER
CRASH, not a diagnostic. On func_8004E4C0 (unk_1C540) a pin on the digit
local -- `register u32 t __asm__("$3")`, and `__asm__("v1")` for the same
register -- makes cc1psx print "abnormal program termination" from reload and
die. Note that `$3` is the register the pin above used successfully, so this
is not a property of the register: the difference is that func_8004E4C0's
pinned local is the destination of a `%` chain, and on MIPS a division's
result arrives through `mflo`/`mfhi`, so reload has its own claim on the
register. That reading is NOT measured -- what is measured is the abort. Pin
somewhere else, or do not pin.

A pin can also be accepted and then IGNORED. `register u32 q __asm__("v0")`
on the same function compiles clean and the quotient still takes `$v1`. So a
pin that changes nothing is not evidence that the register was unobtainable;
check the dump rather than the score.

## TWO ARGUMENT SETUPS IN ONE CALL CANNOT BE REORDERED FROM THE SOURCE

`expand_call`'s register-load loop (`calls.c:1852`) walks the argument vector
FORWARD, and MIPS never gets `PUSH_ARGS_REVERSED` -- `calls.c:42` only defines
it when `PUSH_ROUNDING` is, and MIPS accumulates outgoing args instead. So
`$a0`'s setup insn always has a lower `INSN_LUID` than `$a1`'s, whatever the
argument expressions are, and whether the value is precomputed into a pseudo
or not: when combine folds `addiu P,s2,N` into `move a0,P` it rewrites i3, so
the surviving insn keeps the i3 position.

That matters because sched2 then breaks a tie between the two setups on luid.
`func_80035E58`'s last 2 words were insn 197 `(set (reg a0) (plus (reg s2)
44))` and insn 199 `(set (reg a1) (reg s1))`, both of them filler for a
load-delay slot. They tie on `rank_for_schedule`'s first two keys: both sit at
priority 3, pinned there by the anti-dependence on the preceding call (every
insn after a call inherits the call's priority unless a LOAD lengthens its
chain -- `$s2` here is the node pointer, set in the prologue, so nothing can
lengthen `$a0`'s), and both are class 3 against `last_scheduled_insn`. The
third key is

    return INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2);     /* sched.c:2471 */

with `tmp = *y` and `tmp2 = *x`, so it prefers the HIGHER luid, and the higher
luid gets the LATER slot. The `$a1` move therefore always lands after the
`$a0` setup. The listing wanted the reverse.

The cure is a local register variable for the second argument:

    {
        register u8 *zz_a1 __asm__("$5") = q;

        func_80036988((u8 *)n + 0x2C, zz_a1);
    }

which emits `(set (reg a1) q)` at the declaration, ahead of the call's own
loop; the loop's `(set a1 a1)` is then a no-op and disappears. Worth the last
2 of 129 words, and a device (annotated at the site in `csrc/unk_72A8.c`). It
reads no uninitialised storage and is silent under `-Wall`.

Measured negatives on that function, all 129 of 129 words and 2 DIFF unless
noted: the unit's declared signature on its own, a plain local for the second
argument, a `register` local with no asm name, either of those in a nested
block, a temporary for the first argument, `e + 0xC` for the first argument,
`f + 0x8C` passed directly, a comma operator in the first argument, moving the
`+0x36` store after the call (11), `search.py`'s 24 candidates over 17
transform families, and `unname.py`.

This is the same construct as the pin in the section above, used for a
different mechanism: there it moves an allocator PREFERENCE, here it moves an
`INSN_LUID`. Reach for it when `advise.py` reports an OPCODE finding that is
really two adjacent insns exchanged and both are argument setups for the same
call -- no statement reordering can reach that one.

## `x >= 0 ? x : -x` FOLDS TO `abs`; `x < 0 ? -x : x` DOES NOT

Two spellings of the same absolute value compile to the same three
instructions -- a copy, a `bge` over, a negate in place -- and to different
word counts, because they do not go through the same code.

`fold-const.c:5459` recognises `A op 0 ? A : -A` only with the bare value in
the TRUE arm and the `NEGATE_EXPR` in the FALSE arm:

    if (integer_zerop (TREE_OPERAND (arg0, 1))
        && TREE_CODE (arg2) == NEGATE_EXPR
        && operand_equal_p (TREE_OPERAND (arg2, 0), arg1, 0))
      switch (comp_code) { ... case GE_EXPR: case GT_EXPR:
        return ... fold (build1 (ABS_EXPR, TREE_TYPE (arg1), arg1)); ... }

So `v >= 0 ? v : -v` and `v > 0 ? v : -v` become `ABS_EXPR` and are expanded
by `expand_abs`. Write the arms the other way round, `v < 0 ? -v : v`, and
`arg2` is not a `NEGATE_EXPR`, the rule does not fire, and the `COND_EXPR`
survives to `expr.c:6652`'s `X ? A + B : A` singleton path -- which also
copies, jumps and negates in place, which is why the listing cannot tell you
which one you have.

What it changes is WHERE the branch sits relative to a call's argument setup.
As a call argument, the `ABS_EXPR` form leaves every other argument register
loaded before the branch:

    addiu   $a1, $zero, 0x2
    lb      $a0, 0x2($s1)
    addiu   $s0, $sp, 0x1B
    addu    $a2, $s0, $zero
    bgez    $a0, .L8004970C
     nop
    negu    $a0, $a0
  .L8004970C:
    jal     func_8004E5A0

The `if` statement and the unfolded `COND_EXPR` put the branch first and the
argument setup after it, where a sibling arm making the same call
cross-jumps the whole `addiu $s0 / addu $a2 / jal / jal` tail instead of just
the two `jal`s -- three words short. func_8004951C, 157 words: `v >= 0 ? v : -v`
MATCH, `v > 0 ? v : -v` MATCH, the same `>= 0` ternary with no local MATCH;
`if (v < 0) { v = -v; }` 154, `v < 0 ? -v : v` 154; the call duplicated into
both arms of an `if`/`else` 158.

Section 8's `?:` entry is the other half of this: there the question was the
copies a `?:` keeps when its value is ASSIGNED, here it is which of the two
arm orders the front end rewrites before expansion ever sees it.

## A REDUNDANT TEST STILL HAS TO BE OUT OF THE ARM'S PATH

A test that cannot be true in one arm of a chain still costs that arm words if
the arm's control flow runs through it, because cross-jumping merges an arm's
tail with a later identical tail only when the two reach the same
continuation. func_8004951C ends with

    if (k == 3) { ... buf[0] = 0x7A; ... }
    else { ...chain on p[1]... else if (k == 1) { ... }
           if (k == 1) { ... buf[0] = 0x79; } }
    func_8004E298(dst, buf, 0);

The trailing `if (k == 1)` reads as redundant where it is -- it is inside the
`else` of `if (k == 3)`, so `k` is already known not to be 3, not that it
helps. Lift it out of the `else`, which is the shape that reads naturally, and
the `k == 3` arm falls into it: its `buf[0] = 0x7A` store then has a different
continuation from the `buf[0] = 0x79` store below, keeps its own `sb`, and the
arm's exit branch fills its delay slot from the test (`addiu $v0, $zero, 0x1`)
instead of from the call (`addu $a0, $s3, $zero`). 158 words out of the
`else`, 157 inside it.

The diagnostic is the delay slot and the exit target together: an arm whose
exit branch lands on a later TEST where the listing lands on the shared tail
has one block too many in its path, and the cure is a nesting level, not a
reordering.

## AN `s16` LOCAL READ FROM A `u8` FIELD COSTS A WIDENING COPY

`s16 k = b[i].unk_10;` where `unk_10` is `u8` emits the `lbu` and then an
`addu` into a second register, and every later use of `k` reads that second
register -- the HImode pseudo is not the same quantity as the load's result
and reload cannot coalesce them. Declaring the local `s32` (or `u8`) deletes
the copy. func_8004951C, 158 words with `s16` against 157 with `s32`, every
other word already right; the register-only rows advise.py printed for it
(`slti $v0, $a1` for `slti $v0, $s2`) were the copy's register, not an
allocation problem.

The reverse reading matters more: a widening copy immediately after an `lbu`
whose value is then compared several times is evidence for a NARROW local, and
its absence is evidence against one.

## A GUARD AROUND BOTH LOOPS is how the first test branches to the TAIL

Two sequential loops over the same counter, the second picking up where the
first's `break` left off, is the shape

```c
    *out++ = n % 10 + 0x30;
    for (i = 1; i < lim; i++) { ...; if (n == 0) break; ... }
    for (; i < w; i++) *out++ = pad;
    *out = 0;
```

and the first loop's own entry guard is one word wrong in it. gcc rotates both
loops, so the guard's false edge starts out at the SECOND loop's guard, and
`thread_jumps` then walks it forward: it skips the second guard's `andi` and
`slt` as redundant on that path, but it stops ON that guard's conditional jump
instead of following it to the tail. The reason is in jump.c -- when the
walk-back reaches the label it checks `if (num_same_regs != 0) break;`
(jump.c:4622), and `rtx_equal_for_thread_p` has by then recorded two register
EQUIVALENCES rather than two identities, because the two guards' `slt` results
are different pseudos and so are the two `andi` results. A pending equivalence
is exactly what that check refuses. (That last sentence is read out of
jump.c, not measured; what IS measured is the outcome.) The label gcc emits
for the half-threaded edge is a fresh one placed immediately before the second
guard's branch, so the listing is the right 47 words with one branch
displacement wrong, and re-spelling either loop does not move it -- six
spellings of the pad loop (`while`, `for`, `for (; i < w; )`,
`if (i < w) do {...} while (i < w)`, `(s32) w` as the bound, `out[0] = 0` for
`*out = 0`) all stay at that displacement.

Writing the guard yourself puts the edge where the target has it:

```c
    *out++ = n % 10 + 0x30;
    i = 1;
    if (i < lim)
    {
        while (i < lim) { ...; if (n == 0) break; ... }
        while (i < w) { *out++ = pad; i++; }
    }
    *out = 0;
```

The nesting is semantically free -- `i` is 1 at the guard, so `1 >= lim` means
the pad loop has nothing to do either -- and it costs no word: the guard gcc
would have emitted for the first loop is the guard the source now writes, and
its false edge goes straight to `*out = 0`. func_8004E4C0, 6 DIFF to 5, one
`beqz` displacement (`+0x90`, the pad loop's own branch, for `+0xAC`, the
tail).

Two things measured around it, both negative, so that the next attempt starts
here: hoisting `i = 1` and rotating the first loop by hand
(`if (i < lim) { do {...} while (i < lim); }`) costs three words, gcc
collapsing the hand-written rotation; and putting the pad loop inside the
`if (n == 0)` arm instead -- which gives the same CFG on paper -- costs four
(51 words), because the arm's copy of the loop is not the one the join needs.

Read it the other way round as a diagnostic: when a rotated loop's entry guard
branches PAST a following loop's guard rather than to it, the source has that
following loop inside the first guard's `if`.

### A VALUE'S OWN STATEMENT IS SCHEDULED INTO THE STORE'S ADDRESS-LOAD SLOTS

`*(s16 *) (*(u8 **) (p[8] + 4) + 0xA) = ...` emits the two address loads first
and the value's arithmetic after them, so the dependent second load wants a
`nop`. Splitting the value's own arithmetic into a statement AHEAD of the store
is what fills those slots, and the number of slots it fills is decided by
whether the pieces are INDEPENDENT.

Measured on func_800500B4 (unk_1C540) 2026-10-30, where the target's first
store is six words, `lw / sll / lw / addiu / addu / sh`:

* `b = (...) / (...) - 0x28;` then `= (a << 4) + b;` -- the shift stays inside
  the store statement and nothing reaches the first slot:
  `lw / nop / lw / sll / addiu / addu / sh`, seven words. 139 words, 96 DIFF.
* `a = a << 4;` as its own statement with the `- 0x28` left on `b`'s statement,
  store `= a + b` -- the `sll` and the `addiu` are independent leaves of the
  `addu`, and each takes one slot. Exactly the target's six words.
* `a = a << 4;` with the `- 0x28` moved into the store (`a + (b - 0x28)` or
  `(b - 0x28) + a`) -- `fold` puts the constant on `a` instead (`addiu
  $a1,$a1,-40` right after the `sll`, cf. ":1904 `a - C + b` reassociates"),
  the two become a CHAIN, and a chain fills one slot only. 138 words, 100-110
  DIFF.

**A chain of two also wants two statements, and that makes both in-place.** The
same function's second store is `lw / sll / lw / negu / lw(2nd) / subu`-shaped:
`-(a << 9)` written as one expression emits `sll $v1,$a1,9` / `negu $a1,$v1`
*after* the first load (40 DIFF); written `a = a << 9; a = -a;` it emits
`sll $a1,$a1,9` ahead of the load and `negu $a1,$a1` in its slot (36 DIFF). Two
statements both pinned the destination to the source register AND moved the
chain one slot earlier.

Note what this does to ":1590 The load-delay slot is filled by the NEXT insn
only": the insns that filled these slots stand BEFORE the store in the source,
not after it, so "look at what stands after the load" is the wrong question for
a store whose value is computed in earlier statements. Look instead at how many
independent statements precede it.

## A RECOMPUTED GLOBAL+INDEX WANTS ITS OWN POINTER LOCAL *AND* ITS OWN DESTINATION LOCAL, ONE PAIR PER OCCURRENCE

The section above ("A pointer BUMPED AND RETURNED needs to be its own
variable") gets one word by splitting one pseudo in two. This is the same
switch applied to an address that is **recomputed from scratch** several times
in one function, and on `func_8005BBFC` (unit `unk_2CDC0`, parked 2026-10-30)
it was worth 57 words -- the largest single lever on that function.

`D_80085458 + ch * 0x78` is computed three times there. The target
materialises `%hi/%lo(D_80085458)` three times and lands the three results in
three different registers (`$v0`, `$a1`, `$v0`), interleaving each `lui/addiu`
pair **before** the index arithmetic:

    8005BDF4  lui   $v1, %hi(D_80085458)
    8005BDF8  lw    $v0, 0x10($v0)
    8005BDFC  addiu $v1, $v1, %lo(D_80085458)
    ...
    8005BE18  addu  $v0, $v0, $v1

m2c writes all three as one local, `v = D_80085458 + ch * 0x78;`, which is one
pseudo reused: the allocator gives it one hard register for all three live
ranges and sched2 emits the index arithmetic first. Measured, each step on top
of the one before, all on an idle machine:

    one `v`, `v = D_80085458 + ch * 0x78;` at all three sites        73 DIFF
    three destination locals (v0 / v / v2), same joined expression   49 DIFF
    + three base-pointer locals (s3 / s / s2), `s = D_80085458;
      v = s + ch * 0x78;`                                            16 DIFF

Both halves are needed to reach 16. What the three rows do NOT establish is
that the halves are independent: they are a CHAIN, each measured on top of the
one before, so 73 -> 49 -> 16 gives the destination split's 24 words from the
one-local base and the base-pointer split's 33 only from the already-split
base. Neither was measured alone from the other side, and on this project a
chain has already turned out not to decompose once -- func_800500B4's two
priority lifts, where "either alone made the function worse or no better"
(`:3261`, "Read the table as the method, not the numbers"). So apply both,
and do not quote 33 for the base-pointer split on its own elsewhere until
something measures it that way.

**The statement split is NOT the same thing and does not buy it.**
`v = D_80085458; v += ch * 0x78;` reads like the two-variable form and is the
transform `search.py` offers under `split v = ... + ...`, but it is still one
pseudo set from itself; measured 83 against 81 for the joined form at the
81-DIFF base of the same function. What the allocator responds to is a
*second declared variable*, not a second statement -- the same distinction
section 7863 (`REG_USERVAR_P`) draws. Declaration ORDER is inert: moving one
declaration through all 15 slots of that function's declaration list gave the
identical score at every position, because gcc 2.7.2 orders pseudos by first
use.

Recognising it: in the target listing, count the `lui %hi(SYM)` for one symbol
inside one function. Two or more means the source recomputes the address that
many times, and each occurrence wants its own pair of locals. One `lui` with
the value kept in a callee-saved register means the opposite -- one local, and
"re-dereference rather than cache" (section 4) is the wrong reading there.

## WHICH LOCAL HOLDS A HOISTED SUB-EXPRESSION DECIDES BOTH ITS REGISTER AND ITS SCHEDULE SLOT

Pulling a sub-expression out into its own statement is the standard way to
move it earlier (section 8). What is less obvious is that the *choice of
local* then moves it again, because a local that already has an earlier live
range is a different allocno with a different priority from a fresh one.

`func_8005BBFC` has `attr.addr = D_80086A40[bank].unk_10 + sum * 8;`. The
target emits the `sll` for `sum * 8` at 8005BDDC, in the delay slot of the
`lw` that loads `attr.voice`. Measured on that function, everything else
equal:

    attr.addr = D_80086A40[bank].unk_10 + sum * 8;   (inline)       23 DIFF
    sum *= 8;                                                       23 DIFF
    i = sum * 8;   /  n =  /  a =  /  r =  /  x =    22 / 27 / 22 / 23 / 35
    l = sum * 8;                                                    16 DIFF

Inline, sched2 emits the shift late (8005BDF4). `sum *= 8;` as its own
statement sets the pseudo from itself and emits it too early (8005BDC0) --
the same self-set that defeats the split form in the entry above. Assigning it
to a *different* local that is dead there but has a live range earlier in the
function lands it at 8005BDDC. A freshly declared local scores the same as
inline: `z = sum * 8;` with `s32 z;` measured 109 against the 109 the inline
form scored at that base. It is the pre-existing live range that does the
work, not the extra name.

Sweep the candidates rather than reasoning about them: there are rarely more
than six dead locals in scope and each costs about two seconds to measure.

## OF TWO SYMMETRIC LOCALS, COMPUTING ONE FIRST LENGTHENS ITS LIVE RANGE, AND THAT IS WHAT SPILLS IT

func_800345B8 (unk_72A8) takes the two halves of a projected screen position
and treats them identically:

    x = p->unk_BC - 0xA0;  p->unk_BC = x;
    y = p->unk_BE - 0x78;  p->unk_BE = y;
    if (abs((s16)x) < 0x330 && abs((s16)y) < 0x330) nrep = 5;
    ... later, inside the i loop, each is read twice more ...

Same type, same reference count, same live range to within one insn. One of
them wins the last free callee-saved register and the other is spilled to a
`sh`/`lhu` halfword stack slot, and it is **the one computed FIRST that gets
spilled**. The target keeps `x` in `$s7` and spills `y` to `0x28($sp)`, so `y`
has to be the first statement. Measured on that function with everything else
as it is in its park file:

    y, x, p->unk_BC = x, p->unk_BE = y      546 words,  71 DIFF  (target shape)
    y, x, p->unk_BE = y, p->unk_BC = x      546 words,  75 DIFF
    y, p->unk_BE = y, x, p->unk_BC = x      546 words,  75 DIFF
    x, y, p->unk_BC = x, p->unk_BE = y      547 words, 494 DIFF
    x, y, p->unk_BE = y, p->unk_BC = x      547 words, 499 DIFF

Two things to take from the table. First, the order of the two *subtractions*
is what moves the allocation; the order of the two *stores* is worth 4 more
differing words on top of it and nothing in length. Second, the wrong
allocation is a WORD LONGER, not just differently coloured: the spilled
operand needs an `lhu` the register-resident one does not, and that `lhu`
steals the `bgez` delay slot that the target fills with the next call's
`0x200` argument -- so a +1 LENGTH verdict on a function with a symmetric
pair is worth testing this way round before looking anywhere else.

The two also swap which `lhu` comes first, so the shape finding moves with
the order and reads as an immediate difference (`-0xA0` against `-0x78`) at
the two `addiu`s. Do not chase that; it is the same lever.

**WHY, and it is not a tie-break** -- caller's addition, because the arbitrary
reading of the heading above is both wrong and unusable on a pair that is not
perfectly symmetric. `allocno_compare` (global.c:596) ranks every allocno by

    floor_log2 (n_refs) * n_refs / live_length * 10000 * size

and returns `pri2 - pri1`, so the list is DESCENDING and a SHORTER
`live_length` is allocated earlier. The two locals here have equal `n_refs`
and equal `size`, so `live_length` alone separates them -- and whichever is
computed first is live one insn longer, because both die at the same last
read. Longer live range, lower priority, allocated last, spilled. The rule is
therefore the live range and not the order, and it predicts the asymmetric
cases too: of two rivals for one register, lengthen the one you want spilled.

Note what this is NOT. `allocno_compare` does have a tie-break -- `return
*v1 - *v2;`, by allocno number, and allocnos are numbered in `regno` order,
so a pair that tied EXACTLY would go the other way and hand the register to
the one computed first. The measured behaviour above is a real `live_length`
difference, not that tie-break; do not read it as one.

This is the same formula as "WHICH LOOP A ONE-SET INVARIANT IS ASSIGNED IN IS
AN ALLOCATION-PRIORITY LEVER" below -- two levers, one mechanism, and both
move a callee-saved register by changing nothing but a live range.

## THREE BYTE READ-MODIFY-WRITES ON ONE BASE COME OUT WITH THE SECOND AND THIRD SWAPPED

    prim->r0 = prim->r0 >> 2;   /* 0x4 */
    prim->g0 = prim->g0 >> 2;   /* 0x5 */
    prim->b0 = prim->b0 >> 2;   /* 0x6 */

emits, in order, `lbu 0x4` / `lbu 0x6` / `srl` / `sb 0x4` / `lbu 0x5` /
`srl` / `sb 0x6` / `srl` / `sb 0x5`. The offsets come out 4, 6, 5: the first
statement keeps its place and the second and third trade. sched1 hoists the
later loads above the earlier stores -- constant displacements off one base
are provably distinct, so there is no dependence to stop it -- and once both
of the trailing loads are up front the two read-modify-writes finish in the
opposite order.

So the source order is the REVERSE of the listing's last two offsets, not the
same as it. func_800345B8's target is 4, 6, 5 and wants `r0, g0, b0`;
writing `r0, b0, g0` to chase the listing gives 4, 5, 6 and costs **4 words**
(75 DIFF against 71 at an unchanged 546).

## WHICH LOOP A ONE-SET INVARIANT IS ASSIGNED IN IS AN ALLOCATION-PRIORITY LEVER, NOT ONLY A PLACEMENT ONE

Section 6 already notes that where a pointer local is declared decides whether
its address materialisation is a source statement or a `loop.c` hoist. There is
a second, independent consequence: the live range. `m2 = &p->unk_C8;` in
func_800345B8 is set once and read twice, both reads inside the function's
second loop. Written in the outer loop's PREHEADER the allocno is live across
the whole function; written as the first statement of the outer loop BODY it is
live only from there, `loop.c` hoists the `lui`/`ori` for 0x1F8000C8 into the
prologue in both spellings, and **the shorter live range is what moves it ahead
of another allocno in `allocno_compare`'s priority**. Measured on that
function, everything else equal:

    m2 set in the outer loop's preheader      546 words, 71 DIFF
    m2 set as the outer loop body's first     546 words, 65 DIFF   (target)
    m2 set inside the INNER loop              545 words, 545 DIFF

The 6 words are not at the materialisation at all -- it is in the same
prologue slot either way. They are the save-slot immediates and the register
numbers that follow from the target's order (`m2` in `$s6`, the symmetric
`x` in `$s7`, the repeat count in `$fp`); the preheader spelling puts the
repeat count in `$s6` and pushes the other two along by one. So when a
listing's callee-saved registers are all one off and the shape is otherwise
right, try moving each one-set invariant's assignment into the loop before
reaching for anything else: there are usually only two or three of them and
each costs about two seconds to measure.

Pulling it one loop further in is a different thing and breaks: inside the
inner loop it is no longer invariant with respect to the loop its reads are
in, the hoist does not happen, and the function loses a word.

## A TWO-USE SIGN EXTENSION OF AN `s16` PARAMETER MATERIALISES IN PLACE, AND THAT IS ONE WORD

MEASURED on func_8004CECC (unk_1C540), 2026-10-31. The function is
`u8 *f(u32 h, s16 s, s32 v, u8 *out)` and it both tests `s` against zero and
masks it. The two spellings differ by one instruction:

```c
    if (s == 0) { ... }                    /* in block 0 */
    ...
    sat = s;  sat &= 0xFF;   /* split  */  sll $a1,$a1,16 / sra $a1,$a1,16 /
                                           bnez $a1 ... andi $x,$a1,0xFF
    sat = s & 0xFF;          /* one    */  sll $v0,$a1,16 / bnez $v0
                                           ... andi $x,$a1,0xFF
```

102 words with the split spelling, 101 with the single statement, and the
single statement is the target's. The mechanism is combine's single-use rule,
not a shape choice:

* Both spellings need `(int)s` twice -- once for the HImode compare that
  `expand` widens to SImode, once for the `and`. With the split spelling
  `sat = s` NAMES the widened value, so the pseudo holding the `sign_extend`
  does not die in the insn combine would fold it into:
  `added_sets_2 = ! dead_or_set_p (i3, i2dest)` (combine.c:1489) is nonzero,
  and combine then has to KEEP i2's own set even where it substitutes. So
  the `sll`/`sra` pair survives as real instructions, written back over the
  incoming `$a1` because the parameter pseudo gets its own argument
  register, and the compare just tests `$a1`.
* As one statement the extension has a single use, it dies where it is used,
  and the `and` absorbs it: `andi $x,$a1,0xFF` straight off the raw
  parameter. WHY the compare also collapses to the `sll`-only form is NOT
  established. The obvious candidate is not it: `simplify_comparison`'s
  `case ASHIFTRT` for an equality against zero (combine.c:9909) rewrites the
  `ashiftrt` to an `lshiftrt`, and `simplify_shift_const` folds that pair to
  an `and`, which would emit `andi` rather than the `sll` the target has.
  The measurement is the claim here; the pass is not identified.

So on an `s16` or `s8` parameter that is BOTH compared and masked, naming the
widened value costs a word and reading the parameter once in each expression
does not. The tell in the listing is the destination of the `sll`: `sll $v0,
$a1,16` is the single-use form, `sll $a1,$a1,16` is the materialised one.

## `__asm__("" ::"r"(x))` IS A ZERO-INSTRUCTION REFERENCE, AND IT MOVES TWO DIFFERENT ALLOCATION DECISIONS

MEASURED on func_8004CECC (unk_1C540), 2026-10-31, where every opcode,
immediate, displacement and branch offset already matched and the whole gap
was register assignment. A non-volatile `asm` with one `"r"` input and an
empty template emits nothing, adds one reference to the operand and extends
its live range to that point. The two uses it was put to are distinct:

1. **Recovering a deleted PARAMETER copy.** `v`'s entry copy
   `addu $v1,$a2,$zero` was missing because pseudo(`v`) -- 3 refs, no
   conflict with the long-lived pseudo it feeds, copy preference `$a2` --
   was handed `$a2` by `find_reg`, which makes the copy a no-op that is then
   deleted. One extra reference pushes it off `$a2` and the copy survives:
   101 words / 101 DIFF to 102 words / 45 DIFF. **Every legal spelling that
   should have done the same was inert**, and for one reason: `val = v` makes
   `val` and `v` equal, so cse unifies them and every later `v` reads `val`.
   Ruled out at 101 words: `out[i] = v` in place of `out[i] = val` in all 7
   nonempty subsets of the three stores; an intermediate `vv = v` before the
   `if`; `val = v; val &= 0xFF;`; reusing the parameter as `v &= 0xFF`.
   ("A use before the assignment", above, is the other known cure for a
   parameter's copy. That one is undefined behaviour; this marker is a GNU
   extension that reads an initialised value, and it is a DEVICE because
   the original source cannot have contained it, not because it is UB.)
2. **Swapping two BLOCK-LOCAL quantities along local-alloc's march.**
   `find_free_reg` scans `for (i = 0; i < FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER; i++)` and
   returns the first register free over the quantity's whole range
   (local-alloc.c:2230 -- the `REG_ALLOC_ORDER` override that would change
   the scan order is not defined in `config/mips/mips.h`), so within one
   basic block the long-lived locals land on `$v0`, `$v1`, `$a0`, `$a1`,
   `$a2`, ... in the order `qty_compare_1` sorted them, and whichever is
   allocated first takes the lower register. The marker on the saturation
   local swapped it with the 0x80808081 quantity: sat `$a2` / magic `$a3`
   became sat `$a3` / magic `$a2`, and `$a3` is the target's register for
   sat. Worth 9 DIFF (45 to 36). Two quantities exchanging registers is
   what an exchange in allocation order looks like, and that much is
   measured.
   **WHICH WAY the priority moved is NOT established.** It is
   `floor_log2(refs) * refs * qty_size / (death - birth)`
   (`qty_compare_1`, local-alloc.c:1705; `qty_size` is 4 for an SImode
   quantity), and the marker adds a REFERENCE as well as live length, so
   the numerator rises too -- discontinuously, since
   `floor_log2(refs) * refs` steps from 3 at three refs to 8 at four. The
   direction of the quotient cannot be read off the formula, and
   local-alloc prints the resulting assignment but not the order it
   allocated in. The same marker on four other locals was measured and all
   were worse (36, 38, 41, 44, 59, 66), so this is a per-quantity lever and
   not a general "lengthen something" one.

The price is that a value a global allocno needs cannot be freed this way:
in the same function `val` could not take `$a2` under any spelling tried,
because local-alloc had already given `$a2` to a block-local quantity before
global-alloc ran, and nothing but a hard register live into that block or an
earlier local in `$a2` will make `find_free_reg` skip it
(local-alloc.c:2181). That half is still open; see
`docs/near-misses/func_8004CECC.c`.

## TWO ARGUMENT COPIES IN THE LISTING'S ORDER: EMIT THE SECOND ONE YOURSELF, AS THE FENCE

MEASURED on func_8005A90C (unk_2CDC0), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 103 of 103 words,
`make check` byte-identical. The park sat at 103/103 and 2 DIFF -- `addu
$a0,$s3,$zero` / `addu $a1,$s4,$zero` at 8005AA10 the wrong way round, every
other word right -- after 165,063 permuter candidates, search.py and unname.py
had all returned nothing. It was closed by reading cc1psx's `.sched` dump
(`tools/decomp/sched.py file.c func --sched1 --rtl`) instead of inferring it.

**What the dump showed on the park side.** The block is insns 138-212. The
`e++; e--;` residue, insn 174 `(set (reg 87) (reg 87))`, is the first insn
after the `do { } while (0)` notes and is therefore the FENCE:
`sched_analyze_insn` (sched.c:2088-2111) gives it a link to every earlier
setter and user and sets `reg_pending_sets_all`, which makes it the last
setter of every register for everything after it (sched.c:2146-2150). So
both argument copies, 199 `(set a0 (reg 81))` and 201 `(set a1 (reg 82))`,
have IDENTICAL LOG_LINKS, `(insn_list 174)`, hence identical priority
(`priority`, sched.c:1456-1528: max over links of `priority(x) + cost - 1`,
with every cost 1 here). At T-14 the ready list is `201 (1) 199 (1)`:
`rank_for_schedule` (sched.c:2429-2472) ties on priority, ties on class --
both ALU, cost 1 against the `li 0x7F` last scheduled, so class 3 -- and
falls to `INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2)`, which picks the HIGHER luid
first and places it LATER. 201 is later (calls.c:1852 emits `$a0`'s copy
before `$a1`'s for every call), so `$a0` is emitted first. The park's
standing hypothesis -- "the `$a1` copy needs a dependent in the block that is
not the call" -- cannot be met: any such dependent is after the call in the
RTL, the call is pinned at the block end (sched.c:3351-3371, TAIL_PRIORITY),
and after the call every hard register's last setter is the call. **And
sched2 cannot swap them either**: reload deletes the no-op 174, so in
`.sched2` the first insn after the notes is 199, the `$a0` copy itself, which
becomes the fence (ref_count 10) and pins 201 behind it. Whatever order sched1
emits is final.

**The cure, a DEVICE (annotated at the site in `csrc/unk_2CDC0.c`):**

```c
    e->unk_14 = c;
    do
    {
    } while (0);
    {
        register u32 zz __asm__("$5") = c;
        __asm__("" : "=r"(zz) : "0"(zz));
        e->unk_18 = 0x7F;
        ...                              /* the six stores, unchanged */
        r = func_80059F8C(b, zz);
    }
```

The pinned register variable emits `(set (reg/v:SI 5 a1) (reg 82))` at the
declaration, i.e. BEFORE the call and as the first insn after the loop notes.
On the landed side the dump shows exactly that: insn 172 carries the fence
links (149 150 148 152 141 145 147 140, ANTI 155), the `$a0` copy 199 has
`(insn_list 172)`, the ready list runs `T-14: 199 (1) 174 (1)` / `T-15: 174`
/ `T-16: 172 (0)`, and the emitted order is `sw $s4,0x14` / `addu $a1` /
[asm, nothing] / `addu $a0` / `li 0x7F`. The call's own `(set a1 a1)` (insn
201) survives cse1, loop and cse2 and is deleted by flow as a no-op move
(flow.c:987-998). This is the same construct as "TWO ARGUMENT SETUPS IN ONE
CALL CANNOT BE REORDERED FROM THE SOURCE" above, used for a different key:
there it moves a sched2 luid, here it makes the copy the sched1 fence.

**The asm is the second half, and it is for cse, not sched.** The pinned copy
alone is 1 DIFF: `e->unk_08 = c` comes out `sw $a1,0x8($s0)` for the
listing's `sw $s4`, and it is already `(reg/v:SI 5 a1)` in `.cse2`.
`CHEAP_REG` (cse.c:477-479) prices a USER-VARIABLE hard register at 0 against
a pseudo's 1 (`COST`, cse.c:481-485), and `cse_insn` takes the cheapest
equivalent (cse.c:6834-6837), so wherever `zz == c` is live the store reads
`zz`. The empty asm sets `$a1` from itself: cse invalidates a SET's
destination (cse.c:7294-7313), and anything containing an ASM_OPERANDS costs
1000 (cse.c:732-736), so `$a1` leaves `c`'s class and is never substituted
again. The asm emits no instruction. Two things that do NOT do this, both
measured 1 DIFF: a second `do { } while (0)` between the copy and the stores
-- cse2 ignores LOOP_END, it is cse1's stop only (cse.c:8100-8103,
`! after_loop`) -- and a plain `__asm__ volatile("")`, which flushes nothing
