in cse. Upstream stmt.c:1428 rejects `+` in an output constraint; cc1psx
accepts `"+r"(zz)` and it also matches, but the `"=r"/"0"` spelling is the
one the 2.7.2 source documents, so that is what landed.

**Every spelling measured, all 103 of 103 words:**

    park (do/while fence, e++; e--;, dead test on c)           2 DIFF
    pinned copy after the loop, no asm                         1   (sw $a1,0x8)
    + e++; e--; kept                                           1
    + a second do { } while (0) after the copy                 1
    + __asm__ volatile("") after the copy                      1
    + __asm__ volatile("" : "=r"(zz) : "0"(zz))                MATCH
    + __asm__ volatile("" : "+r"(zz))                          MATCH
    + __asm__("" : "+r"(zz)), non-volatile                     MATCH
    + __asm__("" : "=r"(zz) : "0"(zz)), non-volatile           MATCH  <- landed
    same, dead test on c removed                               MATCH  (landed form)
    same, the do { } while (0) removed                        11      (copy floats to the block top)
    pinned copy BEFORE the do { } while (0)                   11      (same)
    pinned copy with no loop anywhere                         11

The volatile is not needed: a non-volatile asm is not a sched fence
(sched.c:1987 fences only `code != ASM_OPERANDS || MEM_VOLATILE_P`), and it
does not have to be -- the `$a0` copy and the asm tie at priority 1 and the
copy, with the higher luid, is placed later either way, and the asm emits
nothing. The dead test on `c` that the park needed for the `unk_08` store is
not needed once the asm holds `$a1` apart from `c`.

**A second route also MATCHES, and its WHY is only half read.** A plain
`register u32 zz = c;` (no `$5`) with the same asm matches too. Its `.sched`
is the PARK's order (`T-14: 201 (1) 199 (1)`), and its `.greg` has the asm
and the call's `$a1` copy gone and a NEW insn, 284 `(set (reg/v a1) (reg
s4))`, i.e. reload's input reload for the `"0"` constraint once the asm's
output pseudo was allocated `$a1`; the asm is the fence there (`174 (0)` at
T-16), so the reload lands right after the `unk_14` store. That the output
pseudo takes `$a1` is consistent with `qty_phys_copy_sugg` from the call's
copy, but it was not read out of `.lreg`, so the pinned form -- whose every
step is in a dump -- is the one in `csrc/`.

**Two corrections this reading forced**, both marked in place above: the
degenerate-loop lever's "needs that value to have a use in the block besides
the call" (section 3), and "`n_deaths` IS ALWAYS ZERO" (section 8) -- a fence
insn carries the loop notes as fake `REG_DEAD` notes (sched.c:2267) and is
halved to 0 when it is released; it is pinned by its links regardless.

## A TIED PHANTOM COPY: three free references on a two-reference temporary move local-alloc's march

MEASURED on func_80054B08 (unk_264E0), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 84 of 84 words,
`make check` and all three containers byte-identical. The park sat at 3 DIFF
with the FOLDED `w - 0x20 + base` and at 14 with every in-place spelling,
after 247,025 permuter candidates, search.py, unname.py and a 512-member
cross product. It was closed by reading the `.lreg` dump and doing
`qty_compare_1`'s arithmetic by hand, which showed that the 3-DIFF body and
the 14-DIFF body differ by ONE quantity's existence, not by `w`'s reference
count.

**What the `.lreg` dumps say about $v0.** local-alloc numbers each block's
insns and gives a quantity the range `[2 * birth_insn, 2 * death_insn)`
(`reg_is_set`, local-alloc.c:2038; `wipe_dead_reg`, :2057; the scan is
`for (ins = born_index; ins < dead_index; ins++)`, :2108, so a value born in
the insn where another dies does NOT conflict with it). `find_free_reg` then
takes the lowest-numbered free register (:2158), in the order
`qty_compare_1` sorts the quantities (:1598:
`floor_log2(refs) * refs * size / (death - birth)`, ties by qty number).
Block 7 (jal to beqz) in the folded body, suids from the sched1 order:

    q    5 refs  [8,26)   suggested $v0, allocated first
    w    9 refs  [20,40)  5.4   -> $v1   (7 own + 2 from the tied sum temp)
    93   2 refs  [36,38)  4.0   -> $v0   <- `base - 0x20`, the fold's temp
    x   11 refs  [26,60)  3.88  -> $a0   ($v0 blocked by 93, $v1 by w)
    t1   2 refs  [28,34)  1.33  -> $v0
    t2   2 refs  [46,54)  1.0   -> $v0

In the in-place body `w -= 0x20; w += base;` the quantity 93 does not exist
(the sums are `w` itself, or tie into its quantity when spelled with temporaries, :1858-1870), `x` is still 11 refs over
34 and nothing allocated before it occupies $v0 inside [26,60): `q` dies
exactly at `x`'s birth, and the `andi` temp is born after `x`'s death. So
`x` takes $v0, `t1` falls to $a0, `t2` to $v1, and sched2 -- with no
anti-dependence on $v0 -- hoists the `srl`. **The park's reading was right
about the symptom and wrong about the cause: `w` going from 7 to 11
references changes nothing (its priority rises either way and it gets $v1
in both bodies); the fold's 3-word error was what had been holding `x` off
$v0.** Nothing legal blocks it: `t1`/`t2` with 2 refs cannot outrank `x`
(2 refs needs a 2-suid range for 4.0), `q` cannot overlap `x`, and the
`andi` temp cannot be born before the x store because sched1 launches the
`andi` -- a once-set birthing insn, `birthing_insn_p` sched.c:2534,
`adjust_priority` :2544 -- the moment the jump is scheduled.

**The device.** `*(volatile u8 *)(b + 0x31) = (t1 + t1 + t1) - t1 - t1;`
The front end makes it `(t1 << 1) + t1 - t1 - t1` (four insns, `t1`
referenced in all four); cse leaves it; flow counts `t1` at 5 refs; combine
folds the chain to ONE insn `(set 104 (reg 89))` and deletes the other three.
That copy is launched by the `sb` it feeds, so it sits immediately before the
`sb` (after `addu w,base`, before `and x`). At local-alloc `t1` dies in it,
so `combine_regs` ties 104 into `t1`'s quantity (:1858, `qty_n_refs += 2`):
7 refs over [28,40) is `2 * 7 * 4 / 12 = 4.67`, ahead of `x`'s
`3 * 11 * 4 / 36 = 3.67` (the copy is one more insn inside `x`'s range), so `t1` is allocated first, holds $v0 inside `x`'s range, and `x`
falls to $a0; `t2` and the `andi` temp then take $v0 as the listing has.
After allocation the copy is `(set $v0 $v0)`; the `.greg` dump already has
it as `NOTE_INSN_DELETED`, so it costs no word. **WHERE it is deleted is
not established**: upstream's only same-register no-op deleter is
jump.c:474-482 and upstream runs that after sched2 (toplev.c:3690), while
cc1psx has it gone between the `.lreg` and `.greg` dumps, i.e. inside
`global_alloc`/`reload` (toplev.c:3588-3625, global.c:580). The measurement
is what is cited.

**Why the copy must sit BEFORE `and x`, and why `t1` and not `t2`.** The
same phantom on `t2` reaches 7 DIFF, with `x` correctly in $a0 and ALL seven
words `base`/`mask` swapped. Its copy is launched by `sb 0x33`, which is
after `and x` (`mask`'s death) and before `addu x,base` (`base`'s death), so
it lengthens `base` to 42 suids = `mask`'s 42; equal priorities fall to the
qty number, `mask` is born first (its `lui` sinks to the top of the block),
and `mask` takes $a1. The copy for `t1` is inside both ranges, both grow by
2, and `base` keeps its edge. Read this before placing a phantom: an extra
insn is a 2-suid change to EVERY quantity whose range contains it, and a
tie elsewhere can absorb the win.

Measured alternatives, all on the in-place body (verify.py DIFF; the body
itself is 14):

* `(t1 + t1) - t1` alone: 14. One copy is 5 refs over 12, `2 * 5 * 4 / 12 =
  3.33 < 3.67`; `x` still wins. `c1 = (t1 + t1) - t1; ... = (c1 + c1) - c1`
  (two chained copies): 14, combine folds both to a single copy.
* `t1`/`t2` declared `u8`: byte-identical to `u32`. Combine merges the
  narrowing copy into the `sb` (`(subreg:QI (reg) 0)` is a valid movqi
  source), so no copy reaches local-alloc.
* `__asm__("" :: "r"(t2), "r"(t2), "r"(t2))` after the shift: 14. The
  references land (5 refs) but the asm is an insn inside `t2`'s range, not
  a tie, and the range grows to match.
* `t2 += base; t2 -= base;` (the "free reference pair"): 16. combine's fold
  leaves `t2` dying in two places, which takes it out of local-alloc
  altogether (`reg_n_deaths[i] == 1`, local-alloc.c:472).
* `do { } while (0)` opened at each of the 23 statements, closed before the
  `if` or at the end of the arm: 14-66. **A loop note is not a flow block
  boundary**: `find_basic_blocks` starts a block only at a CODE_LABEL or
  after a JUMP/CALL/BARRIER (`if (code != NOTE) prev_code = code;`,
  flow.c:493), and the `.lreg` dump shows block 7 unchanged with every
  pseudo still "in block 7"; what the note does is double every reference
  inside it (loop depth) and fence sched1. The entry "A degenerate loop is a
  BLOCK BOUNDARY" is about sched, and should be read that way.
* The last +0x14 store in both arms (makes `x` global): 47. global.c's
  `find_reg` (:904) takes, in pass 0, the lowest register already in
  `regs_used_so_far` that is outside `hard_reg_conflicts` (:952-956), so a
  global `x` would get $a0 -- but `base` and `mask`, still local, are
  allocated first and take $a0/$a1. The dump shows exactly that. The
  arithmetic says ALL of `x`, `base`, `mask` global would reproduce the
  listing ($a0, $a1, $a2 in priority order, with `n`, `b`, `f`, `t0`
  following), and no legal C references the three in another block at zero
  cost; an `__asm__` in the `if` arm doing so was 27.

The permuter's score-60 body (rejected, semantic break) was the clue: it
had `x` in $a0 with the in-place `addiu` because its `srl` came AFTER the
mask and immediately before the `sb`, a 2-ref temp over 2 suids (4.0) that
sat in $v0 inside `x`'s range. The device is that quantity rebuilt at the
listing's `srl` position.

**WHEN THE TIE DOES NOT TRANSFER (func_8004E4C0, 2026-10-31).** The copy
survives to local-alloc only because combine cannot merge the source's
defining insn into it. Here `t1 = w >> 24` reads `w`, and `w &= 0xFFFFFF`
is set between the shift and the copy, so `can_combine_p` refuses
(`use_crosses_set_p`, combine.c:930) and the copy stays. On func_8004E4C0
the same construct on a quotient `q = n / 10` whose source (the HI copy)
is never reset measured 7 DIFF: combine merged the `srl` INTO the folded
copy, pseudo 88 and its inflated count vanished from the `.lreg` dump, and
the survivor had the plain 6 refs. A self-assigned `q = (q+q+q)-q-q` is 7
as well: the `.lreg` line reads "used 16 times ... dies in 2 places", so
local-alloc.c:472 sends it to global-alloc. The form that works there is
the phantom ZERO below, which needs no copy and no tie.

## A `return 0` BETWEEN A COMPARE AND ITS BRANCH: one jump1 hoist is both the $v1 compare and the delay slot reorg declines

MEASURED on func_8003F368 (unk_12A70), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 113 of 113 words,
`make check` and all three containers byte-identical. The park sat at 4 DIFF
after 179,339 permuter candidates, search.py over 17 families, unname.py and
NINETEEN spellings of the `&&` chain that all measured exactly 4. It was
closed by reading `reorg.c` and the `.jump`/`.lreg`/`.dbr` dumps: the two
"independent" causes the park recorded -- one guard's delay slot left as a
`nop`, and the next guard's compare in $v1 -- are ONE pre-reorg layout fact.

**The listing signature.** Three identical guards fall through to a shared
`return 0`:

    slti  $v0,$v0,0x4B ; beqz $v0,.L510 ; addu $v0,$zero,$zero   <- copy, branch PAST .L50C
    slti  $v0,$v0,0x3C ; beqz $v0,.L50C ; nop                    <- EMPTY, branch TO .L50C
    slti  $v1,$v0,0x4B ; beqz $v1,.L510 ; addu $v0,$zero,$zero   <- $v1, branch PAST .L50C
    bgtz  $s0,.L510    ; addu $v0,$s0,$zero
    .L50C: addu $v0,$zero,$zero
    .L510: epilogue

Read it as: the THIRD guard's `v0 = 0` was its own insn, sitting between its
`slti` and its `beqz` before reorg, and that `beqz` already went to `.L510`.
Everything else follows. The source that produces it is NOT the chain:

    if (A && B) {
        if (!(C)) {
            return 0;
        }
        if (pos > 0) {
            return pos;
        }
    }
    return 0;

The guard written as its own negated early return is the one whose `v0 = 0`
is hoisted; the guard BEFORE it is the one that gets the `nop`.

**1. cc1psx's jump1 hoists the fall-through arm (MEASURED; the code is not
upstream's).** `if (!(C)) return 0;` expands as `bnez t3 -> L_skip; v0 = 0;
jump L_ret; L_skip:`. The `.jump` dump shows the result as `272: t3 = (v0 <=
74); 311: v0 = 0; 273: bne t3 -> 309` where 311 is a NEW insn and 309 is the
return label: the fall-through arm's single assignment is re-emitted
immediately before the last conditional jump of the chain, that jump is
inverted and sent to the join label, and the original `v0 = 0; jump` is
deleted. Three test functions confirm the shape in isolation --
`if (a < 5) return b; return 0;` compiles to `slt; bne $4,$0,$L3 ; move $2,$5
[slot]; move $2,$0; $L3:`, and with a two- or three-term `&&` the hoisted
`move` lands before the LAST branch only, the earlier ones still going to
the `return 0` label. The same hoist is what puts `v0 = pos` before the
`bgtz` in every body of this function (insn 296 in the park, 310 here).
Upstream 2.7.2.3's transformation (jump.c:789-920) hoists the OTHER arm --
`emit_insn_after_with_line_notes (PATTERN (temp2), p, temp2)`, :811, with
`temp2` the insn at the branch target -- and its `nuses` walk (:767-783)
stops at a CALL_INSN with uses outstanding, so it would not fire on this
chain at all. So this is a Cygnus-snapshot change: cite the measurement, not
jump.c.

**2. Why the compare is in $v1 (`local-alloc.c`).** The compare quantity is
born at 272 and dies at 273 (`reg_is_born`, :1969; `wipe_dead_reg`, :2057),
and hard $v0 is reborn at 311 in between: `mark_life` (:1989) puts it in
`regs_live`, which is copied into `regs_live_at[2 * insn_number]` at the end
of that insn (:1416). `find_free_reg` ORs `regs_live_at` over the whole range
`[born, dead)` (:2108), which contains 311, so $v0 is `used`. The quantity's
suggestion IS $v0 -- `combine_regs` records a hard-register operand as
`qty_phys_sugg` (:1815) -- but the suggested-only pass (:1472, :2150) can
only fail, and the general pass takes the lowest free register (:2158):
0 and 1 are fixed, 2 is used, so $v1. The `.lreg` dumps say it directly:
`Register 125 in 2` for the chain, `Register 125 in 3` here. The chain has
nothing reborn between the compare's birth and death, so $v0 is free.

**3. Why the second guard's slot stays empty (`reorg.c`).** `dbr_schedule`
runs `fill_simple_delay_slots` before `fill_eager_delay_slots` (:4329-4331).
The simple pass scans BACKWARD from the third `beqz` (:2907) and finds 311
immediately before it; 311 sets $v0 and the branch needs only $v1 (:2905), so
it is taken (:2943): `update_block (trial, trial)` leaves a `(use (insn
311))` marker at 311's position (:2244) and 311 is deleted. That fills the
third slot from BEFORE the branch, with no redirect needed (the branch
already goes to the return label) -- in the `.dbr` dump the slot insn is
`insn 311`, not `insn/s`, which is how a stolen-from-before insn differs
from a target copy. Now the eager pass reaches the SECOND guard. Its target
thread is the shared `v0 = 0` (not owned: fall-through reaches it,
`own_thread_p` :2175-2185), so the only option is a copy, and a copy is
allowed only if the trial sets nothing live at the OPPOSITE thread, the
fall-through (:3375-3376). `mark_target_live_regs` of that fall-through
(:3293) finds the block from the last BARRIER's label (`find_basic_block`,
:2192 -- it returns that block, 15 here, NOT -1), scans the block up to the
target, then scans forward from the target: the call marks $v0 set and drops
it (:2742-2746), the `slti` sets $v1, and then the USE marker -- "any
registers set by the underlying insn are live since the insn is being done
somewhere else" -- puts $v0 BACK into the live set (:2698-2704), and the
third guard's conditional jump ends the scan (:2724-2738). So $v0 is needed
at the fall-through, `insn_sets_resource_p (trial, &opposite_needed, 1)`
rejects the trial, `lose = 1` (:3457), and with the thread not owned the loop
ends (:3316): no delay list, the branch keeps its label, the slot is a `nop`.
The FIRST guard's fall-through scan (its call, its `slti`, the second `beqz`)
crosses no marker, so its copy goes through (:3430 `copy_rtx`, :3615
redirect past the copied insn). In the chain body there is no marker
anywhere -- the third `v0 = 0` was never separate -- so all three copy, and
that is the park's 4 DIFF. The markers are deleted when reorg finishes
(:4337-4344), so the `.dbr` dump never shows them; infer them from the
sequence structure.

**What the park had recorded, corrected.** The park (and the older lever
"reorg STEALS a delay-slot insn or COPIES it", above) reached
`insn_sets_resource_p (trial, &opposite_needed)` as the condition, which is
right, but explained the liveness by `find_basic_block` returning -1 and
"block-entry layout". `find_basic_block` returns the block head after the
last barrier here (block 15) for every one of the three fall-throughs, and
the register is live because of an `update_block` marker, which is a
consequence of a DIFFERENT branch's slot having been filled from before it.
Nothing about the three guards' own layout distinguishes them.

**The lever, generally.** When a listing has N identical guards sharing one
`return 0` and exactly one of them keeps a `nop` while branching TO the
shared insn, while the others branch PAST it with copies: the guard AFTER
the empty one is written as its own negated early return (`if (!(C)) return
0;`), the guards before it as an `&&` chain, and whatever follows (here
`if (pos > 0) return pos;`) as separate statements inside the same block.
The compare of that next guard will be in a register other than $v0, which
is the second half of the signature. Measured on this tail (verify.py DIFF):

* the `&&` chain in nineteen spellings: 4 (the park's list).
* `if (A && B) { if (C) { if (pos > 0) return pos; return 0; } return 0; } return 0;`: 4.
* `if (A && B) { if (C) { if (pos > 0) return pos; } return 0; } return 0;`: 4.
* `if (A && B) { if (C) { if (pos > 0) return pos; return 0; } } return 0;`: 4.
* `if (A && B) { if (C && pos > 0) return pos; return 0; } return 0;`: 4.
* `if (!(A && B)) return 0; if (!(C)) return 0; if (pos > 0) return pos; return 0;`: 4.
  Its four differing words are the park's four (the `nop` and the $v0
  compare), so the hoist did not happen for the third guard there. WHY is
  not established.
* `if (A && B) { if (C) return pos > 0 ? pos : 0; return 0; } return 0;`: 7.
* `if (A && B) { if (!(C)) return 0; if (pos > 0) return pos; } return 0;`: MATCH.

## A PHANTOM ZERO: `+ ((v + v) - v - v)` is three references on ONE value, no insn, no tie

MEASURED on func_8004E4C0 (unk_1C540), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 47 of 47 words,
`make check` and all three containers byte-identical. The park sat at 5 DIFF
-- a single $v0/$v1 swap across `srl`/`sll`/`addu`/`sll`/`subu` in the digit
loop -- after 152,591 permuter candidates, search.py and unname.py, and it
had done the arithmetic: the quotient needed more references and nothing
legal gave it any without giving the `*10` chain more at the same time.

**The contest, priced per QUANTITY from the `.lreg` dump** (advise.py prints
per-pseudo rows with flow's live length; local-alloc prices the tied
quantity over suids, `qty_compare_1` local-alloc.c:1705). Named-quotient
body `q = n / 10; t = q * 10; t = n - t; t += 0x30; *out++ = t;` (7 DIFF,
the target's pairing with the registers swapped). Block 3 after sched1:
`srl` is insn 3, `sll` 4, `addu` 5, `sll` 6, `subu` 7, `addiu` 8, `sb` 9.

    q      6 refs   born 6, dies 10 (the addu)   2 * 6 * 4 / 4   = 12.0  -> allocated SECOND, $v1
    chain  20 refs  born 8, dies 18 (the sb)     4 * 20 * 4 / 10 = 32.0  -> allocated FIRST, $v0

The chain is ONE quantity: `block_alloc` tries operand 1 of the `addu`
first (local-alloc.c:1350-1408), the shifted temp dies there, so the sum
ties into IT and not into `q`; each later step consumes the last, and
`combine_regs` adds every tied pseudo's count (:1858-1870): 4 + 4 + 4 + 8.
To flip, `q` over its 4 suids needs `floor_log2(r) * r > 32`: r = 11, i.e.
+5 weighted = +3 raw references inside the loop, with no new insn (a
surviving insn inside the chain's range would only lower the chain to
26.7 and would cost a word).

**The device.** `t = q * 10 + ((q + q) - q - q);`

* cse leaves it: the `.cse` dump has `115 = q << 1`, `116 = 115 - q`,
  `117 = 116 - q`, `t = 114 + 117` as four insns.
* flow counts them: `reg_n_refs[regno] += loop_depth` (flow.c:2122) -- the
  `.flow` dump reads "Register 88 used 12 times across 7 insns", 6 raw.
  These are live sets feeding the real expression, so flow does not delete
  them; the "a dead SET does not count" trap in the dead-reference lever
  does not apply.
* combine deletes them: `gen_binary` calls `simplify_binary_operation`,
  whose MINUS case has "X * C - X ... or if the multiplication is written as
  a shift ... maybe just have X (if C is 2 in the example above)"
  (cse.c:3785-3789, code to :3810), so `(minus (ashift q 1) q)` is `q`;
  then `(minus q q)` is 0 (:3743-3746). The remaining `(plus chain 0)` goes
  too and that set is folded into the final `sll`, which then sets `t`
  directly -- but WHERE the additive identity is applied is NOT established.
  It is not :3757, which is "Subtracting 0 has no effect" in `case MINUS`;
  the PLUS case of `simplify_binary_operation` has no `x + 0` rule, and
  `simplify_plus_minus` (:4258, reached at :3712) is gated on an operand
  still BEING a PLUS or MINUS, which a bare `const_int 0` is not. The
  deletion is measured: the `.combine` dump has insns 90/92/94/96 as
  `NOTE_INSN_DELETED`. Nothing reaches local-alloc, so no range changes and
  no word is added.

    q      12 refs  born 6, dies 10   3 * 12 * 4 / 4   = 36.0  -> FIRST, $v0 (find_free_reg :2158)
    chain  20 refs  born 8, dies 18   4 * 20 * 4 / 10  = 32.0  -> $v0 busy over [8,10), $v1

(The chain is now {112, 113, 87} = 4 + 4 + 12: `t` carries the folded
plus's set and the `sll`'s, so its own count rose from 8 to 12 while the
absorbed temp's 4 left -- the quantity total is unchanged, which is the
point: the construct puts references on `q` and NOWHERE ELSE.) MATCH.
`+ ((q + q + q) - q - q - q)` (16 refs) also matches.

**What did not work, and why, all 47 words.**

* The phantom as the MULTIPLICAND, `t = ((q + q + q) - q - q) * 10;` and the
  same through a named `c`: 7. combine folds the chain to a copy of `q`,
  `q` dies in that copy, nothing in the `srl`'s source is set in between
  (`use_crosses_set_p`, combine.c:930, is the only guard and reg 109 is
  never reset), so the `srl` is merged INTO the copy: pseudo 88 is absent
  from the `.lreg` dump and the surviving quotient has the plain 6 refs.
  This is why the TIED PHANTOM COPY (above) did not transfer: there the
  copy's source `t1 = w >> 24` had `w` reassigned before the copy, which is
  what kept the copy alive to be tied.
* Self-assigned `q = (q + q + q) - q - q;`: 7. `.lreg`: "Register 88 used 16
  times across 5 insns in block 3; dies in 2 places" -- the
  `reg_n_deaths[i] == 1` gate (local-alloc.c:472) sends it to global-alloc,
  the chain takes $v0 locally first, `q` gets $v1. The park's die-twice
  forms fail the same way.
* The park's list: every plain named-quotient form 7; `t = n % 10` unnamed
  5 (quotient and digit one global pseudo); no temp 7; `t |= 0x30` 6;
  re-spelling the multiply with a third `q` (`t = q * 8; t += q; t += q;`)
  7, because `t` is referenced in every added statement.

**The recipe.** When the margin asks for +k references on a value that FEEDS
arithmetic rather than being stored, add `+ ((v + v) - v - v)` to the
expression that consumes it. It is +3 raw references on `v` (weighted by
loop depth), zero on everything else, and zero insns. The stored-value case
is the TIED PHANTOM COPY; the branch case is the phantom test; this is the
operand case. The conditions are the phantom test's: written where cse
cannot see `v`'s value, and not hoistable (it is loop-variant here). It is
a device and is marked as one in the source.

## TWO ALIASES SPLIT THE TWO SIZE DECISIONS: an 8-byte alias gives cc1psx the `la`, a 16-byte decoy gives gas a `.extern` it will not call small

MEASURED on func_8004437C (gprel_17B7C), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 100 of 100
words, `make check` and all three containers byte-identical. The park sat at
8 DIFF, VERDICT SHAPE, after 214,931 permuter candidates, search.py over 17
families, unname.py and some twenty-five hand spellings; every differing word
was a register name in the two `lui`/`addiu` pairs for D_80080AF4 (3 at the
first compare, "cluster A"; 5 at the store, "cluster B"). It was closed by
reading, not searching: the two clusters have ONE cause, and the cause is a
declaration, not the body.

**Why cluster A could not be a split pair.** The `(high)` is pseudo 95, local
to block 0, 2 refs; the address is pseudo 94, global (the second comparison
re-uses it across the `bne`), `REG_EQUIV (symbol_ref)`, 3 refs, $a1 from
global-alloc. `combine_regs` refuses to tie 95 into 94 twice over:
`local-alloc.c:1842` (`sreg >= FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER && reg_qty[sreg] == -1`)
and `:1838` (`reg_qty[sreg] >= -1`) both return 0 for a SET register that
local-alloc is not allocating. And allocated on its own, 95 can reach $a1
under NO sched1 order: `find_free_reg` (:2158) takes the lowest register not
in `used` over the quantity's suids, and $v1's only occupant in block 0 is 99
(`lw $v1,0($s0)`, 2 refs over >= 6 suids = 1.33), which `qty_compare_1`
(:1598) orders AFTER 95 (2 refs over 4 = 2.0), while $a0's occupant 92 is
global and invisible to local-alloc altogether. (The park's "global allocno
154" was the `|=` pointer in block 5, not this address.) So the target's
`lui $a1 / addiu $a1,$a1` is not two insns tied; it is maspsx's expansion of
a ONE-insn `la`, which cc1psx emits only for a symbol with SYMBOL_REF_FLAG.

**And in the `la` form cluster B prices itself.** Block 8, post-sched1,
per quantity over suids:

    split pair (park body):
      index chain {184,190,191}  6 refs  [20,30)  2*6*4/10 = 4.8   -> $v0
      address {188 high, 187 lo}  4 refs  [20,30)  2*4*4/10 = 3.2   -> $v1
      stored value 199            2 refs  [28,32)  1*2*4/4  = 2.0   -> $a0
    la (landed body):
      index chain {182,187,188}  6 refs  [20,30)  2*6*4/10 = 4.8   -> $v0
      stored value 196            2 refs  [26,30)  1*2*4/4  = 2.0   -> $v1
      address 185 (one pseudo)    2 refs  [22,28)  1*2*4/6  = 1.33  -> $a0

Removing the `(high)` pseudo takes the address from 4 refs to 2 and the
value is allocated first: value $v1, address $a0, the target's registers.

**The two size decisions, from the source.**

* `SYMBOL_REF_FLAG` is set ONCE, at `make_decl_rtl`, by `ENCODE_SECTION_INFO`
  (mips.h:2783-2788): `size = int_size_in_bytes (TREE_TYPE (DECL))`, flag if
  `size > 0 && size <= mips_section_threshold`. With the flag the movsi
  expander does not split and the output is `la $5,D_80080AF4`.
* The `.extern NAME, SIZE` record is made separately, when the parser meets
  the identifier's FIRST USE (c-parse.c:2062, `assemble_external`, once per
  SYMBOL_REF via `SYMBOL_REF_USED`), through `mips_output_external`
  (mips.c:4282-4291): `len = int_size_in_bytes (TREE_TYPE (decl))` read THEN,
  recorded only if `len > 0`, pushed LIFO (`p->next = extern_head`). At file
  end `mips_asm_file_end` prints the list head first and suppresses later
  records with the same name (`TREE_ASM_WRITTEN (name_tree)`, :4219-4222).
* gas at -G8 makes an undefined symbol $gp-relative from that record alone
  when its size is <= 8, and D_80080AF4 is inside gprel_17B7C's $gp window.

Two declarations with the same `__asm__` name therefore separate them:

```c
    extern u32 *D_80080AF4s[2] __asm__("D_80080AF4");    /* flag: la   */
    extern u32 *D_80080AF4big[4] __asm__("D_80080AF4");  /* .extern 16 */
    ...uses of D_80080AF4s...
    (void) sizeof(D_80080AF4big);   /* parsed AFTER the alias's first use */
```

The decoy's use is parse-time only: the parser's primary rule calls
`assemble_external` on the identifier inside `sizeof` and no RTL is made.
Its record is pushed last, so it is printed first: `.extern D_80080AF4, 16`,
and gas expands both `la`s to adjacent same-register pairs.

**Measured** (verify.py DIFF on gprel_17B7C; listing facts from `ccpsx -S`):

* 8-byte file-scope alias alone: 98 words, 87 -- listing `.extern
  D_80080AF4, 8` and `la $5,D_80080AF4`, gas gives `addiu $a1,$gp,0`.
* alias + 16-byte decoy at file scope, decoy used after the first access:
  MATCH -- listing `.extern D_80080AF4, 16`, same two `la`s.
* both at BLOCK scope inside the function (the landed form): MATCH.
* decoy used BEFORE the alias's first use: 87 -- its record is pushed first,
  printed second, suppressed; `.extern` reads 8 again.
* decoy sized 8 (`[2]`): 87 -- the record is small either way.
* `-Wall`: silent.

**Unit-wide effect, stated.** The unit's `.extern D_80080AF4` line now reads
16 where the incomplete array in structs.h emitted none. No other function in
gprel_17B7C references D_80080AF4 (grep of csrc and the unit's nonmatchings),
and a compiler-split `%hi`/`%lo` pair is not touched by `.extern` in any case.
The declaration in structs.h is unchanged.

**What did not work, so the next attempt does not re-measure it.** All 100
of 100 words, 8 DIFF unless noted: temps for the index, the stored pointer or
the compared operand; `(s32)` casts at all three sites; `*(D_80080AF4 + i)`;
`*(&D_80080AF4[0] + i)`; `*(u32 **) &D_80080AF4[i]`; `D_80080AFC = (s16)
((u16) D_80080AFC ^ 1)`; a memory barrier immediately before the store.
Guarded stores 32/33; `u32 **r = &D_80080AF4[i]; *r = ...` 10; first
comparison's operands swapped 18; barriers at the top / after the store
25 / 30; `(u8 *) D_80080AF4 + i * 4` 79; `u32 **p = D_80080AF4` local 14 at
the first site (pair still untied, `lui $v0 / addiu $a1,$v0`), 89 anywhere
that includes the store. **The TIED PHANTOM COPY on the stored value**
(`u32 q = (u32) D_8006E704[arg0]; D_80080AF4[i] = (u32 *) ((q + q + q) - q
- q);`) is 8: the `.combine` dump has the store reading pseudo 203 with the
plain 2 refs and no copy insn. The value's defining insn is a MEM load with
no `REG_EQUIV` note, so `can_combine_p`'s MEM clause (combine.c:927-930,
which only EXEMPTS a `REG_EQUIV` MEM from the test) sends it to
`use_crosses_set_p`, whose memory rule (`code == MEM && mem_last_set >
from_cuid`, :10134) finds no store between the `lw` and the folded copy;
the load is merged INTO the copy and the tie never forms. That is the
"does not transfer" case of that entry, now seen on a MEM source: for a
loaded-then-stored value the phantom copy only survives if something sets
memory between the load and the store.

## A DEAD SET IN A TWO-OUTPUT ASM: a conflict for global-alloc and a second death for local-alloc, with no insn and no fence

MEASURED on func_8005BBFC (unk_2CDC0), 2026-10-31. LANDED, 333 of 333 words,
`make check` e6bfbb95ff6676899e077481221d73ddd4d3bf52 and all three containers
byte-identical. The park sat at 16 DIFF after 162,955 permuter candidates,
search.py, unname.py and 306 hand variants; the `func_8005EC0C3` alias it
needed to compile at all re-measured at the same 16, so that was the real base.

**The shape.** Two values `l` and `r` are each a copy of a third, `a`, in
opposite arms of a branch, and both are then passed to a call in $a1/$a2:

    then: r = a; l = f(r);        target: sra $a0 ; addu $a2,$a0 ; ... sll $v1,$a2
    else: l = a; r = g(l);                addu $a1,$a0 ; sll $v0,$a1

The target keeps `a` in $a0 and emits BOTH copies. The build put `a` in $a1,
so the else-arm copy was a no-op and the function came out one real word
short -- the count still read 333 because sched2 then had `attr.note`'s
`sh $s7` to spend early and left a nop in the `lhu` delay slot.

**Why `a` takes $a1, read from the dump.** `.greg` prints conflict sets and
preferences. `a` (110) conflicted with neither `l` (111) nor `r` (112): at a
copy whose source dies, `global_conflicts` processes the REG_DEAD before the
SET (global.c:722-731), so source and destination never overlap. `l` had copy
preference $a1 and `r` $a2 from the argument copies (`set_preference`,
global.c:1590-1628), and `expand_preferences` (global.c:783-830) hands a dying
copy source its destination's hard-register preferences UNLESS the two
conflict (:799-800; copy preferences only when the dying reg IS the SET_SRC,
:807). So `a` prefers {$a1, $a2}; it is allocated 5th, before `l` and `r`, and
`find_reg` takes the lowest-numbered copy preference not in `used`
(global.c:1004-1033): $a1. `regs_used_so_far` starts with every call-used
register (global.c:353-355), so the pass-0 exclusion cannot help, and
`regs_someone_prefers` cannot exclude a register the allocno itself prefers
(`prune_preferences`, global.c:879-885). With NO usable preference, pass 0
takes the lowest free regno -- mips.h has no REG_ALLOC_ORDER -- and $v0/$v1
are in `a`'s conflicts, so that is $a0 (global.c:954-983). The target's `a`
therefore conflicted with BOTH `l` and `r`. There is no legal way to say that:

* any READ of `a` after the copy is rewritten to `l`/`r` by cse, because
  `make_regs_eqv` makes the copy's destination canonical when its last uid is
  beyond the block and later than the source's (cse.c:865-869) -- measured
  `r = x * (a << 1) >> 7` 16 (no change), `__asm__ volatile("" ::"r"(a))`
  after the copy 16 (no change: the operand was rewritten too);
* a dead `a = 0;` after the call flips the canonical register (21): now the
  shifts read `a`, sched1 sinks the then-arm copy below the shift since
  nothing depends on it, and `a` dies in the copy again;
* a read at the JOIN is out of cse's reach (the ebb scan stops at any
  CODE_LABEL, cse.c:8087, and follows only conditional jumps whose label
  follows a BARRIER, :8118), but an identical-arm `if (a)` there is a block
  boundary and costs the schedule: 104-122;
* a single-output NON-volatile `__asm__("" : "=r"(a))` after the copy is a
  dead set and flow deletes it (`insn_dead_p`, flow.c:1758-1813; the
  deletion is gated only on `INSN_VOLATILE`, :1478-1481): 16, no change;
* the volatile form `__asm__ volatile("" : "+r"(a))` DOES create the
  conflict -- a volatile asm is never dead -- but sched treats it as using
  and setting every register (sched.c:1987-2000): in one arm 25 (`a` then
  coalesces with the OTHER copy), in both 122-129 at the park's note
  position. (With the note store moved, below, the volatile `"=r"(a)` pair
  matches as well; it was the note, not the fence, that the 129 measured.)

**The device.** A NON-volatile asm with two outputs, one dead, one tied:

    r = a;
    __asm__("" : "=r"(a), "=r"(r) : "1"(r));
    l = (0x40 - (x & 0x3F)) * (r << 1) >> 7;

(and `"=r"(l) : "1"(l)` in the else arm). It emits nothing. flow keeps the
insn because the `r` set is needed, and marks the `a` set with REG_UNUSED
("a dead store that cannot be eliminated because the same insn does
something useful", flow.c:2149-2156). `global_conflicts` runs
`note_stores (mark_reg_store)` on the insn (global.c:731), which records the
`a` set against everything live -- `r` here, `l` in the else arm -- and only
then applies the REG_UNUSED death (:765-767). `a` now conflicts with 111 and
112 in the dump, has no preference line, and is allocated into $a0; `l` and
`r` keep $a1/$a2 from their own copy preferences. sched does not fence on it
(sched.c:1987 fences only `ASM_INPUT` and a VOLATILE `ASM_OPERANDS`). The tie
target is free: `r`/`l`, or `x` in both arms, all MATCH. Both arms are
needed: without the then-arm asm 117, without the else-arm asm 108, without
both 108 (`a` back in $a1, 333 words with the note store in the wrong slot).

**The second half: the same construct as a SECOND DEATH.** With `a` in $a0
the park's other device -- an identical-arm `if (D_80086A40[bank].unk_18)`
in the then arm -- became poison (127). It had bought `x` its $v1 by making
the `unk_18` load temp global (a third reference in another block), so the
temp was allocated AFTER `x` instead of taking $v1 from local-alloc first;
but that extends the temp across `a`'s birth, so it CONFLICTS with `a`, and
the target has both in $a0. The replacement:

    g = D_80086A40[bank].unk_18;
    a = g * v[0x14] * v[0x15] >> 7;
    __asm__("" : "=r"(g), "=r"(x) : "1"(x));

The dead set of `g` in its own block gets the same REG_UNUSED death
(flow.c:2156 is `reg_n_deaths++`), so `.lreg` reads "Register 119 used 3
times across 3 insns in block 17; dies in 2 places", and local-alloc's gate
`reg_basic_block[i] >= 0 && reg_n_deaths[i] == 1` (local-alloc.c:472) sends
it to global-alloc. There it is priority 1.0 against `x`'s 1.565, allocated
after `x`, and takes $a0 -- its range still ends at the `mult`, so no
conflict with `a`. Left to local-alloc it is the 2-ref load temp that loses
$v0 to the `v[0x14]` temp (2 refs over 2 suids beats 2 over 4) and takes
$v1, which puts hard $v1 into `x`'s conflicts and `x` into $a0: 15 DIFF
without this asm. Tie target `l` MATCH, `x` MATCH, `r` 15 (uninitialised
there, so `r` goes live from entry); placed in either arm instead, MATCH.

**The note store moved last.** With the arms right, the park's lever 2 had
to be re-swept: `attr.note = pit;` now sits after `attr.volume.right`, so its
`sh $s7` is what sched2 drops into the `lhu 0x12($v0)` delay slot. 61
positions measured; the two next to it are 2 and 3, the park's old position
94, everything above the clamp 127-271.

**Also measured, for the record.** `a = unk_18; a = a * ... >> 7;` (one
pseudo for the load and the result) 39 with the old device, 41 without: the
longer `a` conflicts with `v` in $a1 and is allocated before `x`. One-argument
`func_8005EC0C(&attr)` 102: it does put `a` in $a0 (no $a1/$a2 preferences
to inherit), but `l`'s $a1 preference also reaches `sum` through
`l = sum * 8` (expand_preferences' non-copy merge, global.c:815-825), and
the loop setup swaps $a1/$a2. The definition lands with the unit's existing
`s16 (s16 x8)` prototype at csrc/unk_2CDC0.c:2567: the all-`s16` signature
and the park's `s32 (s16, s16, u16, ..., u16, u16)` both MATCH.

**The recipe.** When an allocno must CONFLICT with a value it is copied into
(so that it cannot inherit that value's hard register through
`expand_preferences`), or must die TWICE (so that local-alloc leaves it to
global-alloc without lengthening it), dead-set it in a non-volatile asm whose
other output ties a live variable to itself. Zero insns, no fence, no -Wall
warning. The tied output adds two references to that variable; pick one
whose priority has room, and never one that is not yet initialised there.
This is the fourth phantom: the tied phantom copy puts references on a
stored value, the phantom zero on an operand, the phantom test on a branch
condition; this one puts a SET on a value, which is the only one of the four
that reaches the allocator as a conflict.

**Second instance, func_8004E9EC (unk_1C540), 2026-10-31 -- NOT landed,
33 of 33 words at 5 DIFF from 31/32, all measured by verify.py and read in
the dumps.** Three uses of the non-volatile asm on one 33-word function,
each doing a different job, and three facts about what the construct can
and cannot do that the first instance did not need:

* **The dead output is the only way the asm creates a second death.** A
  tied value (`"=r"(p) : "0"(p)`) gets NO `REG_DEAD` for the input that is
  also the output (flow dump: the asm insn carries none), so `.lreg` still
  reads one death and local-alloc keeps the pseudo. The park's pointer `p`
  needed global-alloc (its `$a1` comes from being first in `allocno_compare`
  order with hard 2/3/4 held by the block-local loads), and only
  `__asm__("" : "=r"(p), "=r"(a), "=r"(b), "=r"(c) : "1"(a), "2"(b), "3"(c))`
  after the loads -- p as a DEAD output -- gave "dies in 2 places" and the
  global allocation (`9 regs to allocate: 88 ...`, p first, `88 in 5`).
* **A tied single output is an opaque value for cse and a second set for
  loop.c.** `__asm__("" : "=r"(p) : "0"(p))` right after `p = SYM;` stops
  `find_best_addr` folding the first `(mem (reg p))` into `(mem (lo_sum))`
  (cse.c:2735-2760: ADDRESS_COST is 1 for both a bare REG -- mips.h:3136
  short-circuits `REG_P` ahead of `mips_address_cost` -- and a LO_SUM
  (mips.c:1902-1904), and on an equal address cost `find_best_addr` takes the
  HIGHER rtx cost, cse.c:2744-2746; nested mems fold too via fold_rtx's MEM
  case, cse.c:5064), so all three loads read off p and p conflicts with the first
  load's register; and p now has two sets in the loop, so `scan_loop`'s
  `n_times_set == 1` test (loop.c:804; its `consec_sets_invariant_p` arm at
  :706-708 needs every set invariant, and an asm is not) keeps the
  `addiu %lo` in the loop
  even when the inner loop is a real `while` -- which the `p = 0` lever
  above cannot do, because for a real inner loop its clause (1) holds.
* **An asm is latency-free to the scheduler in BOTH directions, and the two
  rules are different code.** As a PRODUCER it costs 1: `insn_cost` returns
  early for an unrecognisable insn (sched.c:1410-1414, `INSN_CODE (insn) < 0`
  -> `INSN_COST = 1`), where the load it displaces costs 2 (mips.md:157-159,
  load READY-DELAY 2 on r3000). So a store that reads its value through a
  tied asm has priority `priority(asm) + 1 - 1` instead of `+ 2 - 1`
  (priority(), sched.c:1519-1522) -- 1 instead of 2, tying with the biv
  increment. As a CONSUMER it discounts the links into it
  (`LINK_COST_FREE`, :1394-1396, applied at :1402-1403), which keeps the asm
  itself at the loads' priority rather than above them; that rule does NOT
  touch the store's link, so do not reach for it to explain a consumer's
  priority. Conversely an `"r"(x)` input cannot LIFT an insn's priority
  (12 DIFF measured) -- both rules work the one way.
* **Which way that tie resolves, with the direction nailed down.**
  `rank_for_schedule` SWAPS ITS OWN ARGUMENTS (`tmp = *y; tmp2 = *x`,
  sched.c:2433-2434) and its header comment says a positive return prefers
  `y` (:2381-2383), so `ready[0]` is the MOST preferred: highest priority,
  then highest class (:2399-2420 -- class 3 independent of
  `last_scheduled_insn`, class 2 anti/output-dependent on it, class 1 data).
  The pass runs BACKWARD and the first insn chosen becomes the tail
  (sched.c:3847-3849, :3773), so the winner of a tie is emitted LAST. That
  is how the target's `addiu $a3,2` AFTER the three `sb`s was reproduced:
  the increment is the class-3 insn at that tie and the stores class 2.
* **A tied copy with no preference**: `__asm__("" : "=r"(kk), "=r"(r) :
  "0"(n))` as the first statement, kk used everywhere n was. set_preference
  returns because the source is an ASM_OPERANDS, not a REG
  (global.c:1561-1569; rtl.def:417 gives ASM_OPERANDS the format `ssiEEsi`,
  so the 'e'-strip at :1545 does not reach it), expand_preferences never
  looks at a two-output asm at all because `single_set` is 0 on a PARALLEL of
  two SETs (global.c:794; a single-output form instead fails the dying-reg
  allocno test at :798 once n is block-local), reload materialises the "0"
  tie as the target's `addu $t2,$a1,$zero`, and the dead output r pins
  `r = 0` behind n's death (without it sched1 hoists `r = 0` and r conflicts
  with hard 5: 31 DIFF). A legal `kk = n` cannot: make_regs_eqv (cse.c:863-868)
  makes kk canonical, n dies at the copy, kk inherits `5`.

**The floor it left, as a warning.** The copy device cannot reproduce the
target's `$t1`/`$t2` because allocation ORDER is priority
(`allocno_compare`, global.c:587-608: `floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length`
times `allocno_size`, ties by allocno number): a pseudo born at a statement measures
~30 insns of life where the parameter pseudo measures 56, so `kk` (0.258)
outranks the `high` temp (0.058; 0.154 with a real inner loop, whose lo_sum
use weighs loop_depth 3) while the real parameter (0.143) does not. The
target therefore has the PARAMETER in `$t2` with its `$a1` preference somehow
ineffective; under global.c as read that needs hard 5 in n's conflicts before
allocation, and WHY the original has it is not established. The lesson for
the lever: a dead set or tied copy changes conflicts and preferences, never
`live_length`, so it cannot move an allocno past one whose life begins at
the function entry.

## A BLOCK-LOCAL TWIN FOR A GLOBAL VALUE: local-alloc occupies the register global-alloc will hand the global

MEASURED on func_8004CECC (unk_1C540), 2026-10-31, second pass. NOT landed:
the park stays at 102/36, and the structure below reaches 101/100 positional
but only 21 register-only words after alignment -- every long-lived register
in the target's colour block reproduced -- with one word missing for a reason
the source tree cannot show (below).

**The shape.** A value `val` is set in BOTH arms of an `if` and read after the
join (here, in the switch arms); in the long arm it is computed first and then
read by three multiplies. The target keeps `val` in $a2 across the whole arm,
and NO block-local quantity in that arm touches $a2 (sat=$a3, the 0x80808081
constant=$t0), although local-alloc runs first and hands each local the lowest
free register over its range (`find_free_reg`, local-alloc.c:2230-2247, `used`
from `regs_live_at` at :2109).

**Why no legal global can do that.** A hard register live anywhere in a global
pseudo's range is a conflict: `mark_reg_store` on a pseudo that local-alloc
has already renumbered converts it to the hard regno (global.c:1363) and
`record_one_conflict` marks that regno in `hard_reg_conflicts` of EVERY live
allocno (record_one_conflict's hard-reg branch, :1241-1247) before setting
`hard_regs_live` (:1372). So if `val` is
born at the arm's first insn and lives to the join, nothing local can be in
$a2 there without barring `val` from it; and if nothing local is in $a2,
local-alloc gives $a2 to the first local whose range is free there (sat, 4
refs over 40 half-insns, priority 2000 in `qty_compare_1`'s units,
local-alloc.c:1705-1730). The park's two markers moved sat by priority but
could not vacate $a2 for a global.

**The shape that does it.** Split `val` in the long arm into a BLOCK-LOCAL
twin `vv` that the multiplies read, and assign the global at the END of the
arm: `vv = v & 0xFF; ... val = vv;`. Then

* local-alloc allocates `vv` itself and, if its priority falls between the
  two longer locals above sat and sat, gives it $a2 (lowest free over its
  range);
* `val = vv` is a copy from a renumbered pseudo: `set_preference` converts
  the source to its hard reg (global.c:1583-1587) and its second arm then
  sets the preference on the DESTINATION's allocno, because here the hard reg
  is the source (`src_regno < FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER && dest_regno >=
  FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER`, global.c:1611-1628), so `val` gets copy preference
  6; `val` is born where `vv` dies, because a REG_DEAD note is applied before
  the insn's sets are marked live (global.c:722-724 then :729), so it never
  conflicts with hard 6; `.greg` prints
  "85 preferences: 6", "85 in 6", and the copy is a no-op reload deletes;
* every other global keeps its register: `out` $t1 and `h` $t2 because
  hard 6/7/8 are in their conflicts from the locals, p/q/t $a1/$a3/$a0 as
  before.

**The priority window is narrow and sched1 sets it.** sched1 runs before
either allocator and places the end copy -- priority 1, no in-block
consumer -- as latency filler between the last `mult` and the rounding
chains (position 32 of the block in every build measured, ready list
`127 (1) 44 (1)` at T-16), so `vv` dies at half-insn 64. Over [2,64) it needs
floor_log2(refs)*refs/62 between sat's 2000 and the p-numerator's 2500-2608
(x10000): 5 refs (the plain copy) is 1612 -> $t0; 6 refs is 1935 -> $t0 (61
DIFF); 7 refs is 2258 -> $a2; 8 refs is 3870, ahead of the p-numerator -> $a1
(47 DIFF). A simulator of block_alloc over the .lreg RTL (scratch, lasim.py)
reproduces every "Register N in M" line of the device-free dump and these
numbers.

**What buys the 7th reference, measured.** Legal +1 spellings of the copy
(`(vv + vv) - vv`, `vv * 2 - vv`, `(vv << 1) - vv`) all count 6; the phantom
zero counts 8 (and costs a word); the free pair `val = vv + X; val = val - X`
counts 5 for X in {h, f, p, q, t} (71-80) and moves sat's death for X = sat
(52). The one spelling that reached 7 is the tied asm

    vv = v & 0xFF;
    __asm__("" : "=r"(vv) : "0"(vv), "r"(v));

whose two operands on `vv` are the two references, and whose `"r"(v)` input
is scheduled right after the `and` because the asm feeds the multiplies --
so `v` outlives `vv`'s birth, conflicts with hard 6, and takes $v1 (the
target's register) instead of $a2. The park's `__asm__("" ::"r"(v))` as a
statement cannot do the second half: it is filler too, lands at position 31,
and v then lives across the whole block and takes $t4.

**Why it is still one word short, and the two facts that are NOT in the
2.7.2.3 tree.**

1. The grey arm's `val = v` copy, `(set (reg 6 a2) (reg 3 v1))` with REG_DEAD
   v1, is in `.sched2` and gone from `.dbr`; it is gone from the output with
   `-fno-delayed-branch`, and with `-fno-schedule-insns2` it is in `.greg`
   and gone from `.dbr`. So a pass that runs after sched2 and before reorg
   deletes a reg-reg copy whose destination already holds the source's
   value ($a2 was copied to $v1 at the entry and not written since). It
   also deletes `$a2 = $t4` when v is in $t4 and kept alive past the join;
   it leaves the park's `t0 = t4` alone (t0 holds nothing). It is not a
   blanket rule in the TARGET: ovl_dungeon's func_800C6AEC keeps
   `addu $s0,$a0,$zero; sw $ra; addu $a0,$s0,$zero` and func_800A0E6C
   keeps `addu $a0,$v0; addu $v0,$a0`. WHY func_8004CECC's copy survived
   it is not established.
2. cc1psx fills an entry branch's delay slot from the FALL-THROUGH even when
   a parameter copy sits before the test: of the 10 target functions whose
   entry is parameter copies then a conditional branch, 0 have a parameter
   copy in the slot (func_8004E9EC, FGO_04/05/06, S_M_INIT, S_SR, ...),
   where the FSF back-scan (reorg.c:3079-3130) would take one. In our
   builds, once (1) has deleted the copy, the fall-through's first insn is
   a store the slot cannot hoist and the back-scan then does run (`move
   t1,a3` lands in the slot).

**Do not confuse this ordering with the dead-set lever's.** Both read
`global_conflicts`'s per-insn sequence, and they use opposite ends of it. A
REG_DEAD note is applied at global.c:722-724, BEFORE `note_stores
(mark_reg_store)` at :729 -- so a value born at an insn where another dies
does not conflict with it, which is what makes the end copy free here. A dead
SET is the other way round: `mark_reg_store` marks it live at :729 and only
the REG_UNUSED sweep at :765-769 kills it, which is why it reaches the
allocator AS a conflict (func_8005BBFC, above). Same function, two different
note kinds, two different points in the sequence.

**Scope of the recipe.** Whenever a target holds a global in a low register
across a block whose locals all sit one register higher, look for a local
twin assigned to the global at the block's end -- and check the local's
priority against its neighbours with the formula before trusting the copy,
because the copy's scheduled position sets the denominator.

## A GIV IS REPLACEABLE ONLY IF ITS SET SITS ABOVE THE LOOP'S FIRST JUMP -- and a volatile read through it is the tell

MEASURED on func_800345B8 (unk_72A8), 2026-10-31, from the `.loop`/`.cse2`
dumps and loop.c; not landed (546 of 546 words, 65 -> 23 DIFF from this
alone, 21 with the next entry; `docs/near-misses/func_800345B8.c` has the
rest). The shape: a byte cursor `q = (u8 *)&e->unk_01` beside a walked
struct pointer `e`, read through `((volatile u8 *)q)[1]` and `[2]` in four
arms, with `q` assigned INSIDE the `if` whose test opens the loop body. The
listing had one `move a1,s3` in a `beqz` delay slot where the target has
`nop`, two `lbu 2(a1)` where the target reads `2(s2)`, and `s`/`e`'s
registers swapped from the prologue on -- 59 register words that
advise.py's margins priced as "+1 ref on the cursor".

**The mechanism.** `q` is a giv of the biv `e` (`e + 1`, loop.c dump `giv
reg 96 src reg 94 ... mult 1 add 1`) and strength reduction makes it a new
pseudo either way. What the position decides is `v->replaceable`
(record_giv, loop.c:4720-4722):

    regno_first_uid[dest] == INSN_UID (insn)
    && uid_luid[regno_last_uid[dest]] < INSN_LUID (loop_end)
    && (! not_every_iteration || last_use_this_basic_block (dest_reg, insn))

`not_every_iteration` is set the moment the scan passes a JUMP_INSN or
CODE_LABEL (loop.c:3365-3377), so a set below the body's first `if` needs
every use in its own block (`last_use_this_basic_block`, :6326-6338, stops
at the first label or jump). Four arms fail that, the giv takes the `else`
at :4493-4498 ("May still be replaceable"), `check_final_value` (:4551)
wants a final value a `for (;;)` cannot give, and strength_reduce emits
`q = reduced` (:3946-3949, "Not replaceable; emit an insn"). The reduced
pseudo serves the plain reads; the VOLATILE reads keep the original `q`,
because their addresses are never rewritten: loop.c runs under
`init_recog_no_volatile` (loop.c:403) and `general_operand` refuses a
volatile MEM while `volatile_ok` is 0 (recog.c:807), so the
`validate_change` on each of them (loop.c:4174) fails recog. That is the
real reason behind the older "a volatile MEM is not replaced by a reduced
giv" entry in section 8 -- it is recog's state during loop, not a loop.c
rule. cse2 then collapses whichever volatile reads share the copy's
extended basic block onto the reduced giv (the first pair of arms) and
leaves the ones past a join reading the copy (the second pair): a
register, a `move`, and 4 lost references on the cursor.

**The lever is one statement move.** `q = ...` as the FIRST statement of
the body, above the test: the dump prints `giv reg 96 ... replaceable`, reg
96 is gone from `.cse2`, every read is off the reduced giv, the cursor goes
from 63 to 67 refs and from `$s3` to `$s2` ahead of the parameter it had
been losing to, and the two prologue save-slot immediates advise.py had
called IMMEDIATE findings follow (they were `$s2`/`$s3`'s slots, never a
frame difference). Check the `.loop` line for the giv BEFORE pricing a
margin on a cursor: `replaceable` absent on a DEST_REG giv whose uses span
blocks means the copy is there and the refs are split.

## TWO FREE REFERENCES ON A CALL ARGUMENT: write the call in EVERY arm, cross-jumping runs only after flow

MEASURED on func_800345B8, 2026-10-31, on the body above with `x` widened
(see the park). `m2` is an argument to `CompMatrix` whose matrix operand is
chosen by a three-way `if`; written once after the selection it has the
copies `a1 = m2` flow counts at 1 + 3 + 3 = 7 or, with the call in two of
the three arms, 10 (the earlier park's "CompMatrix duplicated into both
arms", 128 -> 125). With the call in ALL THREE arms it has 13 (849 against
the 739 of its rival) and takes the target's `$s6`, and the final code is
the same: the `.rtl`, `.jump`, `.cse`, `.loop` and `.flow` dumps all carry
three calls and `.jump2` carries one, because the only `jump_optimize`
call with `cross_jump = 1` is the post-flow one (toplev.c:3690; the four
earlier calls at :2827, :2870, :2923 and :2929 pass 0). So a shared tail
is counted per arm by flow and merged afterwards -- the same "survives flow,
removed later" rule as the free-reference-pair entries, reached through the
CFG instead of arithmetic. The merged tail is the three arms' `j .L` to one
`addu a1,s6 / jal`, which is what the target has. On that function it costs
a word elsewhere (the arms' `(high)`s tie into `$a0` and the `beqz` slot
empties); the park records it.

## INDEX THE TABLE BY THE COUNTER AND LET loop.c MAKE THE COPY: a compiler-temp giv is reduced even when its store block has been moved out, and cse2's two passes decide which register the block keeps

LANDED func_80059F8C (unk_2CDC0), 2026-10-31, from a park at 145/101 with
8 register-only rows; the volatile hypothesis on that park is a clean
negative (every `volatile` pointer spelling 146-150 words with the same
findings; the `"memory"` clobber 101, unchanged). Five things, each read
off the dumps:

* **The store blocks are placed by loop.c, not by the source.**
  `find_and_verify_loops` (loop.c:2321) takes every block that ends in a
  jump out of its loop (the RETURN/simplejump test, :2332-2337) and is
  hopped over by one conditional jump (the `condjump_p` test, :2384-2392)
  and `reorder_insns` it (:2427) after the first BARRIER at the jump
  TARGET's loop depth found walking BACK from the target (:2399-2402),
  forward only if none (:2404-2408). A `return` block therefore lands after the
  last depth-(-1) barrier before the epilogue -- the pre-loop area, where
  this target has its hit/new-slot blocks -- only when nothing with a
  barrier sits between the loop and the return label: the
  `if (i == lim) return -1; break;` tails are INSIDE the loop and the loop
  falls into `func_80059DAC(); return p;`. A scan's store block lands after
  its own tail's barrier (after the loop) or, when it is the second scan,
  after the earlier `return -1` fall-through (BEFORE the loop).
* **No call in the loop**: a CALL_INSN sets `unknown_address_altered`
  (loop.c:2298-2302) and ends every MEM hoist; the `lbu` is hoisted here.
* **Two equal constants in the loop combine and hoist; a user variable set
  twice does not.** `combine_movables` (:1245-1285) adds the two
  `(set tmp 16)` together, `move_movables` admits them at
  `threshold * savings * lifetime >= insn_count` (:1630-1633) and then
  takes 3 off the threshold (:1719), which is what leaves the `high` of
  the next hoist behind. `lim = 0x10` in both tails fails all three
  admission clauses (:695-700) and the `li $v0,16` stays beside its `bne`,
  to be cross-jumped later.
* **The `lbu` hoist with stores in the loop needs `/s` stores and a
  non-`/s` read at a constant address**: `invariant_p` asks
  `true_dependence (loop_store_mems[i], x)` (loop.c:2897, so the STORE is
  `mem` and the read is `x`), and the third clause (sched.c:834-836, inside
  817-839) clears the pair only when the store is `/s` with a varying
  address and not QImode AND the read is neither `/s` nor varying. The
  QImode test is on the STORE, which the SImode row stores satisfy; the
  read's byte width is NOT what matters -- `! MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (x)` and
  `! rtx_addr_varies_p (x)` are. COMPONENT_REF stores are `/s`
  (expr.c:5748); `D_8007382B[0]` is too, through the PLUS_EXPR clause
  (expr.c:5344-5351); `*(u8 *) (u32) D_8007382B` is neither, being a
  non-aggregate at a symbol constant. 146/112 without it.
* **Index by the counter, no pointer local.** `((Slot *) SYM)[i].len` makes
  the row address a compiler temp. loop.c:3957-3959 charges `copy_cost` only
  to a REG_USERVAR_P giv, so this one is reduced (benefit 4 - add_cost 2)
  although its moved-out store block makes it non-replaceable, and loop.c
  emits `tmp = giv`. cse2 then runs the loop-top block twice: TAKEN (the
  store block inside, `cse_basic_block_end` past it) and NOT_TAKEN (end at
  the back-branch). With the block AFTER the loop, the first pass leaves the
  reduced register canonical and the stores on it, the second makes the copy
  canonical (make_regs_eqv, cse.c:862-869) and puts the load and the
  increment on it: `addu $v1,$a0 / lw 4($v1) / addiu $a0,$v1,8 / sw 0($a0)`
  -- the copy-at-the-top shape that no user-level copy can produce, because
  cse1 retargets `u = X; v = u` into `v = X` (cse.c:7500-7522). With the
  block BEFORE the loop the copy's first reference precedes the block
  (clause 1b) in both passes and the copy dies: one register. The row
  address's `lo_sum` is also born inside the scan, after the `p + n` site,
  so the preheader copies come out high, plus, lo_sum; a pointer local
  initialised in the arm shares the `c` load's lo_sum temp and hoists it
  ahead of the plus (145/9 at best, w/ `s = q` the right order and the wrong
  register).
* **A recomputed invariant is a user variable with a dead earlier set**:
  `e2 = 0` before the loop, `e2 = p + n` at the `slt`; the dead set moves
  `regno_first_uid` off the in-loop set (the `:6095` lever), flow deletes
  it, and the target's `addu $v0,$s0,$a1` stays. 144/37 without it.

## A 3-BYTE STRUCT COPY IS A BLOCK MOVE WHOSE SCRATCHES PRUNE THE PARAMETER'S PREFERENCE

func_8004E9EC landed 2026-10-31 at 33 of 33 words with NO `__asm__` device,
after three devices on the hand-written stores had reached 33 words / 5 DIFF
and 196k permuter candidates could not swap the last two registers. The
three `sb`s are ONE struct copy:

```c
typedef struct Unk4E9EC { u8 unk_00[3]; } Unk4E9EC;
...
*(Unk4E9EC *)&q[i] = *(Unk4E9EC *)D_80080B70;   /* extern u8 D_80080B70[] */
```

THE TELL IN THE LISTING: `lb $v0 / lb $v1 / lb $a0` then `sb $v0 / sb $v1 /
sb $a0`, all three loads before any store, the pieces in consecutive
call-clobbered registers from `$v0`, and the source address formed by a
single `addiu %lo` IMMEDIATELY before the loads with no insn between. That is
`output_block_move` (mips.c:2616): every piece is loaded first
(mips.c:2864-2901) and then every piece is stored (:2717), the byte case is
:2631-2639, and the pieces are the four `=&d` scratches of
`movstrsi_internal` (mips.md:3587-3598). `expand_block_move` (mips.c:2510)
copies both addresses to registers (:2350-2351) and emits that one insn for
any constant size up to `2*MAX_MOVE_BYTES` (:2361-2364). The hand-written
three assignments measured as three loads and three stores scheduled
freely, and needed a tied asm (D3 in the old park) to get the same order.

CAST FROM THE INCOMPLETE DECLARATION. The copy's SOURCE must be the split
(`high`/`lo_sum`) symbol: `extern u8 D_80080B70[]` cast to the struct type.
Declaring the extern AS the 3-byte struct makes it a small-data-sized symbol
(section 6's -G8 boundary) and the source address comes out as a two-word
`la` INSIDE the loop, both halves in `$a1`: 33 words / 15 DIFF. With the
incomplete declaration expand emits `(set hi (high D))` and
`(set p (lo_sum hi D))` (the `rtl` dump, insns 58-59); cse folds the lo_sum
INTO the block move's MEM address (find_best_addr, cse.c:2635; the
equal-ADDRESS_COST, higher-rtx-cost arm at :2719-2725), so no `p` pseudo
survives; loop.c hoists only the `high` (scan_loop's `n_times_set == 1` arm,
loop.c:804) out through both loops, which is the target's `lui $t1` at word
6; and the `addiu $a1,$t1,%lo(D)` is output_block_move's OWN output into
the fourth scratch -- no insn for it exists in the `sched2` or `dbr` dumps.
**ESTABLISHED 2026-11-02 from the real compiler's source.** This was recorded
as "WHY is not established", because the arm does not exist in the upstream
2.7.2.3 tree -- there the only pointer-temp arm is `CONSTANT_P (src_reg)`,
which a LO_SUM is not. The SN tree has it explicitly, in
`output_block_move`, and it says why:

    /* ??? We really shouldn't get any LO_SUM addresses here, because they
       are not offsettable, however, offsettable_address_p says they are
       offsettable.  I think this is a bug in offsettable_address_p.
       For expediency, we fix this by just loading the address into a
       register if we happen to get one.  */

    if (GET_CODE (src_reg) == LO_SUM)
      {
        src_reg = operands[ 3 + num_regs-- ];
        ...
              output_asm_insn ("addiu\t%0,%1,%%lo(%2)", xoperands);

So the `addiu` is a deliberate workaround for a bug they believed was in
`offsettable_address_p`, and -- the part that matters here -- `num_regs--`
means it CONSUMES one of the block move's scratches. That is the register
pressure this whole landing turns on, and it was invisible while the only
readable source was upstream's.

THE ALLOCATION IT BUYS, which no legal spelling of the stores could.
local-alloc allocates the four SCRATCHes (block_alloc,
local-alloc.c:1505-1510, alloc_qty_for_scratch :306) and rewrites them to
hard REGs in place, `PUT_CODE` then `REGNO` (:1549-1554): `$v0 $v1 $a0 $a1`, the `.lreg` dump already showing
`(clobber (reg:SI 5 a1))`. global_conflicts runs `note_stores (PATTERN,
mark_reg_clobber)` on every insn (global.c:718); the hard-reg arm of
mark_reg_clobber (:1422-1430) calls `record_one_conflict`, so every allocno
live across the inner loop -- the parameter `n`, `i`, `m`, the `high` and
the giv -- carries hard `2 3 4 5` in its conflicts (`81 conflicts: ... 2 3
4 5 29`). prune_preferences (:849-862) then strips 5 from `n`'s preference
sets. Order by allocno_compare (:587-608): giv, i, n*2, m, r, hi, n, q;
`r` (4 refs over 15) is allocated long before `n` (4 refs over 44, which
is simply its entry-born life in insns as `.greg` reports it) and
takes `$a1` in find_reg's pass 0 (:951-980) because `n`'s 5 was pruned
BEFORE `r`'s `regs_someone_prefers` merge (prune runs least-important first,
:846-848, merge :870-880). `hi` (4 refs over 36, 0.222) outranks `n` (0.18)
and takes `$t1`; `n` takes the next free register, `$t2`, and its copy is
word 1. `r` is dead across the inner loop (`83 conflicts: ... 2 29`), so the
`$a1` scratch never conflicts with it -- that is how the target's `r` and
its source pointer share `$a1`, and why `addiu $a1,$zero,1` is stolen into
the `beqz` delay slot.

NOT THE `update_equiv_regs` DOUBLING. An earlier draft of this lever
attributed `n`'s live_length of 44 to `reg_live_length[regno] *= 2`
(local-alloc.c:1105). That path cannot fire for a register-passed parameter:
it is gated on a REG_EQUIV note (:1058), `update_equiv_regs` adds one itself
only when the set's source is a MEM (:1051-1055), and `assign_parms` adds one
only when `entry_parm` is a MEM, i.e. a parameter passed on the STACK
(function.c:3979-3985). `n` arrives in `$a1`. The 44 is the plain insn count
over which flow found it live, which is why it exceeds the `high`'s 36 -- the
`high` is born in the outer preheader and `n` at the entry copy. Do not reach
for the doubling when predicting a register parameter's global priority.

THE NEGATIVE THAT POINTED HERE. "Give a lower-priority conflicting allocno a
preference for `$a1` so `n`'s first pass excludes it" cannot work:
prune_preferences AND_COMPLs the allocno's OWN full preferences out of the
merged set when the sizes are equal (:876-878), so a register `n` itself
prefers is never excluded from `n` by anyone else's preference. The only
legal route is hard 5 in `hard_reg_conflicts[n]`, and in a call-free
function the only thing that sets or clobbers `$a1` after the parameter copy
is a scratch -- which only a block move provides.

## A POINTER ASSIGNED AT THE LOOP TOP HOISTS ITS high, THE ARM'S high MATCHES IT, AND RELOAD REMATERIALISES BOTH IN $t0

func_800345B8 landed 2026-10-31 at 546 of 546 words (`unk_72A8`), from a
park at 21 DIFF whose last word was `beqz; nop; lui a0; j; addiu a0,a0` at
the CompMatrix matrix selection against the target's `beqz; lui t0 [slot];
j; addiu a0,t0`, with the same `lui t0 / addiu t0 / sw 0x1C(t0)` pointers
at the store site. One placement gives all of it:

```c
    Unk6CD30 *mb;
    Unk6CD30 *ma;
    for (;;)
    {
        mb = &D_8006CD10[0];     /* at the TOP of the loop body, nowhere else */
        ma = &D_8006A84C[0];
        ...
        D_8006CD30.unk_1C = z = p->unk_C4 << 2;
        mb->unk_1C = z;
        ma->unk_1C = z;
        ...
                if (D_8006A847[i] != 0) { m = &D_8006A84C[0]; CompMatrix(m, ...); }
                else                    { m = &D_8006CD10[0]; CompMatrix(m, ...); }
```

THE TELL IN THE LISTING: a `lui $t0, %hi(SYM)` immediately followed by an
`addiu $a0, $t0, %lo(SYM)` (the high in a DIFFERENT register from the
lo_sum's result, and that register the function's reload register), where a
block-local `&SYM` would give `lui $a0 / addiu $a0,$a0`; and the same SYM
stored through elsewhere in the loop as `lui $t0 / addiu $t0,$t0 / sw
off($t0)`. The two forms are one mechanism: a pseudo with REG_EQUIV
`(high SYM)` and one with REG_EQUIV `(symbol_ref SYM)`, both unallocated
and rematerialised by reload at every use.

WHY THE ASSIGNMENT MUST BE INSIDE THE LOOP: in the preheader (the park) the
pointer's `(set P (lo_sum H SYM))` is not a movable and H dies at once; the
arm's own `(set H2 (high SYM))` is block-local and gets $a0 by
qty_phys_sugg (local-alloc.c:1404, :1824-1834, :1472). At the loop top P
is a user variable set once and used only in its own block, so it is a
movable (scan_loop, loop.c:794-799); the lo_sum forces the high and lends
it its lifetime right there in the same block (`m->forces = m1;
m1->lifetime += m->lifetime;`, loop.c:1320-1321), while the next line
DOUBLES the high's own savings rather than adding the lo_sum's
(`m1->savings += m1->savings;`, :1223 -- plainly a typo in 2.7.2.3, but it
raises the same product either way). This is NOT the lifetime addition in
combine_movables at :1282-1283, which is the separate step below; and
with the use 29 luids away `threshold * savings * lifetime >= insn_count`
(loop.c:1730, threshold = `1 + n_non_fixed_regs` with calls, :532) hoists
the high and then P. combine_movables (loop.c:1331-1384) chains the arm's
equal-valued high to the hoisted one and move_movables replaces its
register and deletes the insn (loop.c:2044-2063). Both pseudos now cross
the whole loop with two or three refs, come last in global.c's order, find
every callee-saved register taken, and are left to reload with their
equivalences (HIGH is CONSTANT_P, rtl.h:207; LEGITIMATE_CONSTANT_P is true
for it on MIPS, mips.h:2607). order_regs_for_reload puts the call-used
register with no pseudo uses first (reload1.c:3919-3926), hence $t0 both
times; the store's `la t0` is the movsi expander with `tem = operands[0]`,
the arm's is a plain reload of `(high SYM)` into the `low` insn's operand.
The hoisted inits are deleted by reload (reload1.c:2062-2066), so the
preheader keeps no trace. The `lui t0` then fills the `beqz` slot because
$t0 is dead at the branch target, where the block-local `lui a0` did not.

A SYMBOL STORED TO DIRECTLY stays block-local: D_8006CD30's arm is
`lui a0 / addiu a0,a0` and its store `lui v1 / sw %lo(v1)`, and the dump
says why (`Insn 385 ... done move-insn matches 95`, 95 `not desirable`).

DO NOT use the pointer locals in the arms: `m = ma;` and `CompMatrix(ma,
...)` both ICE cc1psx ("abnormal program termination"). The culprit is
jump2 (toplev.c:3690), whose `if (c) a0 = A; else a0 = B;` rewrite copies
the `(set a0 (symbol_ref))` that only reload's constraint check had
accepted; the fresh copy is unrecognizable (insn 1364 in the .jump2 dump).

Measured: declarations (park) 547 words / 411 DIFF; loop bottom 547 /
501; loop top with the single CompMatrix 546 / 17; loop top with three
CompMatrix arms 546 / 10; plus the two levers below, MATCH.

DESTINATION BEFORE THE SHIFT. `D_8006CD30.unk_1C = z = p->unk_C4 << 2;`
(not `z = ...; D_8006CD30.unk_1C = z;`) is worth 8 words: expand_assignment
expands the destination first (expr.c:2938, store_expr :2661), so the
store's `(high)` precedes z's shift in the chain; sched1 is a BACKWARD list
scheduler, launches both when the store is scheduled (sched.c:2604-2658,
adjust_priority :2507-2545) and emits the higher LUID last
(rank_for_schedule, sched.c:2472), so the order becomes `lui / sll / sw`,
the high's quantity lives 4 half-insns instead of 2, its qty_compare_1
priority (local-alloc.c:1705-1722) drops from 16 to 8 under z's 14.4, and z
takes $v0 while the high gets $v1 -- after which sched2 floats the `lui v1`
to the top of the block exactly as the target has it.

A STORE AND A REGISTER COPY OF THE SAME REGISTER: `sh v0 / addu s7,v0` is
NOT reachable from `p->unk_BC = t0x; x = t0x;`. Post-reload neither insn
depends on the other, both become ready when the `sll` that overwrites $v0
is scheduled, they tie on priority, and schedule_select (sched.c:2663-2707)
puts the store first in the group because a store has a positive
potential_hazard (sched.c:1349-1375) and an ALU insn none; picked first in
the backward pass means emitted LAST: `move / sh`, 2 DIFF forever. The
landed body uses an empty `__asm__ __volatile__("")` between them, which
sched_analyze_2 treats as using and setting everything (sched.c:1973-2000),
making the copy a successor of the store. It must sit BELOW y's copy and
store or it pins y's spill store too (9 DIFF). Every tied-asm spelling
(`"+r"(t0x)`, `"=r"(x) : "0"(t0x)`) is re-tied to $s7 by regmove and reload
copies $v0 to $s7 before it: back to 2 DIFF. The device is documented at
the site in csrc/unk_72A8.c. WHY the original source produced that
dependence is NOT established; no C spelling found does.

## THE SWITCH INDEX'S STATEMENT POSITION IS A sched1 TIE-BREAK, AND THE TIE-BREAK IS THE WHOLE mfhi/mflo REGISTER BLOCK

func_8004CECC (unk_1C540), third pass 2026-10-31: `idx = h >> 8;` written
between `h %= 1536;` and `f = h & 0xFF;` (switching on `idx`) instead of
`switch (h >> 8)` at the switch took the function from 1 EXTRA `srl` + 17
register-only rows to zero rows in the colour block (101 of 102 words, the
one word being unrelated). The index computation is one instruction either
way; only its LUID moved.

THE TELL IN THE LISTING: the switch index's `srl` sits in a stall slot
between two rounding chains (`subu a1,v0,a1 / srl t0,t2,8 / addu v0,t6,v1`),
and every `mfhi`/`mflo` temporary after it is one or two register numbers
off from yours.

WHY: sched1 is a backward list scheduler (`schedule_block` sched.c:3205).
Insns launched into the ready list all tie at LAUNCH_PRIORITY and
`rank_for_schedule` (sched.c:2429-2472) breaks the tie by INSN_LUID -- the
original insn order -- at :2428, largest first, i.e. the insn written last
is placed last. Written at the switch, the `srl` outranks every rounding
chain at T-3 and lands just before the `sltiu`; written between `h %=` and
`f =`, its LUID falls between p's chain and q's, so it is placed after p and
before q (the `.sched` trace shows the pick: `ready list at T-11: 83 66 132,
now 83`). That position puts the index pseudo in conflict with q's numerator
($v1), t's numerator ($a0), p, val, q and both high-word pseudos, so
global-alloc gives it $t0; t-high then cannot have $t0, pass 0 of `find_reg`
(global.c:907; :952 skips registers not yet in regs_used_so_far) finds
nothing and pass 1 hands it the first fresh register $t3; p-high conflicts
with it and takes $t4; reload's spill register, the lowest UNUSED hard reg
(`order_regs_for_reload` reload1.c:3810, unused-first at :3692), moves from
$t4 to $t5 (`.greg`: `Spilling reg 13`); and the HI_REG/LO_REG-preferring
mult results that global-alloc had put in $hi/$lo and reload spilled out
(reload1.c:3644, :3497 -> `retry_global_alloc` global.c:1213, with the spill
regs and the explicitly-used $v0/$a0-$a3 forbidden, reload1.c:807/:3651)
are retried into $t3 and $t6 instead of $t5. Seventeen register rows, one
statement position. Read the `.greg` lines `Spilling reg N` and `Register N
now in M` before touching anything else when the mfhi/mflo temps are off.

## A REG-REG COPY WHOSE DESTINATION ALREADY HOLDS THE SOURCE IS DELETED BY jump2 -- THE PASS IS IN THE TREE, AND ITS THREE EXITS ARE THE ONLY WAYS TO KEEP THE COPY

func_8004CECC's last word is the grey arm's `val = v` (`addu a2,v1,zero`
in the target's bnez slot) after the entry copy `addu v1,a2,zero`. It is
present in `.sched2` and gone in `.jump2`: toplev.c:3690 runs `jump_optimize
(insns, 1, 1, 0)` after sched2 with noop_moves=1, and jump.c:477-516 deletes
`(set (reg D) (reg S))` when `find_equiv_reg (NULL, insn, 0, S, NULL, D,
mode)` (reload.c:5554) finds an earlier insn copying between the two
registers. The scan back (:5413-5417) stops only at a CODE_LABEL or the
start of the function; the copy survives only if the found insn carries
REG_UNUSED on the value (:5503), the modes differ (:5514), or an insn between
them SETs or CLOBBERs either register (:5578-5641). cc1psx's copy differs
from 2.7.2.3 in one detail: the earlier insn's REG_DEAD is removed only when
the copy IS deleted (2.7.2.3 jump.c:499-506 removes it unconditionally;
measured on a surviving copy's `.jump2`).

The corpus obeys these rules. A scan of asm/ for `move A,B .. move B,A` with
neither register written between finds 40 survivors, every one explained: a
call between (func_800997FC, func_8009DF84: `jal; [s0 = a0]; a0 = s0`), a
label between -- a loop head whose first insn reorg copied into the
back-edge slot and moved the label past (func_800D67B0, func_8008C984:
`a0 = s0; .L: ...; j .L; [a0 = s0]`) -- or a cross-jump tail (func_800A0E6C).
`addu s0,a0; sw; addu a0,s0` in a prologue is NOT such a survivor: f1/f2
test functions compiled here lose the arg copy exactly as FSF says.

What does NOT keep the copy, measured on func_8004CECC: a block-local copy
in the grey arm (cse propagates it into the stores: 99 words), `val = v;
val = v;` or `val = 0; val = v;` before it (cse/flow remove the first), an
asm output on `val` before it (flow deletes the dead asm), a tied asm on `v`
before it (reload ties the asm onto $a2 and jump2 deletes the input reload
instead), hoisting `val = v` above the if (cse canonicalises the longer-lived
register, make_regs_eqv cse.c:838 / canon_reg :2532, and rewrites the colour
arm's `v & 0xFF` as `val & 0xFF`; and jump2 deletes the hoisted copy too).
What DOES keep it: an asm that sets `v` as the FIRST statement (`__asm__(""
: "=r"(v) : "0"(v))`, a SET of $v1 between the two copies) -- but see the
next lever for why that still misses the target. WHY the target's copy
survived is not established; it needs RTL between the two copies that this
source does not produce.

## THE DELAY SLOT OF AN ENTRY BRANCH TAKES THE NEAREST ELIGIBLE INSN BEFORE IT -- NOT "THE FALL-THROUGH"

The second pass on func_8004CECC recorded "cc1psx fills an entry branch's
slot from the fall-through, not from the parameter copies" from a survey of
ten target functions. The survey's fact is right and its reading is wrong.
`fill_simple_delay_slots`' back-scan (reorg.c:3079-3130) walks back from the
branch and takes the FIRST insn that neither references what the skipped
insns set nor sets what they or the branch need; `sll v0,a1,16` is skipped
(it sets the branch's register) and `t1 = a3` is taken. func_8004E9EC's
landed source shows the same rule: its slot holds `addu a3,a1,zero` (`r =
0`), the insn nearest its branch, which happens not to be a parameter copy.
The scan stops at a label, a jump, a filled SEQUENCE or ANY asm insn
(`stop_search_p` reorg.c:683-709) -- an empty `__asm__("" :: "r"(x))` as the
first statement stops it and leaves the parameter copies where they are.
The forward scan that follows (:2971-3050) never takes an insn for a
conditional jump (it requires `target == 0`).

Only then does `fill_eager_delay_slots` (:3632; order :3690-3717) run. With
no loop notes and equal `rare_destination`s, an NE branch is predicted taken
(`mostly_true_jump` :1335) and the TARGET thread is tried first: its first
insn goes in the slot if it sets nothing live at the fall-through
(`fill_slots_from_thread` :3257, the test at :3375). Liveness is
`mark_target_live_regs` (:2441): hard-register REG_DEADs are only pending
until a label (:2624, :2649), and the forward pass from the target (:2672)
drops registers set before they are used. So on func_8004CECC: grey copy
present and the back-scan stopped -> the colour arm's `andi a2,v1,0xFF` is
hoisted into the slot and the label moved past it (102 words / 7 DIFF);
grey copy deleted and the back-scan stopped -> `andi` refused ($a2 is read by
