the grey stores), `sb` refused (memory), slot = nop (102 / 1, the park body).
A fall-through insn lands in the slot only when the target thread yields
nothing. The target's `addu a2,v1,zero` in its slot was therefore the
nearest eligible insn BEFORE the branch: the copy stood in the entry block.

## A RELOAD EMITTED AHEAD OF A BLOCK HEAD IS NEVER SCHEDULED -- and three more facts that landed func_8004B954

func_8004B954 (unk_1C540, 290 words) landed 2026-10-31 from a park at 292 words
/ 247 DIFF whose `advise.py` reading was 2 words and 3 register rows. Four
independent facts, each measured on its own:

**1. jump2 hoists a one-insn then-arm over its branch, and reorg's back-scan
then takes THAT insn, not your copy.** Written `if (A) n = 0x40; else if (B)
n = 0x20; else n = 0x10;`, the sched2 stream is `beq -> L; s5 = 64; j JOIN;
L: ...`. The jump2 dump (the second `jump_optimize`, toplev.c:3688-3690, after
sched2) shows a fresh copy of `s5 = 64` directly in front of the branch, the
branch inverted to `ne -> JOIN`, and the `j`, its barrier and `L` gone (insn
790 with INSN_CODE -1; the originals are unlinked rather than left as
NOTE_INSN_DELETED, which is what jump.c's `delete_insn` does). The back-scan of
`fill_simple_delay_slots` (reorg.c:3079-3130) takes the nearest eligible insn
walking back from the branch, which is now that copy, so a `g = q` sitting
four insns from the top is never reached whatever its placement -- the park's
six placements were all measuring this. The listing has the then-arm LAST
(`bnez -> addiu s5,0x40` placed just before the join), the shape of
`if (A == 0) { if (B) n = 0x20; else n = 0x10; } else n = 0x40;`: a multi-insn
then-arm with the single-insn arm falling into the join leaves nothing to
hoist, the back-scan reaches `g = q`, and the `j` costs its word. 292 -> 293
words but 247 -> 162 DIFF with the first three branch spans exact. WHY the
hoist happens is not established in upstream jump.c: the only post-reload site
that emits a copy is line 811 (the `if (...) x = a; else x = b;` rewrite,
jump.c:817-860) and its last condition -- `reallabelprev == temp2` or a
simplejump right after `x = b` -- fails on this stream; the `bp` dump is
pre-reload so it is not that pass either.

**2. An input reload emitted ahead of a basic-block head is outside the
scheduled region.** With `r += 0xC;` as the first statement of the
`mode != 0` arm, `basic_block_head` is insn 326 `t0 = t0 + 12` and reload emits
the input reload `lw t0,0x5C(sp)` (insn 701) in front of it. reload1.c only
reads `basic_block_head` (lines 904 and 3786; it never assigns it) and
`schedule_block` begins at that head (sched.c:3220-3221), so the `lw` is never
scheduled and its load-delay nop can never be filled -- the listing has the
`lw a1,0x50(sp)` argument reload in it. Give the block a first statement that
needs no input reload: `o = g + 0xC;` is only used inside the arm, and moved
there it puts `s0 = s3 + 12` at the head with the reload inside the block.
293 -> 292, one nop.

**3. A fixed-address load escapes stores through a STRUCT pointer, not through
a cast pointer.** `true_dependence` (sched.c:835-857) returns no dependence
when one MEM is in-struct with a varying address and the other is non-struct
with a fixed address (section 5 above has the rule). In both loops
`*(s32 *) v` is `(mem (plus fp 16))`: fixed and non-struct. The stores
`*(s32 *)(g + 0x10)` are non-struct too, so sched1 gave the `v` load AND the
`q + 0x14` load LOG_LINKS to every preceding store through `g` (insns 387 and
392 each list 379, 384, 389): the two load/store pairs are serialised, the
temporaries never overlap, local-alloc hands both `v0`, and sched2 cannot
interleave them -- one nop per loop, and the `sw v0` where the listing has
`sw v1` is the same fact. As struct member stores (`((Unk4B954W7 *) g)->w4 =
*(s32 *) v;`, local word-record typedefs) the `v` load lifts. The `q + 0x14`
load is varying and stays dependent on the `g` stores whatever its type, so the
listing's `lw v1,0x14(s4)` BEFORE `lw v0,0x10(sp)` needs the `q`-copy statement
written before the `v` statement -- the park's "swapping the two stores is
inert" was true only without the struct type. Both loops swapped and typed:
292 -> 290 words, 131 -> 17 DIFF, every register row gone. Typed but in the
park's order: 288 words, 8 register rows (wrong direction).

**4. `code = 1;` before the pointer copies.** Block 0 is priority 1
throughout; sched1 picked `code = 1` (insn 32) over `g = q` (26) on the
priority-1 tie at T-11, which `rank_for_schedule` decides by class against the
last scheduled insn and then INSN_LUID (sched.c:2429-2472), and that lands its
spill store `sw t0,0x24(sp)` after the first two `lh`, where the listing has it
before them with `li t0,1` third in the function. With `code = 1;` written
first, or second (after `q = p`), both rows close: 17 -> MATCH. Written third
(`q = p; g = q; code = 1; e = q;`) it is still 17. WHY the `li` then lands
exactly third is not established; the measured fact is the statement order.

Also: the unit's prototype declares the sixth parameter `s32` while the body
stores through it, so the definition is `func_8004B954w(...) __asm__
("func_8004B954")` with `s32 *out`, per the lever "A narrow parameter a CALLER must not see: define under an `__asm__` alias".

## loop.c's HOIST THRESHOLD DECAYS BY 3 PER MOVE AND insn_count DOUBLES PER INNER-LOOP HOIST -- A lo_sum's LIFETIME IS THE LEVER, AND A goto LOOP IS NO LOOP AT ALL

func_8005B4D0 (unk_2CDC0), the SPU voice setup: 376 of 376 words with a
spilled `prog` at 0x64, 100 register-only rows and eleven `lui vN` where the
listing has `addiu vN,zero`. 333 -> 76 DIFF, every row from the .loop/.greg
dumps; nothing on the park's REJECTED list was re-adopted.

**1. The hoist decision, with its numbers.** move_movables moves an
invariant when `threshold * savings * m->lifetime >= insn_count`
(loop.c:1730). threshold = `(loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (1 + n_non_fixed_regs)`
(loop.c:631) = 29 in a loop that holds a call (28 non-fixed regs:
regclass.c:392-399 over mips.h FIXED_REGISTERS :1186-1193, FP file fixed by
CONDITIONAL_REGISTER_USAGE :522-534); it is decremented by 3 per MOVABLE
moved, once per arm rather than per insn (loop.c:1818, :1904);
and insn_count is doubled, permanently for the rest of the loop, each time a
movable that was already moved out of an inner loop is examined
(loop.c:1708-1710 -- the dump prints "halved", the code multiplies).
combine_movables (:1232-1285) sums rtx-equal movables'
lifetimes and savings into the first; force_movables (:1193-1223) adds a
lo_sum's lifetime to its high (:1222) and doubles the high's savings (:1223,
the 2.7.2.3 `m1->savings += m1->savings` typo). The two dumps
reconcile exactly: `330 (life 8) savings 8` fails at 8*64 = 512 < 564 (282
insns, one doubling); `348 (life 28) savings 8` passes at 23*224 = 5152
against 283*16 = 4528. That 624 was the whole register budget: the hoisted
D_80086A40 lo_sum took $fp and `prog` went to the stack.

**2. The lifetime is in the spelling.** `D_80086A40[(s16) bank].f` forces
the array's address before the offset (expr.c's ARRAY_REF path), so the
lo_sum spans the sign-extension and the index: life 7 per site, 28 for four
matched sites. `(D_80086A40 + bank)->f` is an INDIRECT_REF of a PLUS_EXPR,
expanded index first with the symbol forced last: life 1. Three sites in
pointer form bring the group to life 20 (3680 < 4528, "not desirable"), prog
gets $fp and the FRAME table empties. Declaring `bank` s16 does the same for
the sign-extension (four `(sign_extend (reg:HI))` pairs, life 12: not
hoisted, re-extended per use as the listing does) and gives the listing's
`addu s5,a0,zero` copy with `sll v1,a0,16` reading the shift temp.

**3. A goto loop has no LOOP_BEG/END notes and loop.c never sees it.** The
listing hoists `high(D_80073734)` into $s0 out of one loop and
`D_80073734[0]-1` out of the other; the park's goto spellings reload both
every iteration, which is what the eleven `lui`-for-`addiu` rows were. As
`while (c) {..}` a loop whose test holds a call matches exactly; one whose
test is a load is ROTATED by expand_end_loop (stmt.c:2274-2365, scan forward
from after the start label, stop at CALL_INSN/CODE_LABEL/BLOCK notes
(:2276-2282) or 30 insns past a found test (:2287-2288), move up to the last
conditional exit). Check first whether rotation runs at all: it is gated off
entirely when the body's last insn is already a conditional jump (:2264-2269,
on `insn = get_last_insn ()` at :2244). `while (1) { if (c == 0) break; .. }` is the one unrotated
spelling, because expand_exit_loop_if_false (stmt.c:2433-2468) with a
constant-true condition emits `jump label; jump end; label:` (do_jump,
expr.c:10153-10157) and the scan rotates only that stub; `for (;;)` and
`do..while (1)` rotate on the first `break`. An increment the listing has in
the back-edge delay slot is written BEFORE the exit test (it executes on the
exit path either way).

**4. Smaller facts that landed words.** `sum += *w++; i++;` put the counter
increment in the load delay (the scheduler is a reverse list scheduler --
sched.c:3846-3850, "the first insn scheduled becomes the new tail"; design
note :58 -- and rank_for_schedule :2385-2428 ends on INSN_LUID).
true_dependence (sched.c:835-857) makes every QI load depend on every
preceding store through another pointer, so a load the listing shows above a
run of stores precedes them in source and its own store sinks to just before
the next load. The callee's arity decides the `jal` delay slot: one argument
puts `addiu a0,sp,0x10` there (76 / 43 register rows against 133 / 65 with
three). The park's free reference pair on `i` is worth 35 DIFF for a reason
the dumps show: it lifts `i` from 18 to 22 references, which orders it ahead
of the cursor in global's allocation, keeps $t0 for `i` and leaves $t1 as the
spill register; without it reload spills $t0.

Not established: the listing's three D_80085458 sites have a high with no
register (`lui t1`) feeding a local lo_sum (`addiu v1,t1,lo`) -- a local
pseudo that local-alloc put in $t1 and reload evicted (retry_global_alloc
retries only pseudos with an allocno), i.e. register pressure -- and all four
D_80086A40 sites in array-form order without the hoist. See the park.

## A QImode COPY OF AN SImode REGISTER IS THE SAME `addu` BUT NOT THE SAME NO-OP -- a one-byte struct is how jump2 keeps the copy, and a dead write is how cse keeps the reads

This is the fourth exit of the lever two above, and it landed func_8004CECC --
byte-identical, all three containers `cmp` identical, 2026-11-01. The unit's
`.rodata` grew 0x20 -> 0x38 with the compiled table, which put two separated
runs in one object and took a sixth cut of the carved unit (at func_800517CC,
giving `csrc/unk_24FCC.c`) to place; see docs/open-matching-problems.md. The target's `addu a2,v1,zero`
in the bnez slot is `val = v` with `val` a ONE-BYTE STRUCT:

* **Why jump2 keeps it.** jump.c:487-489 calls `find_equiv_reg` with `mode
  = GET_MODE (SET_SRC (body))` and :461-463 deletes only when `GET_MODE
  (tem) == GET_MODE (SET_DEST (body))`; inside, reload.c:5720 `if (GET_MODE
  (value) != mode) return 0;` rejects the SImode entry copy `(set (reg:SI
  3) (reg:SI 6))` as the equivalent of a QImode copy. `(set (reg:QI 6)
  (subreg:QI (reg:SI 3) 0))` prints as the identical `addu a2,v1,zero`
  (movqi reg-reg) and survives in `.jump2`.
* **How C produces a QImode reg-reg copy** when PROMOTE_MODE makes every
  scalar local SImode: expand_decl (stmt.c:3448-3455) has no aggregate
  exclusion and promote_mode leaves a RECORD_TYPE alone, so `struct { u8 b;
  } val;` is `(reg/v:QI 85)`; `val.b = v` is store_bit_field's lsb-aligned
  branch (expmed.c:287-307, `emit_move_insn (op0, gen_lowpart (QImode,
  v))`), i.e. `(set (reg/v:QI 85) (subreg:QI (reg/v:SI 83) 0))`, and the
  reads `val.b` are `(reg/v:QI 85)` straight into the `sb`s. `u8 val` does
  NOT do this: the promoted local makes the copy a `zero_extend` (andi).
* **Where it stands.** Hoisted above the `if`: sched2 orders the entry
  `t2=a0; v1=a2; t1=a3; [copy]; sll; bne` and the back-scan (reorg.c:
  2900-2951) takes the copy as the nearest eligible insn. In the grey arm it
  survives jump2 just the same but `t1 = a3` takes the slot (102 / 3).
* **What it costs, and the dead write that pays it.** cse propagates the
  subreg into the three grey stores and the copy dies (99 words, `v` left in
  $a2 -- the park's "one-byte struct copy" dead end, now explained). It would
  not in 2.7.2.3: COST (cse.c:481-486) is 1 for a pseudo against `rtx_cost`'s
  SUBREG `return 2` (cse.c:747-753, taken because MODES_TIEABLE_P holds for
  QI/SI) doubled to 4, `insert` (:1268-1271) would lead the class
  with the REG, and the trial loop (`while (1)` :6767; `src` and `src_folded`
  zeroed at :6703/:6706 because both are in the class) takes the class head.
  cc1psx takes the SUBREG: its cost or its class order differs here, and
  WHICH is not established (the cygnus-97 line's notreg_cost prices a lowpart
  subreg of a pseudo at 1, equal, which under FSF's `insert` still leads
  with the REG). The lever is the validity test in front of the loop, "Skip
  invalid entries" :6772-6774 via exp_equiv_p's REG case (:2110-2131,
  `reg_in_table != reg_tick` at :2129): a DEAD `v = 0;` at the head of the
  grey arm bumps v's reg_tick after the equivalence was recorded, the subreg
  entry is skipped, the stores keep `val`, and flow deletes the write (.flow:
  NOTE_INSN_DELETED). The colour arm is untouched because the equivalence is
  between `val` and the subreg EXPRESSION, not between the two registers, so
  `v & 0xFF` still reads P_v; and `val.b = vv` is `(set (reg:QI 85)
  (subreg:QI (reg:SI 91)))`, which set_preference reads through the SUBREG
  as a copy from vv's hard $a2 (.greg "85 preferences: 6", "85 in 6").
* The entry-asm device of the previous pass is gone (with or without it:
  MATCH); the colour arm's tied asm is still worth the function (without it
  101 / 101).

## THE SCAN LOOP WRITTEN AS THE SIBLING'S INNER-LOOP GIV KEEPS ITS high OUT OF THE OUTER MERGE, A DEAD STORE AT THE BODY TOP MOVES THE MERGED high BEFORE THE DOUBLINGS, AND A MATCHED lo_sum IS NEVER MOVED ON ITS OWN

func_8005B4D0 (unk_2CDC0), the SPU note-on and the project's last function:
76 -> MATCH, `make check` byte-identical. The park's four open items were
one mechanism seen from four sides, and the listing's "three register-less
highs in $t1 feeding local lo_sums, a local high in $v0 at the scan site"
is what every piece follows from.

**1. Where the three `lui t1` come from.** A pseudo with no hard register
whose only set is `(high sym)` is rematerialised by reload at every use
(reload1.c:653-670 take the REG_EQUIV constant; rtl.h:207-210 CONSTANT_P
includes HIGH), in the spill register -- and `lui t1` with `addiu v1,t1,%lo`
writing a DIFFERENT register is the signature of a register-less high with a
local lo_sum, not of a reloaded symbol (that is `lui t1; addiu t1,t1,%lo`,
the park's shape: mips' movsi expander under reload_in_progress writes both
halves into operand 0). The park's "local alloc put it in $t1 and reload
evicted it" cannot be right: order_regs_for_reload (reload1.c:3810-3916)
puts zero-use call-used registers first in regno order, so a $t1 holding
pseudos would have lost to $t2 -- the dumps that do spill $t1 here are the
ones where $t1 holds nothing (`Register 111 now in 9` is a LO eviction, not
a $t1 one). So the high is a global pseudo crossing the calls with every
callee-saved register taken: a loop-hoisted one.

**2. Why the scan site's high is not in that merge.** combine_movables
(loop.c:1343-1382) merges every `(high D_80085458)` movable of the loop into
the FIRST one in insn order, and move_movables decides once for the head;
with `r = D_80085458` before the scan loop that head is the scan site and
the scan site rematerialises with the rest (366 with the dead store of item
3, `lui t1` at the scan). The only exclusion that exists is loop.c:785:
a register "made by loop-optimization for an inner loop" (regno >=
max_reg_before_loop) is skipped. The sibling unit's idiom -- the cursor
computed INSIDE the loop, `r = D_80085458 + ch * 0x78` in a do/while with
the `ch = -1` after it -- hoists the lo_sum out of the scan loop and
regenerates it through emit_move_insn with a FRESH high (loop.c:1801-1808),
which the outer loop never sees; the giv then reduces to the listing's
`addiu a0,v0,%lo` / `addiu a0,a0,0x78` word for word (while(1)/break keeps
the back-branch inside the loop and back_branch_in_range_p (unroll.c:2155-
2107) makes every DEST_REG giv non-replaceable, which is the +2 words of the
first attempt). Per-site: the three v-pointer lo_sums `pN = D_80085458` MATCH
that regenerated lo_sum (.loop "regno 100 (life 4), done move-insn matches
889"), the head fails its own test as "halved since already moved", and a
matched movable is skipped at loop.c:1684 (`!m->done`) -- so clause 3
(loop.c:1731-1732) never runs for them and they stay local. No multiply-set
trick is needed; a compiler temp matches the same way.

**3. Getting the merged head hoisted at all.** With the scan high excluded,
the head is site 1's high, evaluated after the busy loop's two moves (3 off
the threshold each, loop.c:1818) and four doublings (:1609-1611): 23*6*15 =
2070 < 4480, not moved, `lui v0` everywhere (18 DIFF). A dead
`v = D_80085458` at the top of the loop body puts a `(high D_80085458)`
first in insn order, so it is tested before any decay or doubling, at
threshold 29 and insn_count 280; it moves, the three site highs are deleted
into it, and flow deletes the store. (The moved/not-moved verdicts here are
read off the `.loop` dump; only the products are arithmetic.)

**n_non_fixed_regs is 28 and move_movables' threshold is 29 in a loop
holding a call, as the lever above says.** An earlier draft of this lever
read 30 and 31 out of the scan loop's giv line `-124 vs 16`, which is
`lifetime 1 * threshold 62 * benefit -2` against insn_count 16 -- but 62 is
the STRENGTH-REDUCTION threshold, and that one is
`(loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (3 + n_non_fixed_regs)` (loop.c:3359, printed at
:3826-3830), not move_movables' `1 +` at :532. Two different formulas, three
apart: 62 = 2 * (3 + 28) in a call-free loop. The giv line is therefore a
second, independent witness FOR 28 -- and a better one than the array count,
because it also settles that cc1psx fixes the FP file (28 = 25 free of
$0..$31 plus the three MD registers; with the FP file free it would be 60). The hoisted high
has 3 refs against prog's 11 and loses $fp on floor_log2(refs)*refs/length
(global.c:587-608) exactly as the listing wants; with the scan site merged
it would have 4 refs and TAKE $fp (V3c: prog spilled).

**4. The prologue is the late `bank` copy, and the temp must be fresh.**
`bs = D_80086A40[(s16) ab].unk_04; bank = ab;` with `ab = a >> 8` as its own
earlier statement: the copy's LUID is high so sched1 places it at the
bottom (adjust_priority, sched.c:2551-2593, raises a birthing insn's
priority -- but only from the one call at :2592-2603, reached when
scheduling a successor satisfies that insn's LAST requirement, so an insn
already on the ready list never gets the boost), tmp stays live across the
sign-extension, the extension takes $v1, the D_80086A40 lo_sum $a1, `i`
(born at the top, conflicting with $a1-$a3 through the live argument
registers) $t0, and the b spill store rides the anti-dependence on `lui
a1`. The shift temp must be a single-set variable: `x`, set again by the
clamps, fails birthing_insn_p's `reg_n_sets == 1`, floats to the block top
ahead of `andi`, and takes $t0 (83 DIFF). The array form at the prologue
site puts the symbol's LUID before the extension's, which is the listing's
`lui a1; addiu a1; sw v0; sll v1; sra v1` order.

**5. Allocation is in the variable set.** One function-scope `v` is a
global allocno and conflicts with $v0/$v1/$a0 across all three ranges; the
listing's $v0/$a1/$v0 is three block-local pseudos (v, v2, v3), likewise
the adsr temps (t, t2: $a0 then $v1) and the volume.right load (t3: $v0).
A product into a LO-preferring temp is spilled out of $lo and retried with
`forbidden_regs = bad_spill_regs` (reload1.c:807, :3497), which holds the
explicitly-used argument registers, so `rv * ps` can only reach $a1 through
a GR-preferring variable that is dead there: `l = rv * ps`. `sum = sum * 8`
and `l = l * unk_18 >> 7` are the in-place `sll a1,a1,3` / `sra a1,t0,7`.
Loading volume.right into `t3` BEFORE `attr.note = b` is what lets the load
precede the note's reload-and-store (a load after a store that may alias is
a dependence, sched.c:835-857), with the right store after both.

Not established: why the original had a `(high D_80085458)` ahead of the
busy loop. The dead store reproduces the RTL; what statement produced it in
the source is a guess.

## AN ARGUMENT REGISTER SET IN A `jal`'s DELAY SLOT IS THAT CALL'S LIVE ARGUMENT -- AND THE SAME INSN IN EVERY PREDECESSOR'S SLOT IS A SUCCESSOR BLOCK'S FIRST INSN

Two separate readings of a delay slot, both measured on
`func_80025398` (ovl_main_80020000, 53 words):

**A `jal`'s delay slot executes before the callee.** An `a`-register write
there is therefore not dead code to be explained away by scheduling -- it is
how that argument is passed. The listing has

    13  0C0094D6  jal   func_80025358
    14  3C048001  lui   $a0, 0x8001

so the first argument is `0x80010000`, i.e. the function's base pointer. The
park had read word 14 as a dead constant materialisation that reorg happened
to park next to the call, and spelled the call `func_80025358(p - 8, p[10])`;
the argument is `(s32 *)b`.

**The same insn in both predecessors' branch slots belongs to the block they
branch TO.** Both guards here carry an identical `addiu $a0, $s2, -0x20`:

    10  10400019  beqz  $v0, .L80025428
    11  2644FFE0  addiu $a0, $s2, -0x20
    ...
    18  10400011  beqz  $v0, .L80025428
    19  2644FFE0  addiu $a0, $s2, -0x20

and the block at `.L80025428` starts with `lui $v0, %hi(...)`, not with the
`addiu`. That is the fail block's own `func_800230F4((s32)(p - 8))` argument,
hoisted into every predecessor's slot and deleted from the block -- which
reorg can only do when *every* predecessor carries it. Read in reverse: an
identical insn in two slots targeting one label is evidence about the
successor's first statement, not about either predecessor.

Cost of the misreading: exactly one word. Twelve spellings measured at
53 words / 1 DIFF (the constant in a local, re-assigned after the call, a
second local, inline at all three uses; `(s32)p - 0x20` and `(u8 *)p - 0x20`
at the fail site, the call site and both), plus `p - 8` hoisted into a local
at 54 words / 50 DIFF. Changing the one argument to `b`: MATCH.

## CROSS-JUMPING RUNS AFTER sched2 AND BEFORE reorg, AND ONE MATCHING INSN IS ENOUGH -- SO AN EMPTY `__asm__` AT A BLOCK'S END IS A ONE-WORD LEVER

Measured on `func_800210F0` (ovl_main_80020000, 75 words).

The pass order matters and is checkable in the tree at
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/toplev.c`: `schedule_insns` (sched2) at 3117,
`jump_optimize (insns, 1, 1, 0)` -- the one call with `cross_jump` nonzero --
at 3142, `dbr_schedule` at 3167. So cross-jumping sees the *final* instruction
order, already register-allocated and already scheduled, and only delay slots
come after it. Two consequences:

**You cannot out-schedule a cross-jump.** sched2 has already run, so there is
no later pass to restore an order that the merge destroyed. In this function
the `st == 3` body ends `u[0] = 1; D_800287C8 = 0;` and the `st == 1` body ends
`r = 1; D_800287C8 = 0;`; the two trailing stores are the identical word
`ACA087C8`, and the st==1 body's `j out` is retargeted onto the st==3 body's
copy. reorg then fills that jump's slot with the preceding `addiu $s1, 1`
instead of the store, and the function is 74 words. Reordering the st==1 tail
to `D_800287C8 = 0; r = 1;` does break the merge -- back to 75 words -- but
sched2 does not swap the pair back: two leaf stores tie on priority (neither
has an in-block successor) and the tie breaks to source order, so the slot gets
`addiu $s1, 1` again and the block comes out `sw; j; addiu` instead of
`addiu; j; sw`. 75 words, 2 DIFF. That the scheduler *is* running is visible in
the same block: `addiu $v0, 1` is hoisted above the `D_800287C8` store because
it has a successor (`sw $v0, 0($a0)`) and so a longer chain.

**One matching insn is enough.** For an unconditional jump, `jump.c:2188`
calls `find_cross_jump (insn, JUMP_LABEL (insn), 1, ...)` -- `minimum` is 1, so
a single identical insn before the jump and before the label merges them. (It
is 2 for a conditional jump, for a second jump to the same label, and for a
`RETURN`.) There is no profitability test to lose, and nothing to tune from the
C side.

What is left is the match test itself. `find_cross_jump` walks `i1` back with
`prev_nonnote_insn` and breaks before matching anything if
`GET_CODE (p1) != GET_CODE (p2)`. An empty `__asm__ volatile("")` has pattern
`ASM_INPUT`, not `SET`, so one at the end of the st==3 body makes the compare
fail on the first pair with `minimum` still 1, no merge happens, and the asm
itself emits nothing: 75 words, MATCH.

Three things about that lever:

- **It only works at the END of the block whose tail you want to keep.** Put it
  between the two stores and the trailing store is still the last insn: 74
  words again. Put it at the end of the st==1 body instead and reorg loses the
  slot, because `stop_search_p` (`reorg.c:708`) stops the backward scan on
  `ASM_INPUT`: 76 words.
- **`volatile` on the store does not do it.** `*(volatile s32 *)&D_800287C8 = 0`
  on either store is 74 words / 47 DIFF: `rtx_renumbered_equal_p` compares the
  address and the mode, not `MEM_VOLATILE_P`, so the two patterns still match.
  Nor do `*(u32 *)&`, `*(s32 *)&` or `*(&D_800287C8)` -- all 74/47.
- **A trailing `goto` to the next label is not an insn by then.** Writing
  `goto out;` as the st==3 body's last statement would put a `JUMP_INSN` and a
  `BARRIER` before the label, and `find_cross_jump`'s `i2` loop skips only
  `NOTE` and `CODE_LABEL`, so a `BARRIER` would break the compare. But the
  first `jump_optimize` deletes a jump to the following label thousands of
  insns earlier, so by pass 3142 there is nothing there: 74 words / 47 DIFF.
  A trailing `;` or an unused label is 74/47 for the same reason; `return r;`
  is 76/15 and `while (0) {}` is 75/24.

### `if (c) x = 1; else x = 0;` -- WHICH ARM'S ASSIGNMENT COMES FIRST decides whether the compare and the flag share a register

A flag set on one path and cleared on the other, then passed to a call:

```c
if (p[0x12] == 1) { flag = 1; }
else { func_80023A50((s32 *)p[6], p[0x11]); flag = 0; }
```

compiles to the compare's constant in its own register and the flag as a COPY
of it, with the copy in the branch's delay slot:

```
lw    $v1, 0x48($s2)
addiu $v0, $zero, 0x1
beq   $v1, $v0, .L8002506C
addu  $s3, $v0, $zero          # delay slot: flag = 1
lw $a0 / lw $a1 / jal func_80023A50
addu  $s3, $zero, $zero        # delay slot: flag = 0
```

Write the same thing as `flag = 1; if (p[0x12] != 1) { flag = 0; call; }` --
or put `flag = 0;` BEFORE the call in the else arm -- and you instead get
`li $s3, 1` / `beq $v1, $s3`, with the flag's register as the compare operand
and the delay slot filled by stealing the join block's `i = 0` (the branch
displacement grows by one as reorg redirects past the stolen insn). 46 words
either way, 4 DIFF.

The chain, read off `-da` dumps of both spellings:

1. `jump.c:789` ("Simplify `if (...) x = a; else x = b;` by converting it to
   `x = b; if (...) x = a;`") requires `temp2 = next_active_insn (insn)` -- the
   FIRST active insn of the else part -- to be a `single_set` of the same
   register with a REG, SUBREG or CONSTANT source. `flag = 0;` written first
   in the else arm satisfies that, so jump1 hoists `flag = 1` out of the then
   block to just before the branch and inverts the condition. Writing the call
   first makes `temp2` a `CALL_INSN` and the transform declines, so the set
   stays inside the then block. `flag = 1;` before the `if` is already the
   hoisted form.
2. Once hoisted, the flag's `(set r81 (const_int 1))` sits next to the
   compare's `(set r85 (const_int 1))` in one cse block. cse keeps the
   constant (a `const_int` in a SET and a REG both cost 0, and the tie goes to
   `src`), then `insert_regs` merges r81 into r85's quantity, and
   `make_regs_eqv` (`cse.c`) makes r81 the quantity's `qty_first_reg` because
   its last use is beyond `cse_basic_block_end` and later than r85's -- so
   `canon_reg` rewrites the BRANCH to use the flag's register and r85's set
   dies. Nothing downstream can undo it, and the branch now reads $s3, so
   reorg cannot take the flag's set for the delay slot.
3. Left inside the then block, the set survives cse, loop, cse2 and combine as
   `(set r81 (const_int 1))` in a quantity of its own, and becomes
   `(set (reg s3) (reg v0))` with its `REG_EQUAL (const_int 1)` kept only
   after allocation -- first visible in the `.greg` dump, i.e. reload-time
   constant reuse, not cse. reorg then takes it as the insn before the branch.

So the copy-versus-`li` choice is NOT a narrower-destination or
register-pressure question. Measured on func_80025030 (ovl_main_80020000), 46
words (every spelling came out 46 words): the `if`/`else` with the call before
`flag = 0` is a MATCH; the same `if`/`else` with `flag = 0` before the call is
4 DIFF; `flag = 1` before the `if` is 4 DIFF whether the arm is
`flag = 0; call;` or `call; flag = 0;`; so is `flag = 1` at its declaration,
`if (p[0x12] != flag)`, and a shared `s32 one = 1` local. A `u8` or `u16` flag
is 4 DIFF with three different words (it fixes the compare but costs an
`andi` at the call and swaps the prologue's $s3/$ra saves); `s8`/`s16` are 47
words. Hoisting the condition into its own `s32 cond` local is 47 words/40
DIFF -- combine turns it into `xori`/`beqz` instead of `li`/`beq`.

A corollary worth keeping: when a diff is "the target copies a constant into
the flag register and we load it directly", look for an arm whose statements
can be reordered to take `jump.c:789` out of play, before reaching for a
declaration change.

## `while (1)` WITH A `break` DEFEATS LOOP REVERSAL, AND THAT IS WHAT KEEPS A WALKED POINTER

An upcounting loop over a walked pointer -- `for (i = 0; i < N; i++) sum ^=
*q++;` -- does not come out as written. `loop.c:check_dbra_loop` turns the
counter into a downcount (`li N-1` / `addiu -1` / `bgez`) and the `slti`
disappears: one word shorter and nothing like the listing. The route in is
`no_use_except_counting`, which is computed when the compared biv has no givs
and the loop has no exit other than the fall-through, and which is true for
any counter used only to count -- exactly the case here.

Blocking it with the usual levers costs code: a second non-invariant read
(`num_nonfixed_reads <= 1`), a second store (`num_mem_sets <= 1`), a call, or
a `volatile`. Indexing by the counter instead (`q[i]`) does block the
reversal -- the counter acquires a giv, so `no_use_except_counting` stays 0
and the two-iv-class disjunct fails -- but it costs the pointer: the cursor
becomes a loop.c giv, and `emit_iv_add_mult (..., loop_start)` puts its
initialisation at the loop start, i.e. AFTER the source's own `i = 0`.
`combine` then folds the source's `q = base + K` into that copy at the COPY's
position, so the preheader comes out `sum = 0` / `i = 0` / `cursor = base + K`
where the listing has `sum = 0` / `cursor = base + K` / `i = 0`, and
local_alloc, assigning in insn order, gives the counter the lower register.
That residue is 6 DIFF of pure register names and no spelling of the indexed
loop moves it, because the giv's init site is unconditional in loop.c.

The free blocker is the loop FORM. Write the test as a `break` in the body:

    s32 i = 0;
    while (1)
    {
        sum ^= *q++;
        i++;
        if (i >= N)
        {
            break;
        }
    }

`check_dbra_loop` starts with `get_condition_for_loop (PREV_INSN (loop_end))`
and gives up when that is not a conditional branch. Here the loop's last insn
is the backward jump and the conditional branch sits before it, so it returns
0 before any of the conditions above are reached -- the `.loop` dump says
`Loop unrolling: No final conditional branch found` and nothing about
reversing. jump2 then merges the branch pair back into the one `bnez`, so the
emitted loop is identical to the `for`'s -- minus the reversal.

Measured on func_80021EE0 (ovl_main_80020000), 14 words:

* `while (1)` + `i++;` + `if (i >= 0x177E) break;` -- MATCH.
* `while (1)` + `if (++i >= 0x177E) break;` -- MATCH.
* `goto` loop (`loop: ...; if (++i < 0x177E) goto loop;`) -- MATCH. No loop
  notes at all, so check_dbra_loop never runs; same bytes.
* `for (;;)` in place of `while (1)` -- 14 words, 3 DIFF. Not a synonym here:
  the first iteration is peeled (`lw $a2, 0x208($a0)` / `addiu $a1, $a0,
  0x20C` / `li $v1, 1`).
* `if (++i == 0x177E) break;` -- 14 words, 6 DIFF: `bne` against a
  register-held 0x177E instead of `slti`/`bnez`. `check_dbra_loop`'s reversal
  arm also requires `GET_CODE (comparison) == LT`, so `!=` blocks the
  reversal too, but it changes the test's code.
* `for (i = 0; i < 0x177E; i++) sum ^= *q++;` and
  `do { sum ^= *q++; } while (++i < 0x177E);` -- 13 words, 11 DIFF, reversed.
* `q[i]` in twelve spellings (declaration orders, `i = 0` as a declaration
  initialiser, `while`, `do`/`while`, `gsw[0x82 + i]`, `(gsw + 0x82)[i]`,
  `(... ^ sum) == 0`, u32) -- all 14 words, the same 6 DIFF.

Read in reverse: a listing whose loop walks a pointer AND keeps an upcounting
`slti` counter is telling you the exit test was not the loop's last insn in
the source. Its sibling func_80021EB8, which differs only in storing the sum
instead of comparing it, DOES have the reversed form and is spelled as the
downcount.

## A SYMBOL ARRAY REFERENCE EMITS ITS `lui` FIRST AS A *MEM*, ITS `sll` FIRST AS A *POINTER VALUE* -- and the join block's first insn is what reorg puts in the delay slot

The "Statement granularity is what orders the pieces of an address" lever says
one expression emits the INDEX first and the symbol after. For a two-
dimensional **symbol** array under a split (-G0) address that is the wrong way
round, and the contrast is not load-vs-store but MEM-vs-pointer-value.

Measured in isolation (`extern s32 D_80083E98[][32];`, cc1psx -O2 -G0):

```c
D_80083E98[idx][0] = 1;              /* lui, addiu, sll, addu, sw */
return D_80083E98[idx][0];           /* lui, addiu, sll, addu, lw */
s32 *row = D_80083E98[idx];
row[0] = 1;                          /* sll, lui, addiu, addu, sw */
```

The `addu` names the `sll` register first either way, so only the POSITION of
the symbol pair moves -- and with it every register number after it, because
the pseudos are born in the other order.

No spelling of the one-expression form moves it. Eleven were compiled and all
eleven produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL `.s` (same `-da` RTL, same md5 after the
`.file` line): `D_80083E98[idx][0]`, `*D_80083E98[idx]`,
`*(s32 *)(D_80083E98[idx])`, `*(s32 *)&D_80083E98[idx][0]`,
`*(s32 *)(&D_80083E98[idx])`, `((s32 *)D_80083E98)[idx * 32]`,
`*(s32 *)((u8 *)D_80083E98 + idx * 0x80)` in three operand orders, the same
with `(s32)` instead of `(u8 *)`, `idx * sizeof(D_80083E98[0])`, and the
`UnkSaveRow`/`D_80083E98_s` struct alias. Six spellings of the
pointer-in-its-own-statement form all give the `sll` first: the array decay,
`&D_80083E98[idx][0]`, a `s32 (*)[32]` row pointer, declaration-with-
initialiser, separate declaration and assignment, and a byte-offset cast. An
offset local (`s32 o = idx * 0x80;`) does it too.

Why: the two forms are different TREES, not different expansions of one tree.
`-da`'s `.rtl` dump for the MEM form is `high`, `lo_sum`, copy, `ashift`,
`(plus lo_sum ashift)` -- `expand_expr`'s binop path expands `TREE_OPERAND 0`
first, so the ADDR_EXPR is operand 0 there. For the pointer assignment it is
copy, `ashift`, `high`, `lo_sum`, `(plus lo_sum ashift)` into the user's own
`reg/v` -- the scaled index is operand 0. `combine` then rewrites the `plus`
to index-first in both, which is why the `addu`'s operand order is no witness.
The pre-reload scheduler does not touch either block: the `.sched` dump is
insn-for-insn the `.combine` dump.

The visible consequence, and how to read it off a listing: reorg fills an
unconditional `j`'s delay slot with the FIRST insn of the block it jumps to
and bumps the label past it, leaving that insn duplicated -- once in the slot,
once in the fall-through. So in

```
    j      .L80021EA0
     sll   $v0, $t1, 7      <- delay slot
  ...
    sll    $v0, $t1, 7      <- fall-through copy
  .L80021EA0:
    lui    $v1, %hi(D_80083E98)
```

the delay slot is naming the join block's first insn. A `lui` there instead of
the `sll` is this lever and nothing to do with scheduling.

Measured on func_80021DF4 (ovl_main_80020000), 7 of 49 words: the
one-expression store is 7 DIFF in all eleven spellings above, and

```c
s32 *row;
*(UnkRow *)D_80083E98[idx] = *(UnkRow *)(src + 0x200);
row = D_80083E98[idx];
row[0] = 1;
```

is MATCH. Note the block copy on the line above KEEPS the one-expression form:
its address is a MEM and the target wants `lui`/`addiu`/`sll` there. The two
row addresses in that function are the same arithmetic written two ways, which
is exactly what a park note read as "the two orders cannot both be had".

### A HOISTED CONSTANT CANNOT KEEP A COPY -- a body-order preheader can be all STATEMENTS

A preheader whose constants are materialised in the order the loop BODY uses
them is the signature of `loop.c`'s `move_movables`, which inserts each
movable with `emit_insn_before (pattern, loop_start)` in movables-list order
(= first-set order in the body), and then `strength_reduce` appends the giv
initialisations after them. That reading is right about the order and can
still be the wrong conclusion, because **a hoisted pair can never keep its
copy, and two hoisted constants of the same value can never be two
registers.** Two independent passes delete it:

* cse1 runs before loop.c and the whole body is one basic block, so a second
  pseudo holding a known constant is collapsed into the first. The `.cse`
  dump shows it directly: one `(set (reg:QI N) (const_int 5))` and both
  stores reading `reg N`. Widening the source so the move is mode-invisible
  (the `u8 h = w` lever at `:1376`) does NOT save it here -- cse folds the
  source to the constant first, so there is no reg-reg move left for the mode
  test to protect. Measured on func_80022A30 in all of `u8/u8`, `u32/u8`,
  `u16/u8`, `u8/u32`, `u32/u32` and `h1 = 5` instead of `h1 = w1`: 44 words,
  36 DIFF, identically.
* even if one survived cse1, `combine_movables` would match the pair --
  modes equal, `dependencies` both 0 (that field is only ever set for libcall
  blocks, so it never distinguishes two ordinary movables), and the copy's REG
  source satisfies `matched_regs[REGNO (m1->set_src)]` -- and `move_movables`
  then rewrites the second register to the first. Only `m1->global` and
  `n_times_used[regno] != 1` block the match, and a dead pre-loop assignment
  to make the pseudo global does not reach that far, because cse1 has already
  collapsed the pair (measured: still 44w/36).

So when the preheader holds a constant AND a reg-reg copy of it, those two
insns are PRE-LOOP STATEMENTS, not hoists -- the copy survives there because
it sits in a different cse basic block from its only use (the copy before the
loop, the use inside it), so `canon_reg` never rewrites the use. And then the
whole preheader is statements, in source order, and anything the listing puts
BETWEEN two such pairs is a statement too: `:1448`'s local-per-constant.

func_80022A30 (ovl_main_80020000) is the measurement. Its preheader is
`i = 0`, 5, a copy of the 5, 0x48, 0x104058, 6, a copy of the 6, then the giv
`addiu $a0, $a3, 4`. With 0x48 and 0x104058 left as literals at their two use
sites each they ARE hoisted, which puts them after the for-init instead of
between the pairs: 46 words, 8 DIFF. Giving each its own pre-loop local, and
lifting the counter out of the `for` so its initialisation comes first --

```c
    i = 0;
    w1 = 5;
    h1 = w1;
    c = 0x48;
    d = 0x104058;
    w2 = 6;
    h2 = w2;
    for (; i < 4; i++)
```

-- is MATCH. The `for (; i < 4; i++)` is load-bearing: `for (i = 0; ...)`
emits `i = 0` after the six materialisations.

**Corollary for reading a listing:** a reg-reg copy of a constant in a
preheader is positive evidence that the counter's initialisation and the
constants are all plain statements, which also fixes where the loop body
begins. A hoist and a statement are distinguishable at a glance only when the
hoisted set has no copy.

### loop.c's HOIST TEST IS `threshold * savings * lifetime >= insn_count` WITH threshold 60 HERE -- SO AN INVARIANT STAYS IN THE LOOP ONLY IF EARLIER MOVABLES SPEND THE THRESHOLD, A FORCED SHIFT RIDES OUT FREE WHATEVER YOU DO, AND A FOUR-USE CONSTANT CANNOT BE BLOCKED AT ALL

MEASURED on func_80022774 (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), 2026-11-01: 102 words /
84 DIFF to 102 / 3, the whole of it read out of `cc1psx -da`'s `.loop` and
`.sched` dumps. The park's stated cause -- "loop.c hoists all FOUR halvings
here, the target hoists three, a move_movables threshold decision" -- named
the right pass and the wrong lever, and three separate facts were needed.

**The arithmetic, and the one number you need.** `move_movables` moves a
movable when

    already_moved[regno]
    || (threshold * savings * m->lifetime) >= insn_count
    || (m->forces && m->forces->done && n_times_used[m->forces->regno] == 1)

(loop.c:1730), with `threshold = (loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (1 +
n_non_fixed_regs)` (:532) decremented by 3 after every move (:1719, :1904),
`savings = n_times_used[regno]` -- which is a copy of the number of SETS, so
it is 1 for anything set once (:837, :597) -- and `lifetime` the luid span
between the register's first and last mention. `insn_count` is the number the
`.loop` dump prints as "Loop from A to B: N real insns".

**threshold starts at 60 in this compiler.** Bracketed from one dump: in a
38-insn loop the 8th move (lifetime 1, savings 1) still happened and the 9th
did not, so `threshold - 21 >= 38` and `threshold - 24 < 38`, and threshold is
even, so `2 * (1 + n_non_fixed_regs) = 60`. Nothing in the source moves it,
except that a CALL in the loop would halve it.

Two consequences worth having in hand:

* With threshold 60 and a loop of 35-40 insns, **everything invariant moves**
  until about seven moves have gone by. The lever is not "persuade loop.c",
  it is "spend the threshold earlier, in body order". Writing `0x48` and
  `0x104058` as inline literals rather than pre-loop locals added two movables
  AND two insns to `insn_count`, and that alone turned `%hi(D_80027F48)`, the
  `0x90D0E0` load and one `srl` from `moved to N` into `not desirable` in the
  dump. The movables are considered in RTL order, so a movable you want kept
  must sit AFTER the ones you are willing to lose.
* The gate before the threshold (:694) can only ever reject a USER variable:
  its three escape clauses are `!maybe_never && !loop_reg_used_before_p`,
  `!REG_USERVAR_P && !REG_LOOP_TEST_P`, and `reg_in_basic_block_p`, and the
  middle one passes every compiler temp unconditionally. And `maybe_never` is
  0 throughout a rotated `for` body -- it is set only past a CODE_LABEL or a
  JUMP_INSN (:930) -- so the uservar route needs a branch in the body. A dead
  pre-loop `g = 0;` to break `reg_in_basic_block_p` is inert on its own
  (measured, 85).

**A shift of a hoisted sum ALWAYS rides out free.** `force_movables` (:1245)
walks each movable's register to `regno_last_uid`, and if that insn is also a
movable whose `set_src` is not the bare register, it sets `m->forces` -- and
the third disjunct above then moves the dependent at no threshold cost.
`addiu $t4, $v0, 0xA` hoisted with `srl $v0, $t4, 1` left in the loop is
therefore impossible while both are movables, however small the threshold:
measured at 36 DIFF with `p[0xB] = (h + 0xA) >> 1;` written inline. Two cures,
both measured: make the sum a pre-loop STATEMENT, so only the shift is a
movable and it faces the threshold on its own (85 -> the schedule then puts
the sum early, 26 DIFF); or give the sum's register a later use in a
NON-movable insn, so the walk finds nothing and no link is made -- an
`__asm__("" ::"r"(bh))`-style reference does it, and that was worth 25 words
here. The condition is on the register's last mention, not on its uses' kind,
so one extra reference is enough.

**A constant stored four times cannot be blocked by the threshold.** cse1
collapses `*(s32 *)(p + k) = 0x90D0E0;` written four times onto ONE pseudo
(the `.rtl` dump has four `(set (reg N) (const_int 9490656))`, the `.cse` dump
one), and its `lifetime` is then 4, so `threshold * 1 * 4 >= insn_count` holds
for any reachable threshold -- it would take a 145-insn loop. Four separate
`s32` locals do not help (85): cse1 rewrites the later stores onto the first
pseudo and deletes the redundant sets. What does work is a SECOND set of the
same register whose source is not invariant, which makes
`n_times_set[regno] == 1` fail and `consec_sets_invariant_p` fail with it:

    g = 0x90D0E0;
    __asm__("" : "+r"(g) : "r"(i));          /* i varies: the asm is not invariant */

`"+r"(g)` alone is NOT enough -- an `asm_operands` whose only operand is an
invariant register is itself invariant, and the dump then reads `consec 1 ...
moved to 237 moved to 238`, hoisting the pair (84 DIFF). `volatile` instead of
the varying input is 68. With the varying input the lui/ori stays in the loop
where the target has it, at a cost of zero words.

**Reading the dumps.** `tools/cdkgcc -O2 -G0 -da -S` on a standalone
candidate, or `dump.sh`, which does it for you; the dumps land in the current
directory named after the input. (They used to land in the wine prefix's
`Temp` as `PQ2.*`, overwritten per run, which is why this said to pin
`AZURE_WINEPREFIX` and compile one candidate at a time.) The `.loop` dump's
first twenty lines are the whole
hoist decision -- one line per movable, `moved to N` or `not desirable`, with
its lifetime and savings -- and `.sched` prints every ready list, which is
how you learn that sched1 here schedules a block BACKWARD from its end
("ready list at T-1" is the last slot) and that a priority-1 insn with no
in-block dependents is taken whenever nothing else is hazard-boosted.

### A CONSTANT THAT IS ALSO THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT BE THE STORE'S REGISTER -- AN UNEXPLAINED `move` OF A CONSTANT IS EVIDENCE THE FUNCTION IS NOT `void`

MEASURED on func_800213C4 (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), 2026-11-01: 18 words /
10 DIFF to 19 / 0, one word and one word only.

The tail was read as `D_800287E0 = 0; D_800287C8 = 1;` on a `void` function,
and the unit already contains a MATCHED twin of exactly that tail after
exactly the same call-and-spin -- func_800210F0's `st == 1` block, `lui` in
the loop branch's delay slot, `lui`, `sw $zero`, `addiu $v0, $zero, 3`,
`sw $v0`. func_800213C4's target does something else: the constant is
materialised FIRST, in the delay slot, both `lui`s come before either store,
and the store's source arrives through a `addu $v1, $v0, $zero` copy, with the
second `%hi` pushed out to `$a0`.

The cause is the return value. `return 1;` expands to a set of the HARD
register, `(set (reg:SI 2 v0) (const_int 1))`, and cse2 unifies it with the
store's own `(const_int 1)`, so the single pseudo holding 1 is tied to `$v0`
and lives until the `jr`. The store's source therefore cannot be `$v0` and the
copy is not an artifact of anything -- it is the only way to get the value into
a second register. Three values are live at the peak (`$v0` = 1, `$v1` =
`%hi(D_800287E0)`, `$a0` = `%hi(D_800287C8)`), which is also what pushes the
second `lui` off `$v1`. And because the constant is now the first insn of the
block after the loop rather than the fourth, `reorg` takes IT for the loop
branch's delay slot instead of the first `lui`; the delay-slot fill is a
consequence, not a separate decision.

The whole of the park's measured table is explained by the missing return:

| spelling | words | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| `void`, `D_800287E0 = 0; D_800287C8 = 1;` | 18 | 10 |
| `void`, `t = 1;` before the stores, store `t` | 18 | 11 |
| `void`, `while` for `do/while`; the two stores swapped | 18 | 10-11 |
| `s32`, `s32 t = 1;` at the top, store `t`, `return t;` | 21 | 19 |
| `s32`, stores as written, `return 1;` | 19 | **0** |

The last-but-one row is the useful negative: a local that spans the two calls
is not the same thing as a `return` of the constant -- `t` takes `$s1` and
costs the save/restore pair plus a `move`, three words the wrong way.

**Corollary for reading a listing.** An `addu $rD, $rS, $zero` copy of a
freshly materialised constant, immediately before a store of that constant,
with no other use of `$rS` in sight, means the constant is ALSO in `$v0` for a
reason -- and on a leaf tail the only such reason is the return value. Check
the declared return type before spending anything on the spelling of the
store: three callers in this unit discard the result, so the prototype says
`void` and the callers do not contradict it. The sibling rule at `:11120`
(a hoisted constant cannot keep a copy) is what rules out loop.c as the source
of the copy and leaves the hard register as the only candidate.

### WHERE `i++` SITS RELATIVE TO THE POINTER BUMP DECIDES sched1's LOAD-DELAY FILLER -- loop.c pins the reduced giv's update to the biv update, and `rank_for_schedule` breaks a priority tie on the HIGHER LUID

Measured on `func_800242D8` (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), which went from 10 DIFF
to **0** on this one move and on nothing else. The function is four 0x18-byte
sprite records in a loop; the body walks `p` with `p += 0x18` and loop.c
strength-reduces the seven record stores onto a reduced giv `$v1 = p + 0xB`.

The whole residue was a rotation of three insns: the target has
`addu $v0,$a3,$a2` (`&D_80027FD0[i]`) and `addiu $a3,$a3,1` (`i++`) at the top
of the body and the giv update `addiu $v1,$v1,0x18` between the `lbu` and the
`sb`, where the candidate had the giv update before the `addu` and the `i++`
between the `lbu` and the `sb`.

**The mechanism, from the dumps.** In the body's basic block, `sched1` is a
backward list scheduler. After it places the final `sb $v0,0($a0)` there is
one slot that cannot hold the `lbu` feeding it -- the load delay -- and at that
slot the ready list holds exactly two insns, both priority 1 and both in class
3 relative to the last scheduled insn:

    ;; ready list at T-5: 99 (1) 165 (1), now 99 165     <- 10 DIFF: i++ wins
    ;; ready list at T-5: 165 (1) 92 (1), now 165 92     <-  0 DIFF: giv wins

`rank_for_schedule` (`sched.c:2429`) compares priority, then the class of each
insn with respect to `last_scheduled_insn`, and only then falls through to
`return INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2);` with `tmp = *y`, `tmp2 = *x`
(`sched.c:2472`). A positive return prefers `y`, so **the HIGHER LUID wins**,
and `schedule_block` takes `ready[0]` (`sched.c:3846`). So the tie is settled
by which of the two insns was LATER in the pre-sched insn stream.

**And that order is not free, because half of it is pinned.** loop.c emits a
reduced giv's own update immediately before the biv update it is derived from,
so the LUID of `$v1 += 0x18` is fixed to just-before the `p += 0x18` statement
and nothing in the source moves it. The only movable half is `i++`:

| where `i++` is written | pre-sched order (`.regmove`) | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| the `for`'s third clause | `... sb p[0]`, giv, `p += 0x18`, **`i++`** | 10 |
| in the body before `p += 0x18` | `... sb p[0]`, **`i++`**, giv, `p += 0x18` | **0** |

In the `for`-clause form the increment sits past the biv update (at
`NOTE_INSN_LOOP_CONT`) and so outranks the giv update; moved into the body it
is behind it and loses. Nothing else about the body changes -- same opcodes,
same immediates, same registers either way.

**Spellings, all 46 words** (`i = 0` lifted out of the `for` is inert here):

| spelling | DIFF |
|---|---|
| `for (i = 0; i < 4;)` ... `p[0] = D_80027FD0[i++];` then `p += 0x18` | **0** |
| ditto with `p[0] = D_80027FD0[i]; i++;` as two statements | **0** |
| ditto with an address local `q = &D_80027FD0[i]; i++; p[0] = *q;` | **0** |
| `i++` written AFTER `p += 0x18` | 10 |
| `i++` FIRST in the body, read as `D_80027FD0[i - 1]` | 2 |
| `for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)` + an address local at the top of the body | 23 |
| `while (i < 4)` / `do ... while (i < 4)` with `i++` at the top | 14 |
| the byte, not the address, into a local at the top of the body | 17 |

**How to recognise it in a listing.** A loop that walks a pointer AND has a
separate counter whose increment is NOT adjacent to the pointer bump, with a
reduced giv's update sitting in a load-delay slot in between, is this. The
giveaway is that only three insns move and the `lbu`/`sb` pair keeps its
position: the stores are all memory-dependent on each other and on the load,
so the scheduler has no freedom there, and the one free slot is the filler.
The sibling levers at `:5540` (read the scheduler's own decisions) and `:5885`
(preheader giv initialisations are in reverse body order) are the same
machinery seen from the preheader side; this is the body side of it.

## A CROSS-JUMPED TAIL STARTS WHERE THE LABEL IS, NOT WHERE THE INSNS START LOOKING SHARED -- READ THE LABEL'S ADDRESS BEFORE DIAGNOSING ONE

Measured on `func_8002168C` (ovl_main_80020000, 82 words, landed MATCH).

The function's `switch (st)` has arms 1+2, 3, 4+5. The target's arm 3 is four
words and ends in a jump whose target sits inside arm 4/5's code:

```
.L80021750:                       <- case 3
    lui   $v0, %hi(D_80028530)
    addiu $v0, $v0, %lo(D_80028530)
    j     .L8002177C
     sll  $v1, $a0, 2             [delay slot]
.L80021760:                       <- case 4, 5
    lui   $v0, %hi(D_80084118)
    addiu $v0, $v0, %lo(D_80084118)
    sll   $v1, $a0, 2
    addu  $v0, $v1, $v0
    sw    $zero, 0x0($v0)
    lui   $v0, %hi(D_80028530)
    addiu $v0, $v0, %lo(D_80028530)
.L8002177C:
    addu  $a1, $v1, $v0
    lw    $v0, 0x0($a1)
```

Read without checking where `.L8002177C` actually is, this looks like arm 3
zeroing `D_80028530[i]` through a two-word `addu`/`sw` tail shared with arm
4/5, with the arms passing a symbol base and their own `sll`. That reading
is wrong in every particular, and it survived ten measured spellings of a
near-miss because the arithmetic of it works: both readings spend the same 82
words. **`.L8002177C` is at `0x8002177C`, the `addu $a1`** -- three words
below the `addu $v0`, not at it. So:

- arm 3 does not store anything; it computes `$v0 = &D_80028530` and
  `$v1 = i * 4` and jumps to a *load*;
- the merged tail is not the `addu`/`sw` pair, it is the whole
  `D_80028530[i] >= 0xB` check and its body, starting at the `addu $a1` that
  forms the address;
- the two `sll $v1, $a0, 2` are not a shared subexpression kept alive past a
  merge -- they are one per arm, each the arm's own, and `$v1` reaches the
  check because the merge point is *below* them.

So the C is the duplicated form: arm 3 and arm 4/5 each carry a full copy of
the check, and `jump.c:2188`'s `find_cross_jump (insn, JUMP_LABEL (insn), 1,
...)` walks both copies back from the end -- `sw`, `sw`, `addu`, `addiu`,
`lui`, `sw`, `addu`, `addiu`, `lui`, `bnez`, `slti`, `lw`, `addu $a1` -- and
breaks on arm 3's `sll` against arm 4/5's `addiu %lo(D_80028530)`. The label
`.L8002177C` is planted at that break (`jump.c:2754`), which is exactly why it
lands mid-address-computation. `reorg.c:3086`'s backward scan then takes the
first eligible insn before the jump, which is arm 3's leftover `sll`, into the
delay slot.

**Spellings, all with the same `if (st != 0)` / single `return st` frame:**

| arm 3 | words | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| its own full copy of the check (arm 4/5 keeps its copy) | 82 | **0 (MATCH)** |
| `goto check;` into arm 4/5's single copy | 79 | 35 |
| `(&D_80028530)[i] = 0; goto check;` (the near-miss) | 82 | 11 |
| `(&D_80028530)[i] = 0;` + its own copy of the check | 83 | 36 |
| shared `s32 off = i * 4` in both arms, offset-form check | 82 | 6 |
| `off` assigned inside the address, `+ (off = i * 4)` | 82 | 6 |
| base pointer per arm + shared `p[i] = 0` then one check | 81 | 34 |
| base pointer + `off` statements, per-arm store | 82 | 19 |

Two of those are worth keeping as facts about the compiler rather than about
this function:

- **A bare `goto` into another arm is strictly smaller than the duplicate.**
  An arm whose whole body is one jump leaves a block containing only a
  `JUMP_INSN`; `jump.c` retargets the jump *table entry* at the final
  destination and the arm's label disappears. The table still has five entries
  and still points at three distinct labels, so the rodata check passes and
  only the word count shows it: 79 against 82. If a switch arm in a target has
  its own label and only address-setup in it, the source duplicated something.
- **Expansion order inside an arm is set by the form of the address, not by
  cse.** `(&SYM)[i]` expands `high`, `lo_sum`, `ashift`, `plus`
  (symbol first: `expr.c:7347`'s `binop:` expands operand 0 then operand 1,
  and the `ptr_mode` path at the end of `case PLUS_EXPR` reorders only the
  *rtx*, putting the `mult` first). `*(s32 *)((u8 *)&SYM + off)` with `off` a
  local assigned in a preceding statement emits the `ashift` first, so the arm
  comes out `sll`, `lui`, `addiu` -- and that order then *protects* the `sll`
  from a cross-jump, because the mismatching `addiu %lo` is reached first.
  Writing the assignment inside the address (`+ (off = i * 4)`) does not move
  it: the `MODIFY_EXPR` is still expanded before the symbol. Both give 82
  words and 6 DIFF, with every register and the `addu` operand order already
  correct -- a 6-DIFF floor reachable from a completely wrong structure, and
  the reason a low DIFF is not evidence that the shape is right.

## `qty_size` IS IN WORDS, NOT BYTES -- A QImode QUANTITY IS NOT PRICED AT A QUARTER, AND WHICH STATEMENT FILLS A LOAD DELAY DECIDES WHO GETS `$v0`

Measured on `func_80022300` (ovl_main_80020000, -G0, 15 words), which went
from 12 DIFF to **0** on moving one statement, 2026-11-01.

**The correction first, because the section at `:2240` is wrong and it is
wrong in a direction that invents margins.** That section says
`qty_size[qty]` is `GET_MODE_SIZE`, i.e. bytes, citing local-alloc.c:380.
Line 380 is inside `alloc_qty_for_scratch`, which only ever runs for a
`SCRATCH` operand in a `CLOBBER`. Every ordinary pseudo goes through
`alloc_qty` instead (local-alloc.c:279), called from `reg_is_born` as

    alloc_qty (regno, GET_MODE (reg), PSEUDO_REGNO_SIZE (regno), birth);

(local-alloc.c:2068), and `PSEUDO_REGNO_SIZE` is
`(GET_MODE_SIZE (mode) + UNITS_PER_WORD - 1) / UNITS_PER_WORD` (regs.h:65) --
the count of hard registers, stored at local-alloc.c:291. On MIPS
`UNITS_PER_WORD` is 4, so **QImode, HImode and SImode pseudos all have
`qty_size` 1** and the size factor cancels out of `qty_compare_1` entirely
for every single-word quantity. A `u8` quantity is priced at exactly the same
size as an `s32` one.

The same correction applies to that section's "exception": `combine_regs`
escalates only under `if (usize < ssize)` (local-alloc.c:1953), and `usize` /
`ssize` there are `REG_SIZE` (local-alloc.c:1816, :1759), which is the same
words-not-bytes macro. So a `lbu` tied to the SImode destination that consumes
it does **not** become "size 4"; it stays size 1, with `qty_mode` still QImode.
What the tie really buys is only the second half of that section's claim --
`qty_n_refs[sqty] += reg_n_refs[sreg]` (local-alloc.c:1939), the SUM of both
pseudos' references.

So on this target the whole of `qty_compare_1` reduces to

    floor_log2 (qty_n_refs) * qty_n_refs / (qty_death - qty_birth)

and two refs over a one-insn span (1*2/2 = **1.0** in the doubled index units
the pass uses) is the highest price anything can fetch. A four-ref quantity
needs a span under 8 insns to beat it.

**The lever.** The block's four un-suggested quantities are the two byte
constants (`0x28`, `0x13`: 2 refs, born and dead one insn apart, 1.0 each),
the `p[0]` read-modify-write (`lbu` + `ior` tied by `combine_regs`, 4 refs),
and the `0xA04010` word constant (2 refs, a long span, lowest). `find_free_reg`
hands out the first register free *over the quantity's own range* and MIPS
2.7.2 defines no `REG_ALLOC_ORDER`, so that is `$v0`, then `$v1`, then `$a0`.
Which of them gets `$v0` therefore depends only on whether the short, dear
byte-constant ranges OVERLAP the `p[0]` range -- and sched1 decides that:

| `p[0xA] = (n << 3) + 4;` written | sched1 fills the `lbu` delay with | `p[0]` span | `p[0]` price | `0x13` span | gets `$v0` | DIFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4th (the park) | the `sll`/`addiu` pair | 9..13 | 1.0 | 5..6, disjoint | both | 12 |
| **2nd** | the `0x13` set and its store | 8..13 | **0.8** | 9..10, **inside** | `0x13` only | **0** |

sched1 schedules this block backward and fills the load delay of
`lbu $v1, 0($a1)` with whatever pair is still unplaced. Write the `(n << 3) + 4`
store early and its two insns are already consumed, so the `0x13` pair becomes
the filler and lands *inside* the `p[0]` quantity's live range. `0x13` then
outprices `p[0]` 1.0 to 0.8, takes `$v0`, and `p[0]` is pushed to `$v1`. The
`0xA04010` constant, now spanning insns 1..11, is blocked from `$v0` by both
byte constants and from `$v1` by `p[0]`, and lands in `$a0` -- free only
because the first parameter is dead.

**And the register flip is what moves the delay slot, not the other way
round.** With `p[0]` in `$v0` the return value's `(set (reg/i:SI 2 v0) ...)`
has an output dependence on the `sb $v0, 0($a1)` ahead of it, so sched2 cannot
hoist it and it stays the last insn, which is the one `reorg` takes. With
`p[0]` in `$v1` the dependence is gone, sched2 ranks `sb $v1` at priority 2
against the return value's 1 (`;; ready list at T-2: 26 (1) 36 (1) 42 (2)
47 (1), now 42 47 36 26`) and puts the return value at word 9, leaving the
store last for the delay slot. **Do not read a return value in a `jr` delay
slot as a statement-order problem; on a leaf it is usually a statement about
which register the last store's source got.** The two useful negatives: an
explicit `u8` or `s32` temp for `p[0]` as the first statement, and a local for
the return value declared first, both produce the BYTE-IDENTICAL 12-DIFF
stream -- sched1 pulls the return-value computation adjacent to the `(use)`
insn with `LAUNCH_PRIORITY` (sched.c:189, :3902) no matter where the source
puts it, and it sinks the `lbu` to the delay-filling position for the same
reason.

**Cheap method note.** Statement order over five independent stores is 120
candidates; `cpppsx` + `cc1psx -O2 -G0` to a `.s` and a line-by-line compare
against the target's normalised instruction text costs 0.36s each (against
4.5s for `ovlverify.py`, which assembles), agrees with it exactly on the DIFF,
and sweeps the whole space in 45 seconds. For a short leaf with N independent
statements, sweep before theorising: five of the 120 orders matched here and
the next best was 3.

## gcc'S DIVIDE-BY-POWER-OF-TWO COPY SURVIVES ONLY WHEN THE QUOTIENT IS WRITTEN BACK INTO THE DIVIDEND -- cse1's `make_regs_eqv` DECIDES IT, ON THE *LAST* `regno_last_uid` OF THE TWO PSEUDOS

MEASURED on `func_800219B8` (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), 2026-11-01: 18 words /
18 DIFF to 19 / **0**, landed MATCH. Two separate words, one of which is this
one.

`expand_divmod` expands a signed `/ (1 << k)` as

    (set temp dividend)                 ; expmed.c, emit_move_insn
    (bge dividend 0) -> L
    (set temp (plus temp (1<<k)-1))     ; expand_inc
    L:
    (set quot (ashiftrt temp k))

In the listing that `(set temp dividend)` is either a real `addu $rT, $rD,
$zero` (which `reorg` then puts in the `bgez`'s delay slot) or nothing at all
(and the delay slot is a `nop`). It is NOT a scheduling or delay-slot
decision: the move is present in the RTL right through `.lreg` either way, and
`reload` deletes it as a no-op move only when `temp` and `dividend` were given
the same hard register. Whether they can share is decided by whether the
`expand_inc` insn's *source* still says `temp` or has been rewritten to
`dividend`:

| `.cse` shows | `dividend` dies at | `greg` conflicts | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(set temp (plus temp 8191))` | the move | `temp` conflicts with nothing | same reg, move deleted, **nop in the delay slot** |
| `(set temp (plus dividend 8191))` | the `plus` | `temp` vs `dividend` overlap | two regs, **the move survives** |

**The rewrite is cse1's `canon_reg`, and which of the two pseudos is canonical
is settled in `make_regs_eqv` (`cse.c:838`, test at `cse.c:856-869`).** When
cse processes `(set temp dividend)` it calls `make_regs_eqv (temp, dividend)`;
`temp` displaces `dividend` as `qty_first_reg` -- and so is *not* rewritten
away -- only if

    (uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[temp]] > cse_basic_block_end
     || uid_cuid[regno_first_uid[temp]] < cse_basic_block_start)
    && uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[temp]] > uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[dividend]]

The first clause is **always true here**, and not reachable from C. cse1 walks
this region three times, and the `;; Processing block from A to B` lines in the
`-da` `.cse` dump name the boundaries exactly:

    ;; Processing block from 56 to 0, 7 sets.     <- `skip_blocks` AROUND the
    ;; Processing block from 56 to 61, 3 sets.       `plus`; it is invalidated
    ;; Processing block from 62 to 0, 5 sets.        by invalidate_skipped_block

On the first pass `cse_end_of_basic_block` takes the AROUND branch
(`cse.c:8198`, the `skip_blocks && q != 0 && GET_CODE (q) != CODE_LABEL` arm)
because the `bge` jumps around a single label-free insn -- so the `plus` is
never processed and `invalidate_skipped_block` drops `temp`'s equivalence
before the shift. On the NOT_TAKEN rescan the block ends **at the join label**
(`while (p && GET_CODE (p) != CODE_LABEL)`, `cse.c:8087`), so the shift, which
is `temp`'s last use, is always past `cse_basic_block_end`.

**So the only reachable half is the second clause, and the lever is C-level:
`dividend` must be referenced at or after the shift.** Writing the quotient
back into the dividend's own variable does exactly that, because then the
shift's *destination* is the dividend's pseudo:

```c
sum = sum / 0x2000;        /* dividend's last uid IS the shift */
return 0xF - sum;          /* 19 words, 0 DIFF */
```

against

```c
return 0xF - sum / 0x2000; /* dividend dies at the move; 18 words */
```

Nothing else differs -- same opcodes, same immediates. The giveaway in a
listing is that the shift's destination register is the one the dividend was
accumulated in (`sra $a1, $v0, 13` with `$a1` = the sum), which is the
allocator honouring `(set sum (ashiftrt temp 13))`.

**Corollary for reading a listing.** In the divide idiom, `bgez $rD, L` /
`addu $rT, $rD, $zero` / `addiu $rT, $rD, imm` -- the `addiu` reading `$rD`
and not `$rT` -- means the source assigned the quotient back to the dividend.
`bgez $rD, L` / `nop` / `addiu $rD, $rD, imm` means it did not. One word, and
it is not a device, a schedule or a delay slot; it is one `=` in the source.

### THE SECOND WORD: A GIV INITIALISER IS A COPY ONLY IF THE ARRAY BASE IS ALREADY IN A PSEUDO

Same function, same day, the other word. The target's preheader is
`addu $v1, $v0, $zero` -- the walked pointer copied off a base that was
materialised BEFORE the loop guard (`lui` before the `blez`, `addiu` in its
delay slot). `loop.c`'s `strength_reduce` emits a giv's initialiser with
`emit_iv_add_mult (initial_value, mult, add_val, dest, loop_start)`; with
`mult_val` 0 that reduces to `add_val`. If `add_val` is the `symbol_ref`
itself, `force_operand` expands it as `lui`/`addiu` straight into the giv's
register and there is no copy; if `add_val` is a **register**, the initialiser
is `(set giv (reg base))` -- a copy, and the `lui`/`addiu` stay where the
source put them, which is before the loop's entry test.

The only way to get the base into a pseudo is to say so in C:

| spelling | words | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| `D_80028570[i][6]` | 18 | 18 |
| `s32 (*p)[10] = D_80028570;` then `p[i][6]` | **19** | 10 |
| `s32 *p = &D_80028570[0][0];` then `p[i * 10 + 6]` | **19** | 10 |
| `s32 *p = D_80028570[0];` then `p[6]; p += 10;` | 18 | 19 |

The last row is the useful negative: walking the pointer in the source makes
`p` the biv itself, loop.c has no giv to initialise, and the base is
materialised directly into `p` -- the `lui`/`addiu` move to the very top of
the function and the copy never exists. **Indexing off a base pointer and
walking a pointer are not the same shape**; the target does the first and lets
loop.c produce the second.

Combining the two levers is what landed it: index off a `s32 (*p)[10]` base
AND assign the quotient back to the sum. Each alone is 19/10 or 18/18.

## A `while` LOOP'S DUPLICATED GUARD IS REMOVED BY CROSS-JUMPING, NOT BY BLOCKING `duplicate_loop_exit_test` -- AND THE MERGE NEEDS TWO IDENTICAL INSNS, SO THE POINTER BUMP MUST SIT IN THE TEST

A string-walking loop spelled

    while (*s != 0) { s++; len++; ... }

comes out three words longer than the target, with a guard copy of the test
(`lbu`/`nop`/`beqz`) above the loop where the target has a single `j` straight
to the bottom test. The natural reading is that `duplicate_loop_exit_test`
(jump.c:2341, called from jump.c:661) fired when it should not have, and that
the lever is one of its bail-outs -- a `CODE_LABEL`, a `CALL_INSN`, or a
`NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG`/`BLOCK_BEG`/`BLOCK_END`/`LOOP_CONT` note in the scanned
range (jump.c:2369-2398).

**It is not.** Measured on `func_80022BE8` in `ovl_main_80020000`: the `.jump`
dump shows `duplicate_loop_exit_test` firing in the 27-word spelling AND in
the 24-word exact match, identically -- `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_VTOP` appears and the
old test label is gone in both. Two facts make its bail-outs unreachable from
the loop form:

- the scan starts at `NEXT_INSN (JUMP_LABEL (next_nonnote_insn (loop_start)))`
  and stops at `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END` (jump.c:2365-2368), so it sees **only the
  rotated exit test**, never the body. BLOCK notes around a declaration block
  in the body are outside it.
- `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_CONT` is always emitted *before* the test label, so it is
  always outside the scanned range. A plain `while` gets one too --
  `expand_end_loop` emits it at `start_label` when there is no separate
  continue point (stmt.c:2287-2289) -- and for a `for` the note sits with the
  increment, still ahead of the test label. Spelling the inner loop as a `for`
  with `s++` as its increment therefore changes nothing: 28 words, measured.

What actually removes the guard is **cross-jumping in `jump2`**
(`jump_optimize (insns, 1, 1, 0)`, toplev.c:3690). At jump.c:2133-2160, a
conditional jump whose target follows an opposing jump that comes back here --
exactly the guard's `beqz -> loop end` against the bottom test's
`bnez -> body` -- is handed to `find_cross_jump (insn, x, 2, ...)`.
`find_cross_jump` (jump.c:2581) walks **backward** from both conditional jumps
and **stops at the first mismatching pair**; it needs `minimum` = 2 matching
insns. On success the guard's conditional jump is rewritten as an
unconditional one (jump.c:2156-2160) and a fresh label is dropped in front of
the shared tail -- which is the target's `j .L80022C18`.

So the lever is which insn sits immediately before each conditional jump:

| spelling | last two insns of guard | last two of bottom test | words | DIFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `while (*s != 0) { s++; ... }` | `lbu`, `len = 0` | `lbu`, `last = i` | 27 | 23 |
| `for (len = 0; *s != 0; s++)` | `lbu`, `len = 0` | `lbu`, `last = i` | 28 | 23 |
| `while (*s++ != 0) { ... }` | `lbu`, `addiu s` | `lbu`, `addiu s` | **24** | **0** |

With `s++` in the body, `sched1` fills the load delay after each `lbu` with
whatever is free -- `len = 0` in the guard block, `last = i` in the test block
-- so the very first backward pair differs and the scan breaks at length 0;
not even the identical `lbu` is reached, because a cross-jumped tail must be
contiguous. With `s++` in the test it is part of both copies, both tails end
`lbu` + `addiu`, two insns match, and the three words collapse.

Corollary for diagnosis: an "extra guard copy of a loop test" is a
**cross-jumping** residue, not a `duplicate_loop_exit_test` residue. Check
whether the guard and the test end in the same two insns before looking for a
note that blocks the duplication. And `last = i` being sunk to the bottom
block is a symptom of the same `sched1` delay fill, not an independent
problem: it is sunk in the exact match too.

## A DUPLICATED FAIL BODY IS WHAT PUTS IT IN cse1's PATH -- cse CAN ONLY SHARE A `%hi` WITH A BLOCK IT REACHES, AND IT REACHES ONE ONLY ACROSS A **ONE-USE** LABEL

Measured on `func_80021298` (ovl_main_80020000, 57 words, landed MATCH).

The park was 58 words / 23 DIFF and the whole extra word was one
`lui %hi(D_800287C8)`. The function reads `D_800287C8` at the top and writes
it from three different arms; the target has **one** `lui`, in `$s3`, shared by
all five references. The park's `st == 1` fail block re-materialised its own.

**cse1 is the only pass that can share it, and it shares it only inside one
run.** `cse_end_of_basic_block` (`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:8056`)
scans `while (p && GET_CODE (p) != CODE_LABEL)` -- it stops at **every** code
label, not just a multiply-used one. (An earlier note in this file said
otherwise; that was wrong.) What makes the runs longer than one basic block is
the path extension below it, at `cse.c:8151`: a conditional jump is followed
when

    LABEL_NUSES (JUMP_LABEL (p)) == 1 && NEXT_INSN (JUMP_LABEL (p)) != 0

and the label is preceded by a `BARRIER` (`follow_jumps`) or the jump merely
branches around a block nothing else enters (`skip_blocks`). Both flags are on
in this build -- the `.s` header prints `-fcse-follow-jumps`
`-fcse-skip-blocks`. cse then re-runs from the same start with the branches
decided differently, which is why `-da`'s `.cse` dump prints several
`;; Processing block from 2 to N` lines. A block is reached with the first
block's table if it lies on **any** of those paths.

So the rule for a shared `%hi`: every conditional jump on some path from the
function's first insn to that block must have a **single-use** target label.
A fail block shared by two tests has a two-use label and is unreachable for
cse, whatever the source shape -- `&&` with an `else`, `if (a) { if (b) {...} }`
with the fail body after it, and a `switch` all measured 58 words / 23 DIFF
with two `lui`s, because the early `jump_optimize` merges the two adjacent
one-use labels the nested form emits into one two-use label.

**Writing the fail body twice, once per test, is what fixes it.** Each copy
then has a one-use label, cse reaches both, there is one `lui` for the whole
function, and jump2's cross-jumping merges the copies back into one block --
`find_cross_jump (insn, target, 2, ...)` down the `jump_chain` of the shared
`out` label (`jump.c:2198`) matches both insns and then hits the copy's own
`CODE_LABEL`, which spends the last of `minimum` (`jump.c:2619`), so the first
copy collapses to a bare `j` and is tensioned away. The surviving block is the
target's three words.

**But the copies must not be able to merge with the `out` label's predecessor
first, and a trailing `goto` is how you stop that.** `jump.c:2188` tries
`find_cross_jump (insn, JUMP_LABEL (insn), 1, ...)` *before* the `jump_chain`
loop, and `minimum` is 1 there, so one identical insn is enough. Here the
`st == 3` arm also ends `D_800287C8 = 0;` and sits immediately before `out:`,
so each fail copy's trailing store was stolen into *its* block and each copy
lost a word to the merge: 58 words / 25 DIFF, two blocks of `j out` with
`r = 5` in the delay slot. Putting the `default` arm's `r = 5;` in a labelled
block **between** the `st == 3` arm and `out:`

    three:
        ...
        D_800287C8 = 0;
        goto out;
    def:
        r = 5;
    out:
        return r;

makes the insn before `out:` an `addiu $s1, 5` instead, the `minimum`-1 compare
fails on the first pair, and the copy-to-copy merge runs instead. 57 words,
MATCH. The `goto out;` survives the early `jump_optimize`'s
jump-to-next-label deletion precisely because `def:` is in the way, and the
`def` block is later folded back inline: `j def` with an empty slot steals
`r = 5` from its own target and retargets past it, which is how the default
arm comes out as `addiu $s1, 5` in the dispatch `beq`'s delay slot followed by
`j <epilogue>`.

Measurement table, all `ovlverify.py` on this one function, target 57 words:

| spelling | words | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| plain `if`/`else if` chain | 56 | 44 |
| `st != 1` first | 56 | 44 |
| fully nested `!=` | 56 | 44 |
| `switch` | 58 | 23 |
| single-fail `goto` chain (the park) | 58 | 23 |
| duplicated fail bodies, inline (`if`/`else if`/`else`) | 58 | 36 |
| duplicated fail bodies out of line, no `def:` | 58 | 25 |
| duplicated, `D_800287C8 = 0;` before `r = 5;` | 57 | 2 |
| duplicated, `st == 3` arm's two stores swapped | 57 | 2 |
| duplicated out of line + trailing `def:` block | **57** | **0** |

Two cautions this cost:

- **The two 57/2 rows are the same discovery read from the two sides, and
  neither is reachable.** Both break the `minimum`-1 merge by making the last
  insn of one of the two blocks differ -- which also changes the order the
  target prints. sched2 runs at `toplev.c:3661`, *before* the cross-jumping
  `jump_optimize (insns, 1, 1, 0)` at `toplev.c:3690`, so there is no later
  pass to put the pair back: whatever order blocks the merge is the order you
  emit. Only a change to what sits *between* the two blocks escapes that.
- **A merged tail and an unmerged tail can be byte-identical, so the merge is
  not visible in the listing.** After a merge the copy is `addiu; j LNEW` with
  an empty slot; `fill_simple_delay_slots` then takes the preceding `addiu`
  into the slot (two words) rather than stealing from the target, because the
  backward scan at `reorg.c:3067` runs first and the forward "insns from
  beyond" path at `reorg.c:3153` is explicitly closed to a `simplejump_p`. So
  a merged block is always a word shorter here, and `addiu / j / sw` in the
  listing means the merge did *not* happen.

## `;; N regs to allocate:` IN `.greg` IS THE WHOLE ANSWER FOR CALLEE-SAVED REGISTERS -- AND `allocno_compare` IS global.c's, NOT local-alloc's

Measured on `func_80021B98` (ovl_main_80020000, -G0, 45 words), 11 DIFF to
**0**, landed MATCH 2026-11-01.

**Read this before any local-alloc reasoning about an `$s` register.** A value
that is live across a call is live across a basic-block boundary, so it is
never a local-alloc quantity at all: `local_alloc` only handles pseudos with
`reg_basic_block[i] >= 0` (local-alloc.c:472). Every `$s0`-`$s5` assignment in
a function with calls is global-alloc's, and global-alloc has no suggestion
phase, no `combine_regs`, and no `qty_compare_1`. The park for this function
named the local-alloc suggestion phase as the mechanism and that was simply
the wrong pass.

**The dump line that settles it.** `.greg`'s first line is

    ;; 6 regs to allocate: 85 82 84 86 83 81

which is `allocno_order` after `qsort (…, allocno_compare)` (global.c:546),
