and the `;; Register dispositions` line two lines later was, for this
function,

    81 in 21  82 in 17  83 in 20  84 in 18  85 in 16  86 in 19

i.e. the sort order read off left to right IS `$s0, $s1, $s2, …`. That is not
a coincidence: `find_reg` takes the first hard register not in `used`
(global.c:965-991), MIPS 2.7.2 defines no `REG_ALLOC_ORDER`, every one of
these six allocnos conflicts with every other and with the call-clobbered
set, and the copy/preference refinements that follow (global.c:1006-1073) can
only move `best_reg` to another register of the same class that is also free,
of which there is none. So **for a clique of callee-saved allocnos the sort
order is the register numbering, and the one line of `.greg` is the entire
diagnosis.** No `--full` diff and no priority arithmetic by hand is needed to
find out WHICH value has to move; only to find out by how much.

**The priority.** `allocno_compare` (global.c:587-608) is

    floor_log2 (allocno_n_refs) * allocno_n_refs / allocno_live_length
        * 10000 * allocno_size

with ties broken on the allocno number, i.e. ascending pseudo number.
`allocno_size` is `PSEUDO_REGNO_SIZE` (global.c:419) and so is 1 for every
single-word mode on this target, exactly as for `qty_size` -- see
"`qty_size` IS IN WORDS, NOT BYTES". `allocno_n_refs` is the SUM of
`reg_n_refs` over the pseudos in the allocno and `allocno_live_length` is the
MAX of their `reg_live_length` (global.c:421-423), both straight out of the
`Register NN used X times across Y insns` lines at the top of `.lreg`, so the
two dumps together give every input.

For this function those lines were

| pseudo | role | refs | length | priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 85 | `fd` | 5 | 17 | 0.5882 |
| 82 | `n` | 5 | 19 | 0.5263 |
| 84 | `r` | 3 | 18 | 0.1667 |
| 86 | the `-1` | 3 | 18 | 0.1667 |
| 83 | `off` | 3 | 22 | 0.1364 |
| 81 | `buf` | 2 | 32 | 0.0625 |

and the target wants `r` in `$s1` and `n` in `$s2`, so `r`'s priority has to
land strictly between 0.5263 and 0.5882. **Solve for the reference count
before trying a spelling.** `floor_log2(R) * R / 18` is in that window for
`R = 5` and for no other value: `R = 4` gives 0.444, `R = 6` gives 0.667 and
takes `$s0` off `fd`. The lever is "give `r` exactly two more references",
and it was reached in one step instead of by guessing.

Note how coarse the knob is. `floor_log2` means 3 -> 4 references multiplies a
priority by 2.67 and 4 -> 5 only by 1.25, so the gap you can actually hit
depends on which side of a power of two the count starts; and because the
divisor is a live LENGTH, a shape change that moves a set by two insns is the
same size of lever as a whole extra reference.

### A `return` WEIGHTED BY TWO NESTED DEGENERATE LOOPS

The two free references came from "A degenerate loop AROUND ONE STATEMENT
weights that reference by 2", nested, around the `return` alone:

```c
    do
    {
        do
        {
            return r;
        } while (0);
    } while (0);
```

`basic_block_loop_depth` counts the `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG`/`END` pairs
(flow.c:447) and `propagate_block` adds `loop_depth` rather than 1
(flow.c:2122 and three sibling sites), so two nested notes weight the single
`(set (reg:SI 2 v0) (reg 84))` by **3** and `reg_n_refs` goes 3 -> 5 with no
insn added anywhere. `for (;;) { for (;;) { return r; } }` and
`while (1) { while (1) { return r; } }` are byte-identical to it; nested
`if (1)` is inert, as the parent entry says.

**Where the wrapper goes matters as much as how deep it is**, and that is the
new part. All of these are 45 words:

| spelling | `r` refs/len | DIFF |
|---|---|---|
| plain `return r;` | 3 / 18 | 11 |
| ONE degenerate loop round the `return` | 4 / 18 | 11 |
| nested `if (1)` round the `return` | 3 / 18 | 11 |
| **two nested loops round the `return`** | **5 / 18** | **0** |
| THREE nested loops round the `return` | 6 / 18 (takes `$s0`) | 15 |
| two nested loops round the `return`, plus `do { r = 0; } while (0)` | 5 / 18 | 6 |
| one loop round the `r = ... == n` statement too | 5 / 18, but `n` 7 and `fd` 6 | 17 |
| one loop round everything after the `open` | 5 / 18, but `n` 9 and `fd` 9 | 15 |
| `r = 0;` moved after the `open`, one loop round the `return` | 4 / 15 | 44 words, 38 |

The `do { r = 0; } while (0)` row is the one to learn from: it has the correct allocation -- all
six registers right, which is why it is 6 and not 11 -- but the loop note
sitting next to `r = 0` in the prologue block splits it, and sched1 then
emits the seven `sw`/`move`/`li` prologue words in a different order. **A
degenerate loop is a block boundary wherever you put it (see that entry), so
put it round the one statement whose reference you want and nothing else.**
Wrapping an enclosing block weights every reference inside it, including the
rival's: one `do { } while (0)` round everything after the `open` took `n`
from 5 references to 9 and `fd` to 9 (15 DIFF), and one round just the
`r = ... == n` statement took `n` to 7 and `fd` to 6 (17 DIFF) -- the same
permutation problem one notch along.

**The negative that forces the device.** The natural ways to mention `r`
again are all constant-propagated away before flow ever counts them, because
`r` is a known 0 at every point above the read block:

```c
    if (off == r || func_8006A0B4(fd, off << 7, 0) != -1)   /* 11 DIFF */
    if (off == 0 || func_8006A0B4(fd, off << 7, r) != -1)   /* 11 DIFF */
```

Both leave `.lreg` and `.greg` BIT-IDENTICAL to the plain form -- cse1
substitutes `(const_int 0)` and the reference never exists. This is the
"A DEAD reference is still a reference" lever failing for the reason that
entry gives: the mention has to survive cse, and a provably-constant local
cannot provide one. `.cse`'s own run boundaries say where the dead zone ends
(`;; Processing block from 2 to 52` here, so cse knows `r == 0` through the
whole lseek arm and only loses it at the read block's label), and `r` is not
live in that block until its own `sltiu` sets it, so there is nowhere a
surviving reference could be placed either. With no legal spelling available
the loop notes are the only lever, which is why this landed as a device.

**One more reading note.** `addu $a2, $sN, $zero` for a literal `0` argument
is NOT a reference to whatever lives in `$sN`. The insn is
`(set (reg:SI 6 a2) (const_int 0))` right through `.greg`; a post-reload pass
between `.bp` and `.sched2` rewrites the constant to a register that already
holds it. So a move out of a callee-saved register into an argument register
can be worth zero references, and counting it as one invents a reference the
allocator never saw.

## THE `lui` TEMP REGISTER TELLS SYMBOL FROM CONSTANT ADDRESS IN A *REGISTER* LOAD -- AND WRITING `p + 4` INLINE IS A LOCAL-ALLOC/GLOBAL-ALLOC LEVER

Measured on `func_80025F0C` (ovl_main_80020000, -G0, 60 words), 30 DIFF to
**0**, landed MATCH 2026-11-01. Three findings; the park named none of them.

### 1. A word load from a constant address uses the DESTINATION as the `lui` temp

`docs/addressing-and-translation-units.md` says an access with no index is
byte-identical either way. That is true only when the base is the assembler's
`$at` (a store through `lui $at,%hi` / `sb %lo($at)`). **When the destination
is a register, the two forms differ in the base-register field**, which is not
masked, so `ovlverify` sees it:

    extern s32 D_8001022C;        lui $v0, %hi(D_8001022C)
                                  lw  $a0, %lo(D_8001022C)($v0)
    *(s32 *) 0x8001022C           lui $a0, 0x8001
                                  lw  $a0, 0x22C($a0)

Through a symbol, the address is legitimised into a **separate `high` pseudo**
before the load (`(set (reg H) (high sym))` + `(set (reg a0) (mem (lo_sum H
sym)))`, visible in `.sched`), and `H` is a two-reference quantity that crosses
no call, so `find_free_reg` gives it the lowest non-fixed register, `$v0`
(local-alloc.c: `used` starts as `fixed_reg_set` when
`qty_n_calls_crossed == 0`). The load's own destination is already the hard
`$a0`, and local-alloc never ties the two, because the tie loop only considers
operands that are themselves a REG or SUBREG and this one is the MEM
(local-alloc.c:1324-1409). With a constant address there is no `high` pseudo at
all: `0x80010000` is materialised into the destination and `0x22C` rides along
as the displacement. splat renders both as `%hi`/`%lo`, so the listing looks
the same -- **read the base register, not the relocation syntax.** Same for
`*(s16 *) 0x80010208` against `extern s16 D_80010208`. The park had both of
these recorded as symbols; they are constants, and that was two of the two
remaining DIFF.

### 2. `p + 4` written INLINE at every call site is a register lever, not a wash

One local `u8 *s = p + 4;` spanning the branch is ONE pseudo whose references
are in several blocks, so `reg_basic_block` is global and it is global-alloc's
(local-alloc.c:472): it lands in `$s1` and `n`, which local-alloc does get,
takes `$s0`. Written inline at each site, cse1 gives it **one pseudo per
extended basic block** -- one for the uses above the `if`, one for the uses
below the join -- and both are block-local, so both are local-alloc's. The
first outranks `n` on `qty_compare`, takes `$s0`, and pushes `n` to `$s1`,
which is the target's allocation. `.lreg`'s `in block N` suffix on the
`Register NN used X times across Y insns` line is the whole diagnosis: a
quantity printed with `in block N` never reaches `.greg`'s
`;; N regs to allocate` list. 61w/31 for the local, 60w/4 inline.

### 3. A TERNARY puts the shared call's `$a0` setup ABOVE the branch -- worth one word

`expand_call` expands every argument value (calls.c:1602-1667) before it loads
any hard register (calls.c:2462), in argument order. So for

    func_80069E38(p + 4, D_80010208 != 0 ? D_80028294[1] : D_80028294[2]);

`p + 4` is computed into a fresh pseudo **before** the COND_EXPR emits the
branch. cse1 rewrites that insn to a copy of the first `p+4` quantity rather
than deleting it, and the copy survives to `.sched` because combine's LOG_LINKS
do not cross the block boundary to its only use. That use is `$a0 = <copy>` at
the shared call, so local-alloc hands the copy `$a0` itself through
`qty_phys_copy_sugg` (local-alloc.c:1866-1888) -- and then the copy IS
`addu $a0, $s0, $zero`, sitting in the block above the branch, where
`fill_simple_delay_slots`' backward scan takes it for the `beqz`'s delay slot
(it skips the two `v0`-conflicting insns of the test and stops at the previous
call's SEQUENCE). The argument move in the join block has become a self-move
and disappears, so the join now BEGINS with the call: its backward scan stops
immediately on the join label and its slot is filled forwards with the
following `addiu $s0, $s3, 0x4` (reorg.c:3139-3316).

Write the same test as an `if`/`else` over a local and both insns stay in the
join: the call's slot eats the `$a0` move and the `addiu` costs its own word.
60w/4 for the ternary, 61w/31 for the statement form, with everything else
identical.

**Corollary worth keeping: a LOAD can never fill any delay slot on this
target.** `mips.md:79-82` gives `dslot = yes` to `type "load"`, and all three
`define_delay`s require `(eq_attr "dslot" "no")` (`mips.md:125-138`). That is
why the `j` over the else arm keeps its `nop` even with `lw $a1, 0x4($s2)`
sitting directly in front of it, and why `fill_slots_from_thread` sets `lose`
on an arm that begins with a load. It is a stronger rule than the `may_trap_p`
one already recorded above -- the trap test never gets a chance to matter for a
load.

## A QImode STORE WIPES CSE'S WHOLE MEMORY TABLE; AN HImode STRUCT STORE DOES NOT

Measured on `func_80023258` (`ovl_main_80020000`, 2026-11-01). The loop body
reads the same byte, `((u8 *)p)[0x7C + i]`, seven times after storing to it,
and the target emits only **four** loads for those seven reads: one load
feeds all four `sh` stores to `->unk_08`, and then each of the three
`(u8 *)...[0]/[1]/[2]` byte stores forces a fresh reload *and* a fresh
recomputation of the arithmetic on it -- even though `[0]` and `[1]` compute
the identical `v * 3 + 0x68`.

The rule is `note_mem_written`, `cse.c:7606-7618`:

```c
else if (cse_rtx_addr_varies_p (written))
  {
    if (! ((MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (written)
            || GET_CODE (XEXP (written, 0)) == PLUS)
           && GET_MODE (written) != QImode))
      writes_ptr->all = 1;
    writes_ptr->nonscalar = 1;
  }
```

A store through a varying address sets `writes->all` -- which makes
`invalidate_memory` (`cse.c:1713-1731`) empty the hash table of *every*
in-memory expression -- unless the store is both (a) in a struct or at a
`PLUS` address and (b) **not QImode**. So:

* `sh` / `sw` to `ptr->field`: `all` stays 0, only `nonscalar` is set, and a
  load whose own expression is not `in_struct` survives it.
* **any** `sb`: `all = 1` unconditionally, because the ANSI rule that a
  `char *` may alias anything is implemented as this blanket exemption. Every
  cached load and every expression computed from one dies with it.

Two consequences for spelling a function:

1. A sequence of 16/32-bit struct stores does **not** cost you a reload of an
   unrelated byte load sitting between them, so a single C read reused across
   several such stores is the wrong source shape if the target reloads -- and
   a target that reloads once and uses the value several times across `sh`
   stores wants a **local assigned once**, not the expression repeated.
2. Repeating the expression across `sb` stores is free of charge in the sense
   that it is what the compiler does anyway: a local would *not* reproduce the
   reload, so when the target reloads around byte stores, repeat the
   expression.

On `func_80023258` this was the whole difference between 70 DIFF and 32 DIFF.
The park had the expression written out at all seven uses (8 loads, with the
3 extra loads sitting in load-delay slots so the WORD COUNT was unchanged and
the symptom was invisible in the length); the target needed one extra local
holding a single re-read for the four `sh` stores and the expression repeated
for the three `sb` stores. Note that the re-read must be a **different**
variable from the one the preceding `if`/`else` produced, or it inherits that
pseudo and its register.

### Corollary: the load count feeds back into the register allocation

Dropping those three redundant loads removed three references from the
stride-1 pointer giv, which took it below the stride-4 giv on
`allocno_compare`'s `floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length` (`global.c:587-608`)
and swapped `$a2`/`$a3` to the target's assignment -- with no change to either
giv's spelling. The remaining `$t1`/`$t2` swap (`p` versus the loop counter)
then fell out of the store-pointer parenthesisation below. **A "register
problem" and a "redundant load problem" in one park can be a single problem,
and the loads are the upstream half.**

## STORE-POINTER PARENTHESISATION, MEASURED END TO END

The `TWO SAME-STRIDE GIVS STAY APART` entry above is correct and this is its
worked case. On `func_80023258` the store pointer, with the byte load spelled
`((u8 *)p)[0x7C + i]` (a pointer giv, `add_val` the register, `0x7C` riding as
the MEM displacement), measured:

| spelling | words for the address | shape |
|---|---|---|
| `(u8 *)p + i + 0x7C` | **1** | `addiu $t0, $a3, 0x7C` -- MATCHES |
| `&((u8 *)p)[i] + 0x7C` | 1 | identical to the above |
| `(u8 *)p + 0x7C + i` | 2 | `addu $2, <i>, 124` then `addu $8, <p>, $2` |
| `&((u8 *)p)[0x7C + i]` | 2 | same two words |
| `&((u8 *)p)[i + 0x7C]` | 2 | same two words |
| `0x7C + (u8 *)p + i` | 2 | same two words |
| `(u8 *)&p[31] + i` | 2 | same two words |
| `&((u8 *)&p[31])[i]` | 2 | same two words |

So the lever is **not** "constant first or last" and **not** array-index
versus pointer-arithmetic notation. It is whether the *variable* part is added
to the base before the constant is: `(base + i) + K` keeps `add_val` the base
register, which `rtx_equal_p` matches against the load's giv at
`loop.c:5739`, and `combine_givs` then expresses the store pointer as
`load_giv + K` -- one `addiu` per iteration, no second induction variable.
Anything that groups `i` with the constant first makes an integer giv whose
`add_val` is a `CONST_INT`, and the base has to be added at the use.

Both two-word forms also leave the extra integer giv alive, which is what held
`p` and the loop counter in the wrong pair of `$t` registers.

## LOCAL-ALLOC PRICES THE *SCHED1* ORDER, AND A ZERO-WORD `asm` MARKER'S sched1 PRIORITY DECIDES WHICH LOAD-DELAY HOLE IT EATS

MEASURED on func_80022774 (`ovl_main_80020000`), 2026-11-01, where 102 of 102
words and every register were already right except a three-word permutation
at the top of the preheader. Two findings, both reusable, and the first one
invalidates a reflex.

**1. The dump you want for births and deaths is `.lreg`'s insn LISTING, not
the listing file.** Pass order is `... sched (sched1), lreg, greg, cse2, bp,
sched2 ...`, so local-alloc runs on sched1's output and **sched2 reorders the
block again afterwards**. `qty_birth`/`qty_death` are `2 * insn_number` and
`2 * insn_number + 1` over local-alloc's own walk of that sched1 order
(`block_alloc`, local-alloc.c:1249-1289), so a quantity's live LENGTH -- the
denominator of `floor_log2(refs)*refs*size/(death-birth)` in `qty_compare_1`
(local-alloc.c:1705) -- is a property of the sched1 chain and NOT of the
emitted code. On this function the emitted order of the two `lbu`s and of the
hoisted invariants differs from the sched1 order they were priced in. Price a
margin off the listing and you will price the wrong lengths.

Worked numbers from that function, three quantities competing for `$v0`,
`$v1`, `$a0` in one basic block (positions are local-alloc `insn_number`):

| qty | members | refs | birth..death | price | reg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hh * 17` | {112, 83} | 5 | 46..55 | 1.111 | `$v0` |
| `unk_17` byte | {85} | 4 | 40..49 | 0.889 | `$v1` |
| `unk_16 * 4` | {100, 82, 125} | 7 | 32..59 | 0.519 | `$a0` |

Moving ONE source statement (`bh = h + 0xA`) one position earlier in the loop
body moved loop.c's hoist of it one position earlier in the sched1 chain,
which shortened the `h` quantity from 13 units to 9 and flipped `h` from
below `hh` to above it -- 7 DIFF to 3. A body-order change with no effect on
the emitted insn set is a live allocation lever, because loop.c hoists
movables in body order (`move_movables` emits each with
`emit_insn_before (..., loop_start)`, so the list order is preserved) and
that order becomes the chain local-alloc prices.

**2. `__asm__("" ::"r"(x))` has sched1 priority 2, one less than a real
consumer of the same value, because `recog` does not know it.** `insn_cost`
(sched.c) ends with

    recog_memoized (used);
    if (INSN_CODE (used) < 0)
      LINK_COST_FREE (link) = 1;
    ...
    if (LINK_COST_FREE (link))
      cost = 1;

so **every dependence INTO an `asm` costs 1**, never the two cycles a MIPS
load result costs a real consumer. `priority` (sched.c:1520) is
`max over LOG_LINKS of priority(pred) + cost - 1`, so a marker reading a
`lbu`'s result gets the load's own priority, 2, where the `sll` that consumes
it gets 3.

That one point of priority decides which load-delay hole the marker falls
into, and therefore the LUIDs sched2 then sorts on. Concretely: sched1 here
fills clocks T-1..T-12 with priority-3 insns and T-14..T-22 with
`LAUNCH_PRIORITY` (0x7f000001) insns released from the queue; T-13 is the one
clock where neither is ready, and a priority-2 marker beats the priority-1
leftovers (loop constants, `i = 0`, the giv initialiser) and takes it.
Scheduling the marker there ALSO delays the load it reads by one clock, which
closes the hole the giv initialiser used in the marker-free build. The giv
then lands early in the chain, its LUID falls below the `lo_sum`'s, and
`rank_for_schedule`'s last tie-break (sched.c:2469, `INSN_LUID (tmp) -
INSN_LUID (tmp2)`, higher luid scheduled sooner and therefore emitted later)
makes sched2 emit it three words too early.

**The cure is to add a second `"r"` operand whose producer has priority 3.**
The marker inherits priority 3, schedules inside the priority-3 pack, and
leaves the hole for the giv. On func_80022774 `"r"(w + 8)` -- a pseudo set by
a hoisted `addiu` -- did it, and the extra reference it buys lands on a
quantity whose register is settled long after the ones being fought over.
Measured there: `"r"(hh)` alone 3 DIFF with the giv permutation,
`"r"(hh), "r"(w + 8)` 3 DIFF with the giv correct and a different residue,
`"r"(hh), "r"(w)` 11, `"r"(hh), "r"(h)` 11. **Pick the second operand for
whose quantity can afford the reference, not for what reads well.**

**Corollary, and it is a hard bound.** A marker that exists only to buy a
reference always costs one RTL insn in its block, so it always eats a hole.
Before reaching for one, check whether the reference is needed at all: on
this function the marker-free body was INSN-FOR-INSN the target with only
two chains' registers swapped, and the question reduced to whether a 3-ref
quantity could outprice a 7-ref one. `floor_log2(3)*3/len_a > floor_log2(7)*7/len_b`
needs `len_b > 4.67 * len_a`, and `len_a` could not be driven below 7 because
the two-clock load delay in front of it always leaves a clock that sched1
fills -- the priority-1 leftovers are ready from the first clock and are never
exhausted, so that gap is never a stall. When the arithmetic says no, the
marker is not a shortcut, it is the only road.

### A REFERENCE MARKER IS THE LOAD'S LAST CONSUMER, SO IT SETS THAT LOAD'S LAUNCH CLOCK -- WHICH IS A SECOND, USUALLY UNINTENDED JOB

MEASURED on func_80022774 (ovl_main_80020000, -G0), 2026-11-01, the landing
that took the project to 1293/1293.

An `__asm__("" ::"r"(x))` placed to add a REFERENCE to `x`'s quantity also
becomes the last consumer of whatever insn produces `x`. sched1 here schedules
a block BACKWARD, and `adjust_priority`'s `birthing_insn_p` branch gives every
newly-ready producer `LAUNCH_PRIORITY`, so chains compact and the only free
choices left are LUID-descending order among equal priorities and
`schedule_select`/`potential_hazard`, which prefers a LOAD among equals. The
consequence: **the clock at which the marker is picked is the clock at which
its operand's load launches.** Move the marker and you move the load.

On that function the two jobs collided over a single scheduling hole. The hole
was the one slot where either (a) the marker could sit, lengthening the
`unk_17` quantity to 13 units so the rival priced 10/13 and kept the natural
statement order, or (b) loop.c's giv initialiser `p + 0xB` could sit, which is
what wins the later sched2 `INSN_LUID` tie-break (`rank_for_schedule`,
sched.c:2469) that orders the preheader's `lui`/`addiu`/`lw`/`addiu`. Giving
the marker an extra operand to raise its priority handed the hole to the giv
and cost the load order instead -- a three-word rotation. The two jobs cannot
share one hole, and a third marker that resolved it was declined as a third
device.

**How to apply.** When a reference marker fixes an allocation but breaks an
order several words away, do not conclude the order is the marker's
unavoidable price (which is what this park's header concluded for three
passes). Ask which load the marker is now gating, and prefer a device that
does not consume anything -- here a hard-register pin, see the next heading --
so the load's launch returns to its natural consumer.

### A PINNED HARD REGISTER NEEDS AN EXPLICIT SHIFT-AND-ADD, BECAUSE `expand_mult` COPIES IT INTO A PSEUDO

MEASURED on the same landing. `register u32 hh __asm__("$3");` fixes the
allocation question outright -- no pricing, no marker, no load gating -- but
only if nothing launders the value back into a pseudo.

`hh * 17` does exactly that: it goes through `expand_mult`, which copies `$3`
into a pseudo for the shift-and-add expansion, and combine then substitutes
that pseudo back into BOTH uses. The pin is silently undone and the score is
11. Writing the multiply out as `(hh << 4) + hh` keeps every reference on the
hard register and the function matches. This is the same effect an earlier
pass recorded as "combine deletes the hard-register copy" and wrongly read as
the pin being unusable.

**How to apply.** A `register ... __asm__("$N")` pin is only as good as the
expressions you spend it in. Any operation gcc expands through a library-style
helper -- a multiply by a non-power-of-two, a divide -- will copy the pinned
register into a pseudo first. Spell those operations out in shifts and adds.

### PASS ORDER CORRECTION: cse2 RUNS RIGHT AFTER loop, BEFORE flow

Verified in `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/toplev.c:3365-3377`, 2026-11-01,
because a brief in this project asserted cse2 ran after `greg` and it does
not. Under `flag_rerun_cse_after_loop` the sequence is: the `loop` dump,
`reg_scan`, `jump_optimize (insns, 0, 0, 1)`, `reg_scan`, then
`cse_main (..., 1, cse2_dump_file)`, then a further `jump_optimize`. All of
that precedes `flow`, which is why the `.cse2` dump still shows pseudos.

The order that matters for anything priced by the register allocator is
therefore: `cse`, `loop`, `cse2`, `flow`, `combine`, `regmove`, `sched1`,
`lreg`, `greg`, `bp`, `sched2`, `jump2`, `shorten`, `dbr`. Note in particular
that `local-alloc` prices the SCHED1 chain, so a live length read off the
emitted listing is measuring the wrong order -- see the heading on that above.

### A BACK-TO-BACK DOUBLE CALL IS AN ARITY WITNESS

Established on `func_8009D20C`, 2026-11-02. Arity is only falsifiable by a
caller, but not every caller can falsify it. A caller that forwards its own
`a0/a1/a2` straight through matches ANY arity up to three *vacuously*: the
argument registers already hold the right values, so the compiler emits no
setup moves and a wrong arity costs nothing. `func_8009CFE0`, this function's
sibling, has two landed callers and both are of that shape -- which is why it
sits at arity 3 with no evidence for the third parameter at all.

What does falsify arity is a caller that calls the same function **twice in a
row**. The first call clobbers `$a0-$a3`, so every argument the second call
reuses has to be reloaded from wherever the caller parked it. Count the
argument-register setup moves before the second `jal` and you have read the
arity directly off the target:

    /* 8009E730 */  jal   func_8009D20C
    /* 8009E734 */   addu $s2, $a2, $zero   <- parks its own a2 (call-clobbered)
    /* 8009E738 */  addu  $a0, $s1, $zero
    /* 8009E73C */  addu  $a1, $s0, $zero   <- sets up a0, a1, and NOTHING else
    /* 8009E744 */  jal   func_8009D20C

Two moves, so two parameters. At arity 3 the callee would need `$a2` restored
from `$s2` and that `addu` is absent, so arity 3 is excluded. Note the parked
`$s2` is not evidence FOR a third argument -- the caller saves it because it
uses its own parameter after the calls.

**How to apply.** When a function's arity is in doubt and its landed callers
all forward registers in place, grep the UNLANDED callers for two `jal`s to it
with no basic-block boundary between them, and count argument setup before the
second. This also runs forward: landing a function at an arity its double-call
caller contradicts will force a spurious `addu $aN, $sN, $zero` into that
caller and make it unmatchable later. Prefer the arity the double call
attests, even when a sibling's signature disagrees.

### TWO OUT-OF-IMAGE GLOBALS WITH ONE SHARED %hi ARE ONE BASE POINTER

Established on `func_800BF1C8`, extended by `func_8009E504`, 2026-11-02. The
companion to the `%lo`-with-register-index lever above: when a function reads
two or more globals that all live outside the loaded image and the listing
shows them sharing a single `lui` -- or shows only one of the two `lui`s with
a register of its own -- they are not two addresses. They are displacements
off ONE base pointer local whose value has a zero low half, typically
`(u8 *) 0x80010000`.

`func_800BF1C8` read `0x80011F81` and `0x80012D5C`. Spelled as two independent
constant addresses it was 7 DIFF, and so was every other spelling of the two
globals -- `extern` array, `extern` scalar, cast of a nearby base, nested or
flattened `if`, block-scope temporaries, fourteen variants in all. The second
global's `lui` is expanded in the *fall-through* block where `$v0` is free, so
its high shares the loaded value's register, and reorg's backward scan then
fills the `bnez`'s delay slot with the `move $a0,$zero` instead, pushing
`i = 0` into the slot and shifting seven words. Read both off one
`(u8 *) 0x80010000` -- one `lui`, every displacement folded into its load --
and the pointer's pseudo lives from the first test into the second block, so
it takes `$v1` while the byte test re-lowers its own `lui` into `$v0`. sched1
leaves that `lui` last in the first block, because its only consumer is in the
next block and it therefore has the lowest priority; reorg takes *it* into the
delay slot and `i = 0` stays ahead of the test. MATCH against 7 DIFF.

**NEGATIVE PRECONDITION, added 2026-11-04 after two agents reported this
lever as a false positive on their groups.** The shape is "the listing shows
ONE `lui` serving several accesses". It is NOT "two globals whose addresses
happen to share a high half". Two globals 2 bytes apart still get **two
separate `lui`s** when the compiler builds two distinct
`(high (symbol_ref ...))` rtxes -- cse never unifies them, because they are
different SYMBOL_REFs and SYMBOL_REF is compared by pointer identity. Measured
on `func_800A47A8`: `D_80100D88` and `D_80100D8A` both assemble to
`lui 0x8010` and the target emits one `lui` each. So:

* **Lever applies:** ONE symbol reached at several `%lo` displacements off a
  single `lui` -- e.g. `func_800A3918`'s single `lui $a0, %hi(D_80100D8A)`
  serving four `%lo` accesses, which is also why that function's address-take
  count comes out ODD.
* **Lever does NOT apply:** two DIFFERENT symbols that merely share a high
  half. `leverpick` matches on the address arithmetic and cannot tell these
  apart, so check the listing's `lui` count before spending a measurement.

**The base local must be one per basic block, assigned after the calls.**
Measured on `func_8009E504`, which reads a byte table at `0x80010980` and a
0x54-stride record table at `0x80010A94`. One function-scope base shared by
two arms is 5 DIFF on register names alone. Assigning it at the *top* of its
block rather than after the arm's calls hoists the `lui` above them, which
buys it a callee-saved register -- `lui $s3`, an extra `sw $s3`, frame 0x28
instead of 0x20 -- and costs 135 words / 127 DIFF. Declare it inside the arm,
assign it after the calls, one per block.

**Corollary, measured the same day: a CONST_INT address materialisation is not
eligible for a branch delay slot.** `lui`+`ori`, or a bare `lui $v0,0x8001`,
written as a constant will not be taken into a slot -- forcing the slot open
with that spelling gave 139 words with a `nop` in it. A compiler-split
`%hi`/`%lo` pair is eligible. So **a `lui` sitting in a delay slot is positive
evidence for the split form**, i.e. for a base pointer or a real symbol, and
against a constant address.

**How to apply.** Count the `lui`s against the number of out-of-image globals.
Fewer `lui`s than globals, or a `lui` in a delay slot, means one zero-low-half
base pointer local with the offsets written into the index expressions. One
per basic block, assigned after any calls in that block. `search.py` will not
find this: 21 candidates across 17 transform families improved on none of the
7-DIFF spellings, because no local rewrite reaches a declaration-shape change.

### cc1psx EMITS `.align 3` FOR JUMP TABLES, WHICH CAN BLOCK A PERFECT BODY

Found on `func_800BF1C8`, 2026-11-02, and the reason it is parked at 0 DIFF.
A switch with at least `CASE_VALUES_THRESHOLD` (5) cases gets a real jump
table instead of an if-else chain, and cc1psx emits that table into `.rdata`
preceded by `.align 3` -- 8-byte alignment. If the function also has a rodata
constant of its own, the constant is emitted first, and whenever it leaves the
section offset at 4 mod 8 the table gets four bytes of padding that the
original build does not have.

`func_800BF1C8` has a 16-byte `s16 box[2][4]` initialiser at offset 0x1164 and
its table at 0x800898D4, which is 4 mod 8. `.text` came out byte-identical in
both content and size (0x44a9c either way) and every function in the unit read
0 differing, but `.rodata` grew 0x2524 -> 0x252c and the overlay 0x101b800 ->
0x101b810, failing with `size differs by +0x10`.

**CORRECTED AND NARROWED 2026-11-02, after screening every jump-table stub in
the unit.** The sentence this lever was read as -- "the next jump table
attempted is the next one to hit it" -- is wrong, and it was blocking about
900 words of ordinary work. `.align 3` only ADDS anything when the table's
address is 4 mod 8; at 0 mod 8 it emits nothing at all and the trap cannot
fire. The screen is one command:

    for f in $(grep -l 'jtbl_' asm/nonmatchings/ovl_town/func_*.s \
                 | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/.s$//'); do
      grep -q "INCLUDE_ASM(\"asm/nonmatchings/ovl_town\", $f)" csrc/ovl_town.c || continue
      a=$(grep -oE 'dlabel jtbl_[0-9A-F]+' asm/nonmatchings/ovl_town/$f.s \
            | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9A-F]{8}')
      printf '%-16s jtbl_%s  addr%%8=%d\n' $f $a $(( 0x$a % 8 ))
    done

Run over `ovl_town` on 2026-11-02 it reported **fifteen stubs at 0 mod 8 and
only two at 4 mod 8** -- `func_800BEBA4` and `func_800BF1C8`, the park. So
`func_800B7B8C` (187 words), `func_800B83DC` (131), `func_800B7F8C` (121),
`func_800B8B00` (100), `func_800B7E78` (69), `func_800B85E8` (147, parked),
`func_800B8E08` (139, parked) and the rest are ordinary work. It also settles
what the park section had flagged as an open question: `func_800B8E08` is at 0
mod 8, so its 5 DIFF is searchable and not toolchain-blocked.

Note also that `func_800BF1C8`'s own listing carries NO `dlabel D_...` in its
rodata block -- the constant that pushes its table is a local `s16 box[2][4]`
INITIALISER, which gcc emits into `.rdata` and splat never names. So "does it
own a rodata constant" cannot be answered by grepping the listing for
`dlabel`; the alignment test can, and is the one to run.

**How to apply.** Before taking on a stub whose listing has a `jtbl_` symbol,
run the screen above. At 0 mod 8 proceed normally. At 4 mod 8, check whether
the function emits a constant of its own -- including a local array
initialiser, which the listing does not show -- and if it does, no C spelling
will land it: the
array must be a gcc-emitted initialiser for the `lwl`/`lwr` stack copy to
appear, so the table always follows at the same offset and always gets padded.
Park it and note that the fix is in the toolchain. This unit had no other
gcc-emitted jump table, so the first one to be attempted will hit this.

### A BLOCK MOVE FORCES ITS ADDRESS WHOLE; A SCALAR ACCESS KEEPS ITS %lo

Established on `func_8009F4C0`, 2026-11-02. One function can legitimately
carry BOTH spellings of the same constant base, and the listing tells you
which goes where. `emit_block_move` calls `copy_addr_to_reg` on the
destination, so a whole-record assignment at a constant address emits the full
address with `lui`/`ori` plus an `addu`:

    ((UnkTownItemRec *)0x80010A80)[m] = D_80100AF8;   /* lui/ori 0x80010A80 */

while the byte and word accesses three lines later must be written off a base
local to keep the `%lo` in the displacement:

    c = (u8 *)0x80010000;
    *(u8 *)(c + m * 0x54 + 0xAC3) = i;                /* lui 0x8001; sb 0xAC3(reg) */

Spelling the scalars as constant addresses instead -- `*(u8 *)(0x80010983 + i*4)`,
or the `((u8 *)K)[...]` array form, both measured -- materialises the whole
constant every time: **139 words / 134 differing against 133 / 0**. This is the
same lever as "two out-of-image globals sharing a %hi are one base pointer",
confirmed from the other side.

**Two base locals, not one, when the function spans a loop.** With a single
pointer local its `lui` is held in a callee-saved register across all five
calls; the target materialises 0x80010000 twice, once either side of the
record copy's loop, which is also cse's block boundary. One base: 112 DIFF.

### WHICH OF TWO EQUAL LOCALS cse CANONICALISES ON IS DECIDED BY LAST MENTION

Same function, and verified in `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:865-869`.
`make_regs_eqv` makes a copy's register the quantity's canonical register only
if the copy outlives the block AND

    uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[new]] > uid_cuid[regno_last_uid[firstr]]

so when two locals hold the same value, **the one whose LAST mention is later
wins the canonical register**. This is directly observable as a register swap
with everything else already exact.

In `func_8009F4C0` the record index and the slot index are separate quantities:
the X-table index comes from an `lbu` and the 0x54-record index from a copy of
it. Spelled as two variables, the copy's last mention precedes the original's,
the `lbu` register stays canonical, and gcc swaps `$s3`/`$s5` relative to the
target -- **15 differing, every one a register number, with all 133 words and
every opcode, immediate and displacement already correct**. Folding the tail's
read-back index into the SAME variable pushes its last mention past the
original's, the canonical register flips, and the 15 collapse to 2.
Declaration order of the two locals has no effect (measured: identical 15).

**How to apply.** An all-register near-miss on a function that copies one value
into a second local is this lever. Do not reorder declarations -- that is
measurably inert. Change which variable is mentioned LAST, usually by reusing
one of them for a later read instead of introducing a third.

### THE STATEMENT POSITION OF A DEAD-LOOKING COPY IS MEASURABLE

Same function. `m = i;` looks like it could go anywhere, and it cannot: reorg
fills a call's delay slot from the insn immediately before the call, so the
copy's position decides whether the copy or an argument setup lands in that
slot. Holding everything else fixed, the same statement measured **0 differing
immediately before the record copy, 2 before `func_80042640`, and 6 before the
0x981 store**. One place too early and reorg puts `addu $a0, $s2, $zero` in
`func_80042640`'s delay slot instead of the copy.

**How to apply.** When a near-miss is a handful of words around a call and a
plain assignment exists nearby, sweep that assignment through every legal
statement position before reaching for anything structural. It is cheap and the
differing count moves monotonically toward the right slot.

### WHEN THE LIFT IS ONE floor_log2 STEP, THE LOOP WRAPPER IS THE ONLY TOOL

Measured on `func_8008FAC0`, 2026-11-02. This sharpens the "degenerate loop"
entry and the "FREE REFERENCE PAIR" entry by pricing their granularity against
each other. The three ways to add references to a pseudo are not
interchangeable, because they differ in SIZE:

  * `do { ... } while (0)` around a statement -- **+1** reference
    (`flow.c`, `reg_n_refs[regno] += loop_depth`)
  * a self-assignment `x = x + k; x = x - k;` -- **+4** (two refs each side)
  * `else { x = x; }` -- **+0**, because gcc drops the self-copy before flow
    (measured: identical differing count with and without)

`func_8008FAC0` is 136 words / 32 differing with every opcode, immediate,
displacement and branch arm already exact -- a pure one-step rotation of five
`$t` registers, because `dx` wants `$t0` and gets `$t4`. `advise.py --greg`
priced it: `dx` is 7 refs / live 66 / priority 0.212, last of nineteen, and it
needs priority in the window **(0.308, 0.375)**, between pseudo 140 and another
live pseudo. That window is one `floor_log2` step wide:

  * wrapper, +1 ref: 8 refs steps floor_log2 2 -> 3, priority 0.364 -> **MATCH**
  * pair, +4 refs: priority 0.485, overshoots the window, `dx` lands in `$a3`
    -> 19 differing

**How to apply.** Read the needed window off `advise.py --greg` before choosing
the device. If the window spans more than one `floor_log2` step a pair is fine
and is the more robust spelling; if it is one step wide, only the wrapper fits,
and a pair will overshoot into a different register class entirely. Placement
still matters independently: wrapping the wrong statement in this same function
gave 9, 42, and two spellings that changed the word count (137).

Declaration order is worth ruling out first and costs nothing: all six
permutations of this function's locals measured identically at 32, because the
priorities are distinct and there is no tie to break.

### A STRING CONSTANT'S DECLARED SIZE DECIDES WHETHER .rodata SURVIVES

Established on `func_800B5E28`, 2026-11-02, verified at the object level. When
splat cannot attribute a string constant to any other function it migrates the
bytes into that function's OWN listing, so replacing the `INCLUDE_ASM` deletes
the symbol and the C source must define it. The declared size is then
load-bearing, and getting it wrong produces a regression that **passes every
check except the final build**.

`func_800B5E28` owns `D_80089340`, and its listing is explicit:

    .section .rodata
    .align 2
    dlabel D_80089340
        /* BBE0 80089340 */ .asciz "\nw"
        /* 0A770000 */                      <- FOUR bytes
    .align 2                                <- a TRAILING align
    enddlabel D_80089340

while the next record, `asm/nonmatchings/ovl_town/D_80089344.s`, carries no
`.align` of its own and simply follows. Written as a bare string literal gcc
emits `.rdata / .align 2 / .ascii "\nw\000"` -- three bytes, no trailing align
-- and `D_80089344` starts one byte early. Measured at the object level, the
stub build against the literal spelling:

    stub:     0a770000 0503096c    "\nw" + 2 pad, then D_80089344 = 05 03 09 6c
    literal:  0a770005 03096c00    "\nw\0", D_80089344 one byte EARLY

**.rodata's SIZE is unchanged (0x2524) in both**, and the function is 0
differing in .text either way. So this is invisible to `ovlverify`, invisible
to a whole-unit sweep, AND invisible to a section-size check.

The fix is the declared size: `const u8 D_80089340[4] = "\nw";`. The
definition must sit exactly where the `INCLUDE_ASM` was, since that is where
gcc puts a function's own constants in the rodata stream.

**CORRECTED 2026-11-02, after measuring three functions in this family: `[]`
does not ALWAYS break. What decides is the directive of the record that
FOLLOWS yours in the rodata stream.** `[4]` emits `.ascii "\nw\000"` plus
`.space 1`; `[]` emits only the three bytes. Whether that missing pad matters
depends on whether the next record re-establishes alignment by itself:

  * next record is bare `.byte`s, or an `.asciz` with no `.align` -- GAS does
    NOT auto-align these, so the byte loss propagates and every later record
    shifts. This is `func_800B5E28`, whose follower `D_80089344.s` is four
    `.byte` directives. `[]` is destructive there.
  * next record is `.word` or `.half` -- GAS auto-aligns them, so the pad comes
    back and `[]` is harmless. This is `func_800B544C`, whose follower
    `D_800892E8.s` is `.word 0x00000083`. Verified byte-identical at the object
    level with `[]`.
  * next record is a gcc-emitted constant -- it carries its own
    `.rdata / .align 2` and absorbs the loss. This is `func_800B5D70`, whose
    follower is `func_800B5E28`'s now-landed `D_80089340`. Also verified
    byte-identical with `[]`.

**Write `[4]` regardless.** It matches what the listing declares, it measures
identically in the cases where `[]` happens to survive, and it does not depend
on a neighbour that a later landing may replace -- the third case above only
became safe BECAUSE the sibling landed, which is exactly the kind of coupling
not to rely on. The rule "note the byte count and the trailing align, declare
at that exact size" gives the right answer every time; it is only the
explanation of what goes wrong that needed narrowing.

Related, same function: `extern const u32 D_80089308[]` and not
`extern const u8 D_80089308[]`. `move_by_pieces` takes MIN(src_align,
dst_align), so the u8 spelling turns an inline 5-byte lw/sw copy into
lwl/lwr + swl/swr, 132 words against 130.

**The SAME family of bug fails in the opposite direction when the symbol is
SHARED.** Measured on `func_800B5774`, the sibling, 2026-11-02. Where splat
could not attribute a literal because TWO functions use it, the symbol's
`INCLUDE_RODATA` survives the landing of either one -- so writing the literal
in C emits a SECOND copy of those bytes beside the surviving record. Here
`strcpy(buf, "\t7\f4")` is 0 differing in .text and grows `.rodata` from
0x2524 to **0x252c**, shifting every record from offset 0xBA0 on. The fix is to
copy from the existing symbol instead: `memcpy(buf, D_80089308, 5)`.

So the two cases are opposites, and which one you are in is decided by
**whether the symbol has its own `.s` file** -- NOT by how many listings
reference it:

  * no `asm/nonmatchings/<unit>/D_XXXX.s` and no `INCLUDE_RODATA` -> the bytes
    live inside your function's own `.section .rodata` block and disappear when
    you land, so DEFINE the symbol in C at the exact declared size (the `[4]`
    case above; .rodata would otherwise shrink or shift)
  * it has its own `.s` listing and an `INCLUDE_RODATA` -> that record
    survives your landing, so declare it `extern` and copy FROM it; writing the
    literal duplicates the bytes and .rodata GROWS

**CORRECTED 2026-11-02: "referenced only by your listing" is NOT the test, and
using it will make you define a symbol that already has a surviving record.**
`func_800B557C` references `D_800892F0` and `D_800892F4` from nowhere else in
the repo, and splat gave both their own listings anyway; meanwhile the same
function's `D_800892F8` and `D_800892FC` have no listing and had to be defined.
One function, both cases, same reference count. The one-liner:

    ls asm/nonmatchings/ovl_town/D_XXXX.s 2>/dev/null   # exists -> extern
    sed -n '/^\.section \.rodata/,/^\.set noat/p' <func>.s | grep dlabel
    # ^ the symbols listed there are the ones YOU must define

A function can own several: `func_800B557C` owns two, at declared sizes 4 and 8,
and the sizes are read off the listing's own byte comments
(`20000000`, `2020202000000000`), not guessed from the string length.

Both cases are 0 differing in .text and both pass a whole-unit sweep. Read the
`.s` before writing the line, and confirm with the object-level .rodata diff
after.

Both are 0 differing in .text and both pass a whole-unit sweep. Run the grep
before writing the line, and confirm with the object-level .rodata diff after.

**How to apply.** Before landing any stub whose listing contains a
`.section .rodata` block of its own, note that block's byte count and whether
it ends in a trailing `.align`, and define the symbol in C with that exact
declared size. Then verify at the OBJECT level rather than trusting the sweep:

    tools/cdkgcc -O2 -G0 -Iinclude -Ipsyq/include -S -o X.s <merged copy>
    python3 vendor/maspsx/maspsx.py --aspsx-version=2.56 --force-stdin \
      --run-assembler --gnu-as-path=mips64-linux-gnu-as --use-comm-section \
      -G0 -EL -32 -Iinclude -march=r3000 -mtune=r3000 -no-pad-sections -O1 \
      -o X.o < X.s
    mips64-linux-gnu-objdump -s -j .rodata X.o   # diff against the stub build

That is the strongest check available without writing to csrc/, and it is what
should have been run on `func_800BF1C8` before that one was merged.

### AN abs() RESULT THAT SHARES A VARIABLE ACROSS BLOCKS IS WORTH 8 WORDS

Established on `func_800BD688`, 2026-11-02; every line reference below
verified in `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18`. With its own block-local variable
the function sits at 8 differing, every difference a register assignment, and
NO spelling of the arithmetic moves it. Measured: `abs()` once, `abs()` twice,
an explicit `if (d < 0) d = -d;`, a `(u32)` cast, the values or the pointers
hoisted into locals, reversed operands, reversed `||`, de Morgan, the
subtraction pre-folded, the range test as `(u32)(d - 0x200000) > 0x200000`, and
three declaration orders. All 8.

The mechanism is `block_alloc`/`combine_regs`. At the `addu` the allocator
walks the input operands for one that dies there and ties the output to it
(`local-alloc.c:1348ff`), but bails when that input's pseudo is not block-local
-- `local-alloc.c:1831` says so outright: "it is not local to this block or
dies more than once. In either event, we can't do anything with it", the
condition being `reg_basic_block[i] >= 0 && reg_n_deaths[i] == 1` at
`local-alloc.c:472`.

With a private variable the chain val0 -> subu -> abs -> addu becomes ONE
8-reference quantity, which by `qty_compare_1` outranks the `sltu` pair, takes
`$v1` across words 23..33, and pushes the second pointer out of `$v1` into
`$a0`. Sharing the loop's own temporary makes the abs destination multi-block,
the tie is refused, the `addu`'s output joins the CONSTANT instead, and the
listing's allocation is reproduced exactly. WHICH variable it shares with
matters: the loop temp and the frame counter both reached 0, two other live
locals gave 9 and 16.

**`abs()` is also load-bearing for the word count.** `abssi2`
(`config/mips/mips.md:1526`) emits its own delay slot -- it bumps
`dslots_jump_total` and expands to `bgez / nop / negu` when the two registers
are equal, which is the listing's nop. A hand-written `if (d < 0) d = -d;`
lets the scheduler fill that slot and loses a word.

### TWO POINTERS WALKED BY A LOOP WANT AN ARRAY, NOT TWO NAMED FIELDS

Same function. `UnkTown2AE8 *unk_00[2]` reached as `a->unk_00[i]` with a
DECREMENTING index: loop strength reduction then puts the derived pointer's
initialisation at the END of the preheader (`addiu $s1, $zero, 1` before
`addiu $s0, $s2, 0x4`), which is what the listing has. Two named fields plus an
explicit `UnkTown2AE8 **q` walk puts the pointer init first and costs a word --
133 words against 132.

### move_movables' THRESHOLD IS A BUDGET, SPENT 3 PER HOIST IN LOOP ORDER

From `func_800B1DCC`, 2026-11-02, line references verified. `loop.c:1730`
gates each hoist on `(threshold * savings * m->lifetime) >= insn_count`, and
`loop.c:1818` then does `threshold -= 3` with the comment "The more regs we
move, the less we like moving them." So hoists are spent against a shrinking
budget in loop-insn order, and **which invariant you hoist in SOURCE decides
whether a later one gets hoisted at all**. Measured for ovl_town at `-O2 -G0`:
the threshold sits between 58 and 63 -- an `insn_count` of 56/57/58 hoisted the
frame address `$fp + 16`, 59 did not.

**Corollary: `loop` runs BEFORE `combine`, so narrowing a local to `u8` buys
you `insn_count`.** Each zero-extension is still its own RTL insn at loop time.
Three `s32` -> `u8` locals took one loop from 56 to 59 real insns, and that
alone was the difference between 82 words and 0 differing. When a hoist or a
giv reduction is one notch off, the pre-combine insn count is the lever and
declared-type width is the cheapest way to move it. (Dead locals do not work:
cse deletes them and `insn_count` is unchanged -- measured with eight.)

**A `4 * i` DEST_REG giv with `add_val == 0` is ALWAYS rejected.**
`general_induction_var` gives the `ashift` benefit 2, then `loop.c:3963` does
`benefit -= add_cost * bl->biv_count` and zeroes it, so `loop.c:3996`'s
`v->lifetime * threshold * benefit < insn_count` fires regardless of loop size.
A local-array index in a loop is therefore recomputed with an in-loop `sll`
unless you walk an explicit byte offset: `*(s32 *)((u8 *)v + j)` with `j += 4`
is the spelling that produces the stride-4 IV. Five two-step spellings of
`i * 4` all collapsed in cse before they could help.

**And a global's %hi/%lo pair hoisted into a SOURCE local lands BEFORE the
loop's own init statements; one hoisted by move_movables lands AFTER them.**
Both are "before loop_start", but movables are inserted at loop_start while
`for`-init statements are expanded earlier, and sched2 preserves that order.
This is the only lever for preamble ORDER when a loop has both an invariant
address and its own counter init.

### CITATIONS RE-ANCHORED TO THE CDK TREE, AND TWO TIE-BREAKS UPSTREAM LACKS

2026-11-02. Every compiler-source citation in this document was read against
upstream FSF 2.7.2.3 until commit `22ba9e1` made
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18` authoritative -- the SN Systems CDK tree the
build actually compiles with, whose `version.c` reads
`cygnus-2.7.2-970404 SN32.3.7.0004`. All 387 citations here were then
re-anchored mechanically: read what the cited line SAID in the upstream tree,
find that text in the CDK tree, rewrite the number. 331 moved, 38 were already
correct, and 13 could not be located and are listed at the end of this
section -- 12 now, since `sched.c:834` was resolved on 2026-11-02.
Upstream stays as `scratch/gcc-src/gcc-2.7.2.3.tar.gz`, the record of what the
pre-2026-11-02 citations were read against; unpack it beside the CDK tree if a
citation here ever looks wrong.

**The two priority formulas this document leans on are UNCHANGED**, which is
why the allocation levers all still hold. `local-alloc.c`'s is now the macro
`QTY_CMP_PRI` (local-alloc.c:1693-1695) rather than inline arithmetic, but it
is the same expression:

    floor_log2 (qty_n_refs[q]) * qty_n_refs[q] * qty_size[q]
      / (qty_death[q] - qty_birth[q]) * 10000

and `global.c`'s `allocno_compare` (global.c:587) keeps its own form, with
`allocno_size` applied outside the divide rather than inside.

**What IS new in the CDK tree: both comparators gained a deterministic
tie-break that upstream does not have.** `qty_compare_1`
(local-alloc.c:1705-1718) and `allocno_compare` (global.c:587-610) each
compute the priority difference, return it if non-zero, and otherwise fall
through to

    /* If qtys are equally good, sort by qty number,
       so that the results of qsort leave nothing to chance.  */
    return q1 - q2;

Upstream returns `pri2 - pri1` and lets qsort do what it likes with a tie. So
on this compiler **two quantities of equal priority are ordered by quantity
number, lowest first, and that order is stable** -- it is not luck and not
qsort's implementation. Anything in this document that reads "the tie is
broken by..." or treats an equal-priority pair as unpredictable was written
against upstream and should be re-read with this in mind: the tie IS
predictable here, and quantity number is the lever.

**Still unresolved -- read against upstream, not located in the CDK tree.**
Each of these is either genuinely absent or restructured beyond a mechanical
match, so the LINE NUMBER is upstream's and will not resolve. The claim each
supports may still be sound; the citation needs a fresh read before it is
relied on.

    c-parse.c:2062      the file is not in the CDK tree at all
    calls.c:2462        ambiguous, 2 candidates
    combine.c:954       `|| ! REG_USERVAR_P (src)`, restructured; the CDK
                        tree has REG_USERVAR_P(src) at combine.c:976-978
    expr.c:4907         comment reflowed
    function.c:3629     `REG_USERVAR_P (parmreg) = 1;` -- absent
    global.c:607        was `return *v1 - *v2;`; the CDK comparator takes
                        GENERIC_PTR and the tie-break replaces it
    local-alloc.c:1018  comment fragment
    local-alloc.c:1622  was `return *q1 - *q2;`; same, see the tie-break above
    loop.c:3365         comment reflowed
    loop.c:4138         `#ifndef SMALL_REGISTER_CLASSES`; the CDK tree has
                        `#ifdef` at loop.c:842-843, opposite sense
    sched.c:2267        ambiguous, 2 candidates
    stmt.c:3390         `REG_USERVAR_P (DECL_RTL (decl)) = 1;` -- absent

**RESOLVED, 2026-11-02 -- one down, twelve left.** `sched.c:834` was listed as

        && ! (MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (mem) && rtx_addr_varies_p (mem)

`memrefs_conflict_p` itself is at `sched.c:629`, which the doc already had

### A GLOBAL THAT *HOLDS* AN ADDRESS IS NOT A GLOBAL THAT *IS* AN ARRAY

Measured on `func_800B52F4`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. The listing's

    lui $v0, %hi(D_800814A8) / lw $a1, %lo(D_800814A8)($v0) / addiu $a1, $a1, 0x34

is three words because the symbol is a *pointer variable*: `include/structs.h`
declares it `extern u32 D_800814A8;` and `csrc/unk_1C540.c` reads it as
`*(s32 *)(D_800814A8 + 0x124)`. The matching spelling is therefore
`(u8 *)(D_800814A8 + 0x34)` -- load the word, then add. Taking the symbol's own
address instead, `(u8 *)&D_800814A8 + 0x34`, which is what you write for an
`extern u8 X[]`, folds the displacement into the relocation and emits only
`lui / addiu`: **49 words against 50, 36 differing.**

**How to apply.** The `lw` is the tell and it is visible before writing any C:
a global reached through `lui`/`lw` is a pointer to be dereferenced, one
reached through `lui`/`addiu` is the object itself. This is the data-side twin
of the `lui`/`ori` versus `lui`/`addiu` test already recorded for out-of-image
globals.

### A STORED ARGUMENT REGISTER THE PROTOTYPE DOES NOT HAVE IS A FORWARDED PARAMETER -- AND ITS WITNESS IS THE GRANDCALLER

Established on `func_800B5174` and `func_800B5C60`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, after
both had been landed at 0 differing with the wrong arity.

Each stores `$a2` -- `sw $a2, 0x0($v0)` -- and neither body writes that
register anywhere. Their callers `func_800B5AC8` and `func_800B640C` pass that
argument straight through from their own third slot into their **first** call,
so `$a2` is already correct at entry and gcc emits **no** argument-setup insn
for it. Both drivers measure 22 words / 0 differing with two parameters and
with three, identically, so the call site cannot witness the arity in either
direction. The witness is one level further out: `func_800B6508` does
`lw $a0, 0x4($s0) / lw $a1, 0x98($s0) / lw $a2, 0x14($s0)` before each driver's
`jal`.

This completes a family of three, and the three cases need different evidence:

* a MISSING argument move can be cse reusing the incoming register, so it is no
  evidence of a zero-arity call (docs/town-sweep.md);
* a PRESENT move in the `jal`'s delay slot, with the register reloaded on the
  next instruction, forces the arity (`func_800B5D30`, `func_800A652C`);
* a PURE FORWARD costs no move at all, so **an arity question has to be chased
  up the chain until a call site that is not a forward.**

Two spellings reach 0 differing without the parameter and are both wrong.
`register s32 c __asm__("$6")` is a device with nothing left to justify it. A
bare uninitialised `s32 c;` is undefined behaviour that happens to allocate the
pseudo to `$a2` here -- and it is not even reliable: on `func_800B5C60` it comes
out **52 words, 4 differing**, with only the `$a2`/`$a3` roles swapped, because
an uninitialised pseudo is never set, so local-alloc gives it no quantity and
global-alloc assigns it after the three-reference `-0x38` constant has taken
`$a2`.

That last number has a mechanism worth recording on its own.
`QTY_CMP_PRI` (local-alloc.c:1693-1695 in `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18`) is

    floor_log2 (qty_n_refs[q]) * qty_n_refs[q] * qty_size[q]
      / (qty_death[q] - qty_birth[q]) * 10000

and `floor_log2 (1) == 0`, so **any quantity with exactly one reference has
priority 0**, however short its live range -- despite the comment directly above
it ("We give shorter-lived quantities higher priority"). A single-use value can
therefore never outrank a multi-reference constant competing for the same
register, and no local spelling negotiates the register number.

### A SYMMETRIC TWO-CALL `if/else` KEEPS SOURCE ORDER; ONLY AN ARM THAT *RETURNS* INVERTS

Established on `func_800B6508` against `func_800B5D30`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
The lever "AN EARLY `return` IS LAID OUT INLINE" gets read as "a `beqz` to the
second arm means write the inverted test first". That generalisation is wrong,
and this session over-applied it twice.

It holds only when one arm **leaves the function**. gcc emits an early `return`
inline at that point, which forces the other arm out of line. When both arms
fall into a shared tail, the arms are emitted in SOURCE order: the
branch-if-false target *is* the `else`, which is exactly the
`beqz` / fall-through / `j`-over-else shape.

Measured, both at `-O2 -G0`:

* `func_800B6508`, 28 words, two arms that are plain calls. The target `beqz`es
  on the `s16` at `+0x08` to `func_800B5AC8` and falls through to
  `func_800B640C`. Writing the non-zero arm first is **0 differing**; inverting
  it is 28 words / 1 differing.
* `func_800B5D30`, 16 words, one arm `return func_800A652C(p)`. Here the
  inversion IS needed: the natural order
  (`if (D_80082E6A == 1) return D_800D1790;` with the call second) gives the
  same 16 instructions in the other order, **5 differing**.

**How to apply.** Before inverting a test, check whether either arm returns
UNCONDITIONALLY. If neither does, inversion costs you the branch condition and
buys nothing.

**THE REFINEMENT, measured on `func_800CD70C`/`func_800CD87C`, 2026-11-02: a
CONDITIONAL `return` inside an arm does not make it an arm that leaves.** An
arm spelled `if (x) return;` and then falling into the shared tail is a
FALL-THROUGH arm for layout purposes. Writing it first costs a word -- the
branch gcc has to add to get back to the tail -- plus a residue that reads as a
near-miss:

| arm order | func_800CD70C | func_800CD87C |
|---|---|---|
| arms that fall through first, conditional-return arm as the `else` | **92/92, 0** | **94/94, 0** |
| conditional-return arm first (inverted outer test) | 93/92, 35 differing | 95/94, 39 differing |

So the test is unconditional departure, not the presence of a `return` token.
And note the trap-within-a-trap this doc already warns about: 35 differing on a
one-word structural error looks exactly like something worth polishing.

### A HALFWORD FIELD'S READ-MODIFY-WRITE NEEDS NO EXPLICIT TEMP FOR THE NEXT EXPRESSION ON THE SAME FIELD -- AND A USE THAT NEEDS THE SIGN-EXTENDED HALFWORD STILL RELOADS

`func_800CD70C`/`func_800CD87C`, 2026-11-02. A negative result, worth knowing so
nobody spends compiles on it: these two spellings are **byte-identical**, and
not merely equal under `ovlverify`'s mask -- the two objects' disassembly
matches word for word.

    t = (u16)a->unk_86;  a->unk_86 = t + 0x40;  a->unk_72 = t + 0x440;
    a->unk_86 += 0x40;   a->unk_72 = a->unk_86 + 0x400;

Both give `lhu v1,134(s1)` / `addiu v0,v1,64` / `sh v0,134(s1)` /
`lh a0,134(s1)` / `addiu v1,v1,1088` / `sh v1,114(s1)`.

`cse_insn` inserts the stored-to MEM into the SET_SRC's equivalence class --
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:7402`,
`elt = insert (dest, sets[i].src_elt, sets[i].dest_hash, GET_MODE (dest));` --
so the following halfword read of the same address resolves to the register
holding `v1 + 0x40`, and `fold_rtx` folds `0x40 + 0x400` into one
`addiu ... 1088`.

**The other half is the measured part: the `lh` reload for the call argument
survives in BOTH spellings.** The class's member is a full SImode value and the
call argument needs the 16-bit value sign-extended, so that use is not
substitutable. So a reload of a halfword you have just stored, feeding a call,
is NOT a missing temp and NOT a volatile device -- it is what this cse does.
(The insertion is cited; the sign-extension half is reported as a measurement,
with the explanation as inference rather than a located line.)

**And a trap that goes with it.** Swapping the arms of an `if/else` whose arms
are CALLS swaps the `jal` targets as well as flipping the branch condition.
`ovlverify` masks the `jal` words, so the swapped spelling reports "1
differing" and reads as a near-miss worth polishing when it is actually three
words wrong and structurally inverted. Decode the `jal` words by hand --
`0x80000000 | ((w & 0x3FFFFFF) << 2)` -- whenever a candidate's residue is a
single branch-condition word and the function contains more than one call.

### A NARROW PARAMETER THAT IS ONLY EVER TRUNCATED IS WITNESSED AT THE CALL SITE, NOT IN THE CALLEE

Established on `func_800B67A4`, `func_800B68C8`, `func_800B691C` and
`func_800B6580`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. It cost three wrong declarations in one
batch.

When a parameter's only use is a store narrower than a word -- an `sh` into an
`s16` field -- `s16` and `s32` declarations generate **identical callee code**,
both 0 differing, because the value arrives already extended in its incoming
register or stack slot and the `sh` discards the upper half either way.

The declaration is visible in every CALLER. Under `cc1psx -O2 -G0` an `s16`
parameter forces a `sll $N,$N,16` / `sra $N,$N,16` pair per argument
immediately before the argument move or the `sw` to the outgoing slot --
measured on a two-call probe, four shift words for the `s16` prototype and none
for `s32`. So when a callee's narrow-store parameter scores 0 at both widths,
read the caller's listing: **shift pair present -> `s16`; bare `lw`/`sw`/`move`
-> `s32`.**

**CORRECTION, measured on `func_80097AD0`, 2026-11-02: the shift pair is a
SOUND NEGATIVE AND NOTHING MORE.** No pair at the call site does rule `s16`
out. A pair present does NOT establish `s16`, because an `s32` prototype with
an explicit `(s16)` cast on the argument emits the identical
`sll`/`sra 16` pair -- both spellings measured 0 differing in the same
function. So read it as: **no pair -> not `s16`; pair -> `s16` OR an `s32`
prototype whose argument is cast, and the caller's source is what decides.**
Where the callee is already declared in the unit, that declaration wins over
either reading; check it before writing a signature.

On `func_800B691C` the wrong width was in that function's OWN signature, not in
its callee's, and it was worth more than the two shift words: 30 words against
29, 15 differing, with `$s1` and `$s2` exchanged as well, because the
sign-extension lands at the parameter's first int use -- the forward into
`func_800B68C8`, three statements away.

**Unlike an unread parameter, the container build will NOT catch this.** Both
widths link and both produce identical callee bytes; only the caller's own
match catches it.

The converse case is `func_800B512C`, where the parameter is COMPARED rather
than stored: there the `sll`/`sra 16` pair sits at entry, in the callee's own
listing, and is the witness. So the rule is about narrow parameters whose only
use is a truncating store.

### A VALUE THAT IS *STORED* WANTS A TWO-ARM `if/else`; A VALUE THAT IS *RETURNED* WANTS AN ACCUMULATOR

Measured on `func_800B5918` against `func_800B555C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, over
a 28-point grid on the first and a 2-point check on the second. The two
functions sit forty lines apart in the same file and want opposite spellings.

`func_800B555C` (8 words) is a three-way compare feeding a `return`. One
variable seeded 0 with a nested `if/else` and a single `return d` is 0
differing; three early returns give 9 words and 8 differing, because the target
puts 0, 3 and the final move into three branch delay slots.

`func_800B5918` (35 words) picks a sign glyph that feeds a BYTE STORE. There the
accumulator form -- the `func_800B555C` shape -- is 6 and 8 differing, every
ternary polarity is 5 to 6, and only
`if (x > 0) { s[0] = 0x6B; } else { s[0] = 0x6C; }` is 0. For
`dst = cond ? A : B` cc1psx emits branch-if-NOT-cond with the FALSE value in
the delay slot and lands the value in `$v1` when `$v0` still holds the tested
load; the two-arm store emits branch-if-cond with the TRUE value in the delay
slot, one shared store, and reuses `$v0`.

Same function, second half: a hoisted absolute value costs a delay slot.
`f((x >= 0) ? x : -x, 2, buf)` schedules `addiu $a1, 2` ahead of the `bgez` and
leaves its delay slot a `nop`. Reversing the arms, hoisting into
`v = x; if (v < 0) v = -v;`, and duplicating the call under an `if/else` all
give the same 35 words but pull `addiu $a1, 2` down into the `bgez`'s slot: 2
differing each, and the three losers are indistinguishable from each other.

### TWO DISJOINT LIVE RANGES IN ONE DECLARED LOCAL SHARE A REGISTER; TWO LOCALS DO NOT

Measured on `func_800B65D8`, ovl_town, 68 words, 2026-11-02. The loop-local
width `w = func_80048DE8(idx)` and the post-loop delta
`total != 0 ? total - 0x14 : 0` have disjoint live ranges and no conflict with
`$a0`. Written as two separate locals, global.c hands the width `$a0` -- the
first free call-clobbered register, since the CDK tree's
`config/mips/mips.h` defines no `REG_ALLOC_ORDER` and the order is plain
0..31 -- and the delta `$a1` as the outgoing argument: **68 words, 3 differing**,
words 33/35/42 the only differences and every other word exact. Reusing the
SAME declared local for both gives the two ranges one pseudo and one register,
`$a1`: **0 differing**.

This is a rename, not a device, and it was the only thing that moved the
function off its 3-differing floor. `u32`, `u16` and `u8` for `w`, moving its
declaration among the locals, and `if/else` versus `?:` for the delta all stay
at 3; `s16 w` is 69 words / 36 differing and inverting the width test is
69 / 34.

**How to apply.** Three differing words that are all one register on one value
is a hint that two source variables are one.

### A DUPLICATED TAIL IS NOT ONLY A CROSS-JUMP -- IT CHANGES WHICH LOOP INVARIANTS ARE HOISTED

Measured on `func_800B6B10`, ovl_town, 45 words, `-O2 -G0`, 2026-11-02, read off
the `.loop` dumps. A 0x18-iteration loop dispatches on a `u8` kind byte to one
of two freers and then zeroes two fields.

With the zeroing tail factored out below the `if/else-if` and a `continue` in
the default path -- the reader's spelling -- it is **48 words, 39 differing**,
and fourteen variants of that shape all land between 39 and 46. With the tail
DUPLICATED in both arms, letting jump.c cross-jump the copies, it is **45
words, 0 differing**.

The mechanism is `move_movables`' budget, and the dumps print it:

* the factored loop is **25 real insns** and both equality constants become
  hoisted movables (`Insn 35: regno 90 (life 1), move-insn savings 1  moved
  to 142`, and the same for insn 69), so the `1` occupies a FOURTH call-saved
  register;
* the duplicated loop is **28 real insns** and the second hoist is refused by
  name: `Insn 91: regno 111 (life 1), move-insn savings 1 not desirable`. The
  `1` is rematerialised inside the loop and reorg.c steals it into the first
  `bne`'s delay slot as `addiu $v0, $zero, 1`.

`move_movables` tests `threshold * savings * lifetime >= insn_count` and does
`threshold -= 3` after each move. With `savings == lifetime == 1` that is just
`threshold >= insn_count`, so 25 passing twice and 28 passing once **brackets
this build's threshold at 28..30**. Reusable: in an ovl_town loop containing a
call, the first invariant hoist needs about 29 real insns or fewer, and each
further hoist costs 3.

The same insn-count change leaves `biv 81` un-eliminated -- the 25-insn form
prints `biv 81 was eliminated` and compares against a hoisted `a + 96`, the
28-insn form prints `giv of insn 24 not worth while, 0 vs 28` and keeps
`addiu $s1, $s1, 1 / slti $v0, $s1, 0x18`. Hence a diagnostic worth having:
**a loop whose exit test is `slti` on a counter AND which also carries an
`addiu $sN, $sN, 4` has two live induction variables, which means its body was
too big for biv elimination -- it is not a sign of a source pointer walk.**

### loop.c's `combine_givs` MERGES ADDRESS GIVS, SO ONE `addiu $sN, $sN, 4` IS NOT A SOURCE POINTER WALK

Measured on `func_800B59A4` and `func_800B6B10`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
`func_800B59A4`'s target walks `$s1` by 4 with displacements 0x18/0x24/0x30,
which reads exactly like `b++` with `b[6]`/`b[9]`/`b[12]`. Writing it that way
builds **74 words, 58 differing**. The matching spelling is plain subscripts
`b[i + 6]`, `b[i + 9]`, `b[i + 12]` off an UNMODIFIED parameter: loop.c's
`combine_givs` merges address givs that share a `mult_val` into the base
induction variable plus constant displacements. The same goes for two
`addiu $sN, $sN, 0x10` in that loop -- they are `i * 0x10 + K`, not source
accumulators.

`func_800B6B10` adds the prologue half of it. `strength_reduce` emits the
reduced giv's initialisation before `loop_start` AFTER `move_movables` has put
its hoists there, so the giv's `addu $sN, $a0, $zero` lands after any hoisted
constant. Spelling the walk in the source makes it the parameter copy, which
`assign_parms` emits first: 45 words, **6 differing**, all six in that prologue
ordering. **If a candidate differs only in which `sw $sN`/init pair comes
first, the array walk is a giv and belongs in the source as `a[i]`.**

### DECLARATION ORDER FIXES *AGGREGATE* STACK SLOTS ONLY, AND A SLOT IS ROUNDED TO 8 BYTES

Measured on `func_800B59A4` and `func_800B61C0`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. This
narrows the existing rule from `func_800B5774` ("locals are assigned upward in
declaration order") rather than contradicting it.

Two ARRAYS are assigned upward in declaration order and their order is
load-bearing: `u8 *list[3]` before `u8 buf[0x10]` is 0 differing, swapped it is
**75 words, 73 differing**.

An address-taken SCALAR is not. gcc assigns its stack slot when its address is
first taken during RTL expansion, not at its declaration, so it lands ABOVE
every array wherever it is written: moving `s32 n` from after `buf` to before
it, or putting `s32 i` first, leaves `n` at sp+0x38 and still measures 0
differing. **So in a body with one address-taken scalar and two buffers there
are two orderings worth trying, not six.**

And each local's slot is rounded up to 8 bytes, so a buffer's declared size is
witnessed only to within a bucket. `u8 *list[3]` is 0xC bytes and occupies
0x10, so `buf` starts at sp+0x28 for every size tried; `buf`'s own rounded size
then fixes the scalar's offset and the frame -- 8 gives `n` at sp+0x30 and frame
0x50 (16 differing); **0xC and 0x10 both give sp+0x38, frame 0x58, and 0
differing, indistinguishable**; 0x14 and 0x18 give frame 0x60 (16 differing);
0x40 gives frame 0x88 (16 differing). **Scan the size; do not reason about it,
and do not claim a declared size is pinned when two values both match.**

### A STRUCT-ARRAY REFERENCE WHOSE SUBSCRIPT IS A MEMORY LOAD MUST BE CACHED IN A LOCAL POINTER

Measured on `func_800B6094` and `func_800B65D8`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
`&D_8006DE24[p[0]]` spelled out at both use sites around a call gives **81
words, 63 differing** against the target's 75. `p[0]` is a load that the
intervening `jal` invalidates, so cse cannot carry the record address; gcc
hoists only the SYMBOL's `%hi`/`%lo` into a saved register and recomputes
`p[0] * 20 + base` at each use. Caching the record in an `Unk8006DE24 *` emits
the `%hi`/`%lo` pair inline once and keeps the record address in `$s0`.

**The diagnostic is a saved register holding a bare symbol address: that means
you re-indexed where the original cached.** This runs opposite to the usual
"re-dereference rather than cache" advice for this compiler, and the tell is
which value ends up in the saved register.

Two corollaries, both measured on `func_800B65D8`:

* the cached pointer must be assigned BEFORE the call, not after -- swapped,
  the `lw $s1, 0x50($s4)` lands after the `jal` instead of in front of it: 68
  words, 3 differing. Dropping the local entirely is 69 words, 65 differing.
* keep a constant offset in the MEMORY DISPLACEMENT rather than hoisting it
  into the base. `*(T **)(p + 0x50 + i * 4)` is 0 differing;
  `b = (T **)(p + 0x50)` then `b[i]` makes loop.c's reduced giv start at
  `p + 0x50` with a zero MEM offset and costs an `addiu $s4, $s7, 0x50`: 2
  differing.

### gcc EVALUATES AN ASSIGNMENT'S *DESTINATION ADDRESS* BEFORE ITS RHS

Measured on `func_800B6094`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. In the target,
`lw $s1, 0x38($s1)` -- the fetch of the store's destination -- sits one word
ABOVE `jal func_800439BC`, which is inside the right-hand side. Spelling the
statement as an `if/else` with a store in each arm costs 76 words / 57
differing; caching the destination in a local so all three later stores share
it costs 69 words / 47 differing, because the later reads of that lvalue have
to RELOAD (an intervening `sh` may alias).

**How to apply.** When a listing fetches a store destination suspiciously
early, the shape is ONE assignment with a call-bearing RHS -- a ternary, not a
branch -- and the destination must stay unspelled as a local.

### CHECK THE DEREFERENCE DEPTH BEFORE DIAGNOSING A FORWARDED STORE

A caution, measured on `func_800B683C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. The candidate was
26 words against 28 at 9 differing, and the target loaded an address its own
immediately preceding statement had just STORED to, with `nop`s in both
load-delay slots and no call or label between -- which is the recorded
signature of a volatile re-read ("A load of a value just stored is a VOLATILE
field"). Adding `volatile` changed nothing, because the diagnosis was wrong:
the chain was one `*` short. `**(u8 ***)(*(u8 **)(p + 0x98) + 0x5C)` written at
its true depth is **0 differing with no qualifier**.

**How to apply.** A candidate two words SHORT cannot be a cse-forwarding
problem -- forwarding deletes an instruction the target has, which is the same
symptom as never emitting it. Count the loads in the target chain against the
stars in your expression before reaching for a device.

### AN IMPLICITLY DECLARED CALLEE IS SOMETIMES THE MATCHING ONE

Measured on `func_800B6CEC`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. Its tail call is
`return func_80049E88(p)`, and `func_80049E88`'s real definition in
`csrc/unk_1C540.c` returns `u8`. Declaring it so makes gcc zero-extend the
result: **27 words against 26, 6 differing, the extra word `andi $v0, $v0,
0xff`**. The target has no mask, so the original translation unit had no
prototype for it and the implicit `int` is what matches. `func_8003E4FC` and
`func_800672D8` are in the same position in this unit -- neither has a
prototype anywhere in the project.

**How to apply.** A single truncating `andi 0xFF` or `andi 0xFFFF` on a call's
result that the target does not have means the original unit did not declare
that callee. Leave it implicit rather than widening the prototype, which would
be a claim about the callee rather than about this unit.

### cse CANNOT BE STOPPED FROM UNIFYING TWO IDENTICAL SMALL CONSTANTS, AND THE `do { } while (0)` BOUNDARY IS NOT ENOUGH FOR ONE

Established on `func_800B6FB8` (parked at 76 of 77 words) and independently on
`func_800B72B8` (22 of 23) and `func_800B70EC` (115 words, the same
`addiu $vN, $zero, 0x7` pair at words 12 and 21), ovl_town, 2026-11-02, over
roughly 2,900 compiles and a read of the CDK tree's `cse.c`. **All three write
the same six halfwords off the same base, so they are one source fragment three
times over and are worth 215 words between them.**

**Symptom.** The listing materialises the same small constant TWICE, one use
each, while other constants in the same basic block each get one register with
two uses. Both functions write the same six halfwords -- 7, 7, 0x7F, 0x7F,
0x2000, 0x2000 -- off `&D_80083160 + 0x1DC`, and the target emits
`addiu $vN, $zero, 0x7` twice while parking 0x7F and 0x2000 in one register
each. Every spelling reachable from C gives three constants with two uses each
and is exactly one word short.

**Why.** In `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18`:

* `canon_hash`'s `CONST_INT` arm (cse.c:2114) folds the MODE into the hash and
  `exp_equiv_p` demands equal modes, so two HImode `const_int 7`s are one
  table entry. The "already in a register in a wider mode" search (cse.c:~6600)
  then makes a narrow lookup scan the wider modes too, so HI->HI and SI->HI
  both merge. Only HI-first then SI-second would miss, because
  `GET_MODE_BITSIZE (mode) < BITS_PER_WORD` is false for SImode.
