  **CORRECTED 2026-11-03: that arrangement IS reachable from C, and reaching
  it is what landed `func_800AB7FC` (105/105, 0 differing).** The claim here
  was that cse folds a `(subreg:HI (reg:SI))` of a known constant back to the
  narrow `const_int` before the lookup, so the SImode entry never exists. That
  holds for a constant reaching an `s16` store through a CONVERSION -- there is
  a subreg to fold -- but not for one that lives in a **declared `s32` local
  assigned in a statement of its own**. There is no subreg then: the local's
  `(set (reg:SI) (const_int))` IS the SImode entry.

  `func_800AB7FC` needs `-0x800` and `0x800` materialised TWICE each, four
  `addiu $vN,$zero,K` for six halfword stores, split on the light matrix's row
  boundary. Every spelling this lever says to stop trying was re-confirmed
  useless (store permutations, `MATRIX`/`SVECTOR`/`s16[]` views, chained pairs,
  `do { } while (0)`, dead locals -- all 103 words, 72-76 differing). Putting
  the SECOND row's two values in `s32` locals: **103 -> 105 words, 73 -> 2
  differing**, and the rest of the function closed it at 0. The mechanism's own
  prediction is the control and it holds: BOTH rows in `s32` locals is 103
  again, because the SImode set now comes first and the later HImode stores do
  find it through this very loop; row 0 only is 105/3.

  The relevant source is the guard on the back-reference search itself,
  `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:6603-6606`:

      /* See if we have a CONST_INT that is already in a register in a
         wider mode.  */
      if (src_const && src_related == 0 && GET_CODE (src_const) == CONST_INT
          && GET_MODE_CLASS (mode) == MODE_INT
          && GET_MODE_BITSIZE (mode) < BITS_PER_WORD)

  The search runs only when the CURRENT set is narrower than a word and scans
  only WIDER modes, so HImode-then-SImode is invisible in both directions.

  **IT TRANSFERS, measured 2026-11-03.** The two parks on exactly this symptom
  both had their LENGTH fixed by the three lines, which is what had blocked
  them:

  | park | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `func_800B6FB8` | 76 of 77 words, 66 DIFF, VERDICT LENGTH | **77 of 77**, 13 DIFF, VERDICT SHAPE |
  | `func_800B72B8` | 22 of 23 words, 22 DIFF, VERDICT LENGTH | **23 of 23**, 11 DIFF, VERDICT SHAPE |

  `func_800B6FB8` had resisted about 2,900 compiles, including all 720
  permutations of its six stores under four access idioms. The three lines are:

      t->unk_14 = 7;      HImode: the literal
      k = 7;              SImode: an s32 local, in a statement of its OWN
      t->unk_16 = k;

  and the controls run on the park itself are the mechanism's own predictions:
  `k` assigned FIRST and the literal second is 76 words (SI-then-HI merges,
  because the HImode lookup runs the wider-mode search and finds it);
  `s32 k = 7;` as an INITIALISER is 76 words, so the statement form is
  required; and giving the function's OTHER two repeated constants their own
  `s32` locals changes nothing, so only the constant that must be DUPLICATED
  wants this treatment.

  The earlier note "measured four ways (`s32`, `u32`, `u16` temporaries in
  either position): all one word short" was taken on `func_800B6FB8` and is
  not a contradiction: those temporaries were not assigned in a statement of
  their own and read by only the second store.

  Both parks' residue is now register allocation, not length -- the target
  materialises the other two constants BEFORE the prologue's register saves and
  gives them their own registers, while the candidate materialises each just
  before its first use and lets one reuse the register that held the duplicated
  constant. Permuting the stores moves it by one word and no further. A third
  function, `func_800B70EC` (115 words), has the same pair at its words 12 and
  21 and has not been retried.
* `cse_end_of_basic_block` (cse.c:8056) breaks only on `CODE_LABEL`,
  `NOTE_INSN_SETJMP` and `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END`. **A CALL DOES NOT END A cse
  BLOCK**, so no rearrangement around an intervening call can help.
* `update_equiv_regs` (local-alloc.c) cannot supply the duplicate either: it
  needs `reg_n_refs == 2` with `reg_basic_block < 0`, and its two outcomes are
  substitute-at-the-use or move-the-init, never two inits.
* A `volatile` asm, with or without a `"memory"` clobber, does NOT help --
  cse invalidates memory and call-clobbered hard registers there, never a
  pseudo's recorded constant. Both placements measured WORSE, 76 differing
  against 66.

**A CORRECTION TO THE `do { } while (0)` LEVER, which is the part worth more
than either function.** That construct really does end a cse1 block, and cse2
leaves the pair alone as well: dumping every pass on the do/while variant
shows 2 `const_int 7` sets through `.rtl`, `.jump`, `.cse`, `.loop` and
`.cse2`, and 1 by `.flow`. The merge happens between the `.cse2` dump
(toplev.c:3394) and `flow_analysis` (toplev.c:3463), with only
`regclass_init()` in between; which of the two does it was not isolated. So the
boundary is good for stopping cse folding a value FORWARD -- which is what the
lever at "A cse BLOCK ends at a LOOP-END note" was established for -- and is
**not** good for keeping a duplicate constant materialisation. Priced at four
placements, all 76 words and 76 differing.

**How to apply.** A candidate ONE WORD SHORT whose missing word is a repeated
`addiu $vN, $zero, K` is not a spelling problem; stop sweeping source shapes.
Also ruled out by measurement, so that they are not re-derived: all 720
permutations of the six stores under four access idioms (2,880 compiles, every
one the same word count), two struct typedefs over one base interleaved and
grouped, a `union` of halfword and byte views, 16-bit bitfields, `volatile` on
the pointer, an extra dead local, and `goto L; L:` or a bare label (jump1
deletes an unreferenced label before cse1 runs, so both are byte-identical to
the base). What remains is the permuter, which has never been run on it: a dead
test on an uninitialised local IS a construct that can split a cse block, and
it is not something a person writes.

### A FLAT FUNCTION-POINTER TABLE IS AN ARITY WITNESS WHEN ITS OTHER ENTRIES ARE LANDED

Established on `func_800B6FB8`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. docs/town-sweep.md says a
function whose address is only TAKEN has no arity witness and any arity
compiles. That is true of the CALL SITE and not of the program.
`func_800B6FB8` has no caller anywhere -- the only reference outside its own
listing is `.word 0x800B6FB8` at 0x8007194C in `asm/data/game_data.data.s`,
slot 16 of the flat 30-entry table `D_8007190C`. **Thirteen of that table's
thirty entries are already landed C, and all thirteen are `void f(void)`**,
which settles it in one grep loop:

    for f in <the table's entries>; do
      grep -rhE "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_ ]*\\**$f\\(" csrc/
    done

**How to apply.** Before recording an arity as unwitnessed, find the table the
address is stored into and read its siblings. A homogeneous table is a
convention witness: not as strong as a call site, but strong enough to act on,
and if the walker ever lands and disagrees, every entry retypes together and
no bytes move. This does NOT help when the address is taken in CODE rather
than in a table -- `func_800B5B20`, whose address is taken inside the landed
`func_800B6E3C` and nowhere else, remains genuinely unwitnessed.

### A HALF-THREADED GUARD EDGE NEEDS AN INSN THAT BREAKS `thread_jumps`' WALK AND THEN DISAPPEARS

Established on `func_800B62A4`, ovl_town, 82 words, 2026-11-02. This is the
inverse of "A GUARD AROUND BOTH LOOPS is how the first test branches to the
TAIL", and it completes it: that one only knew how to turn half-threading into
full threading.

**Symptom.** A label sits BETWEEN a compare and the branch that uses it --
here `.L800B6370` between `slti $v0, $s1, 0x3` and `beqz $v0, .L800B639C`.
That is a rotated loop's entry guard which was only HALF threaded: it skips the
following test's redundant compare but stops ON that test's branch. The label
is `reorg.c`'s, not `jump.c`'s -- `relax_delay_slots` ("If the first insn at
TARGET_LABEL is redundant with a previous insn, redirect the jump to the
following insn", with `target_label = get_label_before (PREV_INSN (tmp))`) is
what places a label before a conditional jump.

**Why it is hard to reach.** `thread_jumps` (jump.c) walks BACKWARD in lockstep
from the guard's branch and from the next test's branch, and threads the whole
way as soon as it reaches the guard's target label with `num_same_regs == 0`.
With a bare `[loop-end label][slt][beq]` sequence the walk matches the two
`slt`s -- whose SET cancels the only pending equivalence -- and reaches the
label on the next step, so the edge is threaded PAST the test. On
`func_800B62A4` that is `beqz $v0, +0xF4` where the target has `+0xCC`: **82
words, 1 differing, every other word exact, and immovable.** Twenty spellings
of the loop (`while`, `for`, `do/while`, goto-to-test, break-at-top,
`continue`, `3 >`, `<= 2`, a pointer walk) and eleven of the following `if`
(nested, `&&`, goto, `for(;;){...break;}`, `else if`) all stay at that one
displacement, as do seven ways of nesting the loop inside its own `if`.

**What moves it.** ONE INSN between the loop-end label and the test's compare
whose pattern differs from the insn before the guard's own compare: the walk
then breaks on `recog_memoized`/`rtx_equal_for_thread_p` before it ever sees
the label. **The insn must then vanish, or it costs a word.** A store that is
dead, or that cse kills by propagating its value into the test, does both,
since flow deletes it long after `thread_jumps` has run. Re-snapshotting the
loop's own invariant between the loop and the test:

```c
    n = c;
    for (i = 0; i + n < 3; i++) { ... c++; ... }
    n = c;                      /* <- this one */
    if (n < 3 && p[0x49] != 0) { ... }
```

0 differing, against 1 without it. The breaker is generic: `n = c;` is 0,
`n = 0;` 0, `n = i;` 0, `n++;` 0 -- but **`n = n;` is 1, because it emits no
insn at all.**

**Two traps.**

* **An empty `__asm__ volatile("")` is NOT a substitute**, although it is a
  one-word lever for cross-jumping elsewhere in this document. It breaks the
  walk correctly -- the edge stops being threaded -- but it also BLOCKS the
  reorg step, because a volatile insn is never `redundant_insn`, so the compare
  is not skipped and the edge lands one word early: `+0xC8` for `+0xCC`, still
  1 differing. Measured for `("")`, `("" ::: "memory")`, `("" ::"r"(c))`, and
  for placing it after the `if` instead.
* **Do not use a LIVE copy as the breaker.** `i = c;` ahead of the test, with
  the clear loop reusing `i`, breaks the walk, but the copy survives as a real
  insn and cse then makes `i` the canonical register of the quantity --
  `make_regs_eqv` promotes the NEW register when it outlives the old one past
  the cse block end -- so the test is emitted on the wrong register: **13
  differing**, and six spellings of that family are identical.

**How to apply, as a diagnostic.** A label between a compare and its branch
says the source has a statement between the loop and that test which leaves no
instruction behind, and the first thing to try is re-reading the loop's own
invariant into the variable the test uses.

### `<< 7` AND `* 128` ARE NOT THE SAME STATEMENT WHEN THE RESULT IS NARROW

Established on `func_800B7428`, ovl_town, 261 words, 2026-11-02. When a narrow
(`s16`) variable is assigned an arithmetic expression, `convert_to_integer`
distributes the narrowing into the operands so the whole expression is computed
in HImode -- but its `MULT_EXPR` arm
(`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/convert.c:249-266`) requires BOTH operands to fit
the narrow type, and the literal `128` has type `int`, so a multiply by a
constant **blocks** the distribution. `LSHIFT_EXPR` (convert.c:217-247,
"shifting is like multiplication") **allows** it, and `PLUS_EXPR` always does.

Measured: `s16 i = ((y + y0) << 7) + x + x0;` is 261 words / 0 differing. The
same written `* 128` or `* 0x80` is **259 words / 255 differing**, because the
SImode sum then gets cse'd with the loop-invariant `(y + y0) & 1` parity test
and the HImode copy of the parameter disappears. `s32 i` is 227 / 253.

**Diagnostic.** If the target adds two narrow values with NO `sll`/`sra 16` in
front of them while ALSO sign-extending those same two values elsewhere, the
narrow sum is a narrowed assignment and every `* const` on its path has to be
written as a shift.

This refines, and in one direction contradicts, the landed `func_800B7314`'s
comment, where `p[i * 0x80 + j]` matched: there nothing competes for the sum, so
cse has nothing to unify and the two spellings agree. **The lever only bites
when a sign-extended copy of the same operands is live in the same block.**

### WHERE A LOOP'S POINTER INCREMENT IS WRITTEN CHANGES THE DELAY SLOT OF AN EARLY `break`, NOT THE LOOP

Established on `func_800B7428`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, and it is the companion to
"`p++` AS THE LAST STATEMENT IS NOT `*p++`" from `func_800B7978`.

`for (x = 0; x < w; x++) { switch (...) {...} src++; }` and
`for (x = 0; x < w; x++, src++) { switch (...) {...} }` BOTH put
`addiu $a2, $a2, 0x2` in the inner branch's delay slot and are identical in 258
of 261 words. They differ in which insn is first in the loop's continue-target
block when `reorg.c` runs:

* with the increment in the `for` clause, the `case 0` `beqz` -- an EQ test, so
  `mostly_true_jump` predicts not-taken -- finds its fall-through thread
  starting at an already-filled `j`, falls back to its TARGET thread, steals
  `addiu $v0, $a3, 0x1` and retargets past it;
* with `src++` at the end of the body, that block's first insn has already been
  consumed by the loop branch's own slot, so `steal_delay_list_from_fallthrough`
  succeeds instead and takes the default arm's `sll`, after which the `j` takes
  the `sra` behind it.

Worth **3 differing** at a single branch/delay pair, with everything else
already exact. Four unrelated spellings land on the same 3: `case 0: continue;`
for `break;`, `case 0:` written last, a `default:` arm with no trailing
`break`, and flipping the index's operand order.

**How to apply.** When a `for` loop containing a `switch` or an early `break`
is 3 differing in exactly the branch/delay pair at the skip test, move the
increment between the `for` clause and the end of the body before touching
anything else.

### A CONSTANT-BASE POINTER MUST BE RE-ASSIGNED PER `if`, NOT PER BASIC BLOCK

Established on `func_800B8C90`, ovl_town, 94 words, 2026-11-02. The standing
rule for out-of-image globals -- "one zero-low-half base pointer local with the
offsets written into the index expressions, one per basic block, assigned after
any calls in that block" -- is too coarse for a RUN of independent `if`s over
0x8001xxxx flags. The base has to be re-assigned before **each `if`
statement**, and the mechanism is a DELAY SLOT, not a `lui` count:

| spelling for four `if`s over eight flag bytes | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| inline `*(u8 *)0x800133BA` constant addresses | 98 | 66 |
| de Morgan, or nested `if`s, or reversed compare operands | 98 | 66 |
| a `u8` local for the loaded byte, or an `s32` for the constant | 98 | 66 |
| ONE shared `q = (u8 *)0x80010000;` for the whole run | 90 | 58 |
| `extern u8 D_800133BA;` real symbols | 94 | 31 |
| **`p = (u8 *)0x80010000;` immediately before EACH `if`** | **94** | **0** |

Inline, the second `lui` allocates to `$v0` -- the register the `beq` above it
reads -- so `eligible_for_delay` rejects it and the slot stays `nop`: four
pairs, four wasted words. One shared base lets cse unify to a single `lui` and
comes out four words SHORT. Re-assigning per `if` puts that `lui` in `$v1`,
moves the compare constant to `$a0`, and fills all four slots.

**How to apply.** A `lui` in the delay slot of a `beq` whose operand is `$v0`
means the base needs its own assignment statement for that `if`. Both losing
spellings read like ordinary allocation noise, and the cause is one statement.

### TWO LOCAL ARRAYS WITH THE SAME INITIALISER SHARE ONE rodata LABEL ACROSS FUNCTIONS

Same function, same day. `varasm.c`'s constant-pool hash is per TRANSLATION
UNIT, so a 20-byte initialiser appearing in two functions is emitted once.
Reading a rodata block that is referenced by **two** functions therefore does
NOT rule out "local initialised array" -- and the image order (`const` of f1,
f1's jump table, `const` of f2) is positive evidence FOR it.
`func_800B8C90` and `func_800B8B00` share `D_800894D0 = {4, 5, 7, 0x1C, 0x1F}`
exactly that way.

Two consequences for a sweep:

* Landing one of the pair with the local-array spelling DUPLICATES the bytes
  while the other is still asm and references the symbol. The way out is to
  read the surviving symbol as an aggregate -- `UnkTownRo5 a = D_800894D0;`
  with a `struct { s32 v[5]; }` -- which measures identical text and emits no
  rodata. Switch BOTH to the local-array spelling and delete BOTH
  `INCLUDE_RODATA` lines in the same commit, or neither.
* A splat `dlabel` can swallow the FOLLOWING jump table's `.align 3` padding,
  so a 24-byte dlabel can be a 20-byte constant. `D_800894D0` is 5 words, not
  6, and the sixth word belongs to `jtbl_800894E8`.

### CROSS-JUMPING SWITCH ARMS ONTO A SHARED STORE TAIL NEEDS ONE SHARED VARIABLE, NOT A LITERAL PER ARM

Established on `func_800B8B00`, ovl_town, 100 words, 2026-11-02, and worth 14
words there. When several `switch` arms store different constants to the same
location and one arm stores an incoming value there, gcc merges them: each
constant arm collapses to a single `addiu $tN, $zero, K` that either falls
through into the shared store (when the arm PRECEDES it in source order) or
reaches it with `j shared` and the `addiu` in the delay slot (when it follows).

Measured: writing each arm independently -- `*(u8 *)0x800133A7 = 10;` in one
and `= arg;` in another -- is **114 words / 97 differing**. A single
`s16 v = arg;` reassigned in the constant arms, with every arm storing `v`, is
**0 differing**.

The mechanism is the timing. Cross-jumping runs in `jump2`, AFTER `sched2` and
therefore after register allocation, so the merge only fires when the constant
and the default value already occupy the same hard register. Making them one
pseudo in the source is the only reliable way to arrange that -- the allocator
will not coalesce two unrelated constant pseudos into the argument-save
register on its own.

This is the positive counterpart to "TWO JUMP-TABLE ENTRIES WITH THE SAME
TARGET ARE SHARED CASE LABELS": shared **labels** are a source-level fact,
shared **tails** are a post-allocation one, and both have to be right.

A corollary that reads the listing for free: **whether a merged arm falls
through or uses a `j` is decided by source order and nothing else**, so the
listing's block order IS the source order and the arm sequence does not have to
be searched for.

### A `switch` ON A `short` SUBJECT PUTS THE SIGN EXTENSION *AFTER* THE RANGE BIAS

Same function. `addiu $aN, $aN, -K` / `sll 16` / `sra 16` / `sltiu` is a plain
`switch (s16_param)` whose lowest case value is K. There is no cast and no
`s16` local in the source: `stmt.c` folds `index - minval` in the index TYPE,
so for HImode the subtract is free and narrowing, and `do_tablejump` then
converts HImode to SImode with a signed extension.

**The two lines, confirmed 2026-11-03 on `func_800BE4D4` (ovl_town, 363
words, landed with `switch (arg1)` over labels 1..31).** `c-typeck.c:6647`
default-converts the switch quantity to `int`, `:6649` then takes
`index = get_unwidened (exp, NULL_TREE)` and `:6656` hands it back with
`exp = index;` -- so `index_type` goes back to `short` while `nominal_type`
stays `int`. `stmt.c:5261-5264` is where the bias happens:

```c
index_expr = convert (thiscase->data.case_stmt.nominal_type,
                      fold (build (MINUS_EXPR, index_type,
                                   index_expr, minval)));
```

The `MINUS_EXPR` is built in `index_type`, i.e. in HImode, needing no
extension of the operand; only the outer `convert` to `nominal_type` emits the
`sll`/`sra`. Hence bias first, extension second. **So do not write
`switch ((s16)(arg - 1))` over labels 0..N to explain this shape** -- that was
the first hypothesis on `func_800BE4D4` and the source reading replaced it
before it was measured.

### WITH NO `default`, A SHARED TAIL MUST BE A `goto` LABEL INSIDE THE SWITCH

Established on `func_800BE4D4` (ovl_town, 363 words, landed 2026-11-03), a
31-case dispatch where six case groups converge on one tail.

`stmt.c:5013-5020`, comment and all:

```c
/* If we don't have a default-label, create one here,
   after the body of the switch.  */
if (thiscase->data.case_stmt.default_label == 0)
  {
    thiscase->data.case_stmt.default_label
      = build_decl (LABEL_DECL, NULL_TREE, NULL_TREE);
    expand_label (thiscase->data.case_stmt.default_label);
  }
```

The created default label and the `break` label therefore end up at the SAME
place. So a tail written *after* the switch is reached not only by the cases
that fall out of it but by **every unused jump-table index and the
`sltiu`/`beqz` range check as well** -- in this function nine indices (11, 12,
13, 24..29) plus the bounds test, all of which the target instead sends to the
epilogue.

Three spellings, and only the third can produce the listing:

| spelling | what goes wrong |
|---|---|
| tail after the switch | default falls into the tail; unused indices run it |
| `default: return;` | its `j <ret>` needs a word somewhere in the body, and no position in the listing has one |
| **label after the last case body, `goto` from each group** | puts the tail between the last case body and the break label -- where the target has it |

**Fingerprint:** a jump table several of whose entries point at the epilogue,
plus a block that several case bodies branch into which sits BEFORE the
epilogue rather than after the switch. That is a `goto` tail, not a fallthrough
tail.

> **NARROWED 2026-11-03, same day: this holds for the DEFAULT/BREAK
> COINCIDENCE, not for an ordinary shared tail.** On `func_800C035C` a
> three-way shared tail across cases 0/1/2 is **0 differing both** as a `goto`
> label inside the switch and written out three times, because jump2 unifies
> it. The trap above only arms when the created default label and the `break`
> label coincide AND the tail would therefore catch the unused table indices --
> in `func_800C035C` the out-of-range index and `break` both land on the
> post-switch code, so there was nothing to catch. **Check where the table's
> unused entries point before spending anything on this.** `goto` is still
> worth writing when it documents the listing's shape; it is just not forced.

Measured: `s16 arg` is 100 words / 0 differing; `s32 arg` is **98 / 93** (the
`sll`/`sra` pair simply does not appear); `u16 arg` is **99 / 96** (`andi
0xffff` instead of the sign extension).

**The ORDERING is the tell.** A source-level `(s16)(x - 1)` would also give
`addiu` then `sll`/`sra`, but a source-level `s16` parameter used directly
extends BEFORE any arithmetic. So bias first, extension second identifies the
plain `switch` on a `short`.

### DECLARATION ORDER ALSO FIXES INIT-CODE ORDER, NOT ONLY AGGREGATE SLOTS

Same function, and it extends the existing "declaration order fixes AGGREGATE
stack slots only" entry rather than contradicting it. For locals WITH
INITIALISERS, declaration order also fixes the order of the initialisation
code: the parameter-save `addu $t0, $a0, $zero` lands at word 1, ahead of a
10-word struct block copy, only when `s16 v = arg;` is declared BEFORE
`UnkTownRo5 ids = D_800894D0;`.

Measured 0 differing in that order against **33 differing** with the two
declarations swapped, and the same 33 with `v` declared last below the scalars.
**The word count is unchanged**, so this presents as pure SHAPE at the top of
the function and is easy to misread as a scheduling problem.

> **CORRECTED 2026-11-03, SAME DAY, BY A LARGER FUNCTION: the negative result
> below is right for SCALARS and WRONG FOR AGGREGATES, and the split is
> clean.** On `func_800C035C` (475 words, landed) reversing all eleven locals
> is 14 differing; swapping ONLY the two aggregates is the SAME 14, every one
> an `sp` displacement, because those two own the stack slots; reversing ONLY
> the six scalars is 0. So the flat results below were measuring the scalar
> half of a mixed declaration list. **Order the aggregates to the listing's
> slot order and stop permuting the rest.** That also reconciles this entry
> with "DECLARATION ORDER FIXES *AGGREGATE* STACK SLOTS ONLY" rather than
> contradicting it.
>
> And the statement-not-initialiser rule reaches an AGGREGATE BLOCK COPY with a
> far larger blast radius than the pointer case it was recorded for:
> `UnkTown89960 w = D_80089960;` is **392 differing** against 0 for the same
> thing as a statement.

**NEGATIVE RESULT, AND IT BOUNDS THIS LEVER: with no initialisers, order buys
nothing.** On `func_800BE4D4` (ovl_town, 363 words, landed 2026-11-03) six
different declaration orders of THIRTEEN function-scope locals, none of them
initialised, all measured 363 words / 148 differing -- identical, to the word.
So the lever above is specifically about INIT-CODE order, which only exists
when a declaration has an initialiser; it is not a general handle on the
allocator at function scope.

What actually moved the allocation in that function was **which variable a
value is stored into**, not where anything was declared: putting a `strlen`
result back into the existing case counter `i` makes the length a multi-block
pseudo, so `global_alloc` gives it `$s2`, which forces the target's
`addu $s2, $v0, $zero` copy of the return value AND evicts another local from
`$s2` into `$s4` -- which is in turn what lets two other arms keep a row base
in one register with displacements 0/4/8. A private `s32 n` instead is 148
differing. **When a declaration-order sweep comes back flat, stop permuting
declarations and start asking which existing variable a value could be
reusing.**

Two more measurements for the `func_800B8A40` counter-before-base rule, from
the two loops in the same arm: putting `i = 0;` in the `for`'s init clause
instead of above the base assignment is **2 differing per loop**, independently
on each; and sharing ONE base local across the two loops instead of two is **5
differing**. New alongside them: a constant the loop body stores must be
assigned as the arm's FIRST statement -- `v = 9;` moved from the top of the arm
to between the two loops is **20 differing**, even though it is only read in
the second loop.

### A `u16` FIELD PLUS AN EXPLICIT `(s16)` IS NOT THE SAME AS AN `s16` FIELD, AND ONLY THE SIGN-EXTENDED USES WITNESS IT

Established on the `func_8008DA80` collision-sweep set, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
An `s16` field gives a one-insn `lh`; a `u16` field with `(s16)` written at the
use gives `lhu` plus a `sll`/`sra 16` pair, which is what the target has at
seven sites in that function.

**But in a NARROWING context both spellings give `lhu`**, because
`convert_to_integer` distributes the narrowing into the operands -- so
`SP->unk_6C = verts[...].vy - SP->unk_1E;` carries no information about the
field's signedness and only the sign-extended uses do. Read the signed uses,
not the narrow ones.

The cast rides into an array index too: `cells[(s16)SP->unk_04]` folds to
`lhu` / `sll 16` / `sra 15` / `addu`, because combine merges the cast's
`sra 16` with the `u16` element scale's `sll 1` into one `sra 15`. A lone
`sra 15` on an index is therefore a cast-plus-scale, not a divide.

### THE FIRST OF A RUN OF IDENTICAL TESTS ON ONE BASE LOOKS CHEAPER THAN THE REST

Same function, and it cost the reading real time. Two step-selection tests
written **identically** in the source:

```c
if ((s16)SP->unk_1C >= 0x20) SP->unk_54 = 0x40; else SP->unk_54 = -0x40;
if ((s16)SP->unk_1E >= 0x20) SP->unk_58 = 0x40; else SP->unk_58 = -0x40;
```

The first compiles to a bare `slti`, reusing the `andi` result from three
stores earlier -- cse forwards the `sh` past the intervening stores to other
displacements off the same base, and combine then deletes the `(s16)`
altogether because `nonzero_bits(x & 0x3F)` is six bits, so the halfword's sign
bit is known zero. The second compiles to `lhu` / `nop` / `sll 16` / `sra 16` /
`slti` -- **four extra words** -- purely because it sits after the first `if`'s
merge point, where cse's extended basic block ended.

**How to apply.** An asymmetric-looking pair of tests on adjacent fields of one
object can be ONE spelling written twice. Do not go looking for two different
source constructs; cse's block boundary is the whole explanation.

### A SHORT LOCAL SEEDED FROM A PARAMETER IS WHY THE PARAMETER LANDS IN A CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER

Same function. `s16 cx, cy;` left uninitialised, with `SP->unk_50 = x;` storing
the parameter directly, put the `y` parameter's copy in `$t1` and `cx` in
`$a0`. Writing `s16 cx = x; s16 cy = y;` and storing `SP->unk_50 = cx;` makes
each parameter copy and its loop variable ONE pseudo, so they land in `$a3` and
`$s6` and the `sw $s6, 0x28($sp)` moves from prologue word 9 to word 2.

This is the converse of "two disjoint live ranges in ONE declared local share a
register": there the hint is three differing words on one value, here it is
**which CLASS of register the parameter got**, read off the prologue's `sw $sN`
list and the position of the save rather than off the body. A parameter copied
into a callee-saved register whose last use is before the first call is the
signature -- the allocator would never pay for the save otherwise.

### `s16 v = e;` PUTS THE NARROWING AT THE USE; `s32 v = (s16)e;` PUTS IT AT THE ASSIGNMENT

Same function, and worth 11 differing words there. `s16 xb = x & -0x40;` keeps
the raw `and` result in the pseudo and emits the `sll 16`/`sra 16` pair before
the first USE. `s32 ab = (s16)(x & -0x40);` emits the same pair immediately
after the `and`. Identical instruction multiset, different position: 11
differing against 0, because the two insns rotate a nine-insn prologue window.

**How to apply.** When a residue is a short rotation and the rotated
instructions are a sign-extension pair, try moving the narrowing between the
declaration and the use before looking for another mechanism.

### `&arr[i]` GIVES A BASE-FIRST `addu`; `arr[i].field` GIVES AN INDEX-FIRST ONE

Same function, worth 4 words. `SVECTOR *n = &SP->unk_18[p->unk_10];` emitted
`addu $a1, $s3, $a1` where the target has `addu $a1, $a1, $s3`. Repeating the
subscript-and-member form inline -- four `SP->unk_18[p->unk_10].vN` and four
`verts[p->unk_00].vN` in one expression, left for cse to unify -- matched, and
costs nothing, because cse collapses the repeated subscripts into exactly the
two address computations the pointer locals would have given.

This is the same ordering fact as "POINTER arithmetic is always pointer-first;
INTEGER arithmetic keeps source order", reached from the other direction: an
explicit address-of local is pointer arithmetic, a subscripted member access is
not.

### sched WILL REORDER TWO STORES TO DISJOINT DISPLACEMENTS OFF ONE BASE, SO MEASURE BOTH SOURCE ORDERS

Same set. `memrefs_conflict_p` proves two `(plus (reg base) (const_int))` MEMs
with different constants independent, so sched1 is free to swap them, and it
mostly does not: swapping two prologue stores in `func_8008DA80` moved the
output from 18 differing to 11, i.e. source order was honoured. But
`func_8008E4EC` and `func_8008EA20` emit their last two prologue stores in the
OPPOSITE order from the source -- writing them in the emitted order was 6 and 7
differing where writing them in the base sibling's order was **0**.

Two corollaries: store order is a good first guess at source order, and **a
residue that is a one-instruction rotation around two adjacent stores is a
reason to try the other order, not to look for a different mechanism**. The
clean witness for the "will reorder" direction is a dependency-free store --
`SP->BEST = 0;` is first in source in both max variants and comes out second in
both, because sched has nothing to wait for.

### THE PER-`if` CONSTANT-BASE RULE DOES NOT APPLY TO A TYPED SCRATCHPAD POINTER

Same set, and it bounds the lever established the same day on `func_800B8C90`.
One `UnkTownCastSP *SP = (UnkTownCastSP *)0x1F800000;` at the top of the
function, assigned nowhere else, is **0 differing** across a body with roughly
two dozen independent `if`s and three nested loops reading and writing through
it.

"A constant-base pointer must be re-assigned per `if`" is about the
`u8 *base = (u8 *)0x80010000;` out-of-image idiom, where the base is a plain
pointer whose value cse keeps re-deriving. A TYPED STRUCT pointer to the
scratchpad lives in a callee-saved register for the whole function and wants
exactly one assignment. Both forms occur in this unit and they are not
interchangeable -- check which one you have before applying either.

### `CASE_VALUES_THRESHOLD` IS 5 ON THIS TARGET, SO A gcc JUMP TABLE NEEDS FIVE CASE NODES

Established on `func_800B83DC`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, and verified in the CDK
tree. `stmt.c:5085-5094` reads

    #ifndef CASE_VALUES_THRESHOLD
    #ifdef HAVE_casesi
    #define CASE_VALUES_THRESHOLD (HAVE_casesi ? 4 : 5)
    #else
    #define CASE_VALUES_THRESHOLD 5
    #endif
    #endif

and `config/mips/mips.md:6314`'s `casesi` expander carries the condition
`"TARGET_EMBEDDED_PIC"` (mips.md:6333), so `insn-flags.h` gets
`#define HAVE_casesi (TARGET_EMBEDDED_PIC)` -- the macro IS defined, so the
first branch is taken, and the expression **evaluates to 5 at run time** for
this build.

Measured: four case nodes emit **no `.rodata` table at all** -- a balanced
compare tree, 129 words / 120 differing -- while one extra case label anywhere
inside `[minval, maxval]` produces the table and 131 words.

**How to apply.** A listing with an N-entry table tells you the source had at
least FIVE distinct case values, so a missing arm has to be written as an
explicit hole: `case 2: break;`. The hole's value is unwitnessed as long as it
does not move `minval` or `maxval` -- any single label in range, twelve labels,
`case 2: return 0;`, and placing it after the last real arm all give the
identical table. A `- 1` bias in the subject is also unwitnessed:
`switch (p[3])` with cases 1/2/4/8/16 and `switch (p[3] - 1)` with cases
0/1/3/7/15 are byte-identical, because `expand_end_case` computes
`index - minval` itself.

### A CONSTANT ADDRESS IS A TWO-WORD ASSEMBLER MACRO IN ONE INSN; A SYMBOL IS `high` + `lo_sum` IN TWO -- AND ONLY THE SYMBOL'S `lui` CAN FILL A DELAY SLOT

Same function, and it took it from 67 differing to 2.

`*(u8 *)0x800133E6` compiles to `lbu $2,-2147404826` under `.set macro`: one
RTL insn whose length is 2, and atomic -- so a conditional branch immediately
in front of it **cannot** be filled from the fall-through, and reorg steals the
target thread's insn instead, costing a word. `extern u8 D_800133E6;` compiles
to `lui $2,%hi(..)` plus `lbu $3,%lo(..)($2)`, and the `lui` moves into the
branch's delay slot for free.

Measured: 132 words / 67 differing for the constant form against **131 / 2**
for the two `extern` symbols.

**This refines the out-of-image lever rather than contradicting it.** The
base-pointer form -- `u8 *b = (u8 *)0x80010000;` then `b[i * 2 + 0x33A4]` -- is
for a VARIABLE index. With a CONSTANT index the base local is folded straight
back into the address constant and you get the macro, so **a constant-index
out-of-image byte wants a real `extern`**.
`splat/town.bin_undefined_syms_auto.txt` already defines these symbols, so they
link.

### TWO BASE LOCALS IN ONE EXTENDED BASIC BLOCK ARE UNIFIED BY cse INTO ONE `lui`

Same function. The "one base local per basic block" rule only produces two
`lui`s when the blocks really are separate cse runs, and **two locals either
side of one conditional branch are one run**: 130 words, one word short of the
target. Read cse's block boundaries, not the source's braces.

### `u8` VERSUS `s32` FOR A VALUE USED INSIDE A LOOP DECIDES WHETHER A HOISTED `zero_extend` BECOMES A REGISTER COPY

Same function, one word. With `u8 v`, `loop.c`'s `move_movables` hoists
`(zero_extend (reg:QI v))` out of the loop and `emit_move_insn` emits it as
`addu $a1, $v0, $zero` -- a real word in the preheader. With `s32 v` the load
goes straight into the loop's register and that word disappears. 132 against
131 words on the same body.

### TWO SWITCH ARMS SHARE A HARD REGISTER FOR A VALUE ONLY IF ONE DECLARED LOCAL SPANS BOTH

Same function. A function-scope `i` got `$a3` in both arms that use it;
per-arm `i` gave `$a1` in one and `$t0` in the other, 9 more differing. Same
for the shared value: one `s32 v` got `$a1` in both arms, per-arm gave `$v1` in
the second and cost a word.

**But the shared variable has to be the type the OTHER arm needs.** A shared
`u8 v` is erased in the arm where both its uses are zero-extends in one cse
run, so the sharing only bites with `s32 v` fed from a block-local `u8 w`
(`w = q[6]; if (w == 0) return 0; ... v = w;`). And **the `v = w` statement's
POSITION matters**: after the counter's `i = 0;` and the base assignment is 67
differing, before them 19, between them 4.

### A RECORD POINTER WANTS `non-constant-base + index`, NOT AN ARRAY REF OR `symbol + index`

Same function, worth 35 differing words. `(u8 *)D_800D2644[a]`,
`(u8 *)&D_800D2644[a][0]` and `(u8 *)D_800D2644 + a * 0x20` all do two things
wrong: they emit the INDEX before the symbol, because `fold` moves a
`TREE_CONSTANT` left operand of a commutative `PLUS` to the right; and they
fold a later byte offset into the symbol, giving `addiu $v1, $v1, 6` with
`lbu 0($v0)` where the target has `lbu 0x6($v0)`.

Writing `base = (u8 *)D_800D2644; p = base + a * 0x20;` makes the base a
`VAR_DECL`, so there is no swap, the symbol is materialised first, and every
byte offset stays a displacement. 134 words / 108 differing becomes 133 / 73.

### A LOOP-INVARIANT CONSTANT THAT loop.c HOISTS IS A WORD IN THE WRONG PLACE -- MOVE ITS COMPETITOR INTO THE LOOP

Same function. A comparison constant was hoisted into the preheader
(`li $t2, 48`, plus a `nop` where the target has that constant filling a
`bnez`'s delay slot) whenever the loop's record pointer was itself a preheader
local. Writing the record pointer INSIDE the loop body made `move_movables`
hoist the record address instead and left the constant in the loop: 133 words
becomes 132, and that arm became word- and register-exact.

**How to apply.** When a preheader holds a small constant the target fills a
delay slot with, the fix is not to fight the hoist but to give `move_movables`
something it prefers -- its budget is spent in loop order, so an invariant
earlier in the body takes the slot.

### A LOOP COUNTER'S INIT MUST BE SEQUENCED BEFORE A PRECEDING SIGNED DIVIDE, OR reorg.c COSTS A WORD

Established on `func_8009567C`, ovl_town, 57 words, 2026-11-02. A signed divide
by a power of two expands to a real branch -- `addiu K`, `bgez`, `addiu K-1`,
`sra`. If the only statement between that divide and a following loop is the
loop itself, the `bgez`'s block holds nothing independent to pull into its
delay slot, so `reorg.c` falls through to `fill_eager_delay_slots` and
**duplicates the `sra` from the branch target**: one extra word, and every
later word shifts.

Giving the block one independent insn fixes it. Sequence the loop counter's
`i = 0` BEFORE the divide and reorg moves it down into the `bgez`'s slot
instead.

| source order | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| `idx = (v + 0x100) / 0x200 & 7;` then `for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)` | 58 | 41 |
| `idx = ...;` then `i = 0;` then `while (i < 4)` | 58 | 41 |
| `i = 0;` then `idx = ...;` then `while (i < 4)` | 57 | **0** |
| `for (i = 0, idx = ...; i < 4; i++)` | 57 | **0** |

**It is the statement order of the init relative to the DIVIDE, not the loop
form**: `while` and `for` both land and both fail, depending only on which side
of the divide `i = 0` sits.

This is the mirror image of the `move_movables` hoist lever. There the fix is
to give loop.c something it prefers EARLIER in the body; here it is to give
reorg.c something it can move LATER. It generalises to any block ending in a
branch whose only other insn feeds that branch.

### THE `non-constant-base + index` RULE IS WORTH ONE `addu` OPERAND ORDER, AND ONLY ON AN UNSCALED INDEX

Same function, quantifying the existing record-pointer lever at its minimum.
For a byte read at a constant displacement off a non-constant base with a
variable index:

| spelling | differing | the word |
|---|---|---|
| `*((u8 *)p + n + 0x3A)` | **0** | `addu $v0, $s0, $v1` -- base first |
| `((u8 *)p)[n + 0x3A]` | 1 | `addu $v0, $v1, $s0` -- index first |
| `*((u8 *)p + 0x3A + n)` | 1 | `addu $v0, $v1, $s0` -- index first |

`fold` moves the `TREE_CONSTANT` operand of a commutative `PLUS` to the right,
so folding the constant in BEFORE the variable index -- by writing
`+ 0x3A + n`, or by letting a subscript build `n + 0x3A` first -- leaves the
index as the left operand of the final `addu`. Writing the index immediately
after the base, constant last, keeps the base on the left and the constant as a
displacement.

**The useful negative, from the same function: the lever only bites on an
UNSCALED index.** At `*(T **)((u8 *)p + n * 4 + 0x1C)` all four spellings tried
reach 0 differing -- `+ n * 4 + 0x1C`, `+ 0x1C + n * 4`,
`((s32 *)((u8 *)p + 0x1C))[n]`, and `(u8 *)(n * 4) + (s32)p + 0x1C` -- because
the `sll` makes the index a fresh pseudo, which lands on the left of the `addu`
under every spelling. Do not spend compiles permuting a `* 4` subscript's
operand order.

## A HALF-WORD STORE TO A STACK LOCAL MUST BE A COMPONENT_REF, NOT A CAST THROUGH A `u8 *` -- THE CAST LETS THE NEXT ARGUMENT LOAD FLOAT ABOVE THE STORE

Established on `func_80097AD0` and `func_800A895C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, worth
**two words and 66-70 differing out of 96**.

The function builds a 0x18-byte record in a stack local and passes its address.
Spelling the half-word fields as `*(u16 *)((u8 *)&t + 0x2) = ...` instead of
`t.unk_02 = ...` compiles to a function that is **shorter than the target** --
94 words against 96, 66 to 70 differing depending on which fields are cast.
Shorter, not longer, which is the thing to recognise: a cast store is an
`INDIRECT_REF` through an address computed from the frame pointer, so
`MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` is clear on it, `memrefs_conflict_p` cannot prove the next
statement's load of an unrelated global disjoint from it either -- but sched1's
`true_dependence` test (`sched.c`, see also the `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` lever above)
takes the structure flag as licence to *reorder*, and the argument load for the
following call is hoisted above the store, collapsing two insns into one
pattern the target does not have.

With a named field the store is a `COMPONENT_REF` off a `VAR_DECL`, the alias
set is exact, the store stays put, and the record's stores come out in source
order.

**The rule, stated so it is usable: if a candidate for a function that builds a
stack record comes out SHORTER than the target with a large differing count, do
not look for a missing statement -- look for a cast store.** This is the
opposite diagnosis from the usual one, and it is why the cast idiom that is
mandatory for *parameter* records (where the field offsets are not yours to
name) is wrong for *locals* (where they are).

## A NEGATIVE CONSTANT STORED TO A HALF-WORD FIELD WITNESSES THE FIELD'S SIGNEDNESS, IN ONE WORD

Same pair, 2026-11-02, worth exactly 1 differing word.

`f->unk_16 = -4;` where `unk_16` is declared `s16` gives

    addiu $v0, $zero, -0x4

and where it is declared `u16` gives

    ori   $v0, $zero, 0xFFFC

Both store the same 16 bits, so the field's *contents* are indistinguishable at
runtime; only the materialisation differs. The front end narrows the constant to
the field's type before `expand_expr` sees it, and a `u16`-typed `-4` is the
positive `0xFFFC`, which `TARGET_CONST_OK_FOR_LETTER` routes to `ori` rather
than `addiu`.

So a single differing word at a constant store to a half-word field is a
*signedness* report on the field, and the fix is in the typedef, not the
statement. The same tell works in reverse when reading a listing cold: `ori`
with a 0xFFxx immediate into a halfword field means the field is unsigned.

## TWO INDEPENDENT HALF STORES TO ONE STACK LOCAL COME OUT IN SOURCE ORDER, AND A PRE-LOOP STORE TO A FIELD THE LOOP OVERWRITES IS REAL SOURCE

Same pair, 2026-11-02, worth 4 differing words when the order is wrong.

Two consequences of the `COMPONENT_REF` alias exactness above, both measured:

**Order is witnessed.** Two stores to different fields of the same stack record,
with no intervening call or load, are emitted in the order they are written --
swapping them is 4 differing words, not 0. Unlike stores through a cast
(reorderable) or stores to two different globals (sched1 may interleave), these
are a reliable read of source order, and a small rotation in a record-building
prologue is worth permuting on that basis.

**A redundant-looking store before a loop is real.** `func_80097AD0` stores
`t.unk_0A` once before the `for` and again as the loop's first statement, which
looks like a hoist to delete. It is not: the target's `sh` for it sits in the
`blez`'s delay slot at the loop guard, which only happens if the store is
outside the loop in the source. **A store that the loop's own first iteration
immediately overwrites, appearing in a delay slot at the guard, is a source
statement** -- deleting it loses the word and gains nothing, because reorg will
not fill that slot from inside the loop body.

## TWO SHORT LOCALS FOR A REPEATED STRUCT FIELD CAN DECIDE WHICH CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER THE STRUCT POINTER GETS -- `reg_n_refs` IS TAKEN AT *flow* TIME AND NEVER RECOMPUTED

Established on `func_8008D0B8`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02, worth **98 differing
words out of 323** at an identical instruction count.

Writing the eight silhouette corrections as `SP->unk_6C = SP->unk_6C -
SP->unk_1C;` ... `SP->unk_7A = SP->unk_7A - SP->unk_1E;` emits the identical 323
instructions with **`$s0` and `$s1` exchanged** -- the scratchpad pointer in
`$s0` and the polygon pointer in `$s1`, where the target has them the other way
round. Hoisting the two probes into `s16 px; s16 py;` at the top of the polygon
body -- the same instructions, because the two `lhu`s were already CSEd into
registers -- flips the pair and reaches 0.

THE MECHANISM, out of `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18`. `global.c`'s
`allocno_compare` (:587-610) sorts by
`floor_log2(n_refs) * n_refs / live_length`, `find_reg` hands the
first-sorted call-crossing allocno the first free callee-saved register in
`REG_ALLOC_ORDER`, and both inputs come from `REG_N_REFS`/`REG_LIVE_LENGTH`.
**In this compiler those are set by `flow_analysis` and never recomputed.**
`toplev.c`'s pass order is cse -> loop -> cse -> *flow* -> combine -> regmove ->
sched1 -> local_alloc -> global_alloc; unlike later gccs there is no
`recompute_reg_usage` before `local_alloc`. So the counts are taken on the
PRE-COMBINE, PRE-SCHED1 RTL, and `REG_N_REFS` is weighted by `loop_depth`.
Eight redundant reads of `SP->unk_1C`/`unk_1E` four loops deep therefore still
count toward the scratchpad pointer's priority even though cse removed them
long before anything was emitted.

Measured on the dump (`tools/cdkgcc -O2 -G0 -da`, then `.flow` and `.greg`):
the scratchpad pointer was pseudo 87, weighted refs 255 over a 311-insn range,
priority 5.74; the polygon pointer pseudo 84, 66 refs over 144 insns, priority
2.75. `.greg`'s `;; 18 regs to allocate:` lists them adjacent in that order and
`;; Register dispositions:` then shows `87 in 16` and `84 in 17`.

Three corollaries:

- **a pure `$sN`-for-`$sM` exchange across an otherwise byte-exact function is
  this, not a shape error.** Look for a struct field read several times inside a
  deep loop and give it a local.
- **the same locals are worth NOTHING where the inner pointer has a biased
  giv.** In `func_8008D5C4`, where loop.c splits the polygon pointer's
  references between it and a `p + 0xB` giv, the identical change is 0
  differing either way (both measured). The lever fires on the sibling WITHOUT
  a giv.
- declaration order of the locals is inert: five orders, all 98 differing.

## THE SCHEDULER'S PLACEMENT OF A PROLOGUE'S *NON*-STORES IS A SOURCE-ORDER QUESTION TOO

`func_8008D0B8`/`func_8008D5C4`, 2026-11-02, worth 5 differing words in D5C4 and
2 in D0B8.

The existing "sched WILL REORDER TWO STORES" lever says store order is a good
first guess at source order, and it was: all twelve head orders measured emit
the six stores in source order. What moves is the `lw` feeding the last store
and the `addiu` feeding one of the middle ones. With the bound written fifth
(`1C, 1E, 4C, 2C, 4E, 18`) the `addiu` floats to the top of the block and the
`lw` sinks one slot; with the bound written **third**
(`1C, 1E, 2C, 4C, 4E, 18`) both land where the target has them and the function
is 0.

So: **when a residue is a 2-5 word rotation confined to one straight-line
prologue and the stores already agree, permute the source statements anyway** --
the rotation is of the insns that FEED them. A 12-point grid over the head costs
about a minute; the two 18-20 differing rows in it also tell you when you are
permuting in the wrong direction.

## A BACKWARD POINTER WALK WANTS THE DECREMENT PRE-BIASED, NOT AT THE TOP OF THE BODY

`func_8008D5C4`, 2026-11-02, worth one word plus a delay slot: 304 words / 171
differing against 303 / 9.

`for (;;) { p--; ...body...; if (term) break; }` and
`p = arr - 1; for (;;) { ...body...; if (term) break; p--; }` are the same loop,
but only the second gives the target's code. In the first, loop.c's biased giv
(`$s1 = p + 0xB`, created at the terminator's own offset) absorbs the peeled
decrement while the base pointer is left to a `move`: you get
`addiu $s1, $v1, 0xB` / `addiu $s1, $s1, -0xC` / `move $s2, $v1` and an empty
delay slot on the guard. In the second the base is decremented once before the
loop and the giv is derived from the decremented value:
`addiu $s2, $s2, -0xC` in the guard's delay slot, then `addiu $s1, $s2, 0xB`.

This is the mirror of the family's "`p++` as the LAST statement" rule -- run it
in reverse, including where the `-1` goes.

### ONE CELL LIST, TWO POLYGON RECORD SIZES (ovl_town collision geometry)

Not a compiler lever, a fact about the data that cost a wrong reading once.
`m->unk_04[cell]` in ovl_town's collision geometry is reached by six functions
and does **not** have one record type.

- `func_8008DA80`/`DFB4`/`E4EC`/`EA20`/`D0B8` walk a **0x18-byte** record:
  vertex indices at +0x00/02/04/06, normal index at +0x10, flags at +0x16/17.
- `func_8008D5C4` walks a **0xC-byte** record -- vertex indices at
  +0x00/02/04/06, normal index at +0x08, flags at +0x0A/0B -- **backward**,
  gated on bit 6 of the 0x18-record's `unk_17`.

Both put the flag halfword at size-2 with the same bit assignment: bit 0 of the
top byte is the per-polygon skip (`lbu` + `andi 1`), bit 7 is the end-of-run
marker. **The stride in the listing (`addiu $sN, $sN, ±0xC` vs `±0x18`) is what
tells you which record you are looking at**, and a 0xC stride is not a sign you
have mis-read the function.

## A NARROW-TYPED BOOLEAN IS WHAT KEEPS gcc's VARIABLE-ASSIGNMENT COPY ALIVE -- FOUR SPELLINGS, THREE OUTCOMES

`func_800970FC`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. Worth 16 differing words and one word of
length.

`s32 flag = (p != q);` compiles to `(set 109 (gtu ...))` + `(set 94 109)`, and
cse always copy-propagates `94` -> `109`, leaving ONE pseudo whose spill store
lands at the def in the prologue. `s16 flag` / `s8 flag` makes the second insn a
mode conversion instead of a copy; the comparison's `nonzero_bits` is 1, so
combine drops the extension and emits a plain `addu $t0, $fp, $zero`, which cse
cannot propagate away. Reload then spills the COPY (one 8-byte slot) and leaves
the expression in a callee-saved register, which moves the spill store out of
the prologue and down into the first use's delay slot.

Measured, same source logic throughout:

| declaration | words | aligned differing |
|---|---|---|
| `s32` / `u32` | 465 | 25 |
| `u8` / `u16` | 466 | 11 (the zero-extension survives as `andi 0xFF`) |
| `s8` / `s16` | 466 | **9** |

So **a boolean local's declared type is a real lever, not cosmetic**, and the
three outcomes are distinguishable at the listing: no copy at all (`s32`), an
`andi 0xFF` (`u8`/`u16`), a bare `addu ... $zero` (`s8`/`s16`).

## A TEMPORARY FOR THE ADDED OPERAND DECIDES `addu`'s OPERAND ORDER, AND THE SOURCE ORDER DOES NOT

`func_800970FC`, 2026-11-02, worth 18 differing words (29 -> 11) at no change in
instruction count.

`p->x = v + r->field;` emits `addu $v0, $v0, $sN` -- the loaded field as `rs` --
because combine substitutes the load into the `plus` and its "put the more
complex expression first" canonicalisation swaps the operands. Writing
`r->field + v` is **byte-identical**: the source order is not the lever.

`w = r->field; p->x = v + w;` makes the load its own insn, so combine sees
`(plus (reg) (reg))`, does not reorder, and emits `addu $v0, $sN, $v0`.

So when a residue is nothing but `addu` operand order at a store of
`coordinate + field`, the fix is a temporary for the field, one per site.
**It does NOT apply where the sum is stored as a byte**: there combine narrows
the load to `lbu` and the order already matches. Eighteen sites in this
function, all needing it.

## AN EXPLICIT EARLY `return` IS A cse-REGION BOUNDARY LEVER, NOT JUST A LAYOUT ONE -- AND ITS RESIDUE IS INVISIBLE TO ovlverify

`func_800970FC`, 2026-11-02, worth **14 words of length** (480 against 466), a
callee-saved register and a second 8-byte stack slot.

`cse_end_of_basic_block` (`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:8056`) follows a
conditional jump only when `LABEL_NUSES(target) == 1` and the target label is
preceded by a BARRIER, and it follows at most `PATHLENGTH - 1 == 9` of them per
extended block. `if (c) { return 0; }` leaves
`(set v0 0) (jump L_ret) BARRIER` in front of the `if`'s end label, so that
jump becomes followable and consumes a path slot; `if (!c) { everything }` does
not.

On this function that one slot is the difference between cse's first extended
block ending at `0x80097434` and ending 129 words later. With it, the eight
texcoord `bgez`es plus the first `if (flag)` exhaust the budget in the right
place and the later `g->unk_00` / `r1->unk_00` loads keep their `0x0(reg)` form.
Without it cse folds them back to `%lo(sym)($hi)`, which keeps a `%hi` pseudo
live for the whole function, costs a callee-saved register, spills two more
values and adds a second stack slot.

**THE TRAP, and it is the important half of this entry: that residue is
invisible to `ovlverify`.** It masks `%hi`/`%lo`, so `lw $a0, %lo(D_80083160)($s3)`
and `lw $a0, 0x0($s6)` both mask to `8EC40000` -- a function can read
`0 differing` with the wrong addressing form from end to end. Two ways to catch
it: count the `%lo` references in the candidate's own `.s` against the target's
raw words, or gate on `make build/town.bin`, which links the relocations and
compares the real bytes. **The container build is the only authority that sees
through the mask** -- including for a wrong-but-defined `jal` callee, which
links cleanly and then differs by one word.

## A SECOND `extern` WITH THE SAME `__asm__` NAME DEFEATS cse's UNIFICATION OF TWO POINTERS TO ONE GLOBAL

`func_800970FC`, 2026-11-02, worth 2 words directly plus the whole second half's
register assignment.

Two pointer locals both set to `&SYM` are ONE pseudo after cse -- `.rtl` has two
`lo_sum`s, `.cse` has one -- which forces the pointer to live across the whole
function. Every *source* spelling tried failed to separate them: a second
variable, the same variable reassigned, an inline cast expression at each use,
and moving the assignment later. All byte-identical.

Declaring the address a second time and using the alias for the second region
does separate them:

    extern UnkSlot D_80082E80_b __asm__("D_80082E80");

Two pseudos, disjoint live ranges, the allocator reuses the register, and the
second region gets its own `lui`/`addiu`.

This is the same declaration device as `include/structs.h`'s
`extern u32 D_800814A0_a[1] __asm__("D_800814A0");` (`docs/overlays.md` lever 2)
applied to a different mechanism -- there it was `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P`, here it is
cse's value numbering. It is also how to reach one address under two types
without merging the typedefs and disturbing another landed function.

## A SHARED COORDINATE NEEDS ONE VARIABLE PER REGION, NOT ONE PER AXIS

`func_800970FC`, 2026-11-02, worth 41 differing words (70 -> 29) at the same word
count.

The function draws two groups of primitives from two different rects. Its x
lands in the same register in both groups and is ONE variable; its y lands in
two different registers and must be TWO. Measured:

| spelling | aligned differing |
|---|---|
| one `x`, one `y` | 70 |
| one `x`, separate `y`/`y2` | **29** |
| separate `x`/`x2`, one `y` | 55 |
| separate `x`/`x2` and `y`/`y2` | 65 |

**A value that appears in two registers in the target is two source variables;
a value that appears in one is one** -- and that is readable straight off the
listing before any compile. Do not reach for "one local per axis" symmetry; the
regions, not the axes, are what the register assignment follows.

### THE SCRATCHPAD WANTS A STRUCT TYPEDEF, NOT A `u16 *` -- SAME MEM_IN_STRUCT_P RULE AS A STACK RECORD

`func_800970FC`, 2026-11-02, worth the last 4 words (11 differing -> 0).

`u16 *scratch = (u16 *)0x1F800000; scratch[0] = px; scratch[1] = py;` are
`INDIRECT_REF`s of scalar type, `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` is clear, and sched2
interleaves the two `sh`es with the `lhu`/`sh` pairs that follow them. Through a
struct pointer they are `COMPONENT_REF`s, the dependence survives, and the two
stores stay adjacent and in source order.

This is the stack-record cast-store lever above, at a fixed absolute address:
**the 0x1F800000 region wants one typedef per access pattern, and a new typedef
is cheaper than fighting the schedule.** Reaching the word at +0x13C through
`(u8 *)scratch + 0x13C` has the same problem; put it in the struct.

## `schedule_select`'s HAZARD PICK DECIDES WHETHER A LOOP PREHEADER IS EMITTED BEFORE OR AFTER THE STATEMENT THAT PRECEDES THE LOOP -- AND A BYTE STORE WINS THAT CONTEST WHERE A HALFWORD STORE DOES NOT

Established on `func_800BACB0` against `func_800BA930`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
Worth **39 differing words out of 224**, and it is the entire reason two
functions that are one source with two different constants need two different
spellings.

sched1 schedules a block **backward**, so its `T-1` slot is the block's LAST
word. In a block where a loop's preheader shares space with ordinary
statements -- here the merge block of a `% 0x1000` idiom also holds `i = 0` and
three `lui`/`addiu` pairs -- every insn is `priority = 1`, they form ONE group,
and `schedule_select` (`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/sched.c:2662-2742`, the pick
at :2703-2718) hands that last slot to the member with the greatest
`potential_hazard`. The dump says so out loud:
`;; insn 39 has a greater potential hazard`.

**A `movqi_internal2` store (`sb`) wins that contest against an `addiu`; a
`movhi_internal2` store (`sh`) does not.** So:

| before the loop | preheader emitted | differing |
|---|---|---|
| an `sh` and an `sb` | FIRST | 39 |
| only the `sh` (`sb` moved above the modulo) | LAST, correctly | 11 (fails elsewhere) |
| an `sh` and an `sb` + `__asm__ volatile("")` after them | LAST, correctly | **0** |

The empty `asm` gives both stores a dependent, so neither is ready at `T-1`, the
preheader takes the last slots, and the modulo shape, the delay-slot steal and
the whole `$s2`/`$s3` assignment fall out correct in one step.

**What does NOT substitute, all measured at 39:** `volatile` on either store
(`memrefs_conflict_p` separates `0x66+2` from `0x97+1` whatever the qualifiers),
non-struct cast stores for either field, a temp for the call's result in two
declaration positions, three declaration-order permutations, `do/while` and
`goto` loop forms, and a cursor pointer instead of a subscript. Placing the
barrier BEFORE both stores is catastrophic (225 words, 214 differing); between
the two stores it is 8.

## THE SIGNED `x % (1 << n)` IDIOM HAS TWO SHAPES AND WHICH ONE YOU GET IS A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A CAUSE

Same pair, 2026-11-02. Do not spend compiles permuting the division.

- `addu $t, $x, $zero` + `bgez` + `addiu 0xFFF` + ONE `sra`, the copy filling
  the branch's delay slot -- appears when something clobbers `$v0` between the
  compare and the shift.
- `bgez` + a `sra` **duplicated into both arms**, the taken arm's copy stolen
  into the delay slot by reorg's `steal_delay_list_from_target` -- appears when
  nothing does.

So when a residue sits on a `%`-by-power-of-two, **look at what sched put after
it**, not at how the modulo is written. On this pair the two shapes are both
reachable from the same source text and the discriminator is the preheader
lever above.

## A LOAD THAT CANNOT MOVE ABOVE A STORE IS PINNED, AND ITS PINNED POSITION IS WHAT DECIDES THE REGISTER ALLOCATION

`func_800BA930`, 2026-11-02, worth one word of length (223 against 224) and 39
differing.

A value stored through one pointer and a value loaded through another must be
written in the target's order, because the load cannot move above a store gcc
cannot disambiguate. In block 4 the target's `nop` after the last colour `lbu`
is only explicable if `x = o->unk_08` is read **between** `p->unk_0E = ...` and
`p->unk_08 = 0x19`; writing it after both lets sched fill that slot and loses
the word.

The second half is the reusable part: **that forced position is also what makes
`p`'s and `x`'s live ranges overlap**, which is why global-alloc cannot give `p`
the register it gives `x`. A pinned load is an allocation lever, not just a
scheduling one -- so when a residue is a register assignment you cannot explain,
look for a load whose position is forced by a nearby store.

## ONE POINTER VARIABLE REUSED ACROSS N BLOCKS IS A global-alloc QUANTITY AND GETS ONE HARD REGISTER IN ALL OF THEM; N VARIABLES ARE local-alloc QUANTITIES AND GET N

`func_800BA930`, 2026-11-02. Worth 20 differing words, and the wrong answer in
the other direction costs a word of length too.

The function fills four entity blocks through a renderable pointer. The target
uses `$a2` for that role in its two `0x136` blocks and `$a0` in its two `0x36`
blocks -- **two registers, so two variables**:

| spelling | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| one shared pointer | 224 | 20 |
| **two pointers, one per block TYPE** | 224 | **0** |
| four pointers, one per block | 225 | 162 |

**Count the distinct registers the target uses for a role and declare exactly
that many variables** -- not one, and not one per block. This is the same
counting rule as the "shared coordinate needs one variable per REGION" lever,
read off the listing before any compile.

## A `volatile` RE-READ PLUS A DEGENERATE LOOP DOES EVERYTHING A FULL MEMORY CLOBBER DOES

`func_8003E758` in `csrc/unk_11F0C.c` re-reads `q[0]` in one arm where the
entry block has already read it. From 2026-10 that was the project's first asm
device, `__asm__ volatile ("" :: "r" (q) : "memory")`, worth 13 words. It is
three separate jobs, and plain C does all three:

* the read must survive cse (3 words) -- a `volatile` MEM is not a candidate,
  so the arm reloads;
* the `or` of `PHYS_TO_K0` must stay ahead of the reload, which is what leaves
  the load-delay nop (1 word) -- the reload then reuses `$v0` and the
  anti-dependence does it;
* `q`'s allocno priority must clear `nsec`'s so `q` takes `$s1` (9 words) --
  and that was the `"r" (q)` operand's whole contribution, nothing more than
  one free reference.

| spelling | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| **`do { nsec = *(volatile u32 *) q >> 23; } while (0);`** | **698** | **0** |
| the same read wrapped `while (1) { ...; break; }` | 698 | 0 |
| the original asm, memory clobber and all | 698 | 0 |
| `__asm__ volatile ("" ::: "memory")` alone | 698 | 9 |
| that clobber WITH the wrapper | 698 | 0 |
| the volatile read with no wrapper | 697 | 564 |
| ditto via `volatile u32 *vq = q`, or `((volatile u32 *) q)[0]` | 697 | 564 |
| the same read wrapped `for (;;) { ...; break; }` | 697 | 564 |
| the volatile read twice, for q's extra reference | 698 | 5 |
| both arms computing `nsec` themselves | 696 | 560 |
| nothing at all | 695 | 559 |

Two things to carry away. **`for (;;)` is not interchangeable with
`do/while(0)` or `while (1)` as a reference weight** -- it emits no
`NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` here, and that is the whole difference between 698/0 and
697/564. And **a memory clobber whose operand list exists only to add a
reference is two devices wearing one coat**: price the jobs separately before
concluding a clobber is needed, because the reference half is always plain C.

## A `do { } while (0)` AROUND A CALL IS THE GR-CONSTRAINED USE AT A JOIN THAT AN ASM OUTPUT OPERAND OTHERWISE BUYS

`func_8004A574` in `csrc/unk_1C540.c` multiplies in both arms of an `if` and
passes the product to a call. The product's pseudo is `mulsi3_internal`'s
operand 0, constrained `"=l"`, so it lives in `LO` across the arms and the
single `mflo` lands at the argument setup; the listing instead copies `LO` out
at the JOIN and sets `$a0` up separately, for dbr to hoist into the `beqz`'s
delay slot. The device was `__asm__ volatile ("" : "+r" (v) : : "$4")`, and
its comment said a GR-constrained use with no instruction behind it was not
expressible in C. **It is**: a degenerate loop around the call is a block
boundary at the join, and the `LO`->GR copy lands there.

| spelling | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| **`do { } while (0)` around the call + `__asm__ ("" : : : "$4")`** | **41** | **0** |
| the same with `volatile` on the asm | 41 | 0 |
| the original `"+r" (v)` asm with the `$4` clobber | 41 | 0 |
| the wrapper alone, no asm at all | 41 | 2 |
| `v = v + w; v = v - w;` at the join, no asm | 41 | 2 |
| the bare `$4` clobber alone, no wrapper | 41 | 5 |

The residual 2 is the REGISTER, not the position: built is `mflo $a0` with a
nop in the delay slot where the listing has `mflo $v0` and `move $a0, $v0`
hoisted into it. `v` prefers `$a0` from its own argument copy and nothing is
live in `$a0` across the `mflo` to make `prune_preferences` drop it, which is
what the clobber declares. Also 2, all with the wrapper: a `t = v` copy either
side of it, the arms writing `t` and passing it, a block-local `v`, two nested
wrappers, a free-reference pair on `p`, and one extra mention of `s` after the
join; `v = v + s - s` and a free-reference pair on `s` are 12.

**Separate a device's jobs and price each one.** Both levers here came from
splitting an asm that was doing two things, and in both cases one half was
plain C all along.

## A LOOP'S SUBSCRIPT BIAS MUST LIVE IN THE BOUND, NOT IN THE SUBSCRIPT, WHEN THE BODY ALSO STORES A BIASED VALUE -- AND THE WRONG FORM IS *SHORTER*

Measured on `func_800B0024`, `func_800B3734` and `func_800B4D64`, ovl_town,
2026-11-02. Worth one word of length and 41 differing.

The same two-iteration loop writes a pointer into `arr[k]` and a `k`-scaled
halfword into `arr[k]->unk_04->unk_08`, over subscripts 2 and 3:

| spelling | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| `for (i = 2; i < 4; i++)` ... `arr[i]` ... `= (i - 2) * 0x80` | **68/68** | **0** |
| `for (i = 0; i < 2; i++)` ... `arr[i + 2]` ... `= i * 0x80` | 67/68 | 41 |

The two forms are not interchangeable and **the wrong one is SHORTER**, which
is why it reads like a near-miss worth polishing rather than a structural
error. In the `[i + 2]` form the constant folds into both array loads'
displacements (`lw $v0, 0x8($v0)` against the target's `0x0`) and the stored
value becomes a plain `sll $v1, $a0, 7` off the counter; in the `(i - 2)` form
the value cannot be reached with one shift, loop.c gives it its own induction
variable in `$a1` initialised to 0, and the resulting `addiu $a1, $a1, 0x80`
fills the loop branch's delay slot that the other form leaves as a `nop`.

**THE DIAGNOSTIC IN THE DUMP: a `nop` in a loop-closing branch's delay slot
where the target has an `addiu` of a power of two.** That says the VALUE, not
the subscript, carries the bias.

`func_800B0024` demonstrates both halves, which is what makes it a clean
witness: its FIRST loop runs `for (i = 0; i < 2; i++)` with an unbiased
`i * 0x80` and is the `sll ,7` shape, byte-exact. So the rule is about where
the bias is, not about a house style.

The reduce-or-recompute decision itself is
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/loop.c:3996`, `if (v->lifetime * threshold *
benefit < insn_count && ! bl->reversed)` -> leave the giv unreduced, with
`benefit` already docked `add_cost * bl->biv_count` at :3963 for the increments
the reduction would need. **Which of that test's inputs the bias flips has NOT
been traced** -- both spellings produce a giv with `mult_val` 0x80 and they
differ in `add_val` and in how many address givs share the biv. The measurement
is solid; treat the mechanism as the place to look rather than as established.

## A `<< k` BETWEEN A SIGN-EXTENDED LOAD AND A NARROWING STORE TURNS `lh` INTO `lhu`; `* (1 << k)` DOES NOT

Measured on `func_8009792C`/`func_800A878C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. Worth
2 differing on otherwise exact 105- and 116-word functions -- which is exactly
the shape of "near-miss worth polishing" and reads like an allocation problem.

With `extern s16 TBL[];`:

    *(s16 *)(m + 2) = *(u16 *)(t + 2) - (TBL[i] << 4);   /* lh -> lhu : WRONG */
    *(s16 *)(m + 2) = *(u16 *)(t + 2) - TBL[i] * 16;     /* lh        : RIGHT */

Both emit the same eight instructions, `sll $2,$2,4` included -- **only the
load's opcode differs** (`0x25` vs `0x21`). The store is `sh`, so only the low
16 bits of the difference are live; with a `SHIFT_EXPR` in the way the mask is
propagated back through the chain into the load and the `SIGN_EXTEND` is
dropped, while a `MULT_EXPR` blocks it.

Eight variants measured in one probe file:

| spelling | table load |
|---|---|
| `- (TBL[i] << 4)` | `lhu` |
| `- ((s32)TBL[i] << 4)` | `lhu` -- the cast does NOT help |
| `-(TBL[i] << 4) + *(u16 *)(t + 2)` | `lhu` -- commuting does NOT help |
| `- TBL[i] * 16` | **`lh`** |
| `s32 c = ... - (TBL[i] << 4); *(s16 *)(m+2) = c;` | `lh` |
| `s32 c = TBL[i]; ... - (c << 4)` | `lh` |

So the cures are the multiply or an `s32` temp breaking the statement; the
multiply is the one-statement form and also reproduces the target's `addu`
operand order.

Mechanism: the mask propagation is `force_to_mode`, reached from `simplify_set`
for a narrowing `SET_DEST`. `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/combine.c:7672` is the
`case SIGN_EXTEND:` arm of the mode-narrowing walk, and `:7614`/`:7661` are the
`LOAD_EXTEND_OP (...) == SIGN_EXTEND` tests that let a MIPS sub-word MEM be
treated as already extended. **Those arms were read but not instrumented** --
treat the citation as where to look and the two-line measurement as the
evidence.

## WHICH SIDE OF A CALL A STORE SITS ON IS READABLE OFF THE DELAY SLOTS, AND IT IS WORTH A WORD

Established on `func_800AEFD8` against `func_800B6A0C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02.
Two near-siblings that differ in **precisely this one line**, measured in both
directions.

A statement adjacent to a call can only fill that call's delay slot if it is
written BEFORE it. reorg's scan is backward:
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/reorg.c:3086`,
`for (trial = prev_nonnote_insn (insn); ! stop_search_p (trial, 1); trial = next_trial)`,
with `next_trial = prev_nonnote_insn (trial)` at `:3089` and the chosen insn
deleted from its place and prepended to the delay list at `:3118-3124`.
`stop_search_p` will not let the scan cross a label, jump or barrier, so it
never reaches past the call into the following block.

**So the listing tells you the source order directly:**

- a `sw` in the **`jal`'s** delay slot -> the store is written **before** the call;
- a `sw` in the delay slot of the **`j` that follows** the call -> written **after** it.

And the two are not interchangeable:

| | store BEFORE `func_8004491C` | store AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| `func_800AEFD8` (target 66) | 67 words, 30 differing | **66, 0** |
| `func_800B6A0C` (target 65) | **65, 0** | 64 words, 30 differing |

The ±1 word is mechanical and is the thing to recognise. With the store BEFORE
the call it eats the `jal`'s slot, the `addiu $a1,$a1,%lo` becomes an ordinary
insn, and the following `j` has nothing local left -- so it takes
`move $v0, $s0` from its own target and jumps PAST it, leaving the shared copy
alive for the other path. With the store AFTER, the `jal`'s slot takes the
`addiu`, the `j`'s slot takes the `sw`, and the `j` lands ON the shared
`move $v0, $s0` with no duplicate.

This is distinct from the existing "a constant address can fill a slot where a
symbol cannot" lever and from the two entries about WHICH insn a slot takes:
the new content is the inference DIRECTION -- reading a store's side of a call
off the slots -- plus the one-word price, which is what makes it cheap to check
before compiling.

### THREE CORROBORATIONS WITH FRESH NUMBERS, ON THE allocate-or-teardown TEMPLATE

`func_800AEFD8`/`func_800B14B0`/`func_800B6A0C`, 2026-11-02. No new mechanism;
these put numbers on entries that had none.

* **The nested `if` is required; neither early-return shape works.** Lifting
  the null check out as `if (o == 0) return 0;` over a flat body is 66 words
  against 65 and **49 differing** (`func_800B6A0C`). Replacing just the
  teardown arm's `o = 0;` + shared `return o;` with `return 0;` is 65 against
  66 and **46 differing** (`func_800B14B0`).
* **Mirror case for `func_8009792C`/`func_800A878C`**, where the single return
  value IS the pointer that was tested: `if (p != NULL) { ... } return p;` is
  **two words cheaper** than `if (p == NULL) return NULL; ...; return p;` --
  105 against 107, and 116 against 118. The early form costs a `j` to the
  epilogue plus a `move $v0, $zero`. This is the "one arm LEAVES the function"
  case where the inversion is NOT wanted, because the shared tail
  (`addu $v0, $s1, $zero` + epilogue) is reachable from both paths.
* **A named local for an interior view is load-bearing, not cosmetic.**
  `u8 *v = (u8 *)o + 0x20;` against spelling every access as `(u8 *)o + 0x20`
  with absolute offsets off `o`: 65 words / 0 differing against 64 / **45
  differing**. The target keeps the view in a callee-saved register across
  three calls (`addiu $s1, $s0, 0x20` in the `beqz`'s delay slot), which a
  named local gives and which cse will not reconstruct from repeated `o + 0x20`.

### A CALL CAN PERMUTE ITS ARGUMENTS, AND THE CALLEE'S OWN LISTING IS THE CORROBORATION

`func_800AEFD8`, 2026-11-02, worth one word and 45 differing.

Its six parameters do NOT arrive at `func_800AEEF0` in order. The listing's
argument setup is `$a1=p1, $a2=p4, $a3=p5, 0x10($sp)=p2, 0x14($sp)=p3,
0x18($sp)=p6`, i.e. `(v, p1, p4, p5, p2, p3, p6)`, where its two near-siblings
pass theirs straight through. Writing it in order is 67 words / 45 differing.

**The corroboration is one level down and costs one grep:** `func_800AEEF0`
forwards its own args 1/2/3/4/7 into `func_800AEEBC` and its args 5/6 into
`func_800AEBC4` -- two groups, which is exactly why the caller's parameters
arrive split. So when a forwarding call's argument order looks scrambled, read
the CALLEE's listing for a grouping that explains it rather than assuming you
have mis-numbered the parameters.

## THE NARROWED `/ C % C` RESULT HAS TYPE `short`, SO THE DESTINATION LOCAL'S DECLARED TYPE DECIDES WHETHER YOU PAY A WIDENING

Established on `func_800BA00C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. **Worth two words and 229
differing out of 279 -- it was the entire residue of a 109-DIFF park that had
already survived a 142,531-candidate permuter run.**

This extends the existing entry "`% C` is NARROWED by the front end, and a cast
will not stop it", which covers the operand side and the `sll 16`/`sra 16`
*inside* an expression but not the assignment.

`build_binary_op` sets `shorten` for `TRUNC_DIV_EXPR` at
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/c-typeck.c:2024-2032` and for `TRUNC_MOD_EXPR` at
`:2073-2081`, in both cases whenever the divisor is an `INTEGER_CST` other than
-1; `:2352` then runs `get_narrower` on both operands and `:2387-2397` resets
`result_type` to the narrow common type. So with an `s16` source field:

    s32 dir = s->unk_66 / 0x200 % 4;   /* subu ; sll 16 ; sra 16  -- 2 extra words */
    s16 dir = s->unk_66 / 0x200 % 4;   /* subu                                     */
    s8  dir = s->unk_66 / 0x200 % 4;   /* subu                                     */

Measured: `s32` 281 words / 229 differing; `s8` and `s16` 279 / 0. A `(s32)`
cast on the dividend does NOT help -- `get_narrower` strips the `NOP_EXPR` and
the output is identical.

**THE DIAGNOSTIC:** a lone `sll 16`/`sra 16` pair immediately after the `subu`
that completes a modulo and immediately before the next statement. If the
target has no such pair, the local is narrow.

**AND THE COROLLARY, which is worth more than the lever: when 100+ words differ
by register assignment ONLY and the first two divergent words are a two-word
widening, the fault is a DECLARED TYPE, not the allocator.** A park spent a
142K-candidate permuter run against a base that was two words long for this
reason. **A permuter mutates statements; it will never change a declaration.**
Check the declared type of every local that receives a narrowed expression
before concluding a residue is allocation.

## loop.c DOES NOT HOIST A NARROWING TRUNCATION OUT OF A CONDITIONALLY-EXECUTED LOOP BODY, THOUGH IT HOISTS SYMBOL ADDRESSES FROM THE SAME BLOCK

`func_800BA00C`, 2026-11-02. This corrects a prediction a park had recorded as a
reason to avoid a `for` loop.

In a loop whose body is wrapped in `if (o != 0)`, `scan_loop`'s movables
(`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/loop.c:794-815`) hoist the `lui`/`addiu` pairs for
three symbols into the preheader, and leave a `sll 24`/`sra 24` truncation of a
loop-invariant local where it is -- in the delay-slot-filling position the
target wants. So "a `for` loop would hoist the truncation and cost a word" is
unfounded, and dodging it with a `goto` loop is expensive:

| loop form | words | differing |
|---|---|---|
| `for` loop, the three addresses used inline | **279** | **0** |
| the three addresses written as statements before the loop | 280 | 237 |
| `goto` loop | 279 | **261** |

Without `NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` loop.c never runs at all, so the target's
four-insn preheader -- `i = 0` then the three `lui`/`addiu` pairs in the order
the body mentions them -- cannot be built.

**A `goto` loop and a `for` loop can come out the SAME LENGTH and still differ
in 94% of their words. Length is not evidence about loop form.**

### WHICH OF TWO STORES LANDS IN THE `jal`'s DELAY SLOT IS DECIDED BY THEIR SOURCE ORDER, WHEN THEY ARE OFF DIFFERENT BASES

`func_800CDCA8`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. Four differing words, nothing else in
the function moves -- a clean minimal measurement of a consequence the existing
"STORES TO DISTINCT CONSTANT OFFSETS off one base do not pin source order"
entry does not state.

Target left, the swapped source right:

    33   move a1,s0           addu  $a1, $s0, $zero
    34   lhu  v0,110(a0)      sw    $zero, 0x14($a1)    <<<
    35   move a2,s2           lhu   $v0, 0x6E($a0)      <<<
