    36   sh   v0,114(a0)      addu  $a2, $s2, $zero     <<<
    37   jal  func_800CDE9C   jal   func_800CDE9C
    38   sw   zero,20(a1)     sh    $v0, 0x72($a0)      <<<

With the source in target order (`b->unk_14 = 0;` first), the `sw` to `$a1` is
emitted first and the `sh` to `$a0` sinks into the `jal`'s delay slot. Swapping
the two statements swaps both ends at once.

**The discriminator is the one the existing entry gives, and it holds:** these
two memrefs are off DIFFERENT base pseudos (`$a0` and `$a1`), so
`memrefs_conflict_p` cannot separate them and the order is visible. Off ONE
base they would have floated. The located escape is
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/sched.c:852-861` (read, not instrumented).

### ON A TRUNCATING STORE, A `(u16)` CAST IS FREE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

`func_800CDCA8`, 2026-11-02. The existing `lhu` entry says an `lhu` feeding a
truncating store is NOT evidence of a `(u16)` cast in the source. The converse
is also true and was not stated: **adding the cast is free too.**

`a->unk_72 += 0x400;` and `a->unk_72 = (u16)a->unk_72 + 0x400;` are
byte-identical, as are `a->unk_72 = a->unk_6E;` and
`a->unk_72 = (u16)a->unk_6E;`. The truncating store makes the load's extension
irrelevant, so gcc picks the cheaper zero-extending load either way.

So on a truncating store the cast is a pure style choice in both directions.
That matters because the landed `func_800CD70C`/`func_800CD87C` next door DO
carry `(u16)` casts, where they ARE load-bearing (feeding a divide), and a
reader copying that style into this family will not be punished for it.

## A REG-REG COPY SURVIVES WHEN ITS TWO ENDS ARE READ IN DIFFERENT ARMS OF AN `if`/`else` -- AND IT MUST BE TWO STATEMENTS, INTERLEAVED, NOT A BLOCK AND NOT A CHAIN

Established on `func_800CC644`/`func_800CC8AC`, ovl_town, 2026-11-02. Worth
**two words and 39 differing** (44/39 -> 46/0), and it was the whole residue of
both functions after twenty-odd hand spellings capped at 45 words.

The target's entry block holds, per coordinate, a `sll` into a fresh register
and then an `addu rD, rS, $zero` copying it straight back into the register the
pre-shift value occupied:

    addiu $a0, $a0, 0x60      # x = h2 + 0x60
    addiu $t0, $v1, 0x20      # y = h6 + 0x20
    sll   $t1, $a0, 16        # u = x << 16
    addu  $a0, $t1, $zero     # x = u
    sll   $v1, $t0, 16        # v = y << 16
    bgtz  $a3, .L_interp
    addu  $t0, $v1, $zero     # y = v   (reorg's back-scan takes it into the slot)

and then the **snap arm reads `$t1`/`$v1` (the `sll` results) while the
interpolating arm reads `$a0`/`$t0` (the copies)**. Both ends are live across
the branch, so they conflict, get different hard registers, and the copy is not
a no-op reload can delete.

**The source-level rule, all four clauses measured:**

1. **Two statements, not a chain.** `u = x << 16;` then `x = u;`.
   `x = u = x << 16;` is 44 words / 34 differing -- gcc expands the chain as two
   SETs of the same RHS, not as a copy, and cse folds them.
2. **The two ends must be read in DIFFERENT arms**, and the `sll` result must be
   the one the FALL-THROUGH (snap) arm reads. Same end in both arms: 44/39.
   Swapped which arm reads which end: 44/34.
3. **Interleaved with the computations**, `u=x<<16; x=u; v=y<<16; y=v;`. As a
   block after both shifts: 44/34. As a block after both values you get exactly
   ONE survivor (45 words) whichever order you choose, never two.
4. **The `+ offset` must be its own statement before the shift.** Folding it in
   (`x = (h+0x60)<<16; u = x;`) still gives 46 words but **21 differing**,
   because the target schedules both `addiu`s ahead of both `sll`s and that only
   happens when the halves are separate statements.

**MECHANISM: INFERENCE ON A CITED RULE, NOT AN INSTRUMENTED FINDING.**
`cse_end_of_basic_block` (`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:8056`, the forward
scan at `:8087`, the follow-jumps arm at `:8139-8180`) and `cse_main`'s rescan
loop (`:8371-8420`) mean cse processes this entry block TWICE: once walking
straight past the conditional jump into the fall-through arm (the scan stops
only at a `CODE_LABEL`), and once following the branch into the taken arm,
which is permitted here because `LABEL_NUSES(else) == 1` and the label is
preceded by a BARRIER -- both supplied by the `j`-over-the-else shape. Since
the two passes have different `cse_basic_block_end`s, the first clause of
`make_regs_eqv`'s test (see the `regno_last_uid` lever above) is true in one
pass and false in the other, so they canonicalise in opposite directions and
each arm's read lands on a different pseudo. **No `-da` dumps were taken and
the `make_regs_eqv` line numbers are the other entry's, not fresh.** The
four-clause rule above IS measured.

This is the source-level answer to the open question left by "A REG-REG COPY
WHOSE DESTINATION ALREADY HOLDS THE SOURCE IS DELETED BY jump2", which closes
with "WHY the target's copy survived is not established; it needs RTL between
the two copies that this source does not produce" -- the different-arms shape
keeps such a copy with no `asm` device at all.

**The wrong diagnosis to avoid:** "A REG-TO-REG MOVE IN THE LISTING IS A LOAD
cse DID NOT EQUATE" is the entry to chase FIRST and it is wrong here. These two
moves are genuine copies, not loads -- there is no 32-bit store in the entry
block for a load to be equated against.

### A DIFFERING COUNT THAT MATCHES ANOTHER FUNCTION'S IS NOT EVIDENCE

A process trap, measured on `func_800CC644`, 2026-11-02, and worth one line
because it cost an agent a wrong hypothesis and cost me a wrong brief.

`func_800CD70C`/`func_800CD87C`'s conditional-return error is recorded at 35
and 39 differing. `func_800CC644`'s natural spellings came in at 45 words / 35
differing and 44 / 39 -- the same two numbers, from a different cause. On that
coincidence I briefed an agent that the conditional-return lever was the
likeliest explanation. **It was not, and the agent disproved it rather than
assuming:** probe `p4` (arms inverted) and probe `r6` (snap arm ending in
`return`) both compile BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the natural order, 37 insns each,
same instruction stream. The real cause was clause 2 above.

So: a residue's SIZE identifies nothing. Two functions in the same family
reaching the same differing count by different routes is ordinary, because the
count is just "how many words shifted after the first divergence". Match on the
aligned WORD TABLE, never on the number.

## A LOOP BOUND gcc CAN PROVE NON-NEGATIVE MAKES THE GUARD `beqz`, NOT `blez` -- SO A LONE `beqz` IS NOT A MISSING `== 0` GUARD

Established on `func_80097844` against `func_800ABD74`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03,
as a clean A/B: the same `for (i = 0; i < count; i++)` emits

- **`blez $s2`** when `count` is an incoming `s32` parameter (`func_80097844`,
  58 words, 0 differing), and
- **`beqz $s2`** when `count` is `(func_80069EF8() & 7) | 4`
  (`func_800ABD74`, 59 words, 0 differing).

`nonzero_bits` of `(x & 7) | 4` is 7, so the sign bit is known clear, and
`simplify_comparison` rewrites the comparison. The arm, verified in the CDK
tree:

    /* If we are doing a <= 0 comparison on a value known to have
       a zero sign bit, we can replace this with == 0.  */
    else if (const_op == 0
             && mode_width <= HOST_BITS_PER_WIDE_INT
             && (nonzero_bits (op0, mode)
                 & ((HOST_WIDE_INT) 1 << (mode_width - 1))) == 0)
      code = EQ;

`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/combine.c:9331-9337`, with the mirror arm for
`> 0` -> `NE` at `:9361-9367`. (Read, not instrumented; the A/B above is the
evidence.)

**THE DIAGNOSTIC VALUE IS THE NEGATIVE.** A lone `beqz` on a loop bound is NOT
a sign of a missing `if (count == 0) return;` -- it is what the guard-free loop
looks like whenever the bound is masked, `ori`-ed or otherwise provably
non-negative. Reaching for an `if` there is how you end up a word long. The
genuine two-guard shape is visible: `func_80097844`'s target carries BOTH a
`beqz $s2` before the `div` and a `blez $s2` before the loop, and dropping its
source `if` is 57 words against 58 with 55 differing.

### SCOPE CORRECTION: `* (1 << k)` vs `<< k` NEEDS A SIGN-EXTENDED MEMORY *LOAD*

The lever recorded on `func_8009792C` -- a `<< k` between a sign-extended load
and a narrowing store turns `lh` into `lhu`, while `* (1 << k)` does not --
needs the word LOAD in it. The mask has to have a `SIGN_EXTEND` of a sub-word
MEM to propagate back into. With the operand already in a register from a CALL
there is nothing to narrow: `func_80064584(ang) * 0x20` and
`func_80064584(ang) << 5` are byte-identical, measured 0 differing on both
`func_80097844` and `func_800ABD74`. So do not spend a compile on that
spelling when the multiplicand is a call result.

## A STORE PAIR OFF ONE BASE IS ORDER-VISIBLE ONLY WHEN ITS VALUES ARE NOT ALREADY LIVE

`func_800BF3F0`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03. The existing lever "STORES TO DISTINCT
CONSTANT OFFSETS off one base do not pin source order" is true of one pair in
this function and false of the pair beside it, which gives the discriminator:

| pair | swapped in source |
|---|---|
| `*(u32 *)&r->unk_0C = 0x808080` (value already live in `$a0`) against `r->unk_1A = 0` (`$zero`) | **0 differing** |
| `r->unk_1A = 0` against `r->unk_08 = 0x4A` (needs its own `addiu $v0, $zero, 0x4A`) | 55 words, **2 differing** |

**The discriminator is whether either store drags a constant materialisation
with it.** Both values already in registers makes the two stores
interchangeable leaves and sched1 restores one canonical order; a store whose
value needs its own `addiu` carries that insn along, so reordering the stores
reorders the feed and the schedule is no longer free. **Not instrumented** --
the plausible place is sched1's ready-list tie-break, but that was not read.

### THREE MORE MEASUREMENTS THAT NARROW EXISTING ENTRIES

`func_800C5C70`/`func_800C5FDC`, 2026-11-03. All free-choice results, recorded
so nobody spends compiles re-deriving them.

* **The `D_80082660` pointer local is SUFFICIENT, not NECESSARY.** The
  `func_800C2E84` wrapper family's comment says the base "goes through a LOCAL
  assigned after the call, which is what puts its `lui` after the `jal`".
  Measured on this pair, with a bind call ahead of the slot clear,
  `t = D_80082660; t[a->unk_60].unk_00 = 0;` and the direct
  `D_80082660[a->unk_60].unk_00 = 0;` are **byte-identical, 50/0 both ways**.
  The complementary data point is `func_800C5F70`, where the slot clear is
  FIRST with no preceding call and the direct form matches at 27/0 with the
  `lui` at the top of the function. Read the family comment as "sufficient".
* **An inverted guard with an early `return` is FREE when the `if` has no
  `else` and nothing follows it.** `if (cond) { body }` and
  `if (!cond) { return; } body` are the same 50 words, 0 differing. This is the
  shape that LOOKS like the conditional-return error and is not one: with a
  single arm and an empty tail there is no layout choice to get wrong, so
  neither the inversion trap nor the early-return lever has any purchase.
* **Two independent narrow writes to ADJACENT BYTES do not pin their source
  order.** `a->unk_70 = 1; a->unk_71 |= 1;` and the reverse both give 50/0,
  even though the target's `lbu 0x71` precedes the `sb 0x70` -- the load-delay
  scheduler pulls the `lbu` up past the independent `sb` either way. Contrast
  the "two independent in-place increments are load-order visible" entry, which
  DOES pin order: the difference is that one of these two writes is a plain
  store with no load of its own.

**But in the same function the call order and the last store before a tail call
are both HARD**, and the delay slot is no excuse to reorder the source: moving
the bind call after the field stores is 31 differing, and moving the `+0x70`
write after the tail call is 18 differing even though in the matching spelling
that store occupies the call's delay slot.

### `lhu` ON AN `s16` FIELD UNDER A MASK IS NOT EVIDENCE OF `u16`

`func_800C5C70`, 2026-11-03. `UnkTownRend.unk_14` is declared `s16` in the
unit, and `if ((c->unk_14 & 0x6000) != 0)` still emits `lhu`: the mask clears
the sign bit, so combine narrows the sign-extend to a zero-extend. Measured --
the 0-differing candidate uses the existing `s16` field, not a retyped one. So
add the mask to the list of things that make `lhu` uninformative about
signedness, alongside the truncating store.

## A SPLIT GLOBAL'S ADDRESS CHAIN SINKS ITS STORE PAST THE NEXT ONE -- THE LISTING'S STORE ORDER IS NOT THE SOURCE ORDER

Established on `func_800C8C3C` against its near-sibling `func_800A73E0`,
ovl_town, 2026-11-03. Worth **16 differing at the correct word count**, which
is exactly the shape that reads as a near-miss and is not one.

The function advances three 16.16 words in a row:

    b->unk_00 += D_800D636C[0];
    b->unk_04 += D_800D636C[1];
    b->unk_08 += b->unk_14;

and the target **stores them `+0x00`, `+0x08`, `+0x04`**. Writing the statements
in that store order is 16 differing; the natural field order is 0. All six
permutations measured, at 62 words every time:

| source order | differing |
|---|---|
| `00, 04, 08` (natural) | **0** |
| `04, 00, 08` | 12 |
| `04, 08, 00` | 15 |
| `00, 08, 04` (= the listing's STORE order) | 16 |
| `08, 00, 04` | 16 |
| `08, 04, 00` | 18 |

Statement 2's addend waits on the full address chain
`lui %hi` / `addiu %lo` / `lw 0x4(reg)`, while statement 3's addend is a plain
`lw 0x14($s0)` that is ready at once, so the scheduler fills the wait by moving
statement 3's add-and-store ahead of statement 2's.

**THE GIVEAWAY THAT THE STREAM HAS BEEN RESCHEDULED** is that statement 3's
operand load appears at word 12, *before* statement 1's store at word 16. A load
hoisted that far ahead of its own statement means the store order carries no
information about the source.

**The near-sibling is the control, and it is what makes this a finding rather
than a guess:** `func_800A73E0` is the same three statements with the object's
own `+0x0C`/`+0x10` in place of the global's two words -- all three addends
plain `lw`s off one base -- and it **stores in source order** and matched on the
first compile. So it is the split global that does this, not the shape.

**Rule:** when consecutive in-place `+=` statements mix a split-global addend
with an addend loaded off the object, write them in the natural field order and
let the scheduler sink the stores. Reorder the source only if the natural order
fails.

**No CDK citation.** The "sched2 sinks the store" attribution is inference from
the measurement plus the near-sibling control; no pass was read and nothing was
instrumented. The word counts and differing counts are measured, the named pass
is not.

## A FUNCTION'S OWN BODY IS INSENSITIVE TO ITS DECLARED RETURN WIDTH -- ONLY THE WHOLE-UNIT SWEEP CATCHES A WRONG ONE, AND ONLY THROUGH ITS CALLERS

Established on `func_8008F170`/`func_80095978`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03, and it is
the generalisation of the `s32`-not-`s16` warning those two carry.

Both functions end their epilogue in `sra $v0, $v0, 16`, which looks like an
`s16` return. Declaring them `s16` leaves **both bodies at 0 differing** -- the
`sra` is emitted either way, because the value is narrowed inside the function
regardless. So a standalone measurement of the function cannot see the error.

What it costs is in the CALLERS, and only some of them:

| declared return | the two functions | `func_8009B6B4` | `func_8009BC44` | the other nine callers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `s32` | 67/0, 71/0 | 93 words, 0 | 95 words, 0 | 0 |
| `s16` | 67/0, 71/0 | 93 words, **7 differing** | 95 words, **7 differing** | 0 |

The two that move hold the result in an `s32` local and re-extend it with their
own `sll`/`sra 16` pair; an `s16` prototype makes that pair redundant and gcc
drops it. The other nine callers cast `(s16)` at the use and are insensitive.

**Three things follow, and the third is the one to act on:**

1. A trailing `sra ... 16` in an epilogue is NOT evidence of an `s16` return.
2. A wrong return width can be invisible in nine callers out of eleven. A clean
   sweep of SOME callers proves nothing.
3. **So the whole-unit sweep is not merely a regression check -- for a return
   width it is the only instrument there is.** Run it before declaring a width,
   not just after landing, and if the function has no caller that re-extends,
   the width is *merely consistent* and should be recorded as such.
   `func_8008F170`'s is witnessed; `func_80095978`'s identical epilogue is not,
   and the landing says so.

### WHICH LVALUE A POST-CALL RELOAD NAMES IS VISIBLE, AND IT IS WORTH ONE WORD

Same pair, 2026-11-03. Passing `hit` where the target reloads `*t` gives
`lw $v0, 0x30($sp)` against the target's `lw $v0, 0x0($s3)` -- 1 differing in
each function.

**Both spellings produce a RELOAD**, because `&hit` was passed to an earlier
call and so cannot be held in a register across it: a non-`CONST_CALL_P`
`CALL_INSN` runs `invalidate_memory (&everything)` with
`everything = {0, 1, 1, 1}` and then `invalidate_for_call ()` --
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/cse.c:7288-7291`, with `invalidate_for_call` at
`:1737`. (Read, not instrumented.) The single differing word is purely the base
register the source's lvalue implies.

So: **when a value is stored through a pointer parameter and then re-read, name
the lvalue the target's base register says.** The compiler will not choose for
you, and one word of base-register difference reads as noise next to a
structural miss.

### A WRONG *ARGUMENT* TO A MASKED `jal` IS NOT MASKED -- ONLY A WRONG *CALLEE* IS

`func_800A86BC`, 2026-11-03. A useful bound on the masking trap, measured as a
deliberate negative control: passing `q` where the target passes `r` to the
same callee is **20 differing**, because the register feeding `$a0` and the one
kept callee-saved across the call both change.

So the trap is narrower than "anything about a call is invisible". `ovlverify`
hides the `jal` word itself -- the CALLEE -- and nothing else about the call.
Argument identity, argument count and argument order all show up in ordinary
unrelocated words. Decode the `jal` by hand for the callee; trust the verify
for everything else at the call.

### A CHAINED ASSIGNMENT'S RIGHT-TO-LEFT STORE ORDER IS OBSERVABLE FOR BYTE STORES OFF ONE BASE

`func_800A86BC`, 2026-11-03, worth 2 differing. This narrows the existing
"STORES TO DISTINCT CONSTANT OFFSETS off one base do not pin source order"
entry, which concluded that the emitted order "carries no information about the
order the statements were written in".

    r->unk_0D = r->unk_0E = r->unk_0C = r->unk_0C - 0x10;   /* sb 0xC, 0xE, 0xD -- 52/0 */
    r->unk_0E = r->unk_0D = r->unk_0C = r->unk_0C - 0x10;   /* sb 0xC, 0xD, 0xE -- 52/2 */

Same words, same registers, same count; only the two `sb`s swap. C assigns
right to left, so the chain's store order is the reverse of its written order,
and that order survives.

**Disjointness makes sched FREE to reorder; it does not make it WANT to.**
`rank_for_schedule` (`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/sched.c:2429`) tries priority,
then the dependence class against `last_scheduled_insn`, and then falls through
to `return INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2);` at `:2469-2472`, whose own
comment says it sorts by "original insn order ... This minimizes instruction
movement". Three equal-priority `sb`s off one base with no dependence between
them reach that last `return`. (Read, not instrumented -- a dump could still
show the class test deciding it rather than the LUID fall-through.)

So the practical rule is the narrower one: **such stores carry source order
until something gives sched a reason to prefer otherwise**, and permuting them
remains the cheap search dimension the original entry says it is.

### THREE NO-OPS, MEASURED, SO NOBODY SPENDS A COMPILE ON THEM

All 2026-11-03.

* **The pointer-local hoist is a no-op for a global struct field read twice
  with a call in between.** At `-G0`, `D_800FE5C0.unk_14` and
  `UnkTown2AE8 *g = &D_800FE5C0; g->unk_14` are 0 differing both ways on
  `func_80095978` -- cc1psx already hoists the `%hi`/`addiu` pair into a
  callee-saved register with no source-level local.
* **The typed-array spelling of an out-of-image table is free.**
  `extern UnkTownVec16 D_800CFD18[];` passed bare and
  `extern u8 D_800CFD18[];` with a cast at the call are 0 differing, as the
  `-G0` addressing note predicts. So prefer the typed spelling, which documents
  the real shape, over `u8[]`-plus-cast.
* **Re-spelling a byte field after storing to it costs a `move`, not a
  reload.** `r->unk_0C -= 0x10; r->unk_0E = r->unk_0C; r->unk_0D = r->unk_0C;`
  is 53 words / 25 differing with one extra `addu` -- cse DID forward the
  stored value across its own store (one `lbu` in both streams) but forwarded
  it into a fresh pseudo. No CDK line located for why it does not reuse the
  store's source register.

## A GATE WHOSE *BOTH* ARMS LEAVE THE FUNCTION IS STILL LAID OUT IN SOURCE ORDER -- AND INVERTING IT COSTS THE CROSS-JUMP

Established on `func_800930E4`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03. Worth **two words and 71
differing** (93 against 91).

The sweep doc's "DO NOT INVERT AN if/else UNLESS AN ARM RETURNS" invites an
over-reading: that when an arm *does* leave, inverting is licensed. Here BOTH
arms end the function and the `else` arm is only four words, so writing it first
as an early `return` looks obviously right. It is wrong.

**The measured rule is narrower: a `bnez` to a block at the BOTTOM means that
block is the `else` arm and the main body is the first arm, however lopsided
they are.**

The two words are not padding, which is what makes this worth an entry. Written
in the correct order the shared tail call appears **once** in the emitted code
although it is written twice in the source: the two copies cross-jump, and the
first arm's test is left branching FORWARD into the second arm's block
(`bltz -> .L80093220`) instead of carrying its own three-word copy. Inverting
the gate separates the copies so neither is the other's fall-through, the merge
no longer applies, and both survive.

This is the existing "duplicate the tail per arm: cross-jumping puts it back"
result holding in a shape it was not measured in -- across the two arms of a
GATE rather than within one `if/else` -- and the new part is **directional**:
the merge is reachable from only one of the two source orders.

Mechanism, read in the CDK tree and NOT instrumented (the 91/0-against-93/71
measurement is the evidence):

* `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/jump.c:2179` -- the
  `if (cross_jump && simplejump_p (insn))` arm of `jump_optimize`'s main loop.
  The first arm's `j <end>`, preceded by its copy of the call block, is matched
  by `find_cross_jump` against the code before its target label -- the second
  arm's identical block -- and `do_cross_jump` deletes the first copy.
* `jump.c:1947` -- the following "conditional jump jumping over an
  unconditional jump" transform then rewrites the now-adjacent
  `bgez`/`j` pair into the single `bltz` the listing shows.
* `jump.c:2133` -- and this is why it is order-sensitive: the *conditional*
  cross-jump arm is gated on `jump_back_p`, whose own comment says "A
  conditional jump may be crossjumped only if the place it jumps to follows an
  opposing jump that comes back here." That does not hold here, so the merge
  must come through the simplejump path, which exists in only one of the two
  layouts.

### TWO SMALLER MEASUREMENTS FROM THE SAME SET

`func_80092698`/`func_800AA844`, 2026-11-03.

* **A countdown arm's trailing `return` is worth two words and 19 differing.**
  Dropping it so the arm falls into the following flag check is 83 words
  against 85. The `return` is witnessed, not stylistic.
* **Two independent flag tests on one struct are block-order visible.**
  `g->unk_08 & 0xF000` must precede `g->unk_10 & 0x10`; swapping them is
  **4 differing at the same word count** -- a pure block-order difference that
  `ovlverify` does see. So when a residue is a handful of words at the right
  length and the function is a chain of early-returning tests, permute the
  tests.

## A FORWARDED PARAMETER CARRIES A `REG_EQUIV` THAT **DOUBLES** ITS LIVE LENGTH -- COPYING IT INTO A LOCAL *BEFORE* THE BRANCH HALVES IT BACK AND WINS THE `$s` REGISTER

Established on `func_8009AF74`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03. Worth **6 differing at
the correct word count** -- a pure `$s1`/`$s2` exchange on two forwarded
parameters, plus the two callee-saved stack offsets that follow from it. **This
one IS instrumented**: `-da` dumps were taken and the `REG_EQUIV` notes counted.

`assign_parms` hangs a `REG_EQUIV` note pointing at the incoming stack home on
**every** register parameter's entry copy --
`scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/function.c:4011-4015`:

    else if ((set = single_set (linsn)) != 0
             && SET_DEST (set) == parmreg)
      REG_NOTES (linsn)
        = gen_rtx (EXPR_LIST, REG_EQUIV, stack_parm, REG_NOTES (linsn));

`update_equiv_regs` then doubles the live length of any pseudo carrying one --
`local-alloc.c:1094-1106`, whose own comment is the giveaway:

    /* Note that the statement below does not affect the priority
       in local-alloc!  */
    reg_live_length[regno] *= 2;

It says nothing about global-alloc, which is where it bites:
`allocno_compare` (`global.c:586-610`) divides by exactly that doubled number.

**So a parameter that is only FORWARDED runs at HALF the priority its real live
range deserves, and loses the low `$s` register to a parameter that happens to
be born one insn earlier.**

The measured allocation, read out of `.lreg`/`.greg`:

| spelling | pseudo | refs | live length | priority | gets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| natural, 6 differing | 80 `t` | 6 | 26 | 4615 | `$s0` |
| | 81 `b` | 2 | 28 | 714 | **`$s1`** (wrong) |
| | 82 `c` | 2 | 30 | 666 | `$s2` |
| with the local, **0 differing** | 80 `t` | 6 | 28 | 4285 | `$s0` |
| | 83 `d` | 2 | **13** | **1538** | **`$s1`** (right) |
| | 81 `b` | 2 | 30 | 666 | `$s2` |

The instrumented half: the natural version's dumps carry **three**
`REG_EQUIV (mem:SI ...)` notes, one per parameter copy; the local version has
only **two**, and the surviving pseudo is set straight from `$a2` with **no
`REG_EQUIV` note** -- hence 13 and not 26. The third parameter's own pseudo
does not appear as an allocno at all; the local swallowed it.

**Two preconditions, both measured:**

1. **The copy must precede the branch.** After it, the parameter stays live
   across the conditional block, the pseudo it feeds is block-local, and the
   allocno set is unchanged.
2. **It must be the parameter you want to WIN, and nothing else substitutes.**
   A local for the first or second parameter, a local for the countdown value,
   widening the second parameter, and a cast at the call site all leave the
   order exactly as it was -- **a cast creates no pseudo.** The local's own type
   is irrelevant (`void *` works identically).

**THE FREE ALTERNATIVE, and the control that proves the mechanism.**
`func_80091990` is the same shape and needs no local, because its gate READS
the third parameter: that third reference takes it to `3 refs / 26` = 1153
against the second parameter's 714 and wins the same exchange for nothing. So
**a third reference and an undoubled live length are two routes to the same
swap** -- if the function already dereferences the parameter you need in `$s1`,
you need no local. Five of the six members of that set took the natural
spelling for exactly this reason.

### WHEN A FAMILY MEMBER HAS NO ADDRESS-TAKEN SYMBOL AT ALL, A DESCRIPTOR WRITTEN INTO IT IS PURE INVENTION

`func_800C6740`, `func_800CB0F0`, `func_800CB7EC`, 2026-11-03. A sharpening of
the read-every-symbol-from-its-own-listing rule.

All three are members of a binder family whose other members name a descriptor
quad -- and all three carry **zero** `%hi`/`%lo` relocations. Their quads live
in their landed callees (`func_800CB708` and `func_800CB73C` write
`+0x58`/`+0x5C`/`+0x7C`/`+0x80` themselves) and in a stub. So a descriptor
symbol copied in from a sibling would be masked to 0 differing by `ovlverify`
and then rejected by the link.

**Grep each member for `%hi` BEFORE deciding it needs a descriptor at all.** An
empty result is a finding: this member delegates. And in the same set
`func_8009AF74` stores `func_8009AFF4` -- its near NEIGHBOUR, not itself --
which is the other way to get this wrong.

### THE GATE AND THE SLOT CLEAR ARE INDEPENDENT -- `func_800C5ADC` IS THE MEMBER THAT SEPARATES THEM

A correction of scope on the `D_80082660` pointer-local entry, which was
measured on members that do both. `func_800C5ADC` is the rend `+0x14` gate plus
a bind plus a hand-on, with **no slot clear at all** -- the downstream callee
does the clearing. So the "pointer local is sufficient, not necessary" result
has nothing to be sufficient for here, and a reader who treats the slot clear
as part of the family shape will mis-describe this member.

## AN OUTGOING ARGUMENT COPY CANNOT BE MOVED EARLIER FROM THE SOURCE -- IT TIES AT sched2 AGAINST A `high`/`lo_sum` PAIR AND THE TIE BREAKS ON LUID, WHICH `calls.c` FIXES

Established on `func_800991C0` and `func_8009A41C`, ovl_town, 2026-11-03.
Worth 3 differing at the correct 30 words, in both. **Instrumented**: read out
of `tools/decomp/sched.py --sched1 --rtl` dumps, not inferred.

**sched1 is innocent.** It already emits the target's order, with the split
`lui` / `lw` / `lo_sum` the listing has.

**sched2 is the pass.** Its dump says it outright:

    ;; ready list at T-11: 53 (1) 22 (1), now 53 22

insn 53 is `(set (reg:SI 6 a2) (reg/v:SI 81))` -- the outgoing argument copy --
and insn 22 is the `lo_sum` of the record base's symbol. **Both priority 1.**
sched2 schedules backwards, so picking 53 at T-11 places it LATER, into the
`lw`'s load-delay slot, and leaves `lui`/`lo_sum` adjacent. The target wants 53
first after the call, which needs it to have the lower LUID.

The tie-break is `scratch/gcc-src/cdk-gcc-b18/sched.c:2472`, the last line of
`rank_for_schedule`, `return INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2);`, with
`tmp = *y` and `tmp2 = *x` at `:2432-2433` -- **an inverted comparator, so the
HIGHER LUID sorts first in the ready array and is emitted later.**

And the LUID is unreachable from the source. `calls.c:1851`,
`for (i = 0; i < num_actuals; i++)` under the comment "Now do the register
loads required for any wholly-register parms ... Their expressions were already
evaluated", runs *after* `prepare_call_address` at `:1843`: the `$a0`/`$a1`/`$a2`
copies are emitted front-to-back at the very end of the call's expansion. **No
statement order can put an argument copy ahead of a `high`/`lo_sum` pair
belonging to an earlier statement.** (Those two `calls.c` lines were read, not
instrumented.)

**THE CURE, and why the pin alone is not enough.** The existing device "TWO
ARGUMENT COPIES IN THE LISTING'S ORDER: EMIT THE SECOND ONE YOURSELF, AS THE
FENCE" applies here to a THIRD key: there it fixed a sched1 fence AND a sched2
LUID; here only the sched2 LUID is wrong, so the register pin on its own does
nothing and the empty `asm` is load-bearing. Measured ladder, both members:

| spelling | differing |
|---|---|
| plain C | 3 |
| `register s32 zz = b;` (unpinned) | 3 |
| `register s32 zz __asm__("$6") = b;`, no fence | 3 |
| **pinned + `__asm__("" : "=r"(zz) : "0"(zz));`** | **0** |

Without the fence, cse substitutes `b` back for `zz` and the pin is erased.

**THE CHEAPER COROLLARY -- CHECK THIS BEFORE REACHING FOR THE DEVICE.** The
same tie exists in the actor twin `func_800C48DC`, with the same tail, and it
resolves in our favour **with no device at all**: `func_800C2E84`'s call has an
empty delay slot where `func_80094984`'s carries `addu $a1, $s0`. So **the
surrounding call's delay slot is what decides whether this tie has to be paid
for.** Look at it first.

Thirty other spellings were measured and ruled out, all at 30 words: six
base/subscript/pointer forms for the record array (3, 3, 3, 3, 8, 8), both legal
statement orders (3 and 12), a three-argument bind (31 words -- so the copy is
NOT shared with the first call), `do { } while (0)` at five positions
(6/3/9/12/3), a free `__asm__("" ::"r"(b))` either side (3, 3), a dead
`b = b;` (3), and six callee declarations including two narrow return types
(all identical). **The copy's LUID, not `b`'s reference count, is the quantity.**

### A THIRTEEN-MEMBER FAMILY'S STATEMENT ORDER IS NOT INHERITED FROM ITS LANDED RELATIVE

Same batch, 2026-11-03. Eight of the thirteen landed on the first compile by
pure substitution; three needed their own statement order, found by brute force
over the permutations:

| member | permutations measured | the winner |
|---|---|---|
| `func_800947CC` | all **24** of {copy +0x30, copy +0x32, handler, count} | `c30 c32 h00 cnt` at 0; eight orders at 10; four at 25 words |
| `func_80099468` | all **120** of five statements | `clr c30 c32 cnt h04` at 0; twelve at 18-20 |
| `func_80099680` | 9 orders | **two** orders reach 0 |

**In all three the target's order is "copy the fields first, install the handler
last" -- the opposite of what the landed relative's shape suggested.** So a
family's statement order is a lead, not a rule: substitute the symbols from the
relative, then permute the statements if the residue is a handful of words at
the right length. A full 24- or 120-permutation sweep over four or five
statements costs minutes and removes the guesswork entirely.

### `lh` AND `lhu` ON ONE `s16` FIELD IS CORRECT, NOT A TYPING INCONSISTENCY

`func_800A58CC`/`func_800A5DF8`, 2026-11-03. The target reads `g->unk_C4` with
`lh` for `-0x2B0 - g->unk_C4` and with `lhu` two instructions later for the
`+=`, and cse does not merge them.

**A signed-halfword read whose only consumer is a halfword store loads with
`lhu`. The same field read into a word-wide context loads with `lh`.** Probed
on one field at offset `0xC4`, same base:

| source | load |
|---|---|
| `sink = G.unk_C4 + d;` | `lh` |
| `G.unk_C4 = G.unk_C4 + d;` | `lhu` |
| `G.unk_C4 += d;` | `lhu` |
| `G.unk_C4 = (-0x2B0 - G.unk_C4) / d + G.unk_C4;` | `lh` then `lhu`, then `sh` |

Mechanism. `convert.c:275`'s `trunc1:` block re-builds the `PLUS_EXPR` in
`typex`, the 16-bit type, so the add reaches `expand_binop` in HImode.
`optabs.c:555` carries the comment *"For certain integer operations, we need
not actually extend the narrow operands, as long as we will truncate the results
to the same narrowness"* and `optabs.c:564` sets `no_extend = 1` -- `add_optab`
is in the gating list. `widen_operand` with `no_extend` then returns a
paradoxical SUBREG at `optabs.c:331`
(`return gen_rtx (SUBREG, mode, force_reg (GET_MODE (op), op), 0);`) instead of
a `convert_modes` extension, and on MIPS a plain HImode load is `lhu`. The
other read's result is word-wide, so it goes through `convert_modes` with
`unsignedp = 0` and comes out `lh`. The two are different rtl -- `zero_extend`
vs `sign_extend` of the same MEM -- which is why cse leaves both loads standing.

**If a listing shows `lh` and `lhu` on one field, do NOT split the field and do
NOT change its signedness.** Check whether one of the two reads is truncated by
a store.

### A TAIL DUPLICATED INTO BOTH ARMS IS STILL TWO COPIES WHEN THE ALLOCATOR PRICES THE PSEUDOS

`func_8009221C`/`func_80093250`, 2026-11-03. The `func_80092DA8` substitution
gives the exact word count on the first compile with every opcode, immediate
and displacement already right -- 63/63 with **25 differing and 54/54 with 9,
all of them register numbers**. No rewriting of the logic moves them. What
places the registers is writing the tail call at the end of **both** arms
instead of once after the convergence.

**Cross-jumping is jump2, and jump2 runs AFTER register allocation.** In
`toplev.c`:

| line | pass |
|---|---|
| `3548` | sched1, `schedule_insns` |
| `3585` | `local_alloc` |
| `3617` | `global_alloc` |
| `3661` | sched2, `schedule_insns` |
| `3690` | `jump_optimize (insns, 1, 1, 0)` -- the **only** call with `cross_jump` set |

The other five calls (`:3266 :3312 :3373 :3379`) all pass 0. So when
`allocno_compare` (`global.c:587-609`) prices the pseudos there are still two
copies of the tail, and each pseudo carries one extra reference that the emitted
words never show. On `func_8009221C`: `q` crosses `floor_log2`'s step and
overtakes `n`; `p` ties exactly with `t` and wins on allocno `80 < 84`. The greg
order `89 81 84 80 82` becomes `81 89 80 84 82`, which is the target.

**This narrows the entry at `:2088` ("Duplicate the tail per arm: cross-jumping
puts it back").** On `func_80092FF0` the duplicated and single-copy spellings
are *byte-identical* (both 61 words, 0 differing) -- there the duplication buys
nothing. Here it is worth 25 register differences. So the lever is **invisible
where it does not change allocation pricing and decisive where it does**; it is
not "unfalsifiable by bytes", and the question to ask is whether the extra
reference moves a pseudo across `floor_log2`'s step or into a tie.

Add to the cross-jump sites already listed at `:15825`: **`jump.c:2215`** is a
third one, the `if (cross_jump && GET_CODE (PATTERN (insn)) == RETURN)` case
(`find_cross_jump` at `:2581`, `do_cross_jump` at `:2759`), and `toplev.c:3690`
is the call that enables all of them.

### A SHARED `goto` EXIT KEEPS THE FINAL BRANCH FROM BEING IF-CONVERTED

`func_8008FD9C`, 2026-11-03. In a function whose failure exits are all
`return <const>` and whose success exit is another const, **the LAST test gets
if-converted into `slt`/`xori` unless at least two branches share one exit
label.** Six separate `return 0`s give the right word count with a 7-word tail
defect: `slt` / `j` / `xori $v0,$v0,1` where the target has `beqz` with
`addiu $v0,1` in the delay slot. `goto fail;` with a single `fail:` at the end
is the cure and costs nothing once there are two or more failure arms.

Two transforms in sequence. `jump.c:927-1016` rewrites
`if (...) { x = a; goto l; } x = b;` into `x = a; if (...) goto l; x = b;` --
for `if (cond) return 0; return 1;` it inverts the sixth branch
(`invert_jump` at `:1003`) and hoists the `return 1` constant above it
(`:1005`). `jump.c:1200-1502`'s store-flag case 1 then eats the result. The
cost model does *not* block it: `config/mips/mips.h:3178` gives `BRANCH_COST`
1 for the R3000, which kills the `BRANCH_COST >= 2` arms at `:1338-1340`, but
`:1356-1361`'s `STORE_FLAG_VALUE == 1 && exact_log2 (INTVAL (temp2)) >= 0` arm
still fires because `uval` is 1, and `emit_store_flag` with `normalizep = 1` on
a reversed LT is `slt` + `xori`.

What blocks it in the original is **`jump.c:1204-1206`**:
`(temp = next_nonnote_insn (insn)) != 0 && GET_CODE (temp) == INSN`. With one
shared `fail` exit the other five branches keep `LABEL_NUSES` above zero, so
`jump.c:1015`'s `if (prev_label && --LABEL_NUSES (prev_label) == 0)
delete_insn (prev_label);` does not fire, the label survives immediately after
the inverted branch, `next_nonnote_insn` returns a `CODE_LABEL`, and the
store-flag never matches. Six separate returns give the sixth arm a label of
its own, it gets deleted, and the transform fires. (`reg_set_last` at
`rtlanal.c:877-924` stops at a `CODE_LABEL`, which is why this cannot fire on
the *earlier* tests -- only the tail is exposed.)

### AN HImode STRUCT STORE DOES INVALIDATE A FIELD READ OFF A POINTER LOCAL

Refines the entry at `:12903`, which reads "A QImode STORE WIPES CSE'S WHOLE
MEMORY TABLE; AN HImode STRUCT STORE DOES NOT". Both halves are true, but the
second is about `all` only. `func_80092320`/`func_800924EC`, 2026-11-03.

In `cse.c`: `note_mem_written` at **`7618-7622`** suppresses
`writes_ptr->all = 1` exactly when the MEM is `MEM_IN_STRUCT_P` (or a `PLUS`
address), non-`QImode` and not an `AND` address -- so `all` stays 0, as that
entry says. But **`7623`** then sets `writes_ptr->nonscalar = 1`
unconditionally on that path, and `invalidate_memory`'s removal test at
**`1725-1728`** drops every entry that is `p->in_memory` and *either*
`(nonscalar && p->in_struct)` *or* `cse_rtx_addr_varies_p (p->exp)`.

A `COMPONENT_REF` through a pointer local is `in_struct` **and** has a varying
address, so it satisfies both disjuncts and is removed either way. **What
survives an HImode struct store is a MEM at a *fixed* address, not a field read
off a pointer.** Measured: respell `func_80092320`'s countdown as a bare
`a->unk_0A < 0` test with no store and the second `lw 0x10($s4)` disappears
(111 words against 115). This is why the two near-siblings legitimately differ
by one `lw`, and why the shared-local spelling is wrong (114/115, 56 differing).

### THE DECLARED-SIZE RULE GOVERNS GLOBALS, NOT POINTER PARAMETERS

`func_8008FD9C`/`func_800A2A18`, 2026-11-03. "Declared size picks symbolic vs
split addressing, and `lui`/`ori` vs `lui`/`addiu` vs `lui`/`lw` tells you
constant-address vs load" is a rule about **globals**. A pointer *parameter*
dereferenced at constant offsets never materialises an address, so the declared
pointee type is unobservable: `UnkVec *`, `VECTOR *` and `s32 *` are
byte-identical for both functions' `b` and `d`. Six measurements, all 0.

(Related: there is no `Vec3` type in this codebase. Only libgte's `SVECTOR`
and `VECTOR`.)

### TWO NEGATIVE RESULTS WORTH NOT RE-DERIVING

Both measured on 2026-11-03, both places this sweep previously believed there
was a lever.

**Where a truncating cast is written is NOT observable.** `n = (s16)f(...)`
versus `n = f(...)` with `(s16)n` at each use are byte-identical on both of
this unit's compare shapes, in both directions: the **landed** `func_80091AF0`
rewritten from one spelling to the other still measures 58/58 at 0 differing,
and both spellings reach 0 on the `func_80092DA8` shape too. Either way ends as
one pseudo holding the truncated value reached by one `sll`/`sra` pair. The two
families' differing spellings in `csrc/ovl_town.c` carry no information.
**What IS observable is whether the ARGUMENT to `func_80095A94` is truncated**
-- leave it bare while casting only in the compare and you *gain* a word
(64/63 and 55/54). The constraint is the argument, not the cast placement.

**Which side of a comparison the struct field sits on is NOT observable** for
an independent pair of operands.

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-11-03.** A caveat here previously recorded a contrary
> measurement on `func_800C1F8C` that it could not explain. That function is
> now landed and the flip is byte-identical on its landing shape, so the
> contrary measurement was an artifact of a spelling that no longer matters.
> The real rule has its own entry: **operand order is worth a word when it
> decides a block's first insn and that block is a branch target with a free
> delay slot.** See "COMPARISON OPERAND ORDER IS WORTH A WORD WHEN IT DECIDES
> A BLOCK'S FIRST INSN". `expr.c:10944-10951` is accurate -- `compare()`
does expand `TREE_OPERAND (exp, 0)` first -- and `fold-const.c:4906-4916` only
swaps comparison operands when one is an `INTEGER_CST`, so folding is not what
hides it. What hides it is that **sched1 picks the order** (`schedule_insns` at
`toplev.c:3548`, enabled at `toplev.c:3976` under `optimize >= 2`, before
`local_alloc`). Direct evidence: `func_8009221C` and `func_80093250` emit
`sll, lh, sra` while `func_80092DA8` emits `lh, sll, sra` *from the identical
source spelling*.

### A CHAINED ASSIGNMENT EMITS ITS STORES RIGHT-TO-LEFT

`func_800A6DA0`/`func_800A6E1C`, 2026-11-03. Measured on my own probe, four
spellings of three adjacent `s16` fields:

| source | stores emitted |
|---|---|
| `r->unk_1C = r->unk_1E = r->unk_20 = 0xC00;` | `0x20`, `0x1E`, `0x1C` |
| `r->unk_20 = 0xC00; r->unk_1E = 0xC00; r->unk_1C = 0xC00;` | `0x20`, `0x1E`, `0x1C` |
| `r->unk_20 = r->unk_1E = r->unk_1C = 0xC00;` | `0x1C`, `0x1E`, `0x20` |
| `r->unk_1C = 0xC00; r->unk_1E = 0xC00; r->unk_20 = 0xC00;` | `0x1C`, `0x1E`, `0x20` |

So **a chain reads in the opposite order from the stores it emits**, and the
descending chain is byte-identical to three separate statements written
descending (both 0 differing; reversing either is 2 differing).

The mechanism is just the language plus ordinary assignment expansion:
assignment is right-associative, so `a = b = c = v` is `a = (b = (c = v))`,
and `expand_assignment` (`expr.c:2782`) expands the RHS before storing to the
LHS -- `expr.c:2946`, `temp = expand_expr (from, 0, GET_MODE (to_rtx), 0);`.
The innermost assignment's store therefore comes out first. **There is no
special recursion in `build_modify_expr` for this** -- that function is at
`c-typeck.c:3803` and its only recursion (`:3834`) is on the LHS, for the
compound-LHS case. A report claiming otherwise was checked and was wrong.

Practical consequence: when two adjacent stores are in the "wrong" order,
"try both statement orders" has a **third** spelling -- the chain, which reads
naturally while emitting high-offset-first.

### A FORWARDED PARAMETER IS WITNESSABLE WHEN THE CALLER PASSES A CONSTANT

`func_800B44F0`, 2026-11-03. A parameter whose only use is to be handed
straight to a callee's argument register is usually called unwitnessable from
the function's own bytes. It is not, when the call site passes a literal: the
parameter keeps `$a1` live from entry and costs no setup insn, while
substituting the caller's literal `0x21` costs an `addiu $a1, $zero, 0x21` --
**39 words against 38, 31 differing**.

Only the *stored* forwarded argument (`sw $a2, 0x0($v0)`) is genuinely
invisible. So before declaring a forwarded parameter unconstrained, check
whether a landed caller passes a constant and measure the substitution.

### A ONE-ARMED `if` CANNOT HIT THE IF/ELSE INVERSION TRAP

Narrows the entry at `:13769` ("A SYMMETRIC TWO-CALL `if/else` KEEPS SOURCE
ORDER; ONLY AN ARM THAT *RETURNS* INVERTS"). `func_800CD9F4` and
`func_800A7360`, 2026-11-03: when the other arm is **empty**, the inverted
early-`return` spelling and the nested `if` are a **TIE** -- both 0 differing,
measured twice. There is no `jal` to swap, so the trap -- which is dangerous
precisely because it reports as 1 differing while being a 3-word structural
error -- cannot arise. As written, that entry reads like a blanket
prohibition and would have cost a compile.

### `&&` WITH A SIDE-EFFECTING RIGHT OPERAND IS NOT A SINGLE `if`

Narrows `:2072` ("`||` puts the body BETWEEN the two tests") and the
"multiple `&&` terms are one range check" reasoning at `:7086` to
**side-effect-free** operands. `func_80090F00`, 2026-11-03:
`if ((f == a->unk_00) && (--a->unk_0A <= 0))` and the nested form are **both**
0 differing, because the sequencing requirement forces the same two basic
blocks either way.

Corollary worth knowing: a `nop` between a `bne` and the next `lhu` is
therefore **not** evidence for the nested spelling.

### A STORE OF ZERO TO A HALFWORD FIELD IS ONE WORD CHEAPER THAN ANY CONSTANT

`func_800CD9F4` (30 words) against `func_800CDBB8` (29), 2026-11-03: the whole
difference is one constant materialisation. `a->unk_90 = 3` costs
`addiu $v0, $zero, 0x3`, which then fills the `bgtz` delay slot;
`a->unk_90 = 0` stores `$zero` directly and the slot takes the next argument
copy instead. **Check this first when two family members' headers differ by
exactly 4.**

### AN UNREAD THIRD PARAMETER ON ONE CALLEE COSTS A WORD ON A *DIFFERENT*, LATER INDIRECT CALL

`func_800A0708`, 2026-11-03. The symptom is a four-argument indirect call
through a slot coming out **one word long**, with the function-pointer `lw` one
slot too late and a load-delay `nop` after it. Nineteen spellings of the slot
call itself were all stuck at 40 words / 12 differing. **The cause was two
floors away: the arity of an EARLIER call whose callee never reads the
parameter.**

The chain, every link verified:

| citation | step |
|---|---|
| `calls.c:1843` | `funexp = prepare_call_address (...)` runs **before** the argument-register loop that follows it (next comment: "Now do the register loads required for any wholly-register parms"), so the slot load is the **first** insn of the call's expansion, ahead of every `$aN` move |
| `sched.c:2513` | `birthing_insn_p` -- a SET whose destination is already live and whose `reg_n_sets` is 1 |
| `sched.c:2583` | `adjust_priority`'s `case 0:` raises such an insn to `max_priority` = `LAUNCH_PRIORITY` `0x7f000001` (`sched.c:189`, set at `:3998`) |
| `config/mips/mips.md:153` | load latency 2 on the r3000; the scheduler runs **backward**, so a bumped insn is taken first and *placed last* |
| `sched.c:2704` | within one priority group `potential_hazard` decides; both are 0 here, so a bumped insn always beats an unbumped one and only another insn in the same `LAUNCH_PRIORITY` group can hold the load back |

That other insn is the slot call's own `$a2 = q` move, which is birthing **only
while `reg_n_sets[$a2] == 1`**. A third argument to the earlier call emits a
second `(set (reg $a2) ...)` that **survives to sched1** -- it is deleted only
in reload, and sched1 runs before `local_alloc`. So `$a2` stops being birthing,
the move is not bumped, the load sinks past it, and maspsx inserts the nop.

Measured 39 words / 0 differing at two arguments, 40 / 12 at three, every other
variable held fixed.

**Two corollaries.** A *three*-argument slot call cannot show this, because its
last register move goes into the `jalr` delay slot and never competes with the
load -- which is why five landed callers of the same function are byte-identical
at either arity and this never surfaced before. And the recorded trap that an
unread parameter "costs no words" is true of the **callee** and false of the
**caller**.

Cheap probe: a degenerate `do { } while (0)` **between** the load and the call
reaches the right length but leaves the load in the earlier block (39 / 2). On
a `+1 LENGTH` on an indirect call that tells you in one compile whether the
load's position is the defect at all -- then go count the other sets of `$a2`
rather than reaching for a device.

### A FORWARDED PARAMETER PASSED ON TO AN EARLIER CALL WINS THE LOWER `$s` REGISTER

`func_8009A3A4`, 2026-11-03. The free alternative to a local-copy device, and a
second witness for that lever's "FREE ALTERNATIVE" note (which previously had
only the gate-reads-the-parameter route).

Passing a parameter on to an earlier call costs **no instruction** -- jump2
deletes the argument copy because the register still holds the incoming value
(`jump.c:484-493`, `find_equiv_reg` at `reload.c:5554`, under `toplev.c:3690`).
But the copy is still present when global-alloc prices the allocnos against
`allocno_compare` (`global.c:587-609`):

| | pseudo | refs/live | priority | gets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 args (target) | `c` | 3/16 | 1875 | **`$s1`** |
| 2 args | `c` | 2/**26** | 769 | `$s2` |

The 26 is the `REG_EQUIV` live-length doubling a purely forwarded parameter
carries (`local-alloc.c:1102`). The third reference is the way out of it. The
spare prologue copy the two-argument version keeps also fills a load delay, so
**the whole witness for this arity is a `nop` that should be there plus an
`$s1`/`$s2` exchange.** (Open: why the three-argument live length prints 16
rather than a doubled 2x8. The direction and the resulting allocation are
measured; that number is not explained.)

### A `goto` BACK-EDGE IS INVISIBLE TO `loop.c`

`func_800A63C8`, 2026-11-03. **Nothing in a hand-written `goto` loop is
strength-reduced or hoisted**, because `loop.c` never sees it as a loop.

`NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG` is emitted in exactly **one** place --
`emit_note (NULL_PTR, NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG)` at `stmt.c:2214`, inside
`expand_start_loop` (`:2188`), which is the only occurrence in the file -- and
only `while`/`for`/`do` reach it. `loop_optimize` enumerates loops **solely**
by scanning for that note: it counts them at `loop.c:415-421` and scans them at
`:535-537`. So a `goto` loop gets no biv, no giv and no invariant motion.

Measured: every real-loop spelling of `func_800A63C8` is **31 words**, because
`loop.c` strength-reduces the `p + 4` `DEST_ADDR` giv into a second induction
register (a `move` plus two separate bumps) where the target carries both
`0x0($a0)` and `0x4($a0)` off one register. The `goto` spelling is **29 and 0
differing**. Its near-sibling `func_800A6328` does **not** need it, because its
inner base is at offset 0 -- the biv itself, nothing to reduce -- so the pair
does not agree on its outer loop.

**General form: when a candidate comes out 2 words long with a duplicated
induction register and the target carries two offsets off one base, respell that
loop with `goto`.** The cost test that would have declined the reduction in a
bigger loop is `loop.c:3996` (`v->lifetime * threshold * benefit < insn_count`,
threshold at `:3359`).

### A NESTED LOOP'S `i = 0` INIT CAN BE STOLEN INTO THE OUTER LOOP'S DELAY SLOT

`func_800A6328`/`func_800A63C8`, 2026-11-03. Spelled
`for (i = 0;; i += 0xC) { ...; if (term) break; }`, reorg takes the init into
the **outer** back-branch's delay slot and retargets that branch one insn later.
Spelled `do { ...; t = term; i += 0xC; } while (t == 0)` -- terminator captured
in a temp, increment last -- the slot stays a `nop`. 2 differing versus 0 in
both members, every other word identical.

**The fingerprint is a single `move rX,zero` in a delay slot where the target
has `nop`, plus a branch displacement off by one** -- which reads like an
off-by-one in the listing and is not.

### `get_pointer_alignment` IS AN ALIGNMENT LEVER, AND IT IS HOW A STRING'S `.rodata` SURVIVES

`func_800B28A0`, 2026-11-03. A string emitted **inside a function's own `.s`**
(`.align 2`, `.asciz "%&'()"`, trailing `.align 2`, occupying 8 bytes) has to be
reproduced byte-for-byte when the `INCLUDE_ASM` is replaced. Two obvious
spellings both fail:

* **A local array initialiser** (`u8 s[6] = "%&'()";`) is 0 differing in *text*
  but emits six `.ascii` bytes and **no trailing pad**. The next record's own
  `.s` is bare `.byte` directives with no `.align`, so it lands 2 bytes early
  and every later record shifts. (Case 1 of "A STRING CONSTANT'S DECLARED SIZE
  DECIDES WHETHER `.rodata` SURVIVES".)
* **`memcpy(s, D_XXXX, 6)`** off a `const u8 D_XXXX[8]` definition gives the
  array 4-byte `DECL_ALIGN`, so `move_by_pieces` takes the aligned path and the
  copy collapses to `lw`/`lh`/`sw`/`sh` -- **26 words, 27 differing**.
  `__attribute__((aligned(1)))` does not help.

**The spelling that gets both: route the address through a `const u8 *` local
first.** `get_pointer_alignment` resolves a plain pointer `VAR_DECL` to its
*pointee type's* alignment (1) rather than the array's `DECL_ALIGN`, so the copy
stays unaligned (`lwl`/`lwr` + `swl`/`swr`, 30 words, 0 differing) while the
definition keeps its `.align 2` + `.space 2` and occupies the declared 8 bytes.
`make build/town.bin` byte-identical confirms it; a text-only check passes the
broken spelling, so **this class must be gated on the build.**

### C POINTER ARITHMETIC CANNOT EMIT AN INDEX-FIRST ADD

`func_800A6328`, 2026-11-03. The target does `addu $v1, $a2, $v0` -- the
**index** register first. No spelling of C pointer arithmetic produces that:
`c-typeck.c:1985-1988` routes both `p + i` and `i + p` into `pointer_int_sum`
with the pointer as `ptrop`, and `pointer_int_sum` builds
`build (PLUS_EXPR, result_type, ptrop, intop)` at `c-typeck.c:2698`;
`expr.c:5993` then expands operand 0 first.

**Cast the base to `s32` and add as integers** -- that puts both operands on the
integer `common = 1` path (`c-typeck.c:1990`) and the source order survives.
Worth 2 words. So `i + (s32)*p`, not `(u8 *)*p + i`.

### THE CONSTANT-ADDRESS-VS-SYMBOL CHOICE IS WORTH BYTES EVEN FOR A SINGLE `lbu`

`func_800B2834`, 2026-11-03, and it **narrows the recorded `lui`+`ori` vs
`lui`+`addiu` tell**: that tell cannot decide a plain load, because there is no
second address instruction at all -- the `%lo` folds into the load and *both*
`extern u8 D_800133BA;` and `*(u8 *)0x800133BA` emit `lui $r, %hi` +
`lbu $r', %lo(...)($r)`.

The real discriminator is allocation plus scheduling. The **symbol** puts the
`%hi` in a scratch register and the byte in another, and sched1 then runs the
pair **ahead** of a nearby load's pre-test -- 4 differing, the same three words
permuted. The **integer constant** ties `lui` and `lbu` to one register and
schedules the pair **into** that load's delay slot, which is the target's order
and 0 differing.

**Diagnostic: a `lui` whose destination is a *scratch* register rather than the
loaded value's register, with the pair scheduled before a nearby load rather
than into its delay slot.**

### `sched1`/`sched2` ARE STRICTLY PER-BASIC-BLOCK, SO "WHICH BLOCK" IS A SOURCE QUESTION

`func_800C1F8C`, 2026-11-03. `schedule_block` takes its `head`/`tail` from
`basic_block_head[b]`/`basic_block_end[b]` (`sched.c:3220-3221`), and the
backward dependency scan breaks at `prev_head` -- the comment reads *"Don't
overrun the bounds of the basic block"* (`sched.c:3389`).

**Consequence, and this is the reusable part: when an insn appears in a
different basic block in the final listing than in your candidate, the only
pass that can have moved it there is `reorg`, into a delay slot. Everything
else is the C.** That turns "the scheduler did something strange" into a
two-line question.

### `reorg` STEALS FROM TWO INSNS BACK, AND A NEARER CANDIDATE IS A LEVER

`fill_simple_delay_slots` scans **backwards** from the branch and takes the
first insn that is legal to move forward, stopping at a label or jump
(`reorg.c:3067-3077`). The insn immediately before the branch usually *feeds*
it and so is not legal -- which means **an independent insn two back is at
risk**, and the presence or absence of an unconditional copy just before the
branch decides which insn lands in the slot.

Measured on `func_800C1F8C` (parked): with no copy present reorg reaches past
the branch's input and steals the `sll` half of a `(s16)` extension, leaving
the load-delay slot to a `nop` -- two words wrong. Forcing the `sll` into that
block explicitly (`dx = dx << 16;` with `(dx >> 16)` at the compare, and again
as a separate cross-block temp) does **not** help: reorg still moves it
(40 words / 19 differing, both forms). See the park for the open question.

### `expand_abs`'s COPY SURVIVES ONLY WHEN THE TERNARY WRITES A SEPARATE VARIABLE

`func_800C1F8C`, 2026-11-03 — this is the lever that **unparked** two functions
after 49 spellings and a permuter run had missed it.

`adx = dx >= 0 ? dx : -dx;` into **its own variable** emits an unconditional
reg-reg copy of the abs's input, in the branch's delay slot. Writing the abs
in place (`if (dx < 0) dx = -dx;`) does not, and nor does a hand-written
second variable (`adx = dx; if (dx < 0) adx = -adx;`).

| citation | step |
|---|---|
| `fold-const.c:5459` | recognises `A op 0 ? A : -A` — *"this is A, -A, abs (A), or abs (-A), depending on the comparison operation"* |
| `fold-const.c:5476` | the `GT_EXPR` arm builds the `ABS_EXPR` |
| `optabs.c:2152` | `expand_abs` opens with `emit_move_insn (target, op0);` — **that is the copy** |
| `optabs.c:2162` | and it survives because `expand_abs` compares **`target`**, not `op0`: `compare_from_rtx (target, CONST0_RTX (mode), GE, ...)` |

cse equates the two and rewrites the branch's operand back to `op0`, so `op0`
is live **across** the move; the pseudos conflict in `global.c`, take two hard
registers, and reload cannot delete it. Hand-writing the second variable puts
the branch on the **copy's destination**, `op0` dies at the move, the pseudos
share a register and reload deletes it as a no-op — one word short.

**Same `(set temp op0)` / compare / in-place-op skeleton as the
divide-by-power-of-two lever, and the same single `=` decides it.** Listing
tell: `bgez` testing the **subtraction's** register with a copy in the delay
slot means a separate destination and a folding ternary; `bgez` on the temp
with a `nop` means in place.

**And the reason it took 49 spellings: it is a TWO-LEVER INTERACTION.** All
four corners, measured:

| | in-place abs | ternary into its own variable |
|---|---|---|
| **with** a hoisted field read | 40 / 15 | 40 / 15 |
| **without** the hoist | 41 / 35 | **40 / 0** |

Each lever alone is neutral or worse. The park had the hoist fixed — reasonably,
since with the in-place abs it is the only way to reach the right word count at
all — and inside that frame no abs spelling can help. **When a plateau is broad
and a permuter floors on it, suspect that a variable you are holding fixed is
half of the answer.**

### COMPARISON OPERAND ORDER IS WORTH A WORD WHEN IT DECIDES A BLOCK'S FIRST INSN

2026-11-03. This **replaces the CAUTION** previously attached to "which side of a
comparison the struct field sits on is NOT observable", and it is the
established mechanism rather than the interaction that caveat guessed at.

A predicate-preserving flip is unobservable in itself — probed, byte-identical,
with and without a sign extension. But gcc expands the **left** operand first,
so the flip decides which insn is the comparison block's **first**. If that
block is the target of a branch with an otherwise-empty delay slot, `reorg`
duplicates its first insn into the slot; a sign-extending `sll` is eligible and
a field's `lh` is not.

Measured: `func_800C1EA4` is 58 words / 0 differing with `(s16)adx > a->unk_08`
and **59 / 27** flipped — reorg takes the `sll`, or declines the `lh` and the
slot becomes a `nop`. Its near-sibling `func_800C1F8C` is **immune**, because
its two comparisons are `||` terms inside one `if` rather than separate
`if (...) return;` statements, so neither block is a branch target with a free
slot.

**So: do not start with orientation, but do measure it once you are at the
right length with a `nop`-versus-insn discrepancy in a delay slot.**

### TWO INDEPENDENT LOOP COUNTERS: SOURCE ORDER PICKS WHICH DELAY SLOT EACH FILLS

`func_800AF254`/`func_800B2D00`, 2026-11-03. A new consequence of the entry at
`:12165`, in a shape that one does not cover: there an `i++` competes with a
*pinned* reduced-giv update for a **load**-delay slot; here two source-level
counter increments compete for two different **branch** delay slots in one
basic block.

`sched.c` does not split a basic block at a `CALL_INSN`, so a loop body from
the exit `beqz` to the bottom `bnez` is **one** block and both increments are
schedulable anywhere in it. Both are zero-latency and mutually independent, so
`rank_for_schedule` ties on priority and on the three-way class and falls
through to `INSN_LUID (tmp) - INSN_LUID (tmp2)` (`sched.c:2470-2473`) --
**source order is preserved, and that decides which slot each one reaches.**
The increment left at the front of the block goes into the exit branch's slot;
the one left just before the `jal` is taken by `reorg`'s backward scan
(`reorg.c:3066-3077`).

`for (i = ...; ...; i++, j++)` is 0 differing. `j++` as the body's last
statement, or `j++, i++`, swaps both slots: **3 differing**.

**THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE SHARP HALF.** `func_800AF674` is the same loop
and is **completely insensitive** to increment order -- 0 differing all three
ways -- because its exit branch's delay slot is already taken by an
`addiu $a1, $sp` address-of for an out-parameter, so the two increments never
compete for it. **The lever exists only when the slot is otherwise empty**, so
"this loop family needs `i++, j++`" is false for the third member of that very
group.

### A DUPLICATED TAIL *CALL STATEMENT* IS NOT THE DUPLICATED-TAIL LEVER

`func_80097D54`, 2026-11-03, and this NARROWS "a tail duplicated into both arms
is still TWO copies when the allocator prices the pseudos". Writing
`func_80098988(t, b, c); return;` into both exits is 37 words / **0 differing**,
and a `-S` dump shows **one** `jal` -- cross-jumping unified them.

That lever bites when the allocator prices **distinct pseudos** across the two
copies. Two identical tails each ending in a `return`, with the arguments
already in the same hard registers, have nothing to price. On that function
**four** structurally different C spellings generate the identical instruction
stream, `jal`s included. **Do not spend compiles permuting a shared tail into
arms when the arms carry no live pseudos.**

Its fingerprint is **two `reorg` steals from one block**: one branch carries an
argument copy, a later branch carries another, each retargeted a word further
into the tail -- which is why the fall-through sets an argument register a
*second* time. That redundant set reads like a bug if you do not know it.

### A DEAD *MIDDLE* PARAMETER IS WITNESSED; ONLY A DEAD TRAILING ONE IS NOT

`func_800BF15C`, 2026-11-03. **Corrects** the blanket form of "an unread
parameter costs no words in the callee". Dropping an unread *middle* parameter
gives the right word count but **1 differing**, because every later parameter
slides down a register. Probed:

| source | the record pointer lands in |
|---|---|
| `three(s32 a, s32 dead, struct R *r)` | `$a2` |
| `two(s32 a, struct R *r)` | `$a1` |
| `trail(s32 a, struct R *r, s32 dead)` | `$a1` -- same as dropping it |

So the gap in the `$aN` sequence is itself the arity witness. The word count
does not move, which is why this reads as polish rather than an arity error.
Plain o32 argument assignment, not an optimiser decision -- no CDK citation
owed.

### A POINTER-TO-GLOBAL LOCAL MUST BE ASSIGNED AS A STATEMENT, NOT IN ITS DECLARATION INITIALISER

`func_800A2338`, 2026-11-03. **38 words / 0 differing against 37 / 37.** This is
the counterpart of the `local-alloc.c:1142` lever: there the question is *which*
statement, here it is **statement at all**.

`finish_decl` calls `expand_decl_init` **at the point of the declaration** --
`c-decl.c:3947-3948`, *"Compute and store the initial value"*, with
`expand_decl_init` at `stmt.c:3632`. So `u8 *g = (u8 *)&D_80083160;` emits its
`lui`/`addiu` at the top of the enclosing block, **outside** the `else` arm that
uses it. In `func_800A2338` that is one word short -- the `addiu` is no longer
available for the delay slot `reorg` needs -- and the whole allocation shifts.
Written as `g = (u8 *)&D_80083160;` inside the arm it is exact.

**Fingerprint: a declaration-initialiser candidate that is one word SHORT with
a near-total differing count, where the statement form is exact.**

### `*((u8 *)&SYM + N)` FOLDS THE OFFSET INTO THE RELOCATION -- AND `ovlverify` HIDES IT

`func_800A2338`, 2026-11-03. **A blind spot in our own measurement, so it is
worth knowing as a diagnostic rather than only as a lever.**

`*((u8 *)&D_80083160 + 0xA8)` compiles to `lui %hi(SYM+0xA8)` +
`lbu %lo(SYM+0xA8)` with **the addend in the instruction field**. `objdump`
prints `lbu $v1,0xA8($v0)` with an `R_MIPS_LO16` on it, which reads exactly like
a literal displacement and is not. gcc then materialises
`addiu $v0, $v0, %lo(SYM+0xA8)` for the *remaining* accesses and reaches them at
`1($v0)`/`2($v0)`: **37 words, 18 differing**. A pointer local gives one
`lui`/`addiu %lo(SYM)` base and literal `0xA8/0xA9/0xAA` displacements, which is
the target: **38 / 0**.

**`ovlverify`'s masking hides the addend, so the one-word deficit is the only
signal.** Check the relocation list, not the printed displacement:
`R_MIPS_LO16` on the **load** means the fold happened; on the **`addiu`** means
a base register.

### AN ALLOCATE-AND-WIRE BODY NEEDS A POINTER LOCAL FOR THE `n + 0x20` VIEW

2026-11-03, measured from both sides on two functions. A pointer local costs one
word and is **required** when the target has `addiu $vN, $v0, 0x20`; the cast
form (`*(u32 *)((u8 *)n + 0x30)`) keeps the offset in the displacement and is
one word short. `func_800A1C94` is 33/17 cast against 34/0 local;
`func_800BFB00` is 35/13 against 35/0.

### AN INSTALL FEEDING A LATER CALL'S ARGUMENT IS ORDER-SENSITIVE; A SLOT WRITE FOLLOWED BY A CALL THROUGH THAT SLOT IS NOT

Two things that look like one rule, separated by measurement on 2026-11-03
across two install families in ovl_town.

**The rule that holds.** When the installed value also has to reach a
registration call, the store must be written off the node through a local AND
must precede that call -- the store then lands in the `jal`'s delay slot:

```c
o->unk_10 = (u32)func_8008B9D8;
func_8004491C((UnkNode *)o, (u32)D_80033D54);
```

Spelled off the actor view instead: 5 differing. Written AFTER the call: a
26-word function became 29 words and 26 differing.

**The generalisation that does NOT hold**, and an agent drafted it from the
rule above before its own measurement killed it. For a slot write followed by
a call THROUGH that slot, the local buys nothing:

```c
m->unk_68 = (void (*)())m->unk_6C;   /* no local, 17 words, 0 differing */
m->unk_68();
```

cse forwards the +0x68 store to the +0x68 load, so no reload is emitted and
the store still falls into the `jalr`'s delay slot. The local-`f` form is also
17/0. Same on a 13-word sibling: the two-store cross-jumped form and the
local-`f` single-store form are both 0 differing.

**So the discriminator is whether the stored value is also an ARGUMENT.** If it
is, the store's position is load-bearing; if the only later consumer is an
indirect call through the slot itself, cse makes every spelling equivalent.
Over-applying the first rule costs nothing where it does not bite, but it is a
wrong diagnosis to carry into a function where it does.

### TWO FLAGS IN ONE FUNCTION CAN WANT OPPOSITE DECLARATION SCOPES -- `combine_regs` REFUSES THE TIE AT FUNCTION SCOPE

The existing declaration-scope entries say where a variable is declared decides
which allocator sees it. This is the mechanism underneath, and it is sharp
enough to predict which way each variable wants to go. Established landing
`func_80095C80` (ovl_town, 330 words, 2026-11-03), a four-arm wall-slide
resolver with two boolean flags per arm.

`local-alloc.c:470-477` marks a pseudo combinable only when it is single-block
AND dies exactly once:

```c
if (reg_basic_block[i] >= 0 && reg_n_deaths[i] == 1
    && (reg_alternate_class (i) == NO_REGS
        || ! CLASS_LIKELY_SPILLED_P (reg_preferred_class (i))))
  reg_qty[i] = -2;
else
  reg_qty[i] = -1;
```

and `local-alloc.c:1842` refuses the tie outright for the rest:

```c
/* Can't combine if SREG is not a register we can allocate.  */
|| (sreg >= FIRST_PSEUDO_REGISTER && reg_qty[sreg] == -1)
```

**So a flag declared at FUNCTION scope and assigned in four arms has
`reg_basic_block == -1` and `reg_n_deaths == 4`, lands at `reg_qty == -1`, and
`combine_regs` will not tie it to anything.** Declared inside the arm it is
`-2`, the tie runs `(set flag (xor (lt ...) 1))` back through the `slt` to the
`lw` that produced its operand, and the resulting single quantity crosses the
second call in the arm -- so it must be callee-saved. That is a FOURTH saved
register: two words of prologue and epilogue plus five register renames per
arm. Function-scoping it measured 328 words / 326 differing against 330 / 0.

**The converse is the same rule read the other way, and it is why the two flags
want opposite scopes.** The second flag is set in the arm's block and consumed
by a branch that is a block of its own, so it is multi-block WHATEVER its scope
and always goes to global-alloc. At function scope it is one allocno shared by
all four arms and gets one register; per-arm it becomes four allocnos and two
of them take a different register -- 4 differing. So the answer is one flag
per-arm and one at function scope, which no single reading of "declare it
narrow" or "declare it wide" would have produced.

**Diagnosis order, which is the transferable part.** Do not reason from the
schedule. The agent that landed this spent most of its run believing the
argument-setup placement and the `slt`/`xori` schedule were the thing to fix
and that register names would follow; it is backwards -- the schedule
difference was a CONSEQUENCE of the allocation, and one declaration-scope
change fixed schedule, registers and word count together. Two supporting facts
worth having: **a call does not end a basic block**, so an arm's two calls,
both flags and both branches are one scheduling region (which is the only
reason flag scope and the schedule interact at all); and a comparison's operand
order looked decisive at 74 differing but was a red herring -- with the scopes
right it is observable and WRONG at 4 differing, and the natural order is
required.

**Fingerprint:** a function with several structurally identical arms, each
computing a boolean that feeds a branch, where your candidate has one saved
register too many or too few and the differences inside each arm are register
names. Count `reg_n_deaths` by counting the arms that assign the flag.

### loop.c's ADDRESS GIV IS REACHABLE ONLY FROM AN INDEXED SUBSCRIPT -- A POINTER WALK PUTS THE `lo_sum` IN THE WRONG BLOCK

Established on `func_800A9A38` (ovl_town, 41 words, landed 2026-11-03), and it
is a cheap, decisive screen because the two states differ in the ENTRY BLOCK
and nowhere else.

```
candidate: lui $v0,%hi ; addiu $a1,$v0,%lo ; lb $v1,%lo($v0) ; li -1 ; ...beq...
target   : lui $a1,%hi ;                    lb $v1,%lo($a1) ; li -1 ; ...beq...
           [pre-header] addiu $a1,$a1,%lo
```

A pointer assigned in C before the loop puts its `lo_sum` in the ENTRY block,
so the `high` has to survive past the guard branch and takes a second register.
The target's `lo_sum` is in the LOOP PRE-HEADER -- after the guard branch -- and
writes the `high`'s own register, which is `loop.c` strength-reducing the
subscript into an address giv and dropping its initial value there. **Source
level cannot reach that: the pre-header does not exist until loop.c creates
it.**

**The negative half is what makes this worth the entry.** FIVE pointer
spellings measured the same 10 differing, byte-exact from word 11 on:
`while (*q != -1)`, `for (q = X; *q != -1; q++)`, an explicit guard plus
`do/while`, and both of those again with the array declared as a scalar and
taken by `&` instead of `extern s8 X[]`. Three INDEXED spellings all measure 0:
`for (i = 0; X[i] != -1; i++)`, an indexed `while` with `i++` at the tail, and
an indexed guard plus `do/while`. So the loop FORM is free and the
subscript-versus-pointer choice is everything.

**Fingerprint: two registers for a `lui`/`addiu` pair in the entry block where
the target has one register across the guard branch.** That is a
subscript-versus-pointer tell, not an allocator finding, and reasoning about it
as register pressure will not converge.

> **REFINED 2026-11-03, same day, on `func_800A1354`: THE CONSEQUENCE CAN BE
> LENGTH-NEUTRAL, and then the fingerprint above does not appear at all.** There
> the pointer walk measures **286 words, 26 differing** -- the SAME length as
> the indexed form, pure register renaming across the loop, with no extra
> address materialisation in the entry block to count. So the giv difference
> surfaces as ALLOCATION only. This matters because 26-differing-at-the-right-
> length reads like polish and is structural: if a loop walks a table and every
> differing word is a register name, try the indexed form before spending
> anything on allocation levers.

### A LOCAL FED BY A CALL RESULT IS `s32` PLUS A CAST, NOT `s16` -- AND THE SIGN EXTENSION'S SOURCE REGISTER SAYS SO

Established on `func_800C035C` (ovl_town, 475 words, landed 2026-11-03), where
it was the last differing word.

With `s32 n`, `n = call()` is a same-mode `(set pseudo (reg:SI 2))`, and
`make_regs_eqv` (`cse.c:849-874`) prefers a pseudo over a non-fixed hard
register as the quantity's canonical register:

```c
/* Prefer fixed hard registers to anything.  Prefer pseudo regs to other
   hard regs. ... */
```

so `canon_reg` returns the pseudo and a later `(s16)` cast's sign extension
reads the **callee-saved** register the pseudo got. With `s16 n` the assignment
is not a copy at all but `(set (reg:HI) (subreg:HI (reg:SI 2)))`, which enters
the hash table as an EXPRESSION, and cse substitutes the cheaper
`(subreg:HI (reg:SI 2))` -- the return register -- back into the extension.

**Fingerprint: a `sll ..., 16` whose source is a callee-saved register rather
than `$v0` means the local is `s32` with a cast at the use. If it reads `$v0`
directly, the local is `s16`.** One word, and invisible in every arithmetic
use.

### TWO DIFFERENT LOAD WIDTHS FOR ONE `s16` GLOBAL IN ONE FUNCTION IS NOT TWO DECLARATIONS

Established on `func_800A9E68` (ovl_town, 2026-11-03). Its listing loads
`D_80100D18` once with `lhu` plus a shift pair and once with a plain `lh`, in
the same function, which reads as two different declared types and is not.

The `lhu` site is `D_80100D18 / 2`, which emits SIX words:

```
lhu $v1,%lo ; sll $v1,$v1,16 ; sra $v0,$v1,16 ; srl $v1,$v1,31 ; addu $v0,$v0,$v1 ; sra $v0,$v0,1
```

and not the four an already-sign-extended load would give. Bit 31 of `x << 16`
is the same bit as bit 31 of `(x << 16) >> 16`, so combine rewrites the signed
division's sign-bit extract onto the PRE-`sra` value; the `sll` then has two
consumers and can no longer fold with the `sra` into a `sign_extend`, which is
the rewrite that would have produced the `lh`. The plain use of the same global
in the same function does get the single `lh`.

An explicit `(s16)` on the source is free. `>> 1` instead of `/ 2` is 40 words
against 43 and 32 differing, so the signed division is real.

**Corollary, measured on the same function: a truncating destination erases a
halfword global's signedness entirely.** `u16` and `s16` both measure 0
differing for two other globals there, because the result goes through an `sh`
and combine takes the `lhu` either way. Do not read an `lhu`/`negu` pair as a
signedness witness.

### A PLAIN CONSTANT STORE TO A *SIGNED* NARROW FIELD CANNOT PRODUCE `ori`

Established on `func_800A957C` (ovl_town, 2026-11-03). One word, and the knob
is the LVALUE's signedness rather than the value.

The target has `ori $v0, $zero, 0xFF00`. Writing `c->unk_20 = 0xFF00;` against
an `s16` field gives `addiu $v0, $zero, -256` instead. The front end converts
the `int` constant to the lvalue's type, and `force_fit_type`
(`fold-const.c`, body at `:212-215`) does this:

```c
/* Unsigned types do not suffer sign extension or overflow.  */
if (TREE_UNSIGNED (TREE_TYPE (t)))
  return overflow;

/* If the value's sign bit is set, extend the sign.  */
```

So a signed HImode destination gets -256, `SMALL_INT` holds, and expand emits
`addiu`; an unsigned one keeps 65280, `SMALL_INT` fails, and only `ori` can
materialise it. The fix is an unsigned LVALUE: `*(u16 *)&c->unk_20 = 0xFF00;`.
`c->unk_20 = -0x100` is also 1 differing, so writing the negative value does
not help -- it is the destination's type, not the literal's spelling.

This is the BARE-STORE case. The existing entry on constants that are not valid
16-bit immediates covers the ARITHMETIC form and scopes itself to whether the
constant's `plus` is outermost; there the fix is a separate SImode statement,
here it is the lvalue's type.

**Screen: a target materialising a constant with `ori` where your candidate
uses `addiu` on a halfword or byte store means the lvalue's signedness.**

### `preexpand_calls` PUTS THE CALL BEFORE **BOTH** OPERANDS, SO WHERE YOU SPLIT A STATEMENT DECIDES WHICH SIDE OF IT THE ARITHMETIC LANDS ON

Established on `func_800BB798` (ovl_town, 63 words, landed 2026-11-03), where
it was the whole function.

`expr.c:7347-7352`:

```c
 binop:
  preexpand_calls (exp);
  if (! safe_from_p (subtarget, TREE_OPERAND (exp, 1)))
    subtarget = 0;
  op0 = expand_expr (TREE_OPERAND (exp, 0), subtarget, VOIDmode, 0);
  op1 = expand_expr (TREE_OPERAND (exp, 1), NULL_RTX, VOIDmode, 0);
```

and `preexpand_calls`' own comment at `:9923` -- *"Expand all function calls
